Instead, the automatic butler comports itself in the way a stereotypical servant would. Some automatic butlers are created with slightly different skill sets. They can be created to speak more languages beyond that of their creator, making them passable family diplomats who might welcome foreign guests. Some are trained to take care of tasks that require specialization, such as tutoring the youth of the household or tailoring the family's clothes. The sidebar covers some other options for a whole domestic staff of constructed servants.

Automatic Cooks and Gardeners

Should the designs for creating automatic butlers reach the wider world, someone would likely end up creating variations of the magical construct. These creatures would use the same basic statistics as an automatic butler, with a few minor changes. An automatic cook might have cleanse cuisine as an innate spell, a knife Strike, and the ability to shoot a jet of boiling hot water. An automatic gardener might have scatter scree and other spells with the earth or plant traits as innate spells, a hoe or shovel Strike, and the ability to pelt foes at range with seeds.
Studious Butler.languagesDetails: one spoken by its creator (typically Common)

Alarm.name: Alarm
Alarm.description:
You ward an area to alert you when creatures enter without your permission. When you cast alarm, select a password. Whenever a Small or larger corporeal creature enters the spell's area without speaking the password, alarm sends your choice of a mental alert (in which case the spell gains the mental trait) or an audible alarm with the sound and volume of a hand bell (in which case the spell gains the auditory trait). Either option automatically awakens you, and the bell allows each creature in the area to attempt a @Check[perception|dc:15] check to wake up. A creature aware of the alarm must succeed at a Stealth check against the spell's DC or trigger the spell when moving into the area.

Heightened (3rd) You can specify a trigger for which types of creatures sound the alarm spell.

Light.name: Light
Light.description:
You create an orb of light that sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) in a color you choose. If you create the light in the same space as a willing creature, you can attach the light to the creature, causing it to float near that creature as it moves. You can Sustain the spell to move the light up to 60 feet; you can attach or detach it from a creature as part of this movement.

You can Dismiss the spell. If you Cast the Spell while you already have four light spells active, you must choose one of the existing spells to end.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.cVVZXNbV0nElVOPZ]{Spell Effect: Light}

Heightened (4th) The orb sheds light in a 60-foot radius (and dim light for the next 60 feet).

Mending.name: Mending
Mending.description:
You repair the target item. You restore 5 Hit Points per spell rank to the target, potentially removing the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6dNUvdb1dhToNDj3]{Broken} condition if this repairs it past the item's Broken Threshold. You can't replace lost pieces or repair an object that's been completely destroyed.

Heightened (2nd) You can target a non-magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Heightened (3rd) You can target a non-magical object of 2 Bulk or less, or a magical object of 1 Bulk or less.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Telekinetic Hand.name: Telekinetic Hand
Telekinetic Hand.description:
You create a floating, magical hand, either invisible or ghostlike, that grasps the target object and levitates it slowly up to 20 feet in any direction. When you Sustain the spell, you can move the object an additional 20 feet. If the object is in the air when the spell ends, the object falls.

Heightened (3rd) You can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 1 or less.

Heightened (7th) The range increases to 60 feet, and you can target an unattended object with a Bulk of 2 or less.

Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

Soul Fragment.name: Soul Fragment
Soul Fragment.description: Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by soul energy, though the donor soul's personality is suppressed in favor of a simple demeanor, either politely helpful or stoically pragmatic. It also has none of that creature's memories. This soul fragment removes the immunity to spirit most constructs have, but because the automatic butler's personality overrides that of the original creature, the butler does have some resistance to spirit damage.

Right This Way.name: Right This Way
Right This Way.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The automatic butler attempts to usher a creature along while removing their coat. The automatic butler attempts an Athletics check to [[/act reposition]] a Large or smaller creature within reach. On a success, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} on a critical success) as the automatic butler pulls at some part of their clothing or gear. The target can remove this condition by taking an Interact action.

Studious Strike.name: Studious Strike
Studious Strike.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The automatic butler learns from its mistakes. If the butler's last action was to attempt a fist Strike that missed (but not critically missed) its target, the butler makes a fist Strike against the same target. The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the attack, and on a hit, the butler deals an additional 1d6 precision damage.

Trial by Flame Trap.name: Trial by Flame Trap
Trial by Flame Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:23] (trained) to disable the nozzles or @Check[arcana|dc:26] (expert) or @Check[occultism|dc:26] (expert) to disable the nearby magical sensor
Trial by Flame Trap.hazarddescription: Nozzles connected to reservoirs of alchemist's fire are hidden just under the packed dirt of the floor, ready to spew burning jets when deployed.
Trial by Flame Trap.reset: The trap resets when an operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever. The trap can be reset only once per minute.

Burning Jets.name: Burning Jets
Burning Jets.description:
Trigger An operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever

Effect Three hidden nozzles rise from the ground, and each makes a flame jet Strike against a creature in the area marked on the map. A creature can be hit more than once if there are fewer than three targets. On a critical hit, the target takes 1d10 persistent fire damage.

Trial by Ice Trap.name: Trial by Ice Trap
Trial by Ice Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:23] (trained) to jam the vent closed or @Check[arcana|dc:26] (expert) or @Check[occultism|dc:26] (expert) to disable the nearby magical sensor
Trial by Ice Trap.hazarddescription: A hidden vent in the ceiling is attached to a reservoir of freezing alchemical reagents that can create a bone-chilling cloud.
Trial by Ice Trap.reset: The trap resets when an operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever. The trap can be reset only once per minute.

Frozen Mist.name: Frozen Mist
Frozen Mist.description:
Trigger An operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever

Effect A vent opens in the ceiling, issuing forth a cloud of frigid fog that quickly fills the area marked on the map. Each creature in the area takes @Damage[6d8[cold]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:26|basic|options:area-effect] save). Creatures that fail the save also take @Damage[1d8[persistent,cold]|options:area-damage] damage (@Damage[2d8[persistent,cold]|options:area-damage] damage on a critical failure). The area remains cold for the next minute, dealing @Damage[2d6[cold]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:22|basic|options:area-effect] save) to any creature who ends their turn in the area.

Trial by Poison Trap.name: Trial by Poison Trap
Trial by Poison Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:23] (trained) to disable the launcher or @Check[arcana|dc:26] (expert) or @Check[occultism|dc:26] (expert) to disable the nearby magical sensor
Trial by Poison Trap.hazarddescription: A dart launcher embedded in the ceiling holds a cartridge of darts tipped with deadly poison.
Trial by Poison Trap.reset: The trap resets when an operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever. The trap can be reset only once per minute.

Toxic Barrage.name: Toxic Barrage
Toxic Barrage.description:
Trigger An operator at the maze console in area A13 pulls the associated lever

Effect A dart launcher emerges from the ceiling and makes a poison dart Strike against two different creatures in the area marked on the map. A single creature can't be targeted more than once.

Wall Blades Trap.name: Wall Blades Trap
Wall Blades Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (trained) to disengage the mechanisms that operate the blades in one wall
Wall Blades Trap.hazarddescription: A series of rotating, serrated blades attached to long poles routinely slice out of grooves carved into the stone walls.
Wall Blades Trap.reset: The trap deactivates when the room is empty and resets after 1 minute.
Wall Blades Trap.routine: (3 actions) For each wall in which the mechanisms have been disabled or destroyed, the hazard has 1 fewer action. On each action, the hazard makes a serrated blade Strike against one creature within 10 feet of the west, east, or south wall. Each set of wall blades acts once per turn.
Wall Blades Trap.hp: to destroy the mechanisms in one wall

Slide and Dice.name: Slide and Dice
Slide and Dice.description:
Trigger A creature is within 10 feet of a trapped wall

Effect The hazard makes a serrated blade Strike against all creatures within 10 feet of the west, east, or south wall; these Strikes don't take a multiple attack penalty. The hazard then rolls initiative.

Whimsical Butler.publicNotes:

Whimsical Twirl.name: Whimsical Twirl
Whimsical Twirl.description:
Frequency once per round

Effect The automatic butler Strides up to its speed without triggering reactions. Any creature adjacent to the butler at the end of this movement must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:20|options:area-effect] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the beginning of the butler's next turn.

Zombie Shambler.name: Zombie Shambler
Zombie Shambler.publicNotes:
A zombie shambler is a slow-moving horror dangerous in larger groups.

A zombie's only desire is to consume the living. Unthinking and ever-shambling harbingers of death, zombies stop only when they're destroyed.

Jaws.name: Jaws
Jaws.description: Requirements The zombie has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}.

Slow.name: Slow
Slow.description: A zombie is permanently @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} and can't use reactions.

Control Console.name: Control Console
Control Console.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.R4mKMppRfwV3RMAl]{A13. Maze Control Room}

The crystalline “windows” embedded in the control console are valuable but highly fragile. Each can be pried free with a successful DC 20 Thievery check. On a failure or critical failure, the window shatters into shards of worthless crystal. Once removed from the console, the windows lose their magical properties. There are a total of eight windows, each worth 5 gp.

Doll Storage.name: Doll Storage
Doll Storage.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.iUA5BdUE3zGkzxWi]{A7. Doll Storage}

A PC who succeeds at a DC 18 Perception check finds a floppy rag doll among the otherwise mundane dolls.

Floppy Rag Doll.name: Floppy Rag Doll
Floppy Rag Doll.description:
This simple doll is made with scraps of cloth tied or sewn together into a basic humanoid shape, but its appearance belies its strange power over the actions of others. The head and limbs of the doll constantly droop and sway slightly, never able to remain in one position for very long. Whoever holds a floppy rag doll can feel it squirming in their grasp.

Activate—Loose Limbs 1 (manipulate, visual)

Frequency once per hour

Effect You brandish the floppy rag doll at a creature within 30 feet who can see you and shake it about. The creature's own limbs begin moving wildly in a similar fashion, and they must attempt a @Check[will|dc:19|options:inflicts:clumsy] saving throw.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target can't use reactions until the end your turn.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} and can't use reactions until the beginning of your next turn.

Critical Failure As failure, but @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2}

Gem Storage.name: Gem Storage
Gem Storage.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.yscmlk1YElMj6vsX]{A14. Gem Storage}

A PC who is at least trained in Arcana or Occultism notices that one of the crystals is a fear gem.

Fear Gem.name: Fear Gem
Fear Gem.description:
Activate 2 (concentrate)

Dark smoke seems to writhe within this obsidian gem. When you activate the gem, make a melee Strike. If you hit and deal damage, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical hit.

If you have the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.lkcM4V3VDAtjlR9P]{Intimidating Strike} feat, increase the frightened condition value caused by the Strike to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} on a critical hit.

Library.name: Library
Library.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.gh2XqRmZj7ipXARO]{A6. Library}

Two tearaway paper dolls used as bookmarks fall out once the notebook is opened. The rest of the books aren’t particularly valuable, but altogether they can be sold for 30 gp.

Tearaway Paper Doll.name: Tearaway Paper Doll
Tearaway Paper Doll.description:
Activate 1 (concentrate, manipulate)

A humanoid shape has been cut out of a single sheet of colored paper with a face and clothes drawn on. The face looks slightly worried, as if the doll knows what it was made for. You hold up the paper doll in two hands and rip it half, focusing your thoughts on a creature within 20 feet that you can see. That creature takes @Damage[3d6[slashing]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:18|basic] save) as the tears of the paper doll are mimicked on its body.

Books.name: Books
Books.description: These books aren’t particularly valuable, but altogether they can be sold for 30 gp.

Office.name: Office
Office.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.oP9eBmUlMec6nD1x]{A15. Thalleus' Office}

In addition to the papers in Thalleus’s desk, the occult tomes on the bookshelves can be sold for a total of 50 gp.

Some of the items may have been lost to the acid trap, as detailed in the linked journal page.

Scroll of Enlarge (Rank 2).name: Scroll of Enlarge (Rank 2)
Scroll of Enlarge (Rank 2).description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wzctak6BxOW8xvFV]{Enlarge}

Casting a Spell from a scroll requires holding the scroll in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell.

The spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack modifier and spell DC. The spell also gains the appropriate trait for your tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

Any physical costs are provided when a scroll is created, so you don't need to provide them when casting from a scroll. If the spell requires a locus, you must have that locus to Cast the Spell from a scroll.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Armor Potency (+1).name: Armor Potency (+1)
Armor Potency (+1).description:
A magic book that functions as a runestone holding a +1 armor potency rune.

Magic wards deflect attacks. Increase the armor's item bonus to AC by 1. The armor can be etched with one property rune.

You can upgrade the armor potency rune already etched on a suit of armor using the normal process for upgrading items and runes.

Craft Requirements You are an expert in Crafting.

Piles of Bones.name: Piles of Bones
Piles of Bones.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.U1Z3WgcFaRlDVlHo]{A11. Pit of Blades}

A PC who searches the piles of bones finds one of a pair of doubling rings on a bony finger; one of the crawling hands wears the matching ring.

Doubling Rings.name: Doubling Rings
Doubling Rings.description:
This item consists of two magically linked rings: an intricate, gleaming golden ring with a square-cut ruby, and a thick, plain iron ring. When you wield a melee weapon in the hand wearing the golden ring, the weapon's fundamental runes are replicated onto any melee weapon you wield in the hand wearing the iron ring. (The fundamental runes are weapon potency and striking, which add an item bonus to attack rolls and extra weapon damage dice, respectively.) Any fundamental runes on the weapon in the hand wearing the iron ring are suppressed.

The replication functions only if you wear both rings, and it ends as soon as you cease wielding a melee weapon in one of your hands. Consequently, the benefit doesn't apply to thrown attacks or if you're holding a weapon but not wielding it (such as holding in one hand a weapon that requires two hands to wield).

Wardrobe.name: Wardrobe
Wardrobe.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.lUI43ZNScYcgvSWM]{A9. Bedroom}

Once the animated wardrobe has been defeated, PCs who search the construct find a sleeves of storage hanging inside it. The gaudy, colorful robe stands out amid Professor Jongrim’s otherwise dour, uninspiring clothing.

Sleeves of Storage.name: Sleeves of Storage
Sleeves of Storage.description:
This loose robe has wide, voluminous sleeves that each contain an extradimensional space. These spaces each function as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.jaEEvuQ32GjAa8jy]{Spacious Pouch (Type I)} that can hold up to 5 Bulk of items (for a total of 10 Bulk), though no individual item can be of more than 1 Bulk; the sleeves grow slightly heavy as you reach maximum capacity. You can add or remove an item from a sleeve with a single hand free as an Interact action.

If a sleeve is completely empty, you can place your own familiar into that extradimensional space. It can survive comfortably in your sleeve for up to 1 hour, after which it begins to suffocate. While in your sleeve, it can't be affected or targeted by any effects, but you don't benefit from any master abilities. A familiar can exit the sleeve of its own volition with a single action that has the manipulate and move traits. You can't place any other creature into your sleeves, nor can you place your familiar in a sleeve if it's larger than Tiny. If your familiar is in your sleeve, you can't place any items in the sleeve.

Workshop.name: Workshop
Workshop.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.6uAVoIuORZpshY13]{A16. Soul Workshop}

The unfinished automaton’s face plate functions as a persona mask. Though mostly useless, enough of Thalleus’s tools can be salvaged to piece together a sterling artisan’s toolkit.

Persona Mask.name: Persona Mask
Persona Mask.description:
Despite covering the entire face, this alabaster mask does not hinder vision or other senses. Wearing the mask grants a +1 item bonus to Performance checks while acting, orating, performing comedy, or singing.

Activate—Assume Role A (concentrate)

Effect You change the mask's appearance into an artistic rendition of a dramatic character of your choice.

Artisan's Toolkit (Sterling).name: Artisan's Toolkit (Sterling)
Artisan's Toolkit (Sterling).description:
You need these tools to create items from raw materials with the Craft skill. Sterling artisan's tools give you a +1 item bonus to the check.

Different sets are needed for different work, as determined by the GM; for example, a blacksmith's toolkit differs from a woodworker's toolkit. If you wear your artisan's toolkit, you can draw and replace it as part of the action that uses it.

Speak with Plants (Constant, Fungi Only).name: Speak with Plants (Constant, Fungi Only)
Speak with Plants (Constant, Fungi Only).description:
You can ask questions of and receive answers from plants and fungi, but the spell doesn't make them more friendly or intelligent than normal. Most normal plants and fungi have a distinctive view of the world around them, so they don't recognize details about creatures or know anything about the world beyond their immediate vicinity. Cunning plant or fungus monsters are likely to be terse and evasive, while less intelligent ones often make inane comments.

Heightened (4th) The duration is 8 hours.

Verdant Burst.name: Verdant Burst
Verdant Burst.description:
When a fungus leshy dies, a burst of primal energy explodes from its body, restoring @Damage[2d8[healing]] Hit Points to each fungi creature in a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. This area is filled with fungi, becoming difficult terrain.

If the terrain is not a viable environment for this fungi, they wither after 24 hours.

Change Shape.name: Change Shape
Change Shape.description:
The fungus leshy transforms into a giant mushroom or patch of fungi. This ability otherwise uses the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dileJ0Yxqg76LMvu]{One with Plants}.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

Spore Cloud.name: Spore Cloud
Spore Cloud.description:
A fungus leshy can unleash a cloud of spores that irritates the eyes and throats of non-fungus creatures in a @Template[emanation|distance:15]. Each creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:16|options:area-effect,damaging-effect] save or take @Damage[1[persistent,poison]|options:area-damage] damage.

A creature has its vision reduced as long as the persistent damage continues and can see only within 20 feet.

Spores.name: Spores
Spores.description: A creature that takes damage from a fungus leshy's spore pod Strike must attempt a saving throw with the same DC (@Check[fortitude|dc:16]) and effect as its Spore Cloud ability

Big Eye.name: Big Eye
Big Eye.publicNotes:
These roughly human-sized reptiles have amazing feet capable of clinging tenaciously to any surface. Giant geckos are typically docile and shy but can be aggressive when cornered or defending their territory. These large-eyed lizards are found in a wide variety of habitats, from rain forests and deserts to mountain slopes or even underground caverns. They spend most of their time climbing around in large trees or on rocky cliffs, whether hunting for small animals or hiding from predators. A giant gecko's scales are often quite brightly colored or decorated in intricate patterns. Giant geckos span nearly 8 feet in length from head to tail, and they weigh about 120 pounds.

Giant geckos are sometimes used by smaller humanoids as guardians or mounts, as their docile nature makes them relatively easy to tame and train. Their superior climbing skills make giant geckos particularly popular within societies that dwell underground or near cliffs, such as goblins and kobolds. Their bright coloration also makes them favorite pets in high society.

Lizards have a wide range of appearances and abilities, but most share a basic reptilian shape—long tails, wide toothy mouths, and four legs. While a few species are capable of movement on two legs for short periods of time, most are strictly quadrupedal. The three species presented here represent the most common and well-known of the larger species.

Uncanny Climber.name: Uncanny Climber
Uncanny Climber.description: A giant gecko's feet allow it to climb virtually any surface, no matter how slick or sheer. If a giant gecko attempts an Athletics check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} and critically fails, it gets a failure instead.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object a 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.description: These blades come in a variety of shapes and styles, but they are typically 2 feet long.

Blowgun.name: Blowgun
Blowgun.description: This long, narrow tube is used for shooting blowgun darts, using only the power of a forcefully exhaled breath.

Dart.name: Dart
Dart.description: This thrown weapon is larger than an arrow but shorter than a javelin. It typically has a short shaft of wood ending in a metal tip and is sometimes stabilized by feathers or fur.

Dart (Coated with Giant Viper Venom).name: Dart (Coated with Giant Viper Venom)
Dart (Coated with Giant Viper Venom).description: This thrown weapon is larger than an arrow but shorter than a javelin. It typically has a short shaft of wood ending in a metal tip and is sometimes stabilized by feathers or fur.

Giant Viper Venom.name: Giant Viper Venom
Giant Viper Venom.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:17|options:damaging-effect,inflicts:drained]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (1 round)

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The jinkin deals 1d6 extra precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Tinker.name: Tinker
Tinker.description: A group of six jinkins can work together for an hour to imbue an item with a curse at a range of 60 feet. While this process is lengthy, it's also unobtrusive and can be performed while @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.XMcnh4cSI32tljXa]{Hiding}. Jinkins prefer to use this ability on magic items. The curse makes the item unreliable (@Check[flat|dc:5] check or waste any action to Interact with or Activate the item), adds a bizarre requirement to use the item, or imparts some other curse of a similar caliber.

Blood Vendetta.name: Blood Vendetta
Blood Vendetta.description:
Requirements You can bleed.

Trigger A creature deals piercing, slashing, or persistent bleed damage to you.

You curse the target, punishing it for having the audacity to spill your blood. The target takes 2d6 persistent bleed damage and must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half the persistent bleed damage.

Failure The target takes the full persistent bleed damage. Until the bleeding stops, the target has weakness 1 to piercing and slashing damage. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.buXx8Azr4BYWPtFg]{Spell Effect: Blood Vendetta (Failure)}

Critical Failure As failure, but the target takes double the persistent bleed damage.

Heightened (+2) The persistent bleed damage increases by 2d6.

Stupefy.name: Stupefy
Stupefy.description:
You dull the target's mind, depending on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} until the start of your next turn.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3} for 1 minute.

Telekinetic Maneuver.name: Telekinetic Maneuver
Telekinetic Maneuver.description: With a rush of telekinetic power, you move a foe or something they carry. You can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.lOE4yjUnETTdaf2T]{Reposition}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip} the target using a spell attack roll instead of an Athletics check.

Bane.name: Bane
Bane.description:
You fill the minds of your enemies with doubt. Enemies in the area must succeed at a Will save or take a –1 status penalty to attack rolls as long as they are in the area. Once per round on subsequent turns, you can Sustain the spell to increase the emanation's radius by 10 feet and force enemies in the area that weren't yet affected to attempt another saving throw.

Bane can counteract @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.XSujb7EsSwKl19Uu]{Bless}.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.UTLp7omqsiC36bso]{Spell Effect: Bane}

Daze.name: Daze
Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

Detect Magic.name: Detect Magic
Detect Magic.description:
You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies. You detect illusion magic only if that magic's effect has a lower rank than the rank of your detect magic spell. However, items that have an illusion aura but aren't deceptive in appearance (such as an invisibility potion) typically are detected normally.

Heightened (3rd) You learn the rank or level of the most powerful magical effect the spell detects, as determined by the GM.

Heightened (4th) As 3rd rank, but you also pinpoint the source of the highest-rank magic. Like for an imprecise sense, you don't learn the exact location, but can narrow down the source to within a 5-foot cube (or the nearest if larger than that).

Fear.name: Fear
Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

Force Barrage.name: Force Barrage
Force Barrage.description:
You fire a shard of solidified magic toward a creature that you can see. It automatically hits and deals 1d4+1 force damage. For each additional action you use when Casting the Spell, increase the number of shards you shoot by one, to a maximum of three shards for 3 actions. You choose the target for each shard individually. If you shoot more than one shard at the same target, combine the damage before applying bonuses or penalties to damage, resistances, weaknesses, and so forth.

Heightened (+2) You fire one additional shard with each action you spend.

Ill Omen.name: Ill Omen
Ill Omen.description:
The target is struck with misfortune, which throws it off balance. The target must attempt a Will save.

Success The target is unaffected.

Failure The first time during the duration that the target attempts an attack roll or skill check, it must roll twice and use the worse result.

Critical Failure Every time during the duration that the target attempts an attack roll or skill check, it must roll twice and use the worse result.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.AmsVO5Q6078mEvNt]{Spell Effect: Ill Omen}

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description:
You raise a magical shield of force. This counts as using the Raise a Shield action, giving you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, but it doesn't require a hand to use.

While the spell is in effect, you can use the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.jM72TjJ965jocBV8]{Shield Block} reaction with your magic shield. The shield has Hardness 5. You can use the spell's reaction to reduce damage from any spell or magical effect, even if it doesn't deal physical damage. After you use Shield Block, the spell ends and you can't cast it again for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.Jemq5UknGdMO7b73]{Spell Effect: Shield}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.QF6RDlCoTvkVHRo4]{Effect: Shield Immunity}

Heightened (+2) The shield's Hardness increases by 5.

Telekinetic Projectile.name: Telekinetic Projectile
Telekinetic Projectile.description:
You hurl a loose, unattended object that is within range and that has 1 Bulk or less at the target. Make a spell attack roll against the target. If you hit, you deal 2d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage—as appropriate for the object you hurled. No specific traits or magic properties of the hurled item affect the attack or the damage.

Critical Success You deal double damage.

Success You deal full damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

Staff.name: Staff
Staff.description: This long piece of wood can aid in walking and deliver a mighty blow.

Dagger.name: Dagger
Dagger.description: This small, bladed weapon is held in one hand and used to stab a creature in close combat. It can also be thrown.

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

Ring of Sigils.name: Ring of Sigils
Ring of Sigils.description:
This silver band is carved with the personal sigils of different individuals, adding one to represent you when you invest it. The ring allows you to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.AUctDF2fqPZN2w4W]{Sigil} as an arcane innate cantrip.

Activate—Track Sigil 1 (concentrate, detection)

Frequency once per 10 minutes

Effect You detect the general direction toward the most recent sigil you created using the ring. This activation fails if the sigil is more than 5 miles away or if there's lead or running water between you and the sigil.

Giant Viper.name: Giant Viper
Giant Viper.publicNotes:
The giant viper's fangs are a frightening sight, with injection tubes as long as daggers. The sheer amount of venom injected by a giant viper can cause severe blood clotting and leave a victim utterly drained of vitality.

Snakes come in an array of forms, from jungle-dwelling constrictors that wrap around their prey to venomous vipers with deadly bites. Regardless, all snakes consume their prey whole by unhinging their jaws and using powerful muscles to move the food down their throats and into their stomachs.

Coiled Strike (Special).name: Coiled Strike (Special)
Coiled Strike (Special).description:
As Reactive Strike, but the snake can use this reaction only if it's Coiled.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ReactiveStrike]

Coil.name: Coil
Coil.description: The giant viper uses an action to coil itself. While Coiled, the reach of its fangs is 10 feet and it has the Reactive Strike reaction. After the giant viper Strikes with its fangs, it becomes uncoiled.

Giant Viper Venom.name: Giant Viper Venom
Giant Viper Venom.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:17]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}

Hidden Pit.name: Hidden Pit
Hidden Pit.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:12|name:Remove the Trapdoor] to remove the trapdoor
Hidden Pit.hazarddescription: A wooden trapdoor covers a pit that's 10 feet square and 20 feet deep.
Hidden Pit.reset: Creatures can still fall into the trap, but the trapdoor must be reset manually for the trap to become hidden again.
Hidden Pit.stealthdetails: (or 0 if the trapdoor is disabled or broken)

Pitfall.name: Pitfall
Pitfall.description:
Trigger A creature walks onto the trapdoor.

Effect The triggering creature falls in and takes falling damage (typically @Damage[10[bludgeoning]|options:fall-damage] damage). That creature can use the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.3yoajuKjwHZ9ApUY]{Grab an Edge} reaction to avoid falling.

Crossbow.name: Crossbow
Crossbow.description: This ranged weapon has a bow-like assembly mounted on a handled frame called a tiller. The tiller has a mechanism to lock the bowstring in place, attached to a trigger mechanism that releases the tension and launches a bolt.

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.description: These blades come in a variety of shapes and styles, but they are typically 2 feet long.

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

Scamper.name: Scamper
Scamper.description:
Requirements The kobold warrior is adjacent to at least one enemy

Effect The kobold warrior Strides up to their Speed plus 5 feet and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. They must end this movement in a space that's not adjacent to any enemy.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The Shiverscale kobold deals an extra 1d4 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Mocking-Vain.name: Mocking-Vain
Mocking-Vain.publicNotes:
Weaker twigjacks are often found in cultivated forests and even gardens. They seek to drive away interlopers, growing as their environment runs wild.

Maladjusted forest denizens, twigjacks form from the cruel and prankish combination of fey and the very woods in which they reside. A twigjack's body is made up of prickly brambles woven with vines. Shaggy, mossy growth, not unlike hair, tops a twigjack's head. Its mouth is just a canyon of splintered and broken sticks bisecting its face. Leaves and sprigs of new growth randomly sprout from the creature's body. Many dense forests on Golarion have at least a handful of twigjacks living in the undergrowth.

While truculent and violent, twigjacks care deeply for what they consider to be their forests. These creatures harass outsiders who delve deep into their wooded domains, forcing back even the most determined explorers, foresters, and travelers, especially when those intruders cut roads through the forest. However, they are not terribly territorial when it comes to other forest creatures. When sylvan creatures, especially fey, rally against an outside threat, twigjacks in the area eagerly arrive to fight, even if they were not invited.

Bramble Jump.name: Bramble Jump
Bramble Jump.description:
Requirements The twigjack is in undergrowth

Effect The twigjack scrambles into the undergrowth and instantly teleports to a square of undergrowth within 60 feet. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Nether Rift.name: Nether Rift
Nether Rift.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:18|options:disable-nether-rift], @Check[nature|dc:18|options:disable-nether-rift], @Check[occultism|dc:18|options:disable-nether-rift], or @Check[religion|dc:18|options:disable-nether-rift] (trained) to seal the rift, three successes total; or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (3rd rank; counteract DC 17)
Nether Rift.hazarddescription: A chill wind blows from a fissure in the cavern wall.
Nether Rift.reset: The rift reopens after [[/gmr 2d10 #Years to reopen]] years. Killing the Path River Peeler permanently seals the rift.
Nether Rift.routine:
(2 actions) The hazard uses its first action to repeat its Wind from the Netherworld reaction. If any patch of barrow claw remains, one of the patches chosen by the GM releases a cloud of spores. The spores fill the barrow claw's space and last until the beginning of the hazard's next turn. Creatures within the spores become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}, and all creature outside the spores become concealed to creatures within it.

A creature that enters the spores or starts their turn in the area takes @Damage[1d6[persistent,cold]] damage until they brush off the spores as an Interact action.

Wind from the Netherworld.name: Wind from the Netherworld
Wind from the Netherworld.description:
Trigger The Path River Peeler enters the cave

Effect A gust of ice-cold wind from the Netherworld blasts from the rift in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15]. Creatures in the area take @Damage[2d4[cold]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:20|basic|options:area-effect] save). The hazard then rolls initiative.

Path River Peeler.name: Path River Peeler
Path River Peeler.publicNotes:
Like many cryptids, even the name of the Path River Peeler is a matter of dispute. Some say the creature earns its name from the corpses of its victims, which are often found stripped clean of skin but otherwise untouched. Others claim that corpses left in such condition are the exception to the rule. More frequently, no trace of the Peeler's victims is ever found—perhaps these skinless kills were simply abandoned by the Peeler before it could finish with its meal. Those who subscribe to this theory argue that a better name would be the "Pealer," after the echoing cries the beast makes while on the hunt. But what sense does it make to call it the Pealer, when everyone knows loud noises are the best way to drive off the monster? The arguments go round and round, with no end to the debate in sight.

The Peeler is most frequently encountered in a wild and largely unoccupied area north of Grayce called the Shivering Bluffs. Most people in Grayce, with the exception of the elderly who have tales from their youth, think the Peeler is just a story to frighten children and explain the killed and missing sheep that fall victim to wolves or other predators. Even so, everyone who grew up in Grayce can sing a few lines of a popular skipping rhyme the children in town sing while playing.

Barrow Claw

Purported sightings of the Path River Peeler often coincide with an outbreak of barrow claw: a rare, disease-bearing fungus that is cold to the touch and devastates nearby vegetation. Outbreaks of barrow claw have led some enthusiastic scholars to postulate that the cryptid itself is the source of the fungus. A more likely theory is that the Peeler and barrow claw share a habitat in the Netherworld, and that the former simply carries spores of the latter on its bristly hide.

Echolocation.name: Echolocation
Echolocation.description: The Path River Peeler can use its hearing as a precise sense at the listed range.

Flight Response.name: Flight Response
Flight Response.description:
Trigger The Path River Peeler gains the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} condition or its frightened condition increases

Effect The Peeler Strides or Climbs up to its Speed. The Peeler gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement.

Sensitive Ears.name: Sensitive Ears
Sensitive Ears.description: The Path River Peeler's oversized ears make it particularly sensitive to loud noises. A creature that attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize} the Peeler by shouting, banging on a shield, or similar tactic ignores the usual –4 circumstance penalty for not sharing a language with the Peeler. Whenever the Peeler takes sonic damage, it must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:16|options:inflicts:frightened] saving throw or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure).

Blood Run Cold.name: Blood Run Cold
Blood Run Cold.description: The Path River Peeler extends a bony finger at a creature it can see within 60 feet, draining heat from the creature's body and sapping the strength from their muscles. The creature takes @Damage[4d6[cold]] damage with a @Check[will|dc:20|basic|options:inflicts:enfeebled] save. On a failure, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} for 10 minutes (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} for an hour on a critical failure). The Peeler can't use Blood Run Cold again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Blood Run Cold]]{1d4 rounds}.

Otherworldly Cry.name: Otherworldly Cry
Otherworldly Cry.description:
The Path River Peeler makes an eerie, spine-tingling vocalization that can be heard up to a mile away. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] must attempt a @Check[will|dc:20|options:area-effect,inflicts:frightened,inflicts:fleeing] save. Regardless of the result, a creature is temporarily immune to the Peeler's Otherworldly Cry for 10 minutes.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Crossbow.description: This ranged weapon has a bow-like assembly mounted on a handled frame called a tiller. The tiller has a mechanism to lock the bowstring in place, attached to a trigger mechanism that releases the tension and launches a bolt.

Sneak Attack.description: The Shiverscale kobold deals an extra 1d4 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Crossbow.name: Crossbow
Crossbow.description: This ranged weapon has a bow-like assembly mounted on a handled frame called a tiller. The tiller has a mechanism to lock the bowstring in place, attached to a trigger mechanism that releases the tension and launches a bolt.

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.description: These blades come in a variety of shapes and styles, but they are typically 2 feet long.

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

Scamper.name: Scamper
Scamper.description:
Requirements The kobold warrior is adjacent to at least one enemy

Effect The kobold warrior Strides up to their Speed plus 5 feet and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. They must end this movement in a space that's not adjacent to any enemy.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The Shiverscale kobold deals an extra 1d4 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Skeletal Ogre.name: Skeletal Ogre
Skeletal Ogre.publicNotes:
The reanimated bones of giants make excellent necromantic thralls.

Animated skeletons are among the most common types of undead.

Glaive.name: Glaive
Glaive.description: This polearm consists of a long, single-edged blade on the end of a 7-foot pole. It is extremely effective at delivering lethal cuts at a distance.

Half Plate.name: Half Plate
Half Plate.description: Half plate consists of most of the upper body plates used in full plate, with lighter or sparser steel plate protection for the arms and legs. This provides some of the protection of full plate with greater flexibility and speed. A suit of this armor comes with an undercoat of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.zBYEU9E7034ENCmh]{Padded Armor} and a pair of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Ix2vicchE79d6Cl3]{gauntlets}.

Broad Swipe.name: Broad Swipe
Broad Swipe.description: The giant makes two Strikes with its glaive against two adjacent foes, both of whom are within its reach. Both attacks count toward the giant's multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn't increase until after both attacks.

Terrifying Charge.name: Terrifying Charge
Terrifying Charge.description:
The giant Strides and makes a horns Strike with a +4 circumstance bonus to damage.

If the strike hits, the giant attempts to [[/act demoralize]] the target.

Spiked Walls.name: Spiked Walls
Spiked Walls.disable: [[/act disable-device dc=15]]{Thievery} (trained) to snip the trip wire or jam the panel
Spiked Walls.hazarddescription: A low trip wire connects to a lattice panel covered with wooden spikes.

Spiked Wall.name: Spiked Wall
Spiked Wall.description:
Trigger A creature triggers the trip wire

Effect A lattice panel lashed with wooden spikes swings shut across the passage. The triggering creature takes @Damage[3d6[piercing]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:17|basic] save). The panel provides lesser @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.other-effects.Item.I9lfZUiCwMiGogVi]{Cover} and prevents movement along the passage. The panel can be pushed open like a door with an Interact action, but it swings shut again unless wedged open with a heavy object.

Sprigjack.name: Sprigjack
Sprigjack.publicNotes:
Weaker twigjacks are often found in cultivated forests and even gardens. They seek to drive away interlopers, growing as their environment runs wild.

Maladjusted forest denizens, twigjacks form from the cruel and prankish combination of fey and the very woods in which they reside. A twigjack's body is made up of prickly brambles woven with vines. Shaggy, mossy growth, not unlike hair, tops a twigjack's head. Its mouth is just a canyon of splintered and broken sticks bisecting its face. Leaves and sprigs of new growth randomly sprout from the creature's body. Many dense forests on Golarion have at least a handful of twigjacks living in the undergrowth.

While truculent and violent, twigjacks care deeply for what they consider to be their forests. These creatures harass outsiders who delve deep into their wooded domains, forcing back even the most determined explorers, foresters, and travelers, especially when those intruders cut roads through the forest. However, they are not terribly territorial when it comes to other forest creatures. When sylvan creatures, especially fey, rally against an outside threat, twigjacks in the area eagerly arrive to fight, even if they were not invited.

Bramble Jump.name: Bramble Jump
Bramble Jump.description:
Requirements The twigjack is in undergrowth

Effect The twigjack scrambles into the undergrowth and instantly teleports to a square of undergrowth within 60 feet. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Unstable Overlook.name: Unstable Overlook
Unstable Overlook.disable: @Check[acrobatics|dc:20] to tread lightly across the overlook onto more stable ground. Permanently disabling the hazard requires several hours of work and a successful @Check[crafting|dc:23] check (trained).

Collapse.name: Collapse
Collapse.description:
Trigger A Small or larger creature moves onto the weakened section of the overlook

Effect The ledge collapses. Any creature on the ledge that fails to [[/act grab-an-edge dc=20]] plummets 40 feet into the chasm below.

Spear.name: Spear
Spear.description: A long metal shaft ending with a metal spike, a spear can be used one-handed as a melee weapon and can be thrown.

Steel Shield.name: Steel Shield
Steel Shield.description:
Like wooden shields, steel shields come in a variety of shapes and sizes. Though more expensive than wooden shields, they are much more durable.

HardnessHPBT
52010

Leather Armor.name: Leather Armor
Leather Armor.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

Raise a Shield.name: Raise a Shield
Raise a Shield.description:
Requirements You are wielding a shield.

You position your shield to protect yourself. When you have Raised a Shield, you gain its listed circumstance bonus to AC. Your shield remains raised until the start of your next turn.

Scamper.name: Scamper
Scamper.description:
Requirements The kobold warrior is adjacent to at least one enemy

Effect The kobold warrior Strides up to their Speed plus 5 feet and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. They must end this movement in a space that's not adjacent to any enemy.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: Zotri deals an extra 1d4 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Zurkurk.name: Zurkurk
Zurkurk.publicNotes:
Kobold cavern mages are born more than trained, hatching from eggs that absorbed particularly large amounts of primal earth energy. Although there are many elementals and even natural terrain features that can give rise to cavern mages, most are related to the cavern-dwelling earth nymphs known as lampads. These lonely and capricious fey are as enthusiastic to receive the company of a kobold tribe as the kobolds are for the protection they receive in return.

Kobolds are small reptilian humanoids. They lurk in dark spaces, usually tunnels and mines beneath the earth, in either warrens of their own design or complexes discovered and colonized after the original builders have moved on. Though kobolds are far more pragmatic than courageous, they use every inch of their cunning to even the playing field between themselves and other, stronger creatures. They attack from the darkness and at range, and kobold artificers and engineers master the art of simple but effective traps, which they use to protect their lairs. Kobolds are skilled at working together by necessity, and they often set up ambushes or hit-and-run assaults that allow them to do the most damage possible without being harmed in return.

Kobolds are diligent and hardworking creatures. While some kobolds live in communal collectives that maintain neutral relations with the creatures around them, they can be easily swayed into serving malevolent powers or megalomaniacal leaders. This is in part due to kobolds' innate pragmatism, as they would rather concede to servitude than risk being killed, but it is also in part due to a reverence for the power they generally lack. Notably, kobold eggs left in the proximity of magical creatures or places tend to absorb similar traits from the exposure. The resulting physical changes mark the appearance of each tribe, but a few lucky kobolds are also born with magical power that reflects their tribe's patron.

Darkness.name: Darkness
Darkness.description:
You create a shroud of darkness that prevents light from penetrating or emanating within the area. Light does not enter the area and any non-magical light sources, such as a torch or lantern, do not emanate any light while inside the area, even if their light radius would extend beyond the darkness. This also suppresses magical light of your darkness spell's rank or lower. Light can't pass through, so creatures in the area can't see outside. From outside, it appears as a globe of pure darkness.

Heightened (4th) Even creatures with darkvision (but not greater darkvision) can barely see through the darkness. They treat targets seen through the darkness as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}.

Invisibility.name: Invisibility
Invisibility.description:
Illusions bend light around the target, rendering it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible}. This makes it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} to all creatures, though the creatures can attempt to find the target, making it @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} to them instead. If the target uses a hostile action, the spell ends after that hostile action is completed.

Heightened (4th) The spell lasts 1 minute, but it doesn't end if the target uses a hostile action.

Stupefy.name: Stupefy
Stupefy.description:
You dull the target's mind, depending on its Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} until the start of your next turn.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 3} for 1 minute.

Daze.name: Daze
Daze.description:
You push into the target's mind and daze it with a mental jolt. The jolt deals 1d6 mental damage, with a basic Will save. If the target critically fails the save, it is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6.

Enfeeble.name: Enfeeble
Enfeeble.description:
You sap the target's strength, depending on its Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} until the start of your next turn.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 3} for 1 minute.

Fear.name: Fear
Fear.description:
You plant fear in the target; it must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 3} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round.

Heightened (3rd) You can target up to five creatures.

Figment.name: Figment
Figment.description:
You create a simple illusory sound or vision. A sound adds the auditory trait to the spell and the sound can't include intelligible words or elaborate music. A vision adds the visual trait, can be no larger than a 5-foot cube, and is clearly crude and undetailed if viewed from within 15 feet. When you Cast or Sustain the Spell, you can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.GkmbTGfg8KcgynOA]{Create a Diversion} with the illusion, gaining a +2 circumstance bonus to your Deception check. If the attempt fails against a creature, that creature disbelieves the figment.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.2Hg3a06gZCSnUgSA]{Spell Effect: Figment}

Grim Tendrils.name: Grim Tendrils
Grim Tendrils.description:
Tendrils of darkness curl out from your fingertips and race through the air. You deal 2d4 void damage and @Damage[(@item.level)[bleed]] damage to living creatures in the line. Each living creature in the line must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half the void damage and no persistent bleed damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double void damage and double persistent bleed damage.

Heightened (+1) The void damage increases by 2d4, and the persistent bleed damage increases by 1.

Prestidigitation.name: Prestidigitation
Prestidigitation.description:
The simplest magic does your bidding. You can perform simple magical effects for as long as you Sustain the spell. Each time you Sustain the spell, you can choose one of four options.

  • Cook Cool, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material.
  • Lift Slowly lift an unattended object of light Bulk or less 1 foot off the ground.
  • Make Create a temporary object of negligible Bulk, made of congealed magical substance. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile-it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or locus or cost for a spell.
  • Tidy Color, clean, or soil an object of light Bulk or less. You can affect an object of 1 Bulk with 10 rounds of concentration, and a larger object at 1 minute per Bulk.

Prestidigitation can't deal damage or cause adverse conditions. Any actual change to an object (beyond what is noted above) persists only as long as you Sustain the spell.

Protection.name: Protection
Protection.description:
You ward a creature against harm. The target gains a +1 status bonus to Armor Class and saving throws.

Heightened (3rd) You can choose to have the benefits also affect all your allies in a @Template[emanation|distance:10] around the target.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.RawLEPwyT5CtCZ4D]{Spell Effect: Protection}

Shield.name: Shield
Shield.description:
You raise a magical shield of force. This counts as using the Raise a Shield action, giving you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn, but it doesn't require a hand to use.

While the spell is in effect, you can use the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.jM72TjJ965jocBV8]{Shield Block} reaction with your magic shield. The shield has Hardness 5. You can use the spell's reaction to reduce damage from any spell or magical effect, even if it doesn't deal physical damage. After you use Shield Block, the spell ends and you can't cast it again for 10 minutes.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.Jemq5UknGdMO7b73]{Spell Effect: Shield}

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spell-effects.Item.QF6RDlCoTvkVHRo4]{Effect: Shield Immunity}

Heightened (+2) The shield's Hardness increases by 5.

Void Warp.name: Void Warp
Void Warp.description:
You call upon the Void to harm life force. The target takes 2d4 void damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} until the start of your next turn.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.

Staff.name: Staff
Staff.description: This long piece of wood can aid in walking and deliver a mighty blow.

Inspiring Display.name: Inspiring Display
Inspiring Display.description:
Requirements Zurkurk's previous action was to Cast a Spell

Effect Zurkurk uses his magical display to inspire another kobold within 30 feet. That kobold gains 4 temporary Hit Points that last until the start of Zurkurk's next turn.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.smk2cD6M3dsEPBCY]{Effect: Inspiring Display}

Scamper.name: Scamper
Scamper.description:
Requirements The kobold cavern mage is adjacent to at least one enemy

Effect The kobold cavern mage Strides up to their Speed plus 5 feet and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against reactions triggered by this movement. They must end this movement in a space that's not adjacent to any enemy.

Carvings.name: Carvings
Carvings.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11. Coven Cave}

Among the carvings is a stylized image of a cat that any character trained in Occultism recognizes as an ancient symbol of protection. The image is etched into the wall, but the characters can chip it away with a minute of work. Once separated from the stone, the symbol functions as a jade cat talisman.

Jade Cat.name: Jade Cat
Jade Cat.description:
Activate F (concentrate)

Trigger You fall or attempt an Acrobatics check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.M76ycLAqHoAgbcej]{Balance}

Requirements You are trained in Acrobatics

A thumb-sized feline carved of rare stone, the jade cat is typically worn as a pendant upon a suit of armor. For 1 minute after you activate the cat, you treat all falls as 20 feet shorter, you are not @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} when you Balance, and narrow surfaces and uneven ground are not difficult terrain for you.

Remains.name: Remains
Remains.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.Ko6VaK8YonCisnAN]{A10. Hidden Cave}

If the PCs make their way into the cave, they discover Klerran’s bones in a heap against the northern wall. Bloodstains on Klerran’s buckler suggest the man died of violence, though his rapier still rests inside its sheath nearby. Klerran’s pack has mostly rotted away, but among the scraps of leather the PCs can turn up his fateful bugle (a virtuoso musical instrument), as well as a vagabond’s teapot.

Rapier.name: Rapier
Rapier.description: The rapier is a long and thin piercing blade with a basket hilt. It is prized among many as a dueling weapon.

Vagabond's Teapot.name: Vagabond's Teapot
Vagabond's Teapot.description:
These ceramic teapots are highly valued by travelers. While the teapot is filled with water, a creature can use a single action with the concentrate trait to instantly heat the water to boiling, at which point the kettle whistles and the water inside begins to cool at a normal rate. While the water remains heated, it is piping hot, and a creature splashed with it takes @Damage[1d4[fire]|traits:nonlethal]{1d4 nonlethal fire damage}. Instead of filling the teapot with water, you can pour an elixir of 4th level or lower into the pot and use the following activation.

Activate—Share Brew 10 minutes (concentrate)

Frequency once per day

Effect The teapot magically increases the volume of the inserted elixir to produce four uses of the same elixir. Once an elixir has been brewed in the teapot in this way, further attempts that day to brew another elixir spoil the inserted liquid. Any brewed elixir not consumed by the time it cools (typically 10 minutes) loses its alchemical properties.

Virtuoso Bugle.name: Virtuoso Bugle
Virtuoso Bugle.description:
Handheld instruments include bagpipes, a small set of chimes, small drums, fiddles and viols, flutes and recorders, small harps, lutes, trumpets, and similarly sized instruments. The GM might rule that an especially large handheld instrument (like a tuba) has greater Bulk. Heavy instruments such as large drums, a full set of chimes, and keyboard instruments are less portable and generally need to be stationary while played.

A virtuoso instrument is more finely made and gives a +1 item bonus to Performance checks using that instrument.

Rubble and Debris.name: Rubble and Debris
Rubble and Debris.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5. Chasm of Echoes}

The cavern’s floor is littered with rubble and other debris the Shiverscale kobolds have tossed into the chasm. A PC who succeeds at a DC 14 Perception check to Search through the trash discovers a silver bangle, once worn by the ogre as an earring, worth 5 gp.

Scattered Tools.name: Scattered Tools
Scattered Tools.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.3Yz7wzrYSmukQjUp]{A2. Trapped Entrance}

Crumbrunk’s trap making tools function as an artisan’s toolkit worth 4 gp. Among the scattered tools is a thin glass vial that contains a lesser antidote.

Artisan's Toolkit.name: Artisan's Toolkit
Artisan's Toolkit.description: You need these tools to create items from raw materials with the Craft skill. Different sets are needed for different work, as determined by the GM; for example, a blacksmith's toolkit differs from a woodworker's toolkit. If you wear your artisan's toolkit, you can draw and replace it as part of the action that uses it.

Antidote (Lesser).name: Antidote (Lesser)
Antidote (Lesser).description:
Activate A (manipulate)

An antidote protects you against toxins. Upon drinking an antidote, you gain a +2 item bonus to Fortitude saving throws against poisons for 6 hours.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.TjBxxlTvb6tJP1jS]{Effect: Antidote}

Shiverscales' Wealth.name: Shiverscales' Wealth
Shiverscales' Wealth.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.MSBwuZS2h79nNNtf]{A7. Zurkurk's Cave}

The alcove behind the curtain to the southwest conceals Zurkurk’s sleeping space. Blankets and animal pelts crowd the alcove. A shelf carved into the wall holds Zurkurk’s collection of brushes and paints, as well the entirety of the Shiverscales’ wealth: a pouch containing 80 sp and 32 gp, a collection of four minor healing potions, and an ivory walrus tusk worth 10 gp.

Healing Potion (Minor).name: Healing Potion (Minor)
Healing Potion (Minor).description:
Activate A (manipulate)

A healing potion is a vial of a ruby-red liquid that imparts a tingling sensation as the drinker's wounds heal rapidly. When you drink a healing potion, you regain @Damage[1d8[healing]] Hit Points.

Sleeping Shelf.name: Sleeping Shelf
Sleeping Shelf.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.hQcK73p7jr2f9Hqc]{A4. Gecko Grotto}

Zoti’s sleeping shelf is filled with heavy winter blankets and foul-smelling animal furs. Beneath the assorted bedding is a gecko potion.

Gecko Potion.name: Gecko Potion
Gecko Potion.description:
Activate A (manipulate)

A gecko potion is a sticky, tawny brown liquid with flecks of sand suspended in it. For 5 minutes after drinking this potion, your fingertips sprout thousands of microscopic, bristled hairs that cling to objects, granting you gain a +1 item bonus to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ijZ0DDFpMkWqaShd]{Palm an Object} checks and to your Reflex DC against @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm} attempts.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.buJnkFBzL4e22ASp]{Effect: Gecko Potion}

Orc Necksplitter.name: Orc Necksplitter
Orc Necksplitter.description: This single-bladed bearded axe has a jagged blade that's perfect for separating bone from tendon and cartilage.

Orc Necksplitter (yjjV).name: Orc Necksplitter
Orc Necksplitter (yjjV).description: This single-bladed bearded axe has a jagged blade that's perfect for separating bone from tendon and cartilage.

Javelin.name: Javelin
Javelin.description: This thin spear is well balanced for throwing but is not designed for melee use.

Breastplate.name: Breastplate
Breastplate.description: Though referred to as a breastplate, this type of armor consists of several pieces of plate or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.pRoikbRo5HFW6YUB]{Half Plate} armor that protect the torso, chest, neck, and sometimes the hips and lower legs. It strategically grants some of the protection of plate while allowing greater flexibility and speed.

Doubling Rings.name: Doubling Rings
Doubling Rings.description:
This item consists of two magically linked rings: an intricate, gleaming golden ring with a square-cut ruby, and a thick, plain iron ring. When you wield a melee weapon in the hand wearing the golden ring, the weapon's fundamental runes are replicated onto any melee weapon you wield in the hand wearing the iron ring. (The fundamental runes are weapon potency and striking, which add an item bonus to attack rolls and extra weapon damage dice, respectively.) Any fundamental runes on the weapon in the hand wearing the iron ring are suppressed.

The replication functions only if you wear both rings, and it ends as soon as you cease wielding a melee weapon in one of your hands. Consequently, the benefit doesn't apply to thrown attacks or if you're holding a weapon but not wielding it (such as holding in one hand a weapon that requires two hands to wield).

Chopping Frenzy.name: Chopping Frenzy
Chopping Frenzy.description:
Requirements Alendreu is wielding an orc necksplitter in each hand

Effect Alendreu lashes out with both axes. He attempts two Strikes, one with each necksplitter, each using his current multiple attack penalty. Both Strikes must have the same target, and the second strike takes a –2 penalty.

If both hit, combine their damage and apply resistances and weaknesses only once, and the target becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} from the fury of the blow until the start of their next turn. This counts as two attacks when calculating Alendreu's multiple attack penalty.

Consume Flesh.name: Consume Flesh
Consume Flesh.description:
Requirements The ghoul is adjacent to the corpse of a creature that died within the last hour.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[(1+(max(0,floor(@actor.level/2))))d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Ghoul Whispers.name: Ghoul Whispers
Ghoul Whispers.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature is within the ghoul's reach

Effect The ghoul whispers dark thoughts and vile cravings into the creature's ears. The creature must save against the forbidden cravings curse.

Forbidden Cravings (curse) A creature can still eat and drink while sickened by this curse

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:21|traits:curse], using the high spell DC for the ghoul's level

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[void]] damage and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} until it consumes raw meat (1 day)

Stage 3 as stage 2

Stage 4 as stage 2 unless the target has consumed raw meat in the past 24 hours, then it takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until it consumes raw meat;

Stage 5 if the creature has eaten raw meat in the past 24 hours, it dies and rises as a ghoul, if not, it returns to stage 4

Grave Knowledge.name: Grave Knowledge
Grave Knowledge.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The ghoul calls upon knowledge it retains from one creature it has consumed in the past 7 days. The ghoul attempts a skill check using a skill in which the consumed creature was trained (if it's unclear whether the creature was trained, the GM decides). The ghoul is treated as trained and uses the high skill modifier for the ghoul's level ([[/gmr 1d20+12]]). This takes the same amount of actions or time as usual for the check.
