Balance Point.name: Balance Point
Balance Point.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (trained) to attach the balanced stone floor piece to the actual floor and lock it in place, or @Check[crafting|dc:23] (trained) to jury-rig a quick bit of extra support to prevent the floor from tilting
Balance Point.hazarddescription: A 40-foot deep pit is obscured by a false floor set over a single balance point. Pressure on either side to the east or west causes occupants to fall into the depths below.

Tipping Floor.name: Tipping Floor
Tipping Floor.description:
Trigger A creature walks onto one side of the false floor

Effect The triggering creature falls into the pit and takes @Damage[20[bludgeoning]] damage from the fall unless they [[/act grab-an-edge dc=23]]. It's a @Check[athletics|dc:20] check to climb the pit walls.

Darkness.name: Darkness
Darkness.description:
You create a shroud of darkness that prevents light from penetrating or emanating within the area. Light does not enter the area and any non-magical light sources, such as a torch or lantern, do not emanate any light while inside the area, even if their light radius would extend beyond the darkness. This also suppresses magical light of your darkness spell's rank or lower. Light can't pass through, so creatures in the area can't see outside. From outside, it appears as a globe of pure darkness.

Heightened (4th) Even creatures with darkvision (but not greater darkvision) can barely see through the darkness. They treat targets seen through the darkness as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed}.

Grim Tendrils.name: Grim Tendrils
Grim Tendrils.description:
Tendrils of darkness curl out from your fingertips and race through the air. You deal 2d4 void damage and @Damage[(@item.level)[bleed]] damage to living creatures in the line. Each living creature in the line must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half the void damage and no persistent bleed damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes double void damage and double persistent bleed damage.

Heightened (+1) The void damage increases by 2d4, and the persistent bleed damage increases by 1.

Void Warp.name: Void Warp
Void Warp.description:
You call upon the Void to harm life force. The target takes 2d4 void damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a critical failure, the target is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} until the start of your next turn.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.

Shortsword.name: Shortsword
Shortsword.description: These blades come in a variety of shapes and styles, but they are typically 2 feet long.

Padded Armor.name: Padded Armor
Padded Armor.description: This armor is simply a layer of heavy, quilted cloth, but it is sometimes used because it's so inexpensive. Padded armor is easier to damage and destroy than other types of armor. Heavy armor comes with a padded armor undercoat included in its Price, though it loses the comfort trait when worn under heavy armor. You can wear just that padded armor undercoat to sleep in, if your heavy armor is destroyed, or when otherwise not wearing the full heavy armor. This allows you to keep magic armor invested and benefit from the power of any runes on the associated heavy armor, but no one else can wear your heavy armor without the padded undercoat.

Consume Flesh.name: Consume Flesh
Consume Flesh.description:
Requirements The ghoul is adjacent to the corpse of a creature that died within the last hour.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[(1+(max(0,floor(@actor.level/2))))d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Ghoul Whispers.name: Ghoul Whispers
Ghoul Whispers.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature is within the ghoul's reach

Effect The ghoul whispers dark thoughts and vile cravings into the creature's ears. The creature must save against the forbidden cravings curse.

Forbidden Cravings (curse) A creature can still eat and drink while sickened by this curse

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:20|traits:curse], using the high spell DC for the ghoul's level

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[void]] damage and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} until it consumes raw meat (1 day)

Stage 3 as stage 2

Stage 4 as stage 2 unless the target has consumed raw meat in the past 24 hours, then it takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until it consumes raw meat;

Stage 5 if the creature has eaten raw meat in the past 24 hours, it dies and rises as a ghoul, if not, it returns to stage 4

The ghoul can instead automatically learn something specific known by a creature it consumed in the last 7 days, like the location of a hidden treasure or the name of a loved one. The ghoul can do this only once for a given creature, no matter how much of its flesh the ghoul consumed.

Sneak Attack.description: Carexilia deals an additional 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Swift Leap.name: Swift Leap
Swift Leap.description: The ghoul jumps up to half its Speed. This movement doesn't trigger reactions.

Centipede Swarm.name: Centipede Swarm
Centipede Swarm.publicNotes:
Swarms of centipedes are dangerous indeed, ravenous carpets of skittering hunger capable of devouring a traveler whole in a matter of minutes. Kobolds and mitflits are both known to incorporate swarms of centipedes into cunning traps.

Hunters and scavengers that live amid dung and detritus, centipedes are a relatively common and often reviled threat faced by adventurers. Scurrying about with surprising speed on the scores of legs attached to their long, segmented bodies, centipedes strike with poisoned mandibles to slow and torment their prey with a vicious toxin before they settle down to feed in slow and disgusting leisure.

Centipede Swarm Venom.name: Centipede Swarm Venom
Centipede Swarm Venom.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:20]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d6[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[1d8[poison]] damage, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}, and off-guard (1 round)

Swarming Bites.name: Swarming Bites
Swarming Bites.description: Each enemy in the swarm's space takes @Damage[1d8[piercing]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:20|basic|options:area-effect] save) plus centipede swarm venom.

Destroyed Explorer's Clothing.name: Destroyed Explorer's Clothing
Destroyed Explorer's Clothing.description: Adventurers who don't wear armor travel in durable clothing. Though it's not armor and uses your unarmored defense proficiency, it still has a Dex Cap and can grant an item bonus to AC if etched with potency runes.

Hazard Finder.name: Hazard Finder
Hazard Finder.description: Ecaterina gains a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find traps or environmental hazards (but not to finding haunts), to AC against attacks made by traps, and to saves against traps.

Last Second Warning.name: Last Second Warning
Last Second Warning.description:
Trigger A creature Ecaterina can see triggers a hazard

Effect Ecaterina notices the danger a split-second before it activates and calls out a warning to the creature that triggered it. If that creature can hear and understand her warning, it gains a +1 circumstance bonus to its AC against attacks made by the hazard, and to saves against the triggering hazard.

Gauntling.name: Gauntling
Gauntling.publicNotes:
In places like the Gravelands, undeath permeates the very soil of the land. This unholy pollution can have significant effects on regional flora and fauna over the course of generations, causing plants to become twisted and diseased looking and contaminates wildlife so their remains spontaneously rise as mindless undead.

Yet in some cases, particularly for those beasts who forage primarily through the act of scavenging, the consumption of undead flesh can have an entirely different effect over the course of months. How quickly an animal is affected depends on whether it ate from the remains of an undead creature left behind after its destruction or consumed it "fresh" from an undead in a desperate throe of starvation. Assuming the unfortunate creature survives any onset of disease or other afflictions brought on by their ghastly repast, these scavengers sometimes undergo a transformation into a twisted, ravenous beast known as a gauntling.

Most gauntlings arise from scavengers, carnivores, or omnivores, but in certain cases, desperate herbivores can become transformed as well—these creatures are perhaps the most disturbing type of gauntling, due to the significant change in their behaviors pushing them toward diets of fresh meat. Once animals become gauntlings, these creatures abandon their previous wilderness habitats in favor of those near more settled regions and often choose sewers or other underground locales as dens from which they emerge to hunt. In their transformation into a gauntling, regardless of what the creature's previous dietary leanings might have been, all gauntlings share one horrific hunger—the flesh of sapient humanoids. A gauntling looks similar to the animal it was before its transformation, but with large sharp fangs and with painfully emaciated frames, regardless of how much they eat.

This gauntling (as are all of those encountered in Troubles in Grayce) were once boars, but you can use these statistics to represent any terrestrial Medium animal that's succumbed to this unholy transformation. Regardless of its original form, all gauntlings share a mouthful of sharp, twisted fangs.

Other Gauntlings

The gauntling presented here comes from a Medium terrestrial animal (a boar, to be precise), but other animals can be transformed in this way by consuming undead flesh. To represent one from a swimming or flying Medium animal, simply grant it a swim or fly speed equal to its base speed. To represent a smaller or larger creature, use the statistics presented here as a starting point, then rebuild the statistics using the guidelines for building creatures that begin on page 112 of GM Core

Soul Ravage.name: Soul Ravage
Soul Ravage.description:
A gauntling's fangs carry with them a potent curse that eagerly seeps into living flesh. The first time in a round that a creature takes damage from a gauntling's jaws Strike, they must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:18|options:inflicts:sickened] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}.

Failure The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} and can't reduce its sickened value below 1 for 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, but for 1 hour. A creature that dies while under this curse's effects rises within 24 hours as a zombie.

Ghoul Stalker.name: Ghoul Stalker
Ghoul Stalker.publicNotes:
Ghouls stalkers are ravenous undead who haunt graveyards and eat corpses.

Few creatures are more ubiquitous to sinister locations such as lonely graveyards and ruined crypts than the flesh-eating undead known as ghouls.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[1d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Giant Centipede.name: Giant Centipede
Giant Centipede.publicNotes:
Most giant centipedes (known as sewer centipedes when found in cities) nest in small groups but hunt alone when they seek out food. Attempts to domesticate giant centipedes for use as guardians or pets generally end poorly, but some communities of goblins, kobolds, and mitflits have developed effective methods of utilizing these vermin as guardians. Other groups roast and eat centipedes, often with pungent peppers as a savory delicacy, although care must be taken in preparing the meal to avoid tainting the flesh with the creature's venom.

Hunters and scavengers that live amid dung and detritus, centipedes are a relatively common and often reviled threat faced by adventurers. Scurrying about with surprising speed on the scores of legs attached to their long, segmented bodies, centipedes strike with poisoned mandibles to slow and torment their prey with a vicious toxin before they settle down to feed in slow and disgusting leisure.

Giant Centipede Venom.name: Giant Centipede Venom
Giant Centipede Venom.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:14]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[1d4[poison]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[1d4[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} (1 round)

Stage 3 @Damage[1d4[poison]] damage, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} (1 round)

Giant Dragonfly Nymph.name: Giant Dragonfly Nymph
Giant Dragonfly Nymph.publicNotes:
The aquatic, wingless offspring of dragonflies are called dragonfly nymphs. Giant dragonfly nymphs can be several feet in length and mostly hunt in shallow waters, eating carrion and ambushing living creatures with their fully grown counterparts. They're not daunted by larger creatures, compelled by their instinct to eat as much as possible to sustain their growth.

Dragonflies hunt with a combination of agile power and deadly speed. In early life stages, these insects are entirely aquatic predators, but they take to the air once they've molted. Most live around bodies of water suitable for spawning, but giant dragonflies have been known to fly many miles while on the hunt. Though their gossamer wings and colorful bodies are beautiful at first glance, an unwary adventurer lured in by the display runs a very real risk of becoming lunch.

Extend Mandibles.name: Extend Mandibles
Extend Mandibles.description: The giant dragonfly nymph extends its jaws to a surprising distance. The dragonfly nymph makes a mandibles Strike with a reach of 10 feet, but the mandibles lose the agile trait for this Strike.

Inheritor's Kiss.name: Inheritor's Kiss
Inheritor's Kiss.description: This broad-bladed sword, sometimes called the hand-and-a-half sword, has a longer grip so it can be held in one hand or used with two hands to provide extra slashing power.

Breastplate.name: Breastplate
Breastplate.description: Though referred to as a breastplate, this type of armor consists of several pieces of plate or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.pRoikbRo5HFW6YUB]{Half Plate} armor that protect the torso, chest, neck, and sometimes the hips and lower legs. It strategically grants some of the protection of plate while allowing greater flexibility and speed.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Frightful Snarl.name: Frightful Snarl
Frightful Snarl.description: Krethark snarls and glares at a creature within 30 feet that he can see, and then attempts to [[/act demoralize]] that creature; he doesn't take a penalty if the creature doesn't understand his language. A creature that becomes frightened by Frightful Snarl is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} until the start of their turn.

Old Murder Holes.name: Old Murder Holes
Old Murder Holes.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (trained) to deactivate the trigger on the floor, or @Check[athletics|dc:23] to pry up the floor plate to dislodge it from the trigger.
Old Murder Holes.hazarddescription: Several dozen spear holes line the sides of the cavern walls, triggered by a false stone in the partially paved surface of the cavern floor. However, most of the spears used to arm the trap are broken and long forgotten on the dusty cavern floor.

Spear Launcher.name: Spear Launcher
Spear Launcher.description:
Trigger Downward pressure (such as by a footstep) is applied to the false stone

Effect The trap shoots several spears, making an attack against the triggering creature or object on the stone.

Rolling Death.name: Rolling Death
Rolling Death.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:22] (trained) to set the trip wire to a different anchor point without changing the tension
Rolling Death.hazarddescription: A trip wire hidden in the dust of the midway point of the floor releases a large boulder to roll from the northwestern corridor toward A4, crushing anything it meets.

Tumbling Boulder.name: Tumbling Boulder
Tumbling Boulder.description:
Trigger The trip wire is pulled or severed

Effect The boulder careens from its holding area to crush anything in its path. Anyone in area A3 path takes @Damage[(2d12+4)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:25|basic] save).

Rope Pull.name: Rope Pull
Rope Pull.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:20] (trained) to tie off the rope to a more solid support
Rope Pull.hazarddescription: This trap appears to be an obvious 10-foot-deep pit with angled walls to prevent easy escape, but the true danger is represented not by the hole in the ground but from a set of loose stones in the ceiling. A knotted rope hangs from a beam above, seemingly to provide an option to swing across the pit, but any weight on the rope pulls down large, heavy boulders stacked far above.

Boulders from Above.name: Boulders from Above
Boulders from Above.description:
Trigger A Small or larger creature or equivalent weight pulls on the rope

Effect All creatures within the pit or adjacent to the pit take @Damage[(4d6+10)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:23|basic] save) from falling rocks dislodged from above.

Unstable Floor.name: Unstable Floor
Unstable Floor.disable: @Check[engineering-lore|dc:20], @Check[mining-lore|dc:20], or @Check[survival|dc:23] to determine the exact extent of the unstable ground and to optionally cause it to collapse safely into area A2 below
Unstable Floor.hazarddescription: An unstable section of limestone crumbles under the weight of anyone who steps on it.

Deeper into the Darkness.name: Deeper into the Darkness
Deeper into the Darkness.description:
Trigger A Small or larger creature walks onto the weak limestone

Effect The ground collapses, and the triggering creature falls 15 feet into area A2 below. The creature can try to [[/act grab-an-edge dc=23]] to avoid falling, otherwise the fall inflicts @Damage[7[bludgeoning]] damage plus an additional @Damage[(4d6+3)[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:23|basic] save) from falling rubble.

Ecaterina's Belongings.name: Ecaterina's Belongings
Ecaterina's Belongings.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.TLMokELKdcgGMQom]{A12. Primarch's Den}

Ecaterina’s belongings (other than the tattered fragments of her destroyed explorer’s clothing) lie in a heap on the ground to the side of the couch furthest from where she was kept chained up. This gear consists of a +1 dagger, a sterling engineer’s toolkit (treat as a sterling artisan’s toolkit that grants a +1 item bonus to Engineering Lore checks), a hooded lantern, a superb repair toolkit, and a writing set. If she’s rescued, Ecaterina gives the PCs her magic dagger as thanks.

Dagger.name: Dagger
Dagger.description: This small, bladed weapon is held in one hand and used to stab a creature in close combat. It can also be thrown.

Engineer's Toolkit (Sterling).name: Engineer's Toolkit (Sterling)
Engineer's Toolkit (Sterling).description:
You need these tools to create items from raw materials with the Craft skill. Sterling artisan's tools give you a +1 item bonus to the check.

Different sets are needed for different work, as determined by the GM; for example, a blacksmith's toolkit differs from a woodworker's toolkit. If you wear your artisan's toolkit, you can draw and replace it as part of the action that uses it.

Lantern (Hooded).name: Lantern (Hooded)
Lantern (Hooded).description: A lantern sheds bright light and requires 1 pint of oil to function for 6 hours. A hooded lantern sheds light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light in the next 30 feet) and is equipped with shutters, which you can close to block the light. Closing or opening the shutters takes an Interact action.

Repair Toolkit (Superb).name: Repair Toolkit (Superb)
Repair Toolkit (Superb).description: A repair kit allows you to perform simple repairs while traveling. It contains a portable anvil, tongs, woodworking tools, a whetstone, and oils for conditioning leather and wood. You can use a repair kit to Repair items using the Crafting skill. A superb repair kit gives you a +1 item bonus to the check. You can draw and replace a worn repair toolkit as part of the action that uses it.

Writing Set.name: Writing Set
Writing Set.description: Using a writing set, you can draft correspondence and scribe scrolls. A set includes stationery, including a variety of paper and parchment, as well as ink, a quill or inkpen, sealing wax, and a simple seal. If you've written a large amount, you can refill your kit with extra ink and paper.

Grim Remains.name: Grim Remains
Grim Remains.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.fCkeTfUR9gPzVP3H]{A5. Grim Remains}

An exhaustive search of the items strewn on the floor takes 10 minutes of Searching, after which the PCs can gather together all of the items of value left behind, including four daggers, a mace, a breastplate bearing the heraldry of the Knights of Ozem, a leather bandolier containing several broken vials and three unbroken vials of holy water, and a smooth, cloudy gray stone that’s strangely warm to the touch. This final item is a last word stone and the item Jakivi asked the PCs to recover from Relaph.

Dagger.name: Dagger
Dagger.description: This small, bladed weapon is held in one hand and used to stab a creature in close combat. It can also be thrown.

Mace.name: Mace
Mace.description: With a stout haft and a heavy metal head, a mace is sturdy and allows its wielder to deliver powerful blows and dent armor.

Breastplate.name: Breastplate
Breastplate.description: Though referred to as a breastplate, this type of armor consists of several pieces of plate or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.pRoikbRo5HFW6YUB]{Half Plate} armor that protect the torso, chest, neck, and sometimes the hips and lower legs. It strategically grants some of the protection of plate while allowing greater flexibility and speed.

Holy Water.name: Holy Water
Holy Water.description:
Activate A Strike

This vial contains water blessed by a benevolent deity. You activate a vial of holy water by throwing it as a Strike. It's a simple thrown weapon with a range increment of 20 feet.

Holy water deals 1d6 spirit damage and 1 spirit splash damage. Holy water can damage only creatures with the unholy trait.

Last Word Stone.name: Last Word Stone
Last Word Stone.description:
This small, palm-sized smooth crystal has a translucent gray coloration. But with a whisper from the lips of the desperate, a last word stone can be filled with a spark of memory, changing its appearance to an opaque, polished stone that is strangely warm to the touch. These divinely infused objects were initially created by Pharasmin priests to preserve a dying person's last moment of life should loved ones be delayed in their arrival at the dying person's side. But with the tragedy of Lastwall, last word stones have gained a new, more desperate purpose. Here, along the Gravelands border regions, refugees and adventurers have taken to using last word stones to impart important details to recipients outside of endangered places when it seems likely they won't survive to spread the news themselves.

Activate—Capture Memory 3 (concentrate, manipulate, mental)

Requirements The last word stone doesn't contain a memory

Effect You press an empty last word stone to an adjacent willing creature's head. The stone fills with an important memory from the creature's mind, then becomes opaque in appearance. The memory is duplicated, and remains in the target creature's thoughts, but no indication of what type of memory is held within the stone is discernible to anyone else. Which memory is placed in the last word stone is chosen by the creature from whom the memory is copied, and once a memory is stored, the stone can't be used again to Capture Memory. A stored memory can't contain much information beyond a single emotion and a hazy mental picture that, taken together, convey a short message of no more than 10 words—typically enough to impart final words of comfort to a loved one, or to warn one of a specific location that might be trapped, or to impart a bit of news about a noteworthy event. The limit of 10 words represents the hazy and sometimes confusing nature of the mental image.

Activate—Reveal Memory 3 (concentrate, manipulate, mental)

Requirements The last word stone contains a memory

Effect You hold the last word stone to your head and concentrate on its contents. A moment later, the stored memory plays out in your mind and the last word stone crumbles to dust in your hand.

Hidden Stash.name: Hidden Stash
Hidden Stash.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.2h5yLNynxsnsJkCK]{A11. Prayer Chamber}

Although the statue of Arazni was destroyed long ago, a hidden stash of sacred tools remains tucked away behind a secret panel at the base of the pedestal the statue once stood upon. A PC who Seeks this pedestal or the statue, or who spends at least 10 minutes Searching the room as a whole, can attempt a DC 20 Perception check to notice the hidden panel. Within are two scrolls (a 3rd-rank scroll of cleanse affliction and a scroll of crisis of faith) and a channel protection amulet. If the PCs later take the time to rebuild this statue, they’ll automatically discover this hidden stash of treasure as part of that activity.

Scroll of Cleanse Affliction (Rank 3).name: Scroll of Cleanse Affliction (Rank 3)
Scroll of Cleanse Affliction (Rank 3).description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}

Casting a Spell from a scroll requires holding the scroll in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell.

The spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack modifier and spell DC. The spell also gains the appropriate trait for your tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

Any physical costs are provided when a scroll is created, so you don't need to provide them when casting from a scroll. If the spell requires a locus, you must have that locus to Cast the Spell from a scroll.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Scroll of Crisis of Faith (Rank 3).name: Scroll of Crisis of Faith (Rank 3)
Scroll of Crisis of Faith (Rank 3).description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.3x6eUCm17n6ROzUa]{Crisis of Faith}

Casting a Spell from a scroll requires holding the scroll in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell.

The spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack modifier and spell DC. The spell also gains the appropriate trait for your tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

Any physical costs are provided when a scroll is created, so you don't need to provide them when casting from a scroll. If the spell requires a locus, you must have that locus to Cast the Spell from a scroll.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Channel Protection Amulet.name: Channel Protection Amulet
Channel Protection Amulet.description: This nugget of polished tektite is trapped in a cage of braided wire and hangs from a silken cord. When wearing this amulet, you gain resistance 5 against damage from @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wdA52JJnsuQWeyqz]{Harm} spells if you're living, or against @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal} spells if you're undead.

Inside the Coffins.name: Inside the Coffins
Inside the Coffins.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.a3DjkR1v5KOHBoyB]{A9. Cairn Court}

Most of the coffins lining the walls of the crypt are empty save for a few scattered bones and old, broken armor and weapons. Inside a few coffins, the PCs can find the following scattered among the bones: bracers of missile deflection, +1 handwraps of mighty blows, a staff of fire, and a +1 striking spear. The shattered coffin in the corner of the room once held the body of a lower-ranking officer from the Shining Crusade. His bones tangle the suit of full plate armor he wears, and a symbol of conflict is still worn around the officer’s neck.

Bracers of Missile Deflection.name: Bracers of Missile Deflection
Bracers of Missile Deflection.description:
These bracers are made from plates of durable dawnsilver and gleam like the summer sun.

Activate R (manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Trigger A ranged weapon attack hits you but doesn't critically hit

Requirements You are aware of the attack and not off-guard

Effect The bracers send the missile off-course. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. If this would cause the attack to be a failure, the attack misses you.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.PeiuJ951kkBPTCSM]{Effect: Bracers of Missile Deflection}

Handwraps of Mighty Blows.name: Handwraps of Mighty Blows
Handwraps of Mighty Blows.description:
As you invest these embroidered strips of cloth, you must meditate and slowly wrap them around your hands. These handwraps have weapon runes etched into them to give your unarmed attacks the benefits of those runes, making your unarmed attacks work like magic weapons. For example, +1 striking handwraps of mighty blows would give you a +1 item bonus to attack rolls with your unarmed attacks and increase the damage of your unarmed attacks from one weapon die to two (normally 2d4 instead of 1d4, but if your fists have a different weapon damage die or you have other unarmed attacks, use two of that die size instead).

You can upgrade, add, and transfer runes to and from the handwraps just as you would for a weapon, and you can attach talismans to the handwraps. Treat the handwraps as melee weapons of the brawling group with light Bulk for these purposes. Property runes apply only when they would be applicable to the unarmed attack you're using. For example, a property that must be applied to a slashing weapon wouldn't function when you attacked with a fist, but you would gain its benefits if you attacked with a claw or some other slashing unarmed attack.

Staff of Fire.name: Staff of Fire
Staff of Fire.description:
This staff resembles a blackened and burned length of ashen wood. You can Interact to touch the tip of this staff to a torch, tinder, or a flammable substance to ignite a flame.

Activate Cast a Spell

Effect You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.

  • Cantrip @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6DfLZBl8wKIV03Iq]{Ignition}
  • 1st @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.y6rAdMK6EFlV6U0t]{Breathe Fire}

Craft Requirements Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.

Spear.name: Spear
Spear.description: A long metal shaft ending with a metal spike, a spear can be used one-handed as a melee weapon and can be thrown.

Full Plate.name: Full Plate
Full Plate.description: Plate mail consists of interlocking plates that encase nearly the entire body in a carapace of steel. It is costly and heavy, and the wearer often requires help to don it correctly, but it provides some of the best defense armor can supply. A suit of this armor comes with an undercoat of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.zBYEU9E7034ENCmh]{Padded Armor} and a pair of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Ix2vicchE79d6Cl3]{gauntlets}.

Symbol of Conflict.name: Symbol of Conflict
Symbol of Conflict.description:
This tarnished necklace can be attuned only by someone who is holy or unholy. When you attune it, it transforms into your deity's religious symbol or a personal symbol if you don't have a deity. You receive a +1 item bonus to Religion and a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against holy and unholy effects.

Activate—Presence 2 (concentrate, manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect The symbol casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.7ZinJNzxq0XF0oMx]{Bane} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.XSujb7EsSwKl19Uu]{Bless}.

The counteract DC of these effects is 18, and the counteract modifier is +8.

Craft Requirements You must be holy or unholy.

Lost Journal.name: Lost Journal
Lost Journal.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.l9NTQyXqw9xjtC3X]{A4. The Sprung Trap}

One other object of interest can be found here—a lost, leatherbound journal that the PCs can find after Searching the room and succeeding at a DC 18 Perception check.

Scavenger Nest.name: Scavenger Nest
Scavenger Nest.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.YapKLhd1E9VSyfmg]{A2. Scavenger Nest}

Over the years, several charms, trinkets, and gold from the town square above were snatched by pack rats and brought down here. Said pack rats ended up centipede meals, but a scattering of their stolen goods can be found strewn about the place. A 10 minute Search of the room turns up gems and coin worth a total of 15 gp, a copper chain necklace worth 10 gp, a wayfinder, and a ball of lesser twisting twine.

Wayfinder.name: Wayfinder
Wayfinder.description:
Access member of the Pathfinder Society

This compact compass repurposes ancient technology to draw fantastic powers from the mysterious magical items called aeon stones. It serves as a badge of office for agents of the Pathfinder Society and as a status symbol among adventurers of any stripe. A wayfinder functions as a compass.

An indentation in the middle of the wayfinder can hold a single aeon stone. Placing an aeon stone in this indentation provides you all the benefits of having the aeon stone orbiting your head, but it protects the stone from being noticed or stolen as easily. You invest a wayfinder and the aeon stone within it simultaneously, and they count as only one item toward your investiture limit. An invested aeon stone slotted in a wayfinder also grants its resonant power.

If you have more than one wayfinder with an invested aeon stone on your person at a given time, destructive interference from their resonance prevents you from gaining benefits from any of them. You can still benefit from additional aeon stones orbiting your head, just not in wayfinders.

Activate—Light A (concentrate)

Effect The wayfinder is targeted by a 1st-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WBmvzNDfpwka3qT4]{Light} spell.

Twisting Twine (Lesser).name: Twisting Twine (Lesser)
Twisting Twine (Lesser).description:
This ball of hempen twine resists efforts to unravel it by hand.

Activate—Unravel Twine 1 (manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect You toss the ball of twine into a square within 20 feet. The twine then unravels and animates, attempting to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trip} (your choice) a creature in the square with a total of +9 to the Athletics check. At the end of your turn, the twine winds itself back into a ball and returns to your hand; if you don't have a free hand, it returns to your space instead.

Priest Remains.name: Priest Remains
Priest Remains.hazarddescription:
@UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.2Xjn200JX7vr3VLO]{B5. Meeting Room}

If the heroes search the room further, they can find the mostly intact remains of a priest by succeeding at a DC 16 Perception check. While this priest is unfortunately dead and wasted away to bones, his clothing is relatively intact and among his garments are a set of +1 handwraps of mighty blows.

Adventure Summaries.name: Adventure Summaries
Adventure Summaries.text:
Below is a short synopsis for each of the seven adventures presented in this module to give you an idea of what to expect as you lead your players into adventure.

You can click on the header for each block to open its journal! If you want advice on how to use each of these adventures, whether as individual stories or part of a greater narrative, see @UUID[.9233HOESzzEBCjxP]{Adventure Anthology}.

@UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW]{Temple of the Unlit Star}

Level 1—2

By James Case & Luis Loza

Drawn in by a mysterious influence, a group of fledgling adventurers becomes trapped in an abandoned temple to Desna, sunk deep into the earth by a dark force. To escape, the heroes must explore the ruins and recover the shattered pieces of an artifact known as the unlit star to dispel the shadows keeping them imprisoned.

Choose this adventure if you and the players want to explore an ancient temple, solve puzzles, and battle monsters, all while learning how to play Pathfinder.

@UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar]{The Path River Peeler}

Level 2

By Bill Fischer

A local cryptid is active again and a desperate farmer asks a band of adventurers in town to investigate before the creature skins all his sheep. A mix of rumors, reports, and accusations muddy the investigation, but the adventurers find the trail and track the creature to an old cavern system that holds a pathway to worlds beyond.

Choose this adventure if you and the players want to investigate and track down a dangerous local legend.

@UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW]{Sabotage!}

Level 2

By Quinn Murphy

Suspecting there’s some kind of saboteur on the prowl, the town leadership asks the adventurers to help investigate various mechanical failures occurring in important places in town. The culprit is a clever gremlin and his band of troublemakers who was offended that his traps were found and repaired and now wants to collapse the town in on itself by digging out the foundation.

Choose this adventure if you and the players want to talk to people in town to solve a mystery before confronting gremlin traps and dangerous constructs.

@UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw]{They Hunger Below}

Level 3

By Joseph Blomquist

After a sinkhole opened in the town square, the town’s leadership sent word to Caliphas to have a county engineer visit to survey the sinkhole and assess the current and future damage to the town. The engineer went down there yesterday and hasn’t been heard from since, so town leadership asks the adventurers, who have already proved to be capable and helpful, to climb down into the sinkhole and investigate the missing engineer.

Down there the adventurers discover some hidden crypts and come in contact with the ghouls who now call the place home.

Choose this adventure if you and the players want to dig into underground exploration and settle conflicts with intelligent undead to rescue an important person.

@UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r]{The Disgraced Dollmaker}

Level 3

By Jason Keeley

A tax collector from Caliphas asks the adventurers to head a little ways out of town to explore a disgraced reclusive professor’s abandoned estate to find the deed. Once inside they discover that the old man was creating soulbound constructs and his ghost still haunts the place. It’s up to them to put him to rest for good.

Choose this adventure if you and the players want to explore a creepy abandoned house filled with traps and twisted creations… or if you find dolls creepy.

@UUID[JournalEntry.wzqJL0YgefgczTx0]{Sweet Tooth}

Level 4

By Solomon St. John

After the local baker left town in the middle of the night, residents found a note pinned to the door saying that her cousin would be by the next day to take care of the business while she attends to family affairs. This was a ruse orchestrated by a sweet hag who moved into the baker’s place and began preying on Grayce’s populace.

Choose this adventure if you and the players want to uncover a dangerous sham and free some captured townsfolk while clashing with fairy-tale monsters.

@UUID[JournalEntry.xiLOxiL2uVSICHbL]{The Count of Petals}

Level 4

By Mikko Kallio

While the adventurers take a much needed break from their previous adventures, they hear a commotion in the town square. The crowd shrieks as a harpy flies overhead and leaves a powerful message—a vampire blames Grayce for the arrival of a (now deceased) vampire hunter!

Choose this adventure if you and the players want to leave town and head into the Gravelands to slay a vampire in his crumbling castle.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
The small town of Grayce has been having some problems as of late and maybe—just maybe—a group of plucky adventurers are the solution. It’s not going to be easy, though. There have been slaughtered sheep, broken machinery, missing items, a baker skipping town, and to make matters worse, just last week a sinkhole opened in the town square! Things in this normally quiet town are anything but calm and idyllic, and they need some help. Grayce sits along the southern border of the ancient and mist-shrouded nation of Ustalav, just across the Path River from fallen Lastwall, now known as the Gravelands where undead freely roam. The stories in this anthology lean into the world of grim folktales and light horror, but don’t let that scare you away. There’s a hunt for a cryptid, a fight against clever ghouls, pesky gremlins, a cruel scientist’s abandoned home, dark fairy- tale hags, and slaying a vampire once and for all. Some of these stories might be spooky, but they’re not gruesome or dripping with dread. They sit along a comfortable baseline that a GM, depending on their group’s sensibilities, can crank up to full horror or tone down to glaze over the scary bits.

Adventure Anthology

Troubles in Grayce is an anthology of six adventures. They aren’t linked together to follow a singular plotline like you’d find in an Adventure Path. Instead, these six adventures make up a sandbox that are linked by a centralized location and overarching themes of horror. Each adventure in this book deals with a distinct trouble that is plaguing the small agricultural community and don’t necessarily cross over with each other. Since Grayce is a small town, there can be plenty of interconnected elements as the PCs investigate events in town and speak to more of Grayce’s inhabitants. The lengthy @UUID[JournalEntry.de6yWKM2osh6uz88]{gazetteer of the town} fleshes out the details of the town’s features and people beyond what the PCs experience during the course of the adventures. GMs can use this resource to bring the town to life by providing a solid cast of characters who can interact with the PCs during the adventures or befriend the PCs during downtime.

In addition to the six adventures in Troubles in Grayce, this module includes the 1st-to-2nd level adventure @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW]{Temple of the Unlit Star} from Pathfinder Beginner Box: Secrets of the Unlit Star. You can find advice on how to use this adventure as a prelude to the Troubles in Grayce anthology in @UUID[.#make-it-a-campaign!]{Make it a Campaign}.

How Do I Use This Anthology?

There are a number of ways a GM can use this collection of adventures in their games. This anthology includes six adventures for groups of PCs that are 2nd–4th levels. There are two adventures for each of the three levels covered. Each adventure in this anthology contains enough encounters to advance a character to the next level.

Since there are two adventures for each level above 1st, you as the GM will need to choose which of the two adventures in the appropriate level range your group of players will enjoy the most. (You can find a list of @UUID[.26eOEotW7tSQRNsm]{adventure summaries} to help you make this decision)

This means that with this approach, a single group will only experience half of the adventures in this book. An alternative approach to using this anthology would be to use the slow advancement guidelines presented in the Advancement Speeds sidebar on page 57 of Pathfinder GM Core.

You can even further simplify things by using a milestone leveling approach. In this approach, you can run the PCs through two adventures of the same level (2nd if you’re starting this anthology from the beginning) and at the end of the second adventure, allow them to advance their characters to the next level. Then choose which of the 3rd-level adventures to run first and repeat the process for the 4th-level adventures until your players have played through all six in this book. The PCs should be 5th level by the end of Troubles in Grayce.

Make It a Campaign!

Troubles in Grayce can be used as part of an entire campaign if used in between the Pathfinder Beginner Box: Secrets of the Unlit Star and the Bastion of Blasphemies Adventure Path. The adventure included in the Pathfinder Beginner Box: Secrets of the Unlit Star involves brand new characters (or iconic pregenerated characters if you go that route) exploring a hidden ruined temple dedicated to Desna. The Beginner Box provides the tools and advice new players can use to create their own characters. It even suggests that player’s characters might originate from Grayce and you can use the Grayce gazetteer in this module so that the players can be familiar with the town.

If the PCs are from Grayce, they might be already aware of some of the things that have taken place in town recently (depending on how long they were adventuring in the Temple of the Unlit Star) and most certainly have connections with the people of this small community. In this case, they can get to the adventures in this anthology as soon as they return home. If they are from elsewhere, they can experience Grayce for the first time as they head south down the Path River from their previous adventure. “Temple of the Unlit Star” starts the PCs at 1st level and gets them to 2nd, perfect for starting this anthology. Bastion of Blasphemies begins PCs at 5th level and takes place in Ustalav, but on the other side of the nation. The primary quest giver for Bastion of Blasphemies is from Grayce and has returned to investigate the disappearance of her parents and is looking for adventurers. The advice on the @UUID[JournalEntry.JuJVjFYpoh1sTfFg.JournalEntryPage.lGY2myU5PYTxntKh]{Adventure Toolbox} can help you bridge the gap between Troubles in Grayce and Bastion of Blasphemies, which gets PCs to 15th level.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
Welcome! This module contains everything you need to take your group on a series of seven adventures. From humble beginnings at 1st level with the Beginner Box's Temple of the Unlit Star adventure, and continuing through the light-horror adventures found in Troubles in Grayce's six-part anthology, all the way to 5th level. By the end of it, you will have a group of seasoned heroes ready for even greater challenges.

Preparing for your Game

Whether you wish to play through every adventure and make a campaign out of it, or pick and choose your favorite-sounding premise for a few game nights, we have you covered.

There are a few ways to get started. If you're @UUID[.3grBLwBhWarEczdY]{new to Pathfinder}, the linked page provides specific advice for beginners. If you just want to dive right into the adventures, you can check out the @UUID[JournalEntry.49YA870sXCY7Hkxk.JournalEntryPage.26eOEotW7tSQRNsm]{Adventure Summaries} page to help you decide which one to run for your group first, or just as a quick way to familiarize yourself with each adventure.

If this is your first time using a premium adventure module like this one, the @UUID[JournalEntry.49YA870sXCY7Hkxk.JournalEntryPage.1EhnWI6Tfg1VDGFS]{Using this Module} category will outline some of the ways we present information during your adventures, as well as explain some of the tools we provide.

The @UUID[JournalEntry.de6yWKM2osh6uz88]{Grayce Gazetteer} is another great place to start if you want to learn about the small town most of these adventures will take place in. As the GM, you can use the information in it to enrich the setting for the players. The gazetteer includes nearly forty notable locations and plenty of NPCs (including their motivations and demeanors) for the players to interact with. Using the information in this gazetteer can help you breathe life into the town and give flavorful descriptions and likely dialog on what would be a simple pass through town.

This module also contains an @UUID[JournalEntry.JuJVjFYpoh1sTfFg]{Adventure Toolbox} that collects the special treasures the adventurers find throughout their adventures in and around Grayce. Each adventure in Troubles in Grayce has at least one new treasure that fits the theme of that adventure. Likewise, each adventure features a brand new monster. The Toolbox also gives GMs advice for proceeding to the next adventure as well as a table of random encounters the PCs can find themselves dealing with on the road.

Encounters.name: Encounters
Encounters.text:
When reading area descriptions, you will often come across creatures which the players may end up fighting, or hazards that will need to be disabled or otherwise dealt with. In those places, encounter sections such as these will contain all of the information you'll need to run the encounter.

Of course, not every encounter has to end in combat. Many are optional, or provide the heroes with an opportunity for diplomacy. Just because it's in one of these sections, it doesn't mean that a creature couldn't be reasoned with, or even eventually become an ally!

The actors involved in each encounter will be linked in the encounter description for quick access, and their tokens are already placed for you on each scene. The header will also tell you the encounter's threat category per Pathfinder's encounter design guidelines.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.QN9Zv9l71Q1E9bCR] @UUID[Actor.BHq5wpQU8hQEke8D]

This text will often include a information relevant to the encounter as a whole, such as skill checks to possibly avoid combat, or just further context for you as the GM. As shown in this example, you might also see the portrait of one of the encounter participants.

Creature: This section will describe the creatures involved, as well as their tactics or priorities, if any.

Hazard: If there are any hazards in the encounter, they will typically be described in this section.

Of course, you will not have the full picture of the encounter without inspecting the participants' character sheets first, so please make use of the links in the header of each encounter!

Treasure.name: Treasure
Treasure.text:
As the heroes go on their adventures, they may well unearth valuable treasures, coins, or powerful magical items. When that happens, you will see a box like the ones below.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.5QfO6h7sFpCOVsl1]

The header of this box will typically link to a loot actor, a special type of actor that holds items for you to hand out to your players. These actors also have tokens which are placed on the associated scene, hidden by default.

Giving these items to your players is as simple as revealing the loot actor's token placed on the scene by right-clicking it and selecting the "Toggle Visibility State" option. They will be able to open the loot actor's sheet and take items directly from it by dragging them into their inventories.

Merchants

@UUID[Actor.CqrpFjHNo259QhkO]

In a few instances we will link to a merchant actor, which is a different type of loot actor. In those cases, you can drag and drop that actor on the scene or reveal it if it's already placed. The players will be able to buy items by interacting with these merchants just as with loot actors, appropriately deducting their gold as they make purchases.

Foundry Advice.name: Foundry Advice
Foundry Advice.text:
If you ever see a box like the one below, that means we have advice about how to best make use of the module and its content, as it relates to FoundryVTT. The header might include links to effects, ambience sounds, macros, and so on. The following are some of the more common boxes you will encounter.

Effects

@UUID[Item.2SkGy5VVpzvQefYT]{Example Effect}

An effect represents an often temporary change in an actor, such as a bonus, a penalty, or even more complex benefits, like temporary Hit Points.

When an effect is linked in this box, you can use it by either dragging it onto your players' tokens or sheets yourself, or dragging and dropping it onto the chat box and posting it, allowing your players to apply it to their own characters in the same way.

Ambience Tracks

@UUID[Playlist.4kc6sYSc56Q2KYTT.PlaylistSound.zDS7Ru3Rgqe044A8]{Example Ambience}

We have provided ambience sounds for you to play during your adventures. Some of them have been set up to automatically play as the scene is activated, but others benefit from being timed as the characters enter a certain area. When that happens, the box will include a link to the ambience sound in its header. You can simply click on the link to start playing the sound!

Macros

Example Macro

Sometimes, especially as the characters run into traps or otherwise affect their surroundings, we will link a macro that will automate tiles being hidden and revealed, sounds being played, and other effects that will enhance your players' immersion.

Just like ambience sounds, you can click on the linked macro to activate it!

Rewards & Milestones.name: Rewards & Milestones
Rewards & Milestones.text:
The heroes might obtain rewards other than treasure for their accomplishments, or their actions could result in certain developments. In those cases, you will see a box like the one below.

Experience Points

While most encounters in Troubles in Grayce have their @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.ZcddTU02joqYuuoV]{XP Awards} determined by the encounter's threat category, the players might obtain XP for non-combat accomplishments. Additionally, the encounters in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW]{Temple of the Unlit Star} have their XP Awards explicitly stated to make it easier on newer GMs.

Development

As mentioned earlier, this box is also used for developments, such as an area that becomes unlocked when the PCs overcome an encounter, or an event they might witness if they perform certain actions.

New to Pathfinder?.name: New to Pathfinder?
New to Pathfinder?.text:
If you're a new Game Master, the @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW]{Temple of the Unlit Star} adventure is a great place to start. As part of the Beginner Box, it is designed to help you and your players learn the game, gradually unfolding new concepts as you adventure.

If you want to learn more about @UUID[JournalEntry.rvmbULl8e9YZEVbM]{Game Mastering} as a whole, the linked journal will walk you through the basics of running a session of Pathfinder.

Similarly, this might be your first time using a premium adventure module like this one. In that case, the @UUID[.1EhnWI6Tfg1VDGFS]{Using this Module} category will outline some of the ways we will provide information as you read the adventures, as well as explain some of the tools we provide.

The Road to Bastardhall.name: The Road to Bastardhall
The Road to Bastardhall.text:
After completing the adventures in this anthology, the PCs can go on to other adventures of your own design. Alternatively, if you prefer published adventures and you want to keep Trouble in Grayce’s eerie themes of the land of Ustalav, a perfect campaign to follow this anthology is the Bastion of Blasphemies Adventure Path. This campaign involves exploring the haunted castle known today as Bastardhall. Known in its time as Castle Arudora, the castle fell over 500 years ago after a series of tragedies struck. Every century since its fall, a black coach leaves the castle and scours Avistan for people descended from the Arudora family with the intention of dragging them back to the site for unknown but certainly nefarious reasons.

If you intend to run the Bastion of Blasphemies Adventure Path next, the PCs can meet such a descendant here in Grayce. Florin Kindler’s parents, who were from Grayce, were taken by the coach, and the young woman has returned to her hometown to find answers and hopefully some adventurers. Bastion of Blasphemies includes more specific information about the start of that campaign, but you can introduce Florin here and play out some of the travel to Bastardhall, including some @UUID[.#random-encounters]{random encounters} along the way, with the information here.

Taking up Florin’s task, the PCs travel by boat down the Path River to Lake Encarthan. Once reaching the lake, the PCs can stop in Caliphas, the capital of Ustalav, if they need to rest, trade, or research something in a large city. From there, they return to traveling Lake Encarthan up to Avalon Bay in the north. They then travel up the Danver River whose mouth is near the town of Thrushmoor. Roughly 40 miles upriver, the PCs disembark at Rozenport and then follow the roads toward Lantern Lake and then travel along its northern shore and the northern edge of the Forest of Veils before turning due east and heading toward Lake Laroba and Castle Arudora.

Ogre Hunting Party

Moderate 5

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.X7PaA6XgvrY5ByfM] @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.Twvzy1yRo6m6dM8D]{Ogre Warriors x3}

This group of ogres wander the river banks hunting for meat and sport. They are always on the lookout for travelers who aren’t paying attention, but lately they’ve enjoyed finding campsites along the riverbanks from voyaging travelers docking for the night. This group is made up of one ogre glutton and three ogre warriors.

Sinister Canines

Moderate 5

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.AFWmiIBJ7ypgydQD]{Dire Wolves x2} @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.diU0V2M3LiMDMsS0]{Witchwarg}

As the PCs skirt the north end of Lantern Lake and the Forest of Veils, they have a chance to encounter a small pack of three wolves. Two are simple, yet brutal, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.AFWmiIBJ7ypgydQD]{dire wolves}, while the third bears a cruel intellect. This @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.diU0V2M3LiMDMsS0]{witchwarg} leader commands the other wolves to corral their quarry because he likes to talk to his victims before freezing them to death and eating them.

Skeletal Patrol

Low 5

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.FH58AcRBZIfrHKvv]{Skeletal Champion x2} @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.X2vz6CrMaHIso0ha]{Skeletal Horses x2}

Once the PCs begin traveling the roads east of Rozenport, they might come across a skeletal patrol. These undead calvary can also be encountered as the PCs return from the Count of Petals’ ruined keep south of Grayce. The patrol is formed by a pair of skeletal champions mounted on skeletal horses.

@UUID[RollTable.srWnOF2sJFzBdSXE]{Random Encounters}

Automatic Butler.name: Automatic Butler
Automatic Butler.text:
An automatic butler is a magical construct shaped like a wooden humanoid mannequin, usually tailored in a simple black suit and tie. It has only the barest hint of a face on its round head, though its jaw opens on a hinge to simulate regular mouth movements when it speaks. Its voice is often calm and measured, and it speaks quite politely. It follows the orders given to it by its creator (or anyone whom the creator has given permission to issue commands), which usually involves fetching items, keeping a room tidy, or ushering out guests. If unwanted guests become belligerent, an automatic butler can defend itself by battering intruders or using its innate magic to hurl objects with deadly force. Once a fight has ended, an automatic butler usually spends the next hour or so cleaning up the mess left behind.

Automatic butlers are built on designs similar to soulbound dolls. Like other soulbound constructs, an automatic butler is animated by a fragment of the soul of a deceased mortal. This fragment can come from either a willing donor or an unwilling victim, who can resist the process with a successful Will save against the creator’s Crafting DC. While resisting ruins the construct, the soul extraction process is often fatal, and the person dies regardless. Unlike with other soulbound constructs, the personality of the soul used to create an automatic butler is wholly suppressed. Instead, the automatic butler comports itself in the way a stereotypical servant would.

Some automatic butlers are created with slightly different skill sets. They can be created to speak more languages beyond that of their creator, making them passable family diplomats who might welcome foreign guests. Some are trained to take care of tasks that require specialization, such as tutoring the youth of the household or tailoring the family’s clothes. The sidebar covers some other options for a whole domestic staff of constructed servants.

Automatic Cooks and Gardeners

Should the designs for creating automatic butlers reach the wider world, someone would likely end up creating variations of the magical construct. These creatures would use the same basic statistics as an automatic butler, with a few minor changes. An automatic cook might have @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qXTB7Ec9yYh5JPPV]{Cleanse Cuisine} as an innate spell, a knife Strike, and the ability to shoot a jet of boiling hot water. An automatic gardener might have @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.zA0jNIBRgLsyTpbm]{Scatter Scree} and other spells with the earth or plant traits as innate spells, a hoe or shovel Strike, and the ability to pelt foes at range with seeds.

Durtik.name: Durtik
Durtik.text:
Unlike other gremlins who are satisfied with causing discomfort or pain to a few individuals, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.troubles-in-grayce-bestiary.Actor.5UN8SqEfnzVY6P2P]{durtiks} think big. They enjoy overwrought plans and complicated devices that often cause chaos. Durtiks live on the outskirts of societies that possess great engineering prowess, gleaning technical knowledge and expertise. They use these gathered skills to build elaborate death traps. A durtik will happily spend years building a device that chips away at a mountain until it causes an avalanche that destroys a town.

Fortunately for the civilizations they lurk near, durtik plans almost never reach fruition; the fey abhor simplicity and directness, insisting on complexity and grandiosity, making their plans easy to disrupt. Often, these plans overlook a crucial detail or avoid some basic truth that causes them to implode halfway through without anyone in the nearby town any wiser there was a plan at all.

This penchant for self-sabotage, however, doesn’t make durtiks less dangerous. Their desire for grand destruction makes them uniquely inspiring among other gremlins. It’s common to find a durtik surrounded by other gremlins inspired by their vision, even if those followers don’t fully understand it. The gremlins stick around until they lose interest or the plans implode. Until then, a durtik and their crew concentrate their chaos and spread plenty of misfortune as they enact their ill-fated scheme.

Smarter Than You

Because durtiks are often smarter than other gremlins around them, they think they are the smartest person in the room wherever they go. Canny adventurers who are aware of this can butter them up with grandiose compliments, distracting the durtik and making them more likely to accidentally share information.

Gauntling.name: Gauntling
Gauntling.text:
In places like the Gravelands, undeath permeates the very soil of the land. This unholy pollution can have significant effects on regional flora and fauna over the course of generations, causing plants to become twisted and diseased looking and contaminates wildlife so their remains spontaneously rise as mindless undead.

Yet in some cases, particularly for those beasts who forage primarily through the act of scavenging, the consumption of undead flesh can have an entirely different effect over the course of months. How quickly an animal is affected depends on whether it ate from the remains of an undead creature left behind after its destruction or consumed it “fresh” from an undead in a desperate throe of starvation. Assuming the unfortunate creature survives any onset of disease or other afflictions brought on by their ghastly repast, these scavengers sometimes undergo a transformation into a twisted, ravenous beast known as a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.troubles-in-grayce-bestiary.Actor.rQqEjKlfSBfvDcGj]{gauntling}.

Most gauntlings arise from scavengers, carnivores, or omnivores, but in certain cases, desperate herbivores can become transformed as well—these creatures are perhaps the most disturbing type of gauntling, due to the significant change in their behaviors pushing them toward diets of fresh meat. Once animals become gauntlings, these creatures abandon their previous wilderness habitats in favor of those near more settled regions and often choose sewers or other underground locales as dens from which they emerge to hunt. In their transformation into a gauntling, regardless of what the creature’s previous dietary leanings might have been, all gauntlings share one horrific hunger—the flesh of sapient humanoids. A gauntling looks similar to the animal it was before its transformation, but with large sharp fangs and with painfully emaciated frames, regardless of how much they eat.

The gauntling presented below (as are all of those encountered in Troubles in Grayce) were once boars, but you can use these statistics to represent any terrestrial Medium animal that’s succumbed to this unholy transformation. Regardless of its original form, all gauntlings share a mouthful of sharp, twisted fangs.

Other Gauntlings

The gauntling presented here comes from a Medium terrestrial animal (a boar, to be precise), but other animals can be transformed in this way by consuming undead flesh. To represent one from a swimming or flying Medium animal, simply grant it a swim or fly speed equal to its base speed. To represent a smaller or larger creature, use the statistics presented here as a starting point, then rebuild the statistics using the guidelines for building creatures that begin on page 112 of GM Core.

Path River Peeler.name: Path River Peeler
Path River Peeler.text:
Like many cryptids, even the name of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.troubles-in-grayce-bestiary.Actor.65OzVr2FfL0mX3Qy]{Path River Peeler} is a matter of dispute. Some say the creature earns its name from the corpses of its victims, which are often found stripped clean of skin but otherwise untouched. Others claim that corpses left in such condition are the exception to the rule. More frequently, no trace of the Peeler’s victims is ever found—perhaps these skinless kills were simply abandoned by the Peeler before it could finish with its meal. Those who subscribe to this theory argue that a better name would be the “Pealer,” after the echoing cries the beast makes while on the hunt. But what sense does it make to call it the Pealer, when everyone knows loud noises are the best way to drive off the monster? The arguments go round and round, with no end to the debate in sight.

The Peeler is most frequently encountered in a wild and largely unoccupied area north of Grayce called the Shivering Bluffs. Most people in Grayce, with the exception of the elderly who have tales from their youth, think the Peeler is just a story to frighten children and explain the killed and missing sheep that fall victim to wolves or other predators. Even so, everyone who grew up in Grayce can sing a few lines of a popular skipping rhyme the children in town sing while playing.

Barrow Claw

Purported sightings of the Path River Peeler often coincide with an outbreak of barrow claw: a rare, disease-bearing fungus that is cold to the touch and devastates nearby vegetation. Outbreaks of barrow claw have led some enthusiastic scholars to postulate that the cryptid itself is the source of the fungus. A more likely theory is that the Peeler and barrow claw share a habitat in the Netherworld, and that the former simply carries spores of the latter on its bristly hide.

Sangrist.name: Sangrist
Sangrist.text:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.troubles-in-grayce-bestiary.Actor.qvHORqASyD9Poqym]{Sangrists} are born from the bodies of those who bled out completely, often when they are left unburied without proper rites in places tainted by void energy, though the strong presence of void energy is not a requirement. Some victims who rise as sangrists suffered an accident or attack in a remote region and were never found and properly laid to rest, be it a slip of a blade when cleaning game or being gored by a wild hog.

After rising as undead, these tragic creatures are drawn to sites of past carnage where the scent of blood and death lingers. They are commonly found in the war-torn lands of Lastwall, the haunted ruins of Ustalav, and the cursed battlefields of Geb, embodying a relentless hunger for the life they lost.

Sangrists rely on stealth and ambushes, becoming more active at night. During times of inactivity, they fall into a strange stupor. In this state, they rock back and forth and frequently twitch, sometimes emitting a haunting humming sound.

Some sangrists are solitary hunters, often stalking a solitary target for hours if not days. Others form packs, especially if they shared a bond in life. These packs exhibit a chilling, coordinated cunning, reminiscent of wolves on the prowl. Sangrists are patient hunters, sometimes tracking their victims for miles or observing them for hours before making a move. They target the weak and isolated, picking off those they can easily wound so that they bleed out even if they manage to outrun the sangrists. Retaining only a shadow of their former selves, sangrists rarely utter more than single-word sentences, usually to express their hatred for the living, their unending hunger, or where victims can be found.

Although sangrists can’t drink blood or gain nourishment from it, they sometimes pool blood in their cupped hands and pour it on their faces and bodies. They may also lie down next to the body of a slain enemy. This macabre ritual seems to be a desperate attempt to reconnect with the life they once had. These strange proclivities toward blood, nighttime activity, and the yearning for some semblance of their previous lives lead some sangrists to associate with vampires. Vampires generally don’t find sangrists distasteful and find the undead creatures easy to manipulate into serving them as guardians and attendants.

Taste for Blood

These rare creatures have been mistaken for either feral vampires or blood obsessed zombies by soldiers and adventurers who don’t have a firm understanding of the myriad forms undeath can come in. Those familiar with sangrists and who aim to hunt them often set out blood, frequently pig blood, as a lure.

Sticky Toffee Hound.name: Sticky Toffee Hound
Sticky Toffee Hound.text:
Sweet hags have an affinity for baking and take delight in corrupting all that is sweet and scrumptious. Like most bakers, each hag cultivates a personal collection of favorite recipes they keep coming back to. For Larmine, the hag occupying Dalmira’s Bakery, the most loyal of her specialties are her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.troubles-in-grayce-bestiary.Actor.MsELMjof55g0TOoB]{sticky toffee hounds}.

Though modeled after noble hunting hounds, there’s only so much magic can do to hold sponge cake and toffee sauce in a roughly canine shape. These sticky-sweet creations therefore have all the loyalty of a dog and all the versatility of an ooze, to the point that they practically hold themselves together through sheer force of devotion to their creator. However, the saccharine hounds have little awareness of their creator’s mortality; were Larmine ever to die, Grayce would be serenaded nightly for weeks by the burbling howls of her mourning pets. In fact, the toffee oozes might eventually become so desperate for attention that they latch onto defenseless civilians, even suffocating their new (and unwitting) owners in a desperate quest for affection.

A sticky toffee hound is an irresistible trap for insects, whose congregation can give away the ooze’s presence. The hound’s body is ultimately lethal, though, trapping animals in its gooey hide like mosquitoes in amber.

Half Baked Creations

Sticky toffee hounds aren’t the only option for enterprising sweet hags who want to make companions. Creatures like this can be in any form and shape, but animal shapes and behaviors are the most often mimicked. Sweet hags can also make companions out of breads, doughs, and other confections, lending to a buffet of dangerous and potentially tasty allies.

Story Seeds.name: Story Seeds
Story Seeds.text:
The lands of Ustalav hold the potential for many great adventures. If you wish to make use of Ustalav in adventures of your own, consider using the following possible encounters and events as inspiration.

Caravan of the Lost

Every new moon marks the arrival of what locals refer to as the caravan of the lost. A ghostly caravan appears on the southern edges of the Shudderwood and begins its routine movement south. The caravan’s ghosts number in the dozens and each wear the same elegant mask that hides their faces. Once the caravan reaches the Vistear River south of the forest, it stops and every member falls to their knees in anguish. The caravan appears to be harmless, but locals can’t help but wonder where it’s attempting to reach, why the river always halts their journey, and just what it is about the new moon that causes them to return once more.

Cutthroat Keeve’s Mark

Rumors of a strange, dilapidated ship traveling along Ustalav’s rivers have the region’s people on edge. The reports note that the ship is a galleon, a ship much larger than what would normally be found on a river. The ship seems to float above the water, unimpeded by its size or any waterway’s features. The captain of the ship is a skeletal figure known as simply as Cutthroat Keeve. Keeve calls out to anyone that encounters the ship, offering a position on his crew. Those who accept are never seen again and those who decline are left alone, but find themselves with a new tattoo on the back of their hands the next morning. This tattoo seems to slowly grow over time and marked individuals are worried that the tattoo will soon overtake their entire bodies.

The House That Never Sleeps

On the northeastern reaches of Caliphas is a house that’s drawn the attention of locals. The long-abandoned Kinsath manor has earned the nickname of “The House That Never Sleeps” due to the strange lights that begin to flicker and fill the grounds every night. The house’s interior is burned out, a fact that is easy to confirm during the day. Attempting to enter the manor while these lights are flashing appears to be impossible. Entering the house is easy once the sun rises, but nothing inside seems to suggest the cause of these lights. Finally tired of the constant light show, neighbors have pooled a fund of several hundred gold pieces for anyone who can discern their origin and how to finally bring the strange phenomenon to an end.

The Hungry Howls

For the past few months, howls have been ringing through the Hungry Mountains northwest of Grayce. The howls don’t seem to be those of any creature native to the region and even locals who have encountered werewolves claim this howl comes from something else. The howls appear to have a pattern, occurring only on nights following rains during the day, but attempts to locate their origin have been unsuccessful so far. Those who have attempted to follow the howls note that they appear to move. At first locals thought it was to avoid endeavors to locate its source, but after several trips they now believe the howls are attempting to guide listeners somewhere unknown. So far, no one has dared follow them into the mountains for more than a day.

The Storm Signs

Strange lightning storms have been dotting the landscape over the past weeks. While the storms are more visually frightening than anything else, it’s what comes afterward that draws the attention of the people of Ustalav. A strange rune appears burned somewhere on the ground beneath the site of these storms. Each of these symbols is different, but they all share characteristics, including their size and the shape of their burned “strokes.” So far nothing has come from these markings, but the fact that all attempts to remove the markings fail and the storms are becoming more frequent has caused growing concern.

The Wailing Professor

The Brazen Skull, a notable pub in Lepidstadt, has recently become the site of a regular haunting. The ghost of a human man dressed in scholarly clothing appears at midnight every night, interrupting whatever festivities may be at hand within the pub. None of the locals recognize the ghost and all attempts to speak with him so far have been unproductive. While he isn’t violent, the ghost’s occasional screams are disconcerting. After a few hours, the ghost now known as the Wailing Professor vanishes. While it’s unclear as to what causes him to leave, signs point to occurrences within the city’s university as a possible explanation.
