Adventure Toolbox.name: Adventure Toolbox
Adventure Toolbox.text: This journal collects the special treasures and enemies the party will find throughout their adventures in and around Grayce. Nearly every adventure in this module has at least one new treasure that fits the theme of that adventure, the art and statistics of which are presented here. Likewise, each such adventure features a brand new monster, whose lore and illustration can be found here. Finally, the Toolbox also gives GMs advice for proceeding to the next adventure as well as a table of random encounters the PCs can find themselves dealing with on the road.

Grayce.name: Grayce
Grayce.text:
Grayce is a modest old town in Caliphas County on the southern border of Ustalav, just across the Path River from what is now known as the Gravelands. Primarily settled by farmers and ranchers, the town has been a small but solid center of worship since its early days, and the churches of Andoletta, Pharasma, and Iomedae still have a guiding hand in Grayce’s day-to-day activities. The Shrine of Pharasma stands tall over the town, its Chapel Bridge spanning the river.

Grayce’s residents have strong faith, but their superstitions are equally influential on society. Even before the undead activity to the south, Ustalav had long been known as a haunted land, and its hardy people are no strangers to supernatural occurrences or predation. Tales of vampirism are rife throughout Caliphas, but the people of Grayce pride themselves on having been a vampire-free town for generations. The power of superstition can be seen throughout town as people hang braids of garlic near doorways and adorn tree trunks and poles with small oval mirrors.

At its core, Grayce is an agricultural town where most people get along and stubbornly stick together to make life better for everyone. Someone from Grayce will extend a hand to someone who needs one, but will also expect them to pitch in when needed; to do otherwise is just taking advantage.

Grayce

Settlement 4

  • Town

Small town on the border of an undead wasteland.

Government Council (elected council)

Population 2,347 (72% human, 7% aiuvarin, 7% dwarven, 5% dromaar, 3% halfling, 2% elven, 2% gnome, 2% other)

Languages Common, Skald, Varisian

Religions Andoletta, Iomedae, Pharasma, Zohls

Threats undead from the Gravelands, localized monster activity, river raiders

Faithful Residents of Grayce prioritize divine worship. Religious items or divine magic items of up to 8th level are available for purchase.

Jindel Macroi (discerning female human sheriff 6) town sheriff

Sancovel Durantine (pragmatic female aiuvarin human priest of Pharasma 8) head of the church of Pharasma

Synerina Leptinato (straightforward female human administrator 5) Grayce’s head councilor

Yudi Barnthel (caring female human priest 7) head of the church of Andoletta

Like many small towns, everyone knows each other. People might talk, but usually leave others to their business unless they’re hurting someone. Most of the residents are locals whose families have lived in Grayce, or the surrounding region, for generations. Since much of the property in town turns over through inheritance, sometimes the generations sync up in strange ways, with children born around the same time all coming into their inheritance together. The local phrase for this is “turning over Grayce.”

Since Grayce is a town rich in faith with three prominent churches, locals celebrate numerous religious holidays and feast days. Any day held sacred by Andoletta, Iomedae, or Pharasma is a civic holiday in Grayce. Depending on the particular day, this can mean closed shops, government buildings, and other services—even if the proprietor doesn’t worship that particular deity. This doesn’t bother the people of Grayce for the most part, but those visiting sometimes express surprise and frustration at the practice.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Grayce was built up over the years from the shrine at the high riverbank. The small shrine grew into a massive cathedral and more, spreading into a wide town square where people would gather with their neighbors and trade. The town’s growth has been slow over the years, though it’s currently expanding due to the fall of Lastwall, with dozens of new simple houses going up in the west side of town where the smell of cut lumber and fresh paint drifts in the air. There are numerous farms and residences not too far out of town, such as Albin Derkensoor’s farm (encountered in @UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar]{The Path River Peeler}, the abandoned estate of Professor Thalleus Jongrim from @UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r]{The Disgraced Dollmaker}, or the gristmill operated by Arvent and Monnery Daswooren in @UUID[JournalEntry.wzqJL0YgefgczTx0]{Sweet Tooth}).

What follows are some of the most prominent locations in Grayce.

Shrine of Pharasma.name: Shrine of Pharasma
Shrine of Pharasma.text:
Easily the most prominent structure in Grayce, the Shrine of Pharasma is a modest gothic cathedral that has stood overlooking the Path River for over 500 years in its current incarnation. Long ago it was a simple shrine perched on the high banks of the Path River, and over time worshippers built it up. First they added a roof to the original shrine first; Additional walls came later as generation of worshippers expanded on the building. The most notable expansion, the construction of the stone chapel that exists today, occurred after the previous wooden chapel burned down. Rebuilt with quarried stone, the engineer at the time decided to also rebuild the town’s bridge, incorporating it into the new Shrine of Pharasma.

Other than having a drawbridge built into the structure, the Shrine of Pharasma is similar to most other churches of Pharasma in design and function. Its clergy tends to the town’s needs of bringing life into the world and putting it to rest, and guiding the living in between. @UUID[Actor.pWZBBhBcZV87eyon]{Sancovel Durantine} (pragmatic female aiuvarin human priest of Pharasma 8) leads the clergy and staff at the Shrine of Pharasma. She is well respected by the town’s leadership as well as the people of Grayce, and she provides honest wisdom to those coming to her with problems. After the recent troubles to the south, the church has taken on a more defensive position in the community. Working in close collaboration with the Church of Iomedae, many of Grayce’s Pharasmin priests intensified their martial training during the fall of Lastwall to help defend Grayce from undead attacks. During that time and in the years that have followed, the church has attracted clergy from elsewhere who focus on fighting undead, many of whom transferred their appointments to the Shrine of Pharasma permanently.

Chapel Bridge.name: Chapel Bridge
Chapel Bridge.text: This drawbridge spans the Path River and must be raised to allow passage for any river traffic that has a mast or tall payload that won’t pass the 15-foot clearance. The bridge is raised for two hours twice daily (just after dawn and before nightfall); those who fail to pass through during these times must shelter at one of the town’s two docks until the next raising.

Grayce Graveyard.name: Grayce Graveyard
Grayce Graveyard.text: Grayce’s graveyard is a place of beauty and quiet reflection. Ringed by a low stone wall and wrought iron fencing, well-maintained statues stand among an army of headstones, some dating back to Grayce’s early days. In the last decade, this graveyard reached capacity and the church built a new one just next door.

Gravedocks.name: Gravedocks
Gravedocks.text: Formally called the West Docks, the larger set of docks in Grayce is relatively new and has expanded significantly during the last decade. Called the Gravedocks due to its proximity to the town’s cliffside graveyard, the Gravedocks has more ships docking there overnight than the East Docks. Even so, most merchants traveling through end up stopping at the Gravedocks regardless, as it is where the Grayce Toll House is located, which weighs goods and collects taxes. Those who feel the taxes are too high often apply an additional significance to the name Gravedocks, exclaiming that “these taxes are going to put me in the grave.” Like at the Grayce Docks, dock workers use a system of pulleys and ladders to load and unload cargo from the docks up the steep riverbanks to the town proper.

East Docks.name: East Docks
East Docks.text: Though the smaller of the two sets of docks in town, the East Docks are the oldest and sit east of the Chapel Bridge. Most of the traffic that docks here comes from Caliphas or other small settlements along the Path River heading deeper inland. Due to the steep riverbanks, the docks in Grayce are outfitted with sturdy wooden frames set with pulleys so dockworkers can draw up cargo from the boats below and into the nearby warehouses.

Harbormaster's Office.name: Harbormaster's Office
Harbormaster's Office.text: This small building serves as the office for the harbormaster, where @UUID[Actor.NybYUAgycRo0rUA6]{Ulaptisk Nannocurt} (orderly male dromaar human harbormaster 4) manages incoming and outgoing vessels, handles disputes at the docks, and works closely with Mariv Sonnal at the Toll House to see that everything is documented and collected. The harbormaster’s role is also entwined with the workings of the Church of Pharasma, as Ulaptisk is in charge of the scheduled opening and closing of the Chapel Bridge but not the mechanism to perform that action, which lies with the church. In the event of an emergency where the bridge must be raised or lowered outside of the scheduled times, one must find and convince Ulaptisk to break schedule and send the request to the Chapel Bridge.

North Encarthan Shipping.name: North Encarthan Shipping
North Encarthan Shipping.text: This is a branch office of the shipping company that handles trade throughout the Lake Encarthan region. As trade has increased further inland into Belkzen in recent years, an enterprising senior clerk in the shipping company had the idea to open a location on the Path River to facilitate this new trade market. @UUID[Actor.hlyoGRqr1RCUqQwQ]{Belos Lunata} (shrewd male dhampir human clerk 2) offers new customers a discount if they intend on using his services for a regular shipping route.

Apple Tree Stables.name: Apple Tree Stables
Apple Tree Stables.text: While each inn in town has a small stable, most who travel to Grayce by road board their horses at Apple Tree Stables. Shabin Jaeth’s grandson, @UUID[Actor.itIOqO6kyuI3lG1X]{Molvin Jaeth} (kindhearted male human groom 1) keeps travelers’ horses in fine condition and maintains a job board for delivering small packages—or loads of fruit—to remote villages. Anyone can take up one of these jobs provided they have the means to carry the parcel in a reasonable timeframe.

Jaeth's Orchard.name: Jaeth's Orchard
Jaeth's Orchard.text: This small orchard provides more apples, pears, and plums than the town alone can use, so owner and operator @UUID[Actor.sZFY4gUmkNYubJSX]{Shabin Jaeth} (warm old female human farmer 6) built up trade with other nearby towns. She’s waiting to hear back on a deal with a merchant in Caliphas who will buy enough bushels of fruit that she’ll have to start more trees this season to keep up if things go well. The orchard boasts enough different varieties of apples and pears that the trees produce in all months except those that fall during the depths of winter’s frost.

Chapel Bistro.name: Chapel Bistro
Chapel Bistro.text: After gaining a reputation during his stint as the chief cook at the Riverbend Inn, @UUID[Actor.biunRqbp1EUND2p8]{Lowrie Mols} (passionate male human cook 6) opened his own place a few years ago with the blessing and support of Jabric Roshin. The Bistro provides delicious breakfasts, takeaway snacks, and lunches daily, but only opens every other evening for dinner. This daytime business keeps the establishment’s doors open, and traffic surges when boats dock and people crowd the small cafe. The increased attraction to the restaurant has frustrated some townspeople, but deep down they know that they have a true jewel in their town. Plus, most of the daytime traffic doesn’t get to enjoy Lowrie’s exquisite dinners, where he tracks down special ingredients and painstakingly creates multicourse meals three times a week. To be able to share with the town as much as possible, he keeps his prices low and discourages people from taking advantage of reservations.

Sing-A-Long Bar.name: Sing-A-Long Bar
Sing-A-Long Bar.text:
Though shabby, this ramshackle bar grows lively at night as folks of all sorts visit to enjoy drinks with their friends and sing. @UUID[Actor.oSqYB63MGd9ztg9J]{Fram Trangle} (jovial female goblin proprietor 5) opened the place up a few years ago after coming to Grayce with a group of Lastwall refugees. Fram loves to sing and encourages all of her patrons to do so as well. She greets newcomers with an offer: “Song or coin gets you a drink!” In addition to surprisingly high-quality drinks, Fram serves all manner of pickled and salty snacks to her clientele.

@UUID[Actor.HphgVWl9pem6gZRr]{Dim-Dim} (enthusiastic male goblin dentist 5), Fram’s partner, runs a side business from a back room in the tavern, where he performs crude dentistry. Dim-Dim became fascinated with how other humanoids’ teeth, for the most part, weren’t pointy and wanted his teeth to look like that. His early attempts with a stolen file resulted in a nasty infection that was healed by a traveling cleric. This cleric became a mentor of sorts, and Dim-Dim followed him around for months watching the man treat others along the way. Eventually, he settling in Grayce after becoming smitten with Fram (a sentiment she quickly reciprocated). Dim-Dim has a knack for treating sore or bad teeth, but he’s always up for cosmetic experiments—either making pointy teeth flat or flat teeth pointy.

Ash Inn.name: Ash Inn
Ash Inn.text: The Ash Inn is a down-to-earth place ready to provide lodging, a hearty meal, and a strong drink to all who visit. Decades ago, the Ash Inn began under its former name, the Lilac Inn. Rasoni and Marika Shaldove built the quaint establishment after saving up for years, and it was a hit with travelers and locals alike. The locals came for the noontime tea Marika was known for and the vibrant social setting the place took on in the evenings. However, a year to the day after the inn opened, fire consumed the building, and despite the efforts of the townspeople, the purple-hued building burnt to the ground. They never figured out how the fire started, and the town quickly pitched in to help the Shaldoves rebuild both their inn and their spirits. But the whole ordeal was too much for the Shaldoves, and their normally upbeat attitude turned morose and self-defeating. They reopened a less lively place and named it the Ash Inn in a somber nod to their previously destroyed dreams. The couple only ran the Ash Inn for its first four months before selling it and leaving town. The Ash Inn changed hands again six years ago, when former soldier @UUID[Actor.rXZwcTC1CC0ll8Kn]{Jakivi Rindix} (cordial male human innkeeper 4) spent his life savings on a place to settle down. The inn is livelier these days and draws people from all walks of life to its bountiful tables and comfortable beds.

Sheriff's Office.name: Sheriff's Office
Sheriff's Office.text: It’s rare to find anyone in one of Grayce’s three jail cells, but if you came to town looking for a captured fugitive, you’d find them here. The building also serves as the headquarters for Grayce’s largely volunteer town guard, led by @UUID[Actor.L5QFgAu5iTTuy3co]{Jindel Macroi} (perspicacious female human sheriff 6). A veteran of battles in Lastwall, Jindel was never actually a knight, but she was in her late teens when she slipped out of town, snatched armor from a cart piled with scavenged spoils of war on the road south through Lastwall, and joined up with a group of beleaguered knights. She fought many battles with them, and while she was accepted by her unit, she was never made an official knight. When she returned home to Grayce, she didn’t want to take what she felt was undue praise, so she bundled up her armor and buried it in the woods in a shrine to her fallen comrades that she visits on each of their birthdays.

Grayce General Goods.name: Grayce General Goods
Grayce General Goods.text: If you need something in Grayce, a suitable first spot to look is Grayce General Goods. @UUID[Actor.ESURU33xyLebJb9I]{Denval Troben} (warm male dwarf merchant 3) welcomes visitors with a robust greeting asking shoppers what they’re searching for. He mainly deals in basic sundries, but he also has a whole section of his shop stocked with random goods he’s bought off merchants coming through town. He prides himself in having a network of merchants and claims he can order someone anything they can’t find in his store. Unfortunately, Denval’s network isn’t as vast or as competent as he imagines, and customers are occasionally disappointed. Nevertheless, he tries.

Town Hall.name: Town Hall
Town Hall.text: This two-story timber building stands prominently on the east side of the town square and serves as the center of Grayce’s civic operations. Head Councilor @UUID[Actor.Xb8xaZUnuOLTgIC1]{Synerina Leptinato} (straightforward female human administrator 5) keeps open office hours for any of Grayce’s citizens to voice their concerns and requests, and hosts a monthly town hall for more public hearings. Each of the council members has an official office in the building, though many of them see to their civic duties in their churches or guildhalls. An exception to this is @UUID[Actor.cB8fHcG1KNpwazOS]{Halgert Nosmin} (grumpy male human farmer 4), a former member of the town council whose family has been in Grayce for generations. He irritates Synerina at times with his constant negativity, but she knows he cares deeply for the town and that Halgert spends so much time in Town Hall because he doesn’t want to be home alone after the passing of his wife three years ago.

Church of Iomedae.name: Church of Iomedae
Church of Iomedae.text: While also serving as a place of worship, the church of Iomedae also oversees the town’s security and defense. During the fall of Lastwall, church membership swelled with the knights and soldiers coming to town to aid in defense or to rest and resupply before heading back into what would become the Gravelands. The church also administered aid and support to the hundreds of refugees who came through Grayce seeking safety from the Tyrant’s undead horrors. In recent years, things have settled back to normal, though head priest @UUID[Actor.ceVuBuMFao4wmXWN]{Restevis Celamandru} (prosaic male human priest of Iomedae 7) still leads martial drills at the barracks with regularity. He also keeps up the old practice of having regular communal meals provided by the church in the town square, though these days he only has time for them once every two weeks.

Grayce Barracks.name: Grayce Barracks
Grayce Barracks.text: Grayce doesn’t have a standing army, but a few years ago during the fall of Lastwall when defense was high on the list of concerns for people in town, the church of Iomedae built these barracks to house guards and trainees coming to the border to help. These days only a handful of people use the building, but it’s a place for guards to call home and safe storage for the town’s arms and defenses. The church of Iomedae holds periodic arms training courses at the barracks that are open to the public.

Sun After Rain Barber and Balms.name: Sun After Rain Barber and Balms
Sun After Rain Barber and Balms.text: This small shop caters to the beauty of Grayce’s citizens. Run by @UUID[Actor.7WiXbI4D38nDrY98]{Sun After Rain} (enterprising female leshy barber 1), the shop features two comfortable chairs and a handful of stools of varying sizes the small leshy uses to get to the tops of her clients’ heads during haircuts. Business has picked up over recent years. At first, Sun After Rain’s business struggled since most people in town take care of their own grooming, and the leshy practically had to drag people into her shop to get them to give it a try. Sun After Rain does a meticulous job, and she listens to her client’s wishes—and also their troubles. Many people in town these days come by the shop to talk or hear gossip, something Sun After Rain never shares with other people, but her clients sure do. In addition to haircuts and small talk, Sun After Rain gives beauty advice to those who inquire. The quality of the advice about an embarrassing skin condition impressed one of Sun After Rain’s clients so much that they encouraged the leshy to branch out to providing balms and oils that can treat many conditions. She doesn’t advertise it, but with a little digging, prospective customers find that she dabbles in all sorts of extracts and concoctions and has a makeshift apothecary’s worth of chemical marvels.

Grayce Outdoor Stage.name: Grayce Outdoor Stage
Grayce Outdoor Stage.text: A relatively new addition to the scene in Grayce, this small wooden stage at the corner of Maple and Ash lanes has stout poles driven in at each corner to support a tarp that can be extended out over the rows of benches. Initially the stage went mostly unused, but now has enough frequent activity that neighbors complain about the noise during especially boisterous performances. One of the acts drawing this kind of complaint as of late is the traveling band the Querulous Quartet. Their performances are lively and loud, and the crowd typically has a reaction in kind. For a traveling band, they’ve sure stayed put, according to some in town. The group has been sticking around Grayce for months, but they do their best to get along with everyone and pay their bills, and, as even some of the critics begrudgingly say, bring joy to the people in town.

Grayce Schoolhouse & Library.name: Grayce Schoolhouse & Library
Grayce Schoolhouse & Library.text: This tree-shaded building bustles with the eager energy of children during the day. Headmaster @UUID[Actor.NnqS0XcIbw4qdUDV]{Netessa Colvinshire} (effusive female gnome teacher 3) and two other teachers manage classes of kids of all ages. The school is far more impressive than what one would expect in such a small town and resembles a miniature university building. Netessa is an energetic teacher who throws herself into a topic, often getting deeper into her subject than many want. She frequently invites other educators to town to cover expanded topics drawn from the students’ interests. She has a surprisingly large network of academics she can call on for these lessons, and parents are often surprised that she can draw them to Grayce so quickly and with little to no additional cost. A sizable library adjoins the school. The library holds all manner of books, but its shelves are particularly rich in fiction from across Avistan and beyond.

Riverbend Tavern & Inn.name: Riverbend Tavern & Inn
Riverbend Tavern & Inn.text: Commonly just called the Riverbend, this establishment is the largest and oldest place of lodging and eatery in Grayce. Carefully run by @UUID[Actor.rk26tOBkdO3YhaBL]{Jabric Roshin} (attentive male aiuvarin human innkeeper 3), the Riverbend stands proudly at the north end of the town square. The inn has two dozen rooms and four suites. Diners can find high quality meals ranging from common fare to the kind of fine meals you’d find in the capital. The Riverbend is popular with merchants and leisure travelers, and lets the Ash Inn cater to others. Jabric has been known to host some guests from far-flung locations, and people in town can tell he’s trying to ingratiate himself with these guests by how much he redecorates the inn or orders imported foods for the inn’s menu.

Dalmira’s Bakery.name: Dalmira’s Bakery
Dalmira’s Bakery.text: Owned and operated by @UUID[Actor.oj6Hnf2XBAxDqdhe]{Dalmira Eranhal} (friendly female human baker 2), this spot is a must-visit for any travelers, though locals flock to the bakery for her signature sweets in droves as well. The morning air in the town square is filled with the aroma of baked goods coming from Dalmira’s every day. However, not too long ago, residents didn’t awaken to the smell of baking bread and instead found a note presumably from Dalmira saying she had urgent family business to attend to, and her cousin would be filling in. Skeptical at first, the people of Grayce came to love what Larmine cooked up; some even whispered that her treats were better than Dalmira’s.

Weaver’s Hall.name: Weaver’s Hall
Weaver’s Hall.text: Home to the Weaver’s Guild, this cozy building’s interior is full of thick rugs and walls draped in rich tapestries displaying the artistry of Grayce’s weavers, knitters, and spinners. With its healthy herds of sheep, Grayce is known for the quality of its woolen yarn, which holds dyes especially well. People come from miles away to buy the town’s supply after the spring shearing. The harvest from the waving fields of linen and flax outside of town also find their way to the town’s weavers, who craft beautifully patterned fabrics seen in the headscarves of working people throughout the region—a specialty of @UUID[Actor.YvbgZG8eMHymMqXu]{Jeneece Krieggen} (skilled female halfling weaver 4), town council member and head of the Weaver’s Guild.

Carpenter’s Hall.name: Carpenter’s Hall
Carpenter’s Hall.text: As would be expected, the home of the town’s Carpenter’s Guild is a marvel of skilled woodworking. The building is made from a combination of different lacquered woods, and is carved with exquisite patterns that tell a story of the town’s history and the contributions of those who built it. After his father’s passing, Wurt Nommensill threw his hat into the race to be head of the Carpenter’s Guild, but lost to his longtime friend @UUID[Actor.bAZpNV5GDiARk4cm]{Rolm Barnthel} (easygoing male nephilim human guildmaster 3).

Shepherd’s Hall.name: Shepherd’s Hall
Shepherd’s Hall.text: This building is a guild hall for the ranchers in town, though the townspeople who make up the Rancher’s Guild use this building as a casual gathering place for catching up with friends, having drinks, and playing games more than for official guild business. These informal “guild meetings” happen daily in the late afternoon. Lately, the ranchers have been on edge as it seems a local legendary creature—the Path River Peeler—is on the prowl again, leaving the carcasses of skinned sheep in its wake. Guildmaster and town council member @UUID[Actor.6s0DQuMjsYaE6Jhr]{Albin Derkensoor} (hardy male human rancher 3) is determined to get to the bottom of this, even if it means having to hire transient adventurers to investigate.

Grayce Green Market.name: Grayce Green Market
Grayce Green Market.text:
The market swells on weekends when farmers from the outskirts and traveling merchants join the locals and set up shop in the town square. Some stalls are permanent fixtures for convenient regular shopping where townspeople mingle with their neighbors and pick up meat and produce to supplement what they get from their personal gardens and farms.

A recent disruption to business as usual is the giant sinkhole that opened up on the southeastern end of the town square. The ground collapsed during the night a few weeks ago, and while no one was around to see it, the noise woke many who lived nearby. Those who run market stalls are thankful that it didn’t open up under the market itself, but they’re mostly concerned about the stability and safety of the town square. Even though the town councilors are doing what they can to investigate the sinkhole, a small group of grocers have been asking the authorities for updates nearly every day since it opened up.

Vintage Gearworks.name: Vintage Gearworks
Vintage Gearworks.text: Settling into town after the troubles in Lastwall, @UUID[Actor.YmLtIdJHzVM4hiQb]{Krenvus Sang} (curious male human inventor 3) purchased his humble shop using some treasures he came by in his adventuring days, days he proudly claims are behind him now. Krenvus opened his shop with barely a dozen modified mechanical tools, unique contraptions, and fun and playful gizmos that were an instant hit with Grayce’s children. People initially found it strange that this kind of industry would pop up in a town like Grayce, but Krenvus’s modifications to common farm tools turned out to be successful, and the weavers in town were glad to have him around to fix and maintain their smooth moving looms. Some people call his shop a “junk shop” and don’t see the point of it all. Regardless, many in town came to appreciate Krenvus’s knack with small machines over time.

The Grayce Gazette.name: The Grayce Gazette
The Grayce Gazette.text:
It might seem odd that a town as small as Grayce has its own broadsheet—The Grayce Gazette—but thanks to the diligent work of @UUID[Actor.IrnXdvibF2AU00fM]{Father Wren} (studious male human priest of Zohls 10), the ledger of trade prices and regional news comes out every week, helping merchants plan their trade throughout the region and allowing local farmers to more accurately set prices for their commodities. He produces this broadsheet locally using a fully functional printing press he and his staff maintain.

The Grayce Gazette has only been in town for the last dozen years, and in addition to the broadsheet, the press also produces books and pamphlets. They mostly print holy books for the town’s resident faiths, but the Gazette also takes orders from other sources ranging from wanted posters commissioned from the county sheriff to scholarly treatises destined for the University of Lepidstadt. The broadsheet is often only one folded page published each week; weeks that are busy enough to require a second paper, or one that has more than one page, are often called “two-paper weeks” or “two-page weeks.”

While it’s not a proper church with a large congregation, Father Wren also uses the building to hold worship services dedicated to Zohls, the empyreal lord of determination, investigation, and truth. Father Wren doesn’t advertise these services and tends not to talk much about his faith or his past, lending to the rumors that he once led a life of adventure before settling down. As he gets older, it’s becoming more and more difficult to maintain the broadsheet, the printing press, and a congregation, so in recent years he’s hired on more staff, keeping a keen eye on them to evaluate who he’s leaving the place to when he either passes on or becomes too old to adequately run the busy operation.

Grayce Toll House.name: Grayce Toll House
Grayce Toll House.text: This stout building serves as the home of the largest and most accurate scale for hundreds of miles. As such, Caliphas County depends on Grayce to collect tolls and duties for goods brought down the Path River from deeper inland. There’s no guarantee that river traffic would turn north to Caliphas to pay their taxes after reaching Lake Encarthan at the Path River’s mouth, so since Grayce is the largest and oldest town along the way—despite being a hundred miles inland—it gets the honor of collecting these taxes and seeing that they get to Caliphas safely. @UUID[Actor.8sV8CqSM6to7aItl]{Mariv Sonnal} (suspicious female changeling human tax collector 3) is a liaison for the prince and maintains detailed records of all goods trafficked past Grayce by river. The building has an impenetrable safe and multiple rooms stacked with files, and also serves as a supplemental harbormaster’s office where all docking records are kept.

Cockrie’s Smithy.name: Cockrie’s Smithy
Cockrie’s Smithy.text: Cockrie’s Smithy makes everything from tools to cookware to weapons, but mainly tools and cookware. @UUID[Actor.oCExmGhWCaYVwI1D]{Mason Cockrie} (rugged male human blacksmith 3) inherited the shop from his father, who inherited the shop from his father. Cockrie’s Smithy has been a mainstay in Grayce for generations and provides most of the town’s metalworking needs. Years ago, when Krenvus Sang arrived to a lukewarm reception, Mason was responsible for fomenting some of that negative sentiment. He felt Krenvus’s creations were drawing away customers who would normally come to him. The two were gruff with one another when they crossed paths in town. However, one Ascendance Day, the two artisans ended up seated next to one another at the feast table and grudgingly struck up a conversation that quickly turned to friendly shop talk. The change of heart didn’t take hold immediately, but over the course of a few months the two became good friends, and frequently spend time with each other now.

Bedanta’s Blooms.name: Bedanta’s Blooms
Bedanta’s Blooms.text: This manor home on the western edge of town is awash in color nearly year round thanks to @UUID[Actor.lS9GpEbS0MbRVI2g]{Bedanta Thromire} (bubbly female halfling botanist 3). The Thromires have lived in Grayce for three generations as grain farmers. Bedanta took her family’s agricultural interest in a different direction, growing flowers ever since she was a child. When her parents passed nearly 20 years ago, she leased the family’s fields to another farmer whose land bordered their acreage and expanded her garden at home. She was already selling flowers at the Grayce Green Market and to the inns and eateries in town, but this let her focus on expanding the variety of the flowers she grows and creating new hybrids. The grounds surrounding her home are lush with azaleas, rhododendrons, zinnias, and roses of all colors. A wrought iron fence surrounds the garden in back to prevent deer from grazing on her blooms, and narrow paths weave through the perfumed colorscape. While she often sells at the market, regular customers are welcome to visit her at home to buy bouquets, and she even hires local children as couriers to bring orders directly to people’s doors.

Chapel of Andoletta.name: Chapel of Andoletta
Chapel of Andoletta.text: Frolicking, stern, and inquisitive carved crows decorate the trim of this dark wooden building, home of the church of Andoletta, empyreal lord of consolation, respect, and security. People gathered to worship Grandmother Crow in this spot for thousands of years, much like the original shrine of Pharasma. Long before the worship of Iomedae came to town, the faithful of these two religions intermingled as Grayce grew from an ancient gathering place to a proper town. As such, the church of Andoletta holds significant sway in the goings-on in Grayce. @UUID[Actor.ZCOTQME0JufH65Yv]{Yudi Barnthel} (caring female human priest of Andoletta 7) leads the faithful and embraces her role as town council member. She’s a stern but compassionate woman who always tries to encourage the best behavior in others. Popular with the children of Grayce for her skill at storytelling, she invariably weaves a lesson into her tales and always has a healthy little treat for the children. Disapproving parents claim the kids flock around Yudi for her treats more than her stories.

Sawmill.name: Sawmill
Sawmill.text:
Built on the edge of town, this simple sawmill runs under the steady hand of @UUID[Actor.d61WekXuu6a00tZH]{Wurt Nommensill} (eager male human carpenter 2) who recently inherited the sawmill from his father after he went to Pharasma’s embrace. Wurt’s father built this sawmill when he was Wurt’s age. His father moved the town’s original sawmill, which he inherited from his own father, further back from the river as the town grew. The people of Grayce were happy when the sawmill moved because it cut down on the noise, but as the town has expanded in recent years, complaints of the noise are starting to return, and Wurt is concerned he’s not going to be able to satisfy everyone for long.

The sawmill produces clean, high-quality planks and posts, and the establishment charges fair prices for the quality of work produced. The Nommensills have long been known in Grayce as being matter-of-fact people who bother more with quality and consistency than artistic frills to their work, and Wurt continues that tradition. The sawmill doesn’t have a name and is just called “the sawmill.” In fact, the business is recorded in town records as either “sawmill” or “Nommensill.” Word is that Wurt’s grandfather didn’t see the point in naming the place and just recorded his surname and business in the ledger.

Harding’s Smokehouse.name: Harding’s Smokehouse
Harding’s Smokehouse.text:
Tucked back behind some homes on Oak Road sits Harding’s Smokehouse. This is a place that you often smell before seeing, unless of course you look to the skies and see smoke wafting from one of the building’s many chimneys. Not only a smokehouse, this establishment also serves as a butcher shop under the watchful eye of @UUID[Actor.rzvUwWgZ5c2XfbTc]{Grambleson Harding} (jovial male human butcher 2).

Grambleson built this shop after moving to town almost a decade ago. He started off dressing and processing sheep and hogs from the local farms and ranches, as well as wild game like deer, boar, pheasants, and rabbits in a much smaller building. As business grew, he expanded from a couple tiny smoke sheds behind the butcher shop to the full building it is now. The shop itself is small and cramped, with two massive oak butcher tables taking up most of the space. However, the door behind the counter leads to a barn-sized room that smells of burned wood and curing meats. The smoke room is sectioned off into separate enclosed stalls so Grambleson can use specific woods for each kind of meat. Whole animal carcasses hang on iron hooks while links of sausage hang like meaty garlands from the low rafters. Grambleson runs the smokehouse nearly around the clock and keeps odd hours to make sure the smoldering fires burn uninterrupted. Most of the meat he works with is already spoken for by the hunter or rancher who brought him the animals, but he also sells remaining smoked and cured meats at the Green Market and to some of the dining establishments in town.

Falcon Lodge.name: Falcon Lodge
Falcon Lodge.text: It’s been years since this hunting lodge saw regular activity. It was originally the meeting hall for local hunters, but a series of tragedies led to the group disbanding and the lodge sitting empty. The fellowship of hunters was a small group numbering no more than six or seven at any point. Eight years ago, a stag gored Dalsom Mandrifer during a hunt. Three months later, the founder of the lodge, Mel Ranbicher, and his longtime friend and neighbor Keldy Finnstrop both disappeared while out hunting pheasants, and neither have been heard from since. Mel was a bachelor, but Keldy left behind a wife and two children. The remaining members of the lodge, mostly elderly residents, pooled together the remaining coin from the lodge’s coffers and donated it to the Finnstrop family. Since Mel owned the building, it can’t be sold or seized by the town until it can be proven that Mel didn’t just run off and is in fact dead. After 10 years, a point in time that is rapidly approaching, the town can seize the property and either sell or absorb the abandoned lodge.

Baltronis Estate.name: Baltronis Estate
Baltronis Estate.text:
Most of the year, this fine manor house sits empty. The Baltronises were once well-to-do landowners and ranchers in the area, but as the matriarch and patriarch of the family aged, they transferred much of the family business operations to their children. The children, who were educated in Caliphas and Lepidstadt, grew tired of rural living and convinced their family to sell their sheep and horses as well as most of their land so they could relocate to Caliphas and live among high society there. They were tired of being looked at as ignorant hayseeds while rubbing elbows with the aristocracy in the capital. It took some convincing, but the children ultimately got their way and moved the whole family, keeping the manor house in Grayce to serve as a summer home.

The Baltronises return to town at least once a year, typically during late summer, where they relax for almost a month before returning to Caliphas. Their annual return isn’t a celebrated event to the hardscrabble working people of Grayce. The Baltronises stroll through town with their noses up, as if they were forced to visit some backwater village, loudly talking, often critically, about whatever minor changes have taken place in Grayce during the year. When they visit the town’s shops or eateries, they’re always critical and generally act snooty. Most of the town just tries to tolerate the family’s vacation time.

Horvat Estate.name: Horvat Estate
Horvat Estate.text: Retired farmer turned amateur cryptozoologist @UUID[Actor.lNBrn40Ljk6FmTgA]{Titus Horvat} (credulous nonbinary human cryptozoologist 2) inherited this place from their uncle and quickly moved in. Their uncle, a professor of biology at the University of Lepidstadt, left not only the modest home, but also a library of books and journals, many of which were filled with diagrams of fantastic and strange creatures he encountered during his studies. Titus was intrigued and pored over the books and journals in short order. They retired from farming, deemed themself a cryptozoologist, and began hunting down any evidence of odd creatures in the surrounding region. The most popular subject of their new profession is the Path River Peeler, a mysterious monster said to call the region its hunting grounds for hundreds of years. It’s never been caught—something that Titus feels could give them real credentials in the field of cryptozoology if they became the first to do so.

The Daring Tree.name: The Daring Tree
The Daring Tree.text:
An old gnarled oak tree stands on the edge of town and has been a part of the folklore for Grayce’s youth for generations. The Daring Tree, as it’s known, is a nexus of all manner of dares, rendezvous, and youthful challenges. The original dare, when the town was small and the tree was beyond sight of the town’s lights, was for a child to spend the night in the boughs of the oak. As the town spread out over the years, it’s begun to encroach on the tree, but the traditions handed down from parent to child have remained close. Sometimes when a dared kid slept in the tree for the night, their friends­—typically older youth—would creep near the tree and make spooky sounds to scare the sleeper, hoping to make them forfeit the dare. Over the years, the challenges have expanded and diversified beyond a night spent alone away from town. Some kids dare each other to climb to the highest point to pluck an acorn, while teenagers picked the Daring Tree as a site for grudge-settling brawls. Some youths claim it’s good luck to run to the tree during thunderstorms, while others say that if you make a tea from the tree’s bark and two acorns, your crush will notice your affections and approach you within a week.

Some kids who’ve slept in the tree claim they dreamed the tree was alive and spoke to them. Others swear that this experience comes from a dryad living in the tree. Adults in town, most with their own Daring Tree stories, believe supernatural claims are just childhood imagination, but every so often doubts surface, and they wonder if growing out of that sense of whimsy and wonder was worth it.

Government.name: Government
Government.text:
Grayce has a tight-knit community, and most conflicts work themselves out with friendly conversation and compromises. However, sometimes officials of the town need to get involved. More importantly, someone needs to see to the community’s interests, provide safety, and ensure prosperity when possible.

Grayce is governed by a town council made up of seven council members, which has a somewhat unique arrangement. Due to the town’s core of faith and its founding on a site of worship, three of the council members are selected from the clergy of the churches of Andoletta, Pharasma, and Iomedae. The next three members are selected from the three major trade guilds: the Carpenter’s Guild, the Rancher’s Guild, and the Weaver’s Guild. The council members don’t necessarily need to be the heads of these organizations, but it frequently works out that way. The seventh council member is the head councilor, who oversees much of the routine civic work of the town and is relied upon to break tie votes should the trade guilds and churches have stark ideological conflicts, or for any other decision that is locked in debate. The head councilor also serves as an administrator, calls meetings, negotiates with other communities within the county, and serves as a representative should Caliphas call for one from Grayce.

Council seats are filled democratically. Members of the trade guilds and churches vote for council seats from their organizations, and the whole town votes for the head councilor. Elections are held every five years and there is no limit to the number of terms a council member can hold their seat. The last election was last year, and only the Carpenter’s Guild seat went to a new council member.

Civic services are handled by different groups in town. For example, the church of Andoletta is in charge of judicial duties, and the church of Iomedae is responsible for providing security for the town. The harbormaster and tax collector stationed at the Toll House are technically employed by Caliphas County, but report to and work closely with the head councilor.

History.name: History
History.text:
Despite being a small town, Grayce is extremely old. Long before Grayce was a settlement, the cliffs along the river looked south over rich, forested land, and people of many faiths came there to pray and meditate. The people of differing faiths respected one another and would cede watch over the area when another faith’s holy days came around. A group of Pharasmins were the first to erect a shrine in this location. Later, a band of Andoletta’s worshippers followed and established their own semi-permanent place of worship a few hundred yards away, nestled in the forest. These worship sites were destinations of special journeys and pilgrimages, and generations would pass before people began to settle here permanently. The story goes that a Pharasmin priest felt the call of the Lady of Graves and was determined to pass into the Great Beyond at this site. However, the priest’s health stabilized, and they remained there for another three years. In that time, others began to stay longer, and the scattering of tents became clusters of shacks, their roofs thatched with pine boughs.

As more pilgrims remained at the site year round, the religious settlers began planting gardens and raising animals. The shacks turned to homes and proper chapels, built with goods traded with nearby communities. Seeing this place as a blessing of their divine patrons, the people who collectively built this growing village named it Grayce. The population remained stable at barely over a hundred people for decades, as few outsiders were eager to intrude on the religious settlement. Over time, more people traveling down the river would stop in Grayce to rest or purchase some of their goods, specifically their fine wool and sturdy yarns, and would end up staying. Since the town was so distant from the capital of Caliphas, Grayce was largely left alone by the rest of the county, which didn’t quite notice it or recognize it as a settlement under the prince’s domain. Though as the village grew over the years, so did their ties to the crown.

Grayce’s population was nearly 500 when Tar-Baphon rose from the dead and conquered Ustalav. Soldiers from Caliphas never made it to Grayce when the Tyrant’s forces came through. Many were outright slaughtered, but the majority of residents managed to get some warning and hid in a small network of caves accessible from both the river’s edge and another entrance deep in the woods. After the initial assault, the monstrous enforcers from Tar-Baphon’s armies largely left Grayce alone as long as they paid their tithes with regularity. Their worship was punished and both churches were burned to the ground, forcing the faithful to hide their devotion and worship in the caves and tunnels below town.

When the Shining Crusade finally challenged Tar-Baphon, Grayce provided what aid they could when the armies came through. Legend claims that the then-mortal Iomedae herself camped once on the high banks of the Path River one night while marching through.

After Tar-Baphon’s defeat, things calmed down and returned to normal for hundreds of years. Grayce flourished during this time, but never grew to hold much more than a thousand people. This changed in 4719 when, once again, the Whispering Tyrant brought his blight across the land. During the fall of Lastwall, Grayce fell under attack by the Tyrant’s armies. They withstood two undead sieges and numerous events with lone, wandering undead. To protect the town, Grayce broke with its bridge schedule and left it in the raised position. The town coordinated with the Knights of Lastwall to lower it to help with movement of troops and supplies. The town also took in hundreds of refugees who had lost their farms and villages as Lastwall was overrun with undead. Some of those refugees moved on, but many chose to call Grayce home. A few years ago, they began building houses on the west side of town to accommodate this surge in population.

Those rough and deadly times brought the already close-knit community closer, and they depended on one another for not just safety, but also for prosperity. The people of Grayce didn’t let much stop them from their industrious ways, but they were smarter about it. On the border of a land haunted by undead, the people of Grayce trained under priests of Iomedae and Pharasma to watch for those unholy creatures and defend their town against attacks. When things were still dangerous, a volunteer watch stood throughout town at all hours and a code of whistles would indicate what kind of danger was at hand. Though these strong protocols and defenses have been greatly relaxed in the last few years, everyone who lived in Grayce at the time remembers the drill, and they’re ready to stand up when called. Even young children today can tell you that three whistles means a ghost and two short ones means shamblers.

Under Grayce

Over the years of the town’s existence, the people of Grayce have dug below the surface for various reasons. Many of the chambers and tunnels were dug for practical reasons like cellars and crypts, but when Tar-Baphon ruled over Ustalav, the faithful of Grayce created larger chambers and connecting tunnels so they could continue to worship their preferred gods in safety during the Whispering Tyrant’s brutal reign. It was during this time that the relationship between the three prominent churches knitted together to serve and save the town. In safer times, the tunnels fell out of use and were sealed up to prevent accidents and vermin coming up into the town.

The tunnels came into use again in 4719 when Lastwall fell to the Tyrant’s forces and undead scoured the land for the living. The leadership of Grayce reopened some of the tunnels, particularly the pair of entrances built into the steep riverbanks, to help those fleeing the southern conflict gain entrance to Grayce as the Chapel Bridge remained raised during the troubles.

Caliphas County.name: Caliphas County
Caliphas County.text:
These adventures take place in @UUID[.M3uc2nArpK22LCPj]{Grayce}, a small town in the fog-shrouded nation of Ustalav just across the border from the undead-ravaged Gravelands. Ustalav is an ancient land first settled by Varisian families over 5,000 years ago. There were numerous conflicts among the settlers claiming land and the people they displaced in its early years. As infighting grew more prevalent, King Kaldemov split the land into sixteen counties assigned to various noble families. These counties operate almost as individual nations in some ways, but the act of splitting the nation brought prosperity to the horror-touched land.

Today, Ustalav is known for its misty skies, dark forests, and prevalence of eerie monsters and unsettling events. Not every city and town in Ustalav harbors horrors, but enough of them do to make travelers to this land on edge and leaping at every sudden sound or surprising sight. Grayce, as it happens, has been a serene and peaceful town and the populace brags that there hasn’t been a vampire in the area in generations.

Grayce is in the southern edge of Caliphas County, named for Ustalav’s capital. It’s bordered by the Path River to the south and expansive wooded hills and cleared fields as far as the eye can see. One section of these wooded hills not too far from town is called the Shivering Bluffs that locals (rightfully) claim is home to dangerous supernatural creatures.

The Temple of the Unlit Star, the location of the adventure in the Beginner Box, is northwest of Grayce about 50 miles as the crow flies. The mouth of the Path River is approximately 70 miles downriver, and the capital of Caliphas is another 60 miles along the shoreline of Lake Encarthan once you sail from the mouth of the river.

A Day in the Life.name: A Day in the Life
A Day in the Life.text:
Grayce wakes up early. As an agricultural town, most of Grayce’s residents are awake by dawn. Most eat at home, but the two inns serve breakfast and Dalmira’s Bakery does steady business for people either picking up their daily bread when it’s still warm or sampling one of the many sweet treats to go along with their tea or coffee. The docks are typically awake and buzzing by the time the sun starts casting shadows across them, as workers load boats and those docking overnight cast off their moorings and head downriver. Few boats arrive overnight except those who calculated their travels poorly or met misfortune as they traveled the Path River.

By midday the small town is a bustle of activity, with children taking their lunches outdoors and playing in between chores or their morning classes for those enrolled in the schoolhouse or one of the churches’ educational programs. The farmers and shepherds who started their day when it was still dark begin making their way back to town in the late afternoon, sometimes stopping at one of the inns or taverns to have a refreshment before getting home to start dinner.

As things start winding down for the day, visitors begin making their way to those same inns and taverns after their business is completed for a good meal and relaxing beverage. On special nights and most weekends, people gather for performances in the evenings at the town’s stage, or even join in on the festivities at the Sing-A-Long Bar. Since Grayce wakes early, it also goes to bed early, and it’s not uncommon to find shops shuttered and streets empty only a few hours after dark, with the exception of the inns and taverns—to the chagrin of those establishments’ neighbors.

Ustalav.name: Ustalav
Ustalav.text:
Ustalav is a land known for the terrors that haunt it. Whispers outside its borders speak of a nation where monsters roam free, the dead rise to feed upon the living, and every citizen holds their share of dark and mysterious secrets. Within these exaggerations live hints of truth. Despite the dangers and horrors of the region, Ustalav is home to many ordinary and well-meaning people. The horrors, however, are still all too real.

Vampires, werewolves, ghosts, demons, and alchemical creations all stalk in the dark streets and forsaken forests of Ustalav. As cold nights fade into misty mornings, bells sound from the countryside churches and soaring cathedrals of Pharasma. But the goddess’s most zealous followers, tasked with sending lost souls to her judgment, have been called south to contain a rising threat. Ustalav is truly a land in need of new heroes.

The lands of Ustalav have been haunted for over a thousand years by the legacy of Tar-Baphon, an undead wizard-king known as the Whispering Tyrant. Although he was defeated and imprisoned in the neighboring nation of Lastwall, centuries of his rule left a stain on the land. His admirers had moved in the shadows for that time, finally emerging when his prison was destroyed, taking the nation of Lastwall with it. While the Whispering Tyrant has yet to return to Ustalav directly, his liberation has left the people of Ustalav in a state of underlying dread.

The nearest town to the Temple of the Unlit Star is @UUID[JournalEntry.de6yWKM2osh6uz88]{Grayce}, but Ustalav’s capitol of Caliphas is only a few days away. The fog-haunted lakeshore city holds more than its share of mysteries. Intriguing nobles gather from across the county to hold court here, while rumors of a matching court of vampires hidden beneath the streets garners just as many whispers. Whether there is one court or two, the city meets their every demand of luxury and entertainment.

Further to the east, the cursed fortress of Castle Arudora, called Bastardhall by most who must call it anything, is spoken of only in whispers. Dozens of wild tales claim to explain the downfall of the Arudora family and the ways their black coach can still be seen abroad. Though the residents of nearby villages joined together to burn the castle to the ground centuries ago, no sign of the damage can be seen now, with the fortress standing tall among those who dare not look up at it.

Northern Ustalav is a land of harsh winters and is isolated from other nations, even from their kin to the south. The Shudderwood is a rich forest filled with predators, human and inhuman alike. Local communities say that “by moonlight, all men cast the shadow of beasts.” Although werewolves undeniably stalk the dark forest alongside mundane wolves and mysterious fey, some locals believe their predation is all that holds back demons from the nearby Sarkoris Scar.

On the border of the Shudderwood, Lepidstadt is known as a center of learning for Ustalav and lands beyond. Although the university’s courses in alchemy and surgery are constantly mired in controversy, they are undoubtedly among the best on the continent. Their recent experiments with the principles of electricity have led to greater understanding of the body and revealed the whisperings of ghosts. The city is isolated quite far from Caliphas, however, leaving it exposed to many threats as the price for its academic freedom.

Introduction.name: Introduction
Introduction.text:
Every Pathfinder game needs a Game Master (GM for short). As Game Master, you run each game session, providing the link between the players and the world of the game. It’s up to you to set the scene as the heroes battle monsters, interact with other people, and explore the world.

Being a GM is like organizing a party for your friends. You want to make sure they arrive on time, have plenty to do, and have a good time. You’re in charge of...

  • Telling the story of the group’s adventures in a compelling and consistent way.

  • Fleshing out the world in which the game takes place.

  • Entertaining the players and yourself and rewarding creative ideas.

  • Preparing for game sessions by studying or building adventures and creating characters and plots.

  • Improvising the reactions of characters the heroes meet as the players do unexpected things.

  • Making rules decisions to ensure fairness and keep the game moving at a good pace.

  • Rewarding the heroes for their deeds with Experience Points (XP) and treasure.

You’re not trying to “win” the game by beating the heroes. Your job is to provide a fun story with some challenges. Those challenges can be tough to beat, and the heroes can fail sometimes or even die on occasion. But they should always have a fighting chance!

Common Terms

The following terms are used to describe certain common game elements.

  • Challenge: A challenge is one short scene that puts the heroes to the test. This could be anything from fighting a monster to chasing a thief or getting past a deadly trap.

  • Encounter: An encounter is a combat that plays out in a series of rounds with creatures taking actions in turn.

  • Exploration: Between encounters, heroes are exploring. Usually, this means exploring an environment, but they might explore a social situation, a puzzle, or something else.

  • Session: A session is a single period of gaming, ranging from about 2 hours up to an entire weekend. In a session, you might complete a whole adventure or just part of one.

  • Adventure: An adventure is one story that the heroes experience. It’s made up of a series of explorations broken up by a series of encounters. Adventures might take one or more sessions to complete.

  • Campaign: Campaign is a term used to describe all of the adventures that the heroes experience. The adventures might relate to one another, but not all of the adventures have to be tied into the same overarching plot.

Preparing an Adventure.name: Preparing an Adventure
Preparing an Adventure.text:
Before you can run a game, you need to prepare the adventure your group will play through. An adventure is a self-contained collection of story elements, characters, and settings that become the basis for the story you and the other players tell. Think of the adventure as an outline for your story. You’ll have major plot points you want to include, some consistent characters, and themes you want to convey, but all sorts of things can change during the process of turning the outline into a completed story!

The @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW]{“Temple of the Unlit Star”} adventure has much of the preparation done for you. Reading the adventure and looking over the materials in the Beginner Box: Secrets of the Unlit Star gives you enough preparation to run that adventure. “Temple of the Unlit Star” and other prewritten adventures are built for groups of a specific level. They include setup information and nonplayer characters (NPCs) needed for the story, plus all the locations, maps, and monster groups; they also give out the appropriate amount of XP and treasure. Running a prewritten adventure as your first game can help you see how adventures are structured, which makes it easier to write your own later if you choose. Though a published adventure is prewritten, its events aren’t set in stone. Changing the details of an adventure to suit your group isn’t just OK, it’s preferred! Adjust things to make the adventure appeal to your players more, tweak plot events to account for unexpected developments, and add to the adventure in ways that will make your players happy.

When writing your own adventures, you’ll need to prepare further by picking monsters, drawing maps, coming up with NPCs that live in the world, and determining treasure that the heroes earn from their foes or discover during their journeys. This takes more time on your part but also lets you customize your game to your group.

Character Creation.name: Character Creation
Character Creation.text: Before you start running your adventure, the players should create their heroes. It’s usually best to get all the players together and talk through the characters they’re making. This process can even be part of the first session of your game. Players can share story ideas with one another, and you can contribute too. These discussions can help give the players an idea of where the adventure begins so they can make characters that fit. Talking through the process together also helps everyone understand the rules!

Game Sessions.name: Game Sessions
Game Sessions.text:
You play out an adventure over a series of sessions, which usually last several hours and involve multiple encounters and some exploration. Each session can noticeably differ from the last. Think of a session as an episode of a TV show—it should include some twists, turns, and changes so that the players are excited about what comes next.

Types of Adventures

Adventures can be structured in different ways. A linear adventure has a set path with one encounter leading to another. A nonlinear adventure involves creating an environment with multiple paths the heroes can explore in any order. Finally, a sandbox adventure takes place over a wide environment with the players setting their own goals. For your first adventures, start simple with either a fully linear adventure or one with only a small number of optional paths.

Planning a Session

Often, the responsibility of scheduling the game falls on you as the GM since you have to prepare the game between sessions. Choose a time everyone can attend and a place to gather, whether it’s around the kitchen table or in an online space. Many games have a set schedule, such as once per week, once every 2 weeks, or once per month. (Your first game might not be so predictable, though!) The less frequently your group meets, the better notes and recaps you’ll need to keep everyone on the same page. If another player wants to take session notes, that’s great too, especially if they set up a shared document everyone can reference online. Plan a time for everybody to arrive, and also try to set a time when playing the game will begin. Having this planned can make it easier for everyone to finish catching up so you can start playing the game. Having an end time in mind is also important. A typical game session lasts about 4 hours. Less than 2 hours usually isn’t enough time to get much done.

Starting a Session

Once everyone is ready to play, get everyone’s attention and cover the following topics. These are in a rough order that you can change based on your group’s style or a given session’s needs.

  • Recap what happened during the previous sessions (if this isn’t the first session).

  • Establish where the heroes are at the beginning of this session. Have they been resting since their last challenge? Did you leave off with them in a hallway, preparing to raid the next room of a dungeon? Tell players whether their heroes had time to rest or recover since the last session.

  • Establish goals. Repeat any goals the group already had, then let the players weigh in on whether these goals still apply and on whether there’s anything else they hope to accomplish during the session.

  • Commence adventuring! Usually the first thing you’ll do in a session is describe the environment and sensations that surround the heroes, allowing them to react in the moment.

Running a Session

During a session, you’re in charge of keeping the game’s action moving, answering questions, and making rules decisions. You’ll also want to keep a rough eye on the time, so you can end when it’s most convenient for the group.

You’re the one who customizes the rules you need from the imagined world you and the other players share. It’s up to you to establish what’s true in the world, but you have help in doing so! You’re informed by the setting’s backstory, your preparations, and the suggestions the other players make. You can adjust things on the fly from what you planned, too. You might have an idea in your notes that changes when a player does something unexpected.

You’ll determine when heroes and foes need to attempt checks as well as what happens as a result of their rolls, which comes up most often during exploration. In an encounter, a player can usually determine their own hero’s turn with you chiming in only to say whether an attack hits or if something in the environment requires a hero to attempt a check.

The Spotlight

As you run the game, keep track of which player has the spotlight. You can easily keep attention on the most outgoing player or hero, but you need to check in with all the players. If a player hasn’t contributed in some time, stop and ask, “What’s your hero doing at this point?” If the player isn’t sure, add a detail or NPC to the scene that the player might find interesting.

Distractions and Interruptions

Maintaining the players’ attention keeps a game moving and leads to memorable moments when everyone’s in the zone. Too many interruptions break the flow. Some distractions will always happen, like jokes at the table, but make sure interruptions aren’t too frequent. It helps to plan breaks into the game. A 10-minute break is a great time to grab a snack, use the restroom, or look up something on your phone.

Secret Checks

Some rolls work better if the player doesn’t know the result of their roll. For instance, the Recall Knowledge action from skills can give false information on a critical failure, so the player shouldn’t know whether their hero’s check succeeded or not! These actions have the secret trait. For a secret check, ask the player what their statistic for the skill is. Roll the d20 somewhere the players can’t see and calculate the result normally. Then tell the player what they learned or what happens.

If you're playing on FoundryVTT, your players can roll on "Blind GM Roll" mode instead, which will show you the result as the GM, but hide it from them, all while allowing them to make the roll themselves.

Using the Rules

As the GM, you’re responsible for resolving any questions or disputes about the rules. Remember that keeping your game moving is more important than being 100% correct. Looking up rules at the table can slow the game down, so in many cases, it’s better to make your best guess rather than scour the book for the exact rule and take time to find the correct ruling at a later time. To make calls on the fly, use the following guidelines.

  • If you don’t know how long a quick task takes, go with 1 action, or 2 actions if a character shouldn’t be able to perform it three times per round.

  • If you’re not sure what action a task uses, look for the most similar basic action.

  • When two sides are opposed, have one roll against the other’s DC. Don’t have both sides roll (initiative is the exception to this rule). The character who should roll is the one acting, except in the case of saving throws.

  • If something a character does raises or lowers the chances of success, grant a +1 circumstance bonus or a –1 circumstance penalty.

  • If you don’t know what check to use for something a hero is attempting, pick the most appropriate skill.

  • When a hero accomplishes something noteworthy that doesn’t have already give XP, award them XP for a minor or moderate accomplishment (10 to 30 XP).

  • When the heroes fail at a task, look for a way they might fail forward, meaning the story moves forward with a negative consequence rather than the failure halting progress entirely.

Ending a Session

It’s best to have a planned end time before your session starts. As your game goes on, keep an eye on the time. When you have around 20 minutes left in your session, start looking for good stopping places. Unless you’re finishing up an adventure, try to find a good cliffhanger to end on. This can be just before a fight starts, the moment the heroes find out a new piece of information or enter a new area, or any other point that creates suspense! Alternatively, a moment of respite just before returning to the adventure can create a feeling of anticipation for the next session!

Before everybody leaves, have them tally up their XP. They’ll need to level up before the next session if it’s over 1,000! The characters can also divide treasure and items.

Before your next session, you might need to prepare for the next stage of the adventure. If the adventure concluded this session, talk with the players about whether they want to start a new adventure. If so, start preparing the next adventure for your upcoming session!

Exploration.name: Exploration
Exploration.text:
Between encounters, the heroes often explore dungeons or other environments. Time is more flexible during exploration than in encounters and is measured in 10-minute intervals or more. You tell the players what happens, and you can skip over any parts of their travels that aren’t interesting!

As the group explores, describe the sights, sounds, and sensations. Encourage the other players to have their heroes truly explore, and reward their curiosity. The things they try to do in exploration mode show you what they’re interested in and what they consider important. As you play, you should get a good feel for what intrigues certain players, and you can add more of those things to your adventures or emphasize these points in published adventures.

Set a Party Order

When the group starts exploring, let the players decide among themselves where in the group their heroes are while exploring. This order can determine who gets attacked first when enemies or traps threaten from various directions. It’s up to you to determine the specifics of who gets targeted based on the situation.

When an encounter starts, the group usually remains in the same general formation. With the heroes’ input, decide their positions when you put the pawns on the grid. If they get the drop on their enemies or detect a hazard in advance, they can move around as they see fit before dealing with it.

Exploration Activities

Exploration Activities While the party explores, each player who wants to do something beyond just traveling chooses an exploration activity for their character. Players usually choose from the default activities, but there’s no need for them to memorize the exploration activities and use them exactly. Instead, allow each player to describe what their character does. Then as the GM, you can determine which activity applies.

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.IE2nThCmoyhQA0Jn]{Avoid Notice}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Yb0C1uLzeHrVLl7a]{Detect Magic}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.JuqmIAnkL9hVGai8]{Hustle}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigate}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kV3XM0YJeS2KCSOb]{Scout}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.fJImDBQfqfjKJOhk]{Sense Direction}

  • @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Track}

Activities like Detect Magic, Investigate, and Search can tip off a player that something is odd about an area. But that doesn’t mean they know exactly what it is! Instead, use these as a starting point for a roleplaying scene. For instance, if a character finds something magical with detect magic, the party likely still needs to stop and look at the surroundings in more detail to figure out what it is.

Similarly, if a character got a 22 on their Perception check to Search while traveling through an area containing a trap that needs a DC 20 to detect it, you should tell the player that their character noticed a trap in the area, and you can give a rough idea of the trap’s location and nature. The party needs to stop and examine the area more to learn specifics about the trap.

Improvising New Activities

If a player wants to do something not on the list of exploration activities above, you can let them if they could reasonably do it while walking around. If the activity is similar to an action someone could use in an encounter, it usually consists of a single action repeated roughly 10 times per minute. You might find that a player wants to do something equivalent to spending 3 actions every 6 seconds (18 times per minute), just like they would in combat. However, heroes can’t maintain that level of exertion in exploration mode without getting exhausted. They can do so in combat only because combat lasts such a short time.

Environments

Exploration gets slower or harder when the party faces dense jungles, deep snow, sandstorms, extreme heat, or similar conditions. You decide how much these factors impact the heroes’ progress. The specific effects of certain types of terrain and weather are described starting on.

Hazards

Exploration can get broken up by traps and other hazards (see @UUID[.mkx3KE2OFwg7vOlm]{Hazards}). Most hazards, like the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.menace-under-otari-bestiary.Actor.2XOgNOupUBGr6K6S]{falling shelves} in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.Y3qqpMInXdFsr58a]{Temple of the Unlit Star}, pose a threat to the heroes only once and can be dealt with in exploration mode without needing to start an encounter. Heroes have a better chance to detect hazards while exploring if they use the Search exploration activity.

Rolling Initiative

An encounter starts with rolling for initiative, and you’re the one who calls for the roll! Players each roll for their characters, and you roll for their enemies. Call for the roll as soon as two opposing groups come into contact or when a creature on one side decides to take action against the other. Here are some examples:

A group of heroes are exploring a cavern. They enter a narrow passage patrolled by a group of hostile goblin warriors. Now that the two groups are in the same area, it’s time to roll initiative.

Amiri and Sajan are attempting to break open a cage to free captives while Lem and Seoni sneak along to spy on kobold guards taking a break in a guard room. The guards haven’t noticed the heroes, but they arm themselves to go back on patrol. Lem decides to launch a surprise attack from hiding. As soon as he says this is his plan, you call for initiative, letting Lem and Seoni use Stealth for their initiative!

Character Placement

When calling for initiative for an encounter, you also need to decide where the participants in the encounter go on the battle map. Use the party’s traveling order as a starting point. You can move forward heroes who are using Stealth to get into position, placing them where they could reasonably have moved before they had a chance to be detected. Consult with each player to make sure their position makes sense to both of you.

Difficulty Classes.name: Difficulty Classes
Difficulty Classes.text:
As the Game Master, it’s up to you to set the difficulty classes (DCs) for checks that don’t already say what the DC is. Most adventures include the most important DCs in them, but the players will improvise and try things the adventure writer didn’t think of! Always base the DC on how hard the task is, regardless of how good at it the heroes are. Sometimes the players will attempt something that’s really easy for them, and that’s okay!

If the DC is for something with a level, like a spell or item, see Level-Based DCs below. In other cases, select a simple DC from the table below by estimating which proficiency rank best matches the task (that rank isn’t required to succeed at the task, just used for guidance).

  • If pretty much any person would have a decent chance, use the untrained DC (DC 10).

  • If anyone with some training has a solid chance, use the trained DC (DC 15).

  • If someone has to be highly skilled, use the expert DC (DC 20).

  • If this task is highly unlikely for a hero to be able to achieve, use the master DC (DC 30).

When you’re determining a skill DC based on something that has a level or rank, such as when a hero needs to Recall Knowledge about a creature or Identify a Spell, use a level-based DC. Find the level of the subject on the table, and assign the corresponding DC. Creatures and spells use different scales, so make sure you use the correct column.

You can further customize the DC as described under Adjusting Difficulty below.

Adjusting Difficulty

You might decide a DC should differ from the baseline. For instance, maybe when the heroes reached a cliff, they climbed it with a DC of 15, but when they came back, it was raining. You could adjust the DC up to 17 because it’s harder to climb in these conditions. Similarly, conditions could make a check easier and lower the DC.
