An exhaustive search of the items strewn on the floor takes 10 minutes of Searching, after which the PCs can gather together all of the items of value left behind, including four daggers, a mace, a breastplate bearing the heraldry of the Knights of Ozem, a leather bandolier containing several broken vials and three unbroken vials of holy water, and a smooth, cloudy gray stone that’s strangely warm to the touch.

This final item is a last word stone and the item Jakivi asked the PCs to recover from Relaph. If the PCs learn how to activate it (requiring a @Check[religion|dc:18|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check or @Check[arcana|dc:20|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[nature|dc:20|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], or @Check[occultism|dc:20|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic}) and replay the memory stored in it, they experience emotions of resignation and sadness along with a brief image of Relaph wishing his family and Jakivi long, fruitful lives as he prepares to buy his allies time to escape by holding the line against an advancing armored skeleton.

Reward

Later, if the PCs return the last word stone to Jakivi, he tears up and is thankful—grant the PCs 80 XP.

Feeding Mound.name: Feeding Mound
Feeding Mound.text:
An unsettling pile of corpses, all of them emaciated boars with unusually large fangs, stands in an inglorious heap in the center of this cavern.

If a PC @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Tracks} in this room, a @Check[survival|dc:20|options:action:track|name:PF2E.Actions.Track.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check is enough to see the tracks from area @UUID[.fCkeTfUR9gPzVP3H]{A5} led here, only to be caught in some sort of scuffle with several things that left barefoot tracks, after which two sets of barefoot tracks led south while several others seem to head back to the eastern part of the cave. (Ecaterina was overwhelmed and knocked unconscious by this chamber’s ghoul denizens, and two of these ghouls then brought her deeper into the tunnels.)

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.o4ggs2JHTn1RwA7j]{Ghoul Stalkers x4}

The ghouls who survived their clash with the invading gauntlings in the room to the west relocated here to recover. They managed to scavenge a few of their fallen foes as they fled, and gathered their corpses into a pile to let the meat age until it was more properly palatable to their decay-addicted tongues. The first time the PCs enter this chamber, the ghouls have just begun their awaited feast, and are gathered around the dead gauntlings, discussing with unnerving decorum and grace which parts of the decaying porcines might prove the most detectable.

The ghouls don’t take kindly to the PCs interrupting their meal, as they’ve waited more than long enough to feed. They spit and snarl as soon as they notice the party, with one musing aloud that the aged meat of a “proper humanoid” would make a lovely gift for “the Primarch.” They attack at once and fight until they’re destroyed. If the PCs look like they’re about to flee, the ghouls try to herd them south to area @UUID[.qcSD4ZwhjSGO4KEG]{A7}, where they might be attacked by the leashed gauntlings.

Impromptu Kennel.name: Impromptu Kennel
Impromptu Kennel.text:
This large chamber has a high ceiling, one that stretches twenty feet above the moist, warm floor. Stone footers and other foundational elements of the town above peek through the stalactites in the ceiling. The air in this cavern smells a bit rank and sour—not quite of decaying meat, but not far from it.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.rQqEjKlfSBfvDcGj]{Gauntlings x2}

Creatures: When the sinkhole collapsed, four of the gauntlings were knocked out rather than slain, and the surviving ghouls dragged them here and tethered them to stalagmites along the western wall with lengths of old chain, intending to keep them alive for now so that they could either be used as guardians or kept food for later. At about the time the PCs first enter the dungeon, two of the gauntlings escaped and have made their way further into the dungeon (see area @UUID[.a3DjkR1v5KOHBoyB]{A9}), but the other two remain alert, hungry, and cranky. Their chains prevent them from being able to reach those who move through the room while remaining adjacent to the eastern wall, but they can attack anyone else in the area.

The gauntlings fight to the death, although a PC who wishes to set one loose from a chain can do so with a @Check[athletics|dc:18] check. Each time a gauntling is freed, attempt a @Check[flat|dc:15] check. On a failure, the gauntling flees into the deeper caves, but on a success the creature remains to fight to the death.

Sprung Leak.name: Sprung Leak
Sprung Leak.text:
This corridor bends counterclockwise from a southwestern entrance up toward a northeastern exit. The corridor varies from ten feet wide in some parts up to twenty-five feet, but is never more than ten feet tall, even as the ground slopes downward slightly as the corridor traverses east. Old, rotten wooden supports haphazardly shore up the southern walls, yet where the shoring has broken or crumbled over time, the waters from the Path River have begun to trickle into the chamber. The southern half of the tunnel is flooded getting up to five-feet deep in the southeastern corner. Only three feet of rubble from the ceiling of the tunnel that has fallen into three-foot piles near the northern entrance has thus far kept the waters from flowing into the other chambers to the beyond.

The first thing the PCs need to contend with in this room is the dangerous denizen who lurks in the waters along the southern wall—see “Creatures” below. Once this inhabitant is dealt with, a PC who spends 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EwgTZBWsc8qKaViP]{Investigating} this room and then succeeds at a @Check[type:engineering-lore|dc:18|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits::concentrate,exploration,secret] or @Check[mining-lore|dc:18|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits::concentrate,exploration,secret] check or a @Check[type:crafting|dc:20|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits::concentrate,exploration,secret] check realizes that not only is this area’s current shoring faltering, suggesting that a full-on flood from the Path River is imminent. Such an event could result in a much larger and far more devastating sinkhole. Fortunately, “imminent” in this case still leaves time for the townsfolk above to get to work repairing the leak here—as long as the engineer or the PCs report this leak to the authorities, a greater sinkhole catastrophe can be avoided. If the PCs say nothing, the timing of when this larger disaster strikes central Grayce is left to you to decide.

Once the PCs reach the bend in this area, they can clearly hear the sounds of battle from area @UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.a3DjkR1v5KOHBoyB]{A9} to the north.

Encounter

Trivial 3

@UUID[Actor.OYBkVqJA95V3J1WG]

Creatures: A couple of narrow, twisting, submerged tunnels lead further west underwater from this area— tunnels that can be discovered by PCs who spend 10 minutes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searching} underwater and succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:20|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to locate. These tunnels are narrow and dangerous to traverse for anything other than Tiny creatures. Small creatures can navigate them by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeezing} with a @Check[acrobatics|dc:25|options:action:squeeze|name:PF2E.Actions.Squeeze.Title|traits:exploration,move] check, but larger creatures can’t navigate them at all.

It’s merely a @Check[athletics|dc:10|options:action:swim|name:PF2E.Actions.Swim.Title|traits:move] check to swim in the water. While these tunnels aren’t a great option for most PCs to travel through, they’re no big deal for animals

While these tunnels aren’t a great option for most PCs to travel through, they’re no big deal for animals like fish—the sort of prey that lured a much more dangerous creature in here only a few hours before the PCs entered the caves.

This creature is a giant dragonfly nymph—an aquatic predator that has taken a liking to the narrow channel of water it’s found here after chasing some fish through the tunnels. The three-foot-long insect lurks at the southernmost point of the water’s edge, ready to attack most creatures who come within five feet by Extending its Mandibles out of the water to bite at passing food. (The giant dragonfly nymph won’t attack creatures that are undead—or that “smell” undead adjacent, such as a gauntling; some PC ancestries might qualify as smelling in such a way!) The giant dragonfly nymph pursues PCs onto land if they retreat from the water’s edge, but won’t chase them beyond this area, in which case it retreats to the water to hide again. If reduced to fewer than 15 Hit Points, the giant dragonfly nymph loses interest in its new home and flees back into the river—in this event, it does not return to the caves.

Reward

If the PCs determine the danger here and report to the authorities, grant the party 120 XP.

Cairn Court.name: Cairn Court
Cairn Court.text:
This massive chamber is different than the rest of the tunnels so far. Here, the rough natural caverns are left behind for walls cut roughly but more or less squarely from solid stone. These rough-hewn walls and flagstone floors speak of the technique of this chamber, but the rows of stone coffins below glowing stones reveal its intent as some sort of crypt. A shattered coffin lies in ruins amid the bones of whoever once rested at the far end of the western row. To the north, a shallow flight of stone steps lead upward to a smaller room.

This large chamber is decorated with unadorned coffins lining each wall, each dragged here by ghouls from various other locations in the region to serve as food stores.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.rQqEjKlfSBfvDcGj]{Gauntling x2} @UUID[Actor.o4ggs2JHTn1RwA7j]{Ghoul Stalker x4}

Creatures: The first time the PCs approach this room, they find it to be the scene of a clash between several ghouls and a pair of furious gauntlings—the two gauntlings who escaped from area @UUID[.qcSD4ZwhjSGO4KEG]{A7} have found their way here. The gauntlings have each taken some damage, but there are three destroyed ghouls on the floor already, leaving only four to continue the fight. If the PCs do nothing but watch, you can either play out the combat normally, giving the party chances to intervene when they wish, or you can simply rule that the gauntlings manage to finish off the ghouls before they turn on the PCs anyway (at which point each gauntling is down to 30 HP).

If the PCs join the gauntlings in battle against the ghouls, the gauntlings attack them as well as soon as the ghouls are destroyed, showing no indication of gratitude for the aid in battle.

If the PCs aid the ghouls in killing the gauntlings though, any surviving ghouls hold up their hands to offer a truce, assuming that no PC attacked a ghoul during the fight. If the PCs agree to a truce, the ghouls say that they think they caused the sinkhole during a larger fight against the full group of invading gauntlings, and “for what it’s worth, we didn’t intend to make a mess of things like that. Beside, it only might’ve been us. There’s a group of gremlins in the tunnels too, and they’ve been making a lot of noise.” Causing a sinkhole, the ghouls realize, forces their hand—they would have been content to continue living secretly and continuing to feed off of Grayce’s dead (and, perhaps, a few extra snacks snatched from the streets after dark now and then). They promise to leave the tunnels in thanks for the PCs’ mercy, but note that they can’t make the same promises for their leaders who dwell further inside. If the PCs press for more information, the ghouls look nervously to each other before one points up the stairs and says, “You should head up there and chat with Krethark. He knows more about what’s going on than we do!”

If the PCs attack both the gauntlings and the ghouls, the resulting free-for-all would technically be beyond a Severe 3 encounter, but with the foes already wounded and certainly with some focusing on each other rather than the PCs, the threat level of this encounter is lower.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.XkpEb1KXn3iFE3mP]

Most of the coffins lining the walls of the crypt are empty save for a few scattered bones and old, broken armor and weapons. Inside a few coffins, the PCs can find the following scattered among the bones: bracers of missile deflection, +1 handwraps of mighty blows, a staff of fire, and a +1 striking spear. The shattered coffin in the corner of the room once held the body of a lower-ranking officer from the Shining Crusade. His bones tangle the suit of full plate armor he wears, and a symbol of conflict is still worn around the officer’s neck.

Reward

If the PCs make a truce with the ghouls and get them to leave, grant them XP as if they’d defeated them in combat. If the PCs simply sit back and watch the ghouls and gauntlings fight, they only earn XP for the victorious gauntlings they face soon thereafter.

Mausoleum Entrance.name: Mausoleum Entrance
Mausoleum Entrance.text:
At the top of this wide stairwell, a fifteen-foot-wide stone archway carved with the images of frolicking skeletons affords passage into a rectangular room. Six tall, thick granite pillars line the sides of the entryway to the east and west, holding up a ceiling nearly two stories above. A stone double door inlaid with metal spiral shapes closed beyond the entryway, although the inlaid spirals have been hacked and scratched and damaged by unskilled hands with crude tools.

Any PC who’s at least trained in Religion or succeeds at a @Check[type:religion|dc:10] check recognizes the spiral symbols as the religious symbol of Pharasma. On a critical success, they note that the symbols likely once served as an anchor of sorts for some sort of minor magical effect meant to ward off undead creatures, and that the damage to the symbols has destroyed this effect. (Indeed, these symbols once exuded a fearful aura intended to frighten off undead, but the areas’ recent intruders managed to withstand these effects to deface the protection, ruining it.) Should the PCs wish to restore these symbols, it’ll take time and resources, but the reward might be worth it—see “@UUID[.Og6H4tSPjkNE5hJP]{Restoring the Mausoleum}” at the end of this chapter.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.gHEJR7R7CYBmG315]{Krethark}

Creatures: An old, lanky-framed bugbear ghoul named Krethark sits quietly to the east, leaning against the central pillar as he listens with passive interest to the sounds of combat and the PCs exploring in area @UUID[.a3DjkR1v5KOHBoyB]{A9}. Once the PCs move up into this area, he greets them: “Sounds like you’ve just come from one battle below. Are you planning to start another so soon?” The armored ghoul waits patiently for an answer, the threat implied in his tone. If the PCs attack, the ghoul sighs in what almost sounds like boredom, and as he stands up to join the fight, he says, “As you wish. Not sure which of you I’ll eat first.” In combat, Krethark fights until destroyed, hoping that if he can win this battle he’ll find treasures and items among the PCs’ remains that might help him regain his position of power here in the tunnels.

If the PCs hold off an attack, though, Krethark invites them to be seated and join him in a short bit of resting before they move on deeper into the chambers beyond. Krethark is tired, worn down, and still recovering mentally from a clash a few months ago that cost him the primacy over the local ghouls. If the PCs agree to rest and chat, he draws the surprisingly ornate bastard sword off his back and sets it on the ground next to him as he speaks. With a hoarse, gruff voice, he introduces himself as Krethark and apologizes that he can’t be more cordial, noting with a bitter lilt that, while he bought this group of ghouls together, they’ve turned their back on him and he is no longer their Primarch.

Krethark begins this encounter indifferent to the PCs. If the PCs can make him @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v66R7FdOf11l94im]{Friendly} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful} by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Making an Impression} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coercing} him, the ghoul agrees to answer a few of their questions without expecting answers from them in turn. Otherwise, before he’ll answer any questions the PCs pose him, he’ll demand they answer one of his. Krethark’s questions run along the lines of “Who are you?”, “Why have you come down here?”, “Do you intend to wipe us all out?”, “Have you ever tried the flesh of your kin?”, and “Wouldn’t you find it less complicated living down here than up above?” If at any point the PCs grow abusive or insulting, he grumbles in annoyance before sweeping up his sword and rising to attack.

Likely questions the PCs might pose Krethark and his answers to the same are given below.

Who are you?

“As I said, my name’s Krethark. Once, this name drew terrified screams and frightened oaths from the rangers of Fangwood. But in death, I’ve becoming something far more terrifying than a bully backed by higher-ranking bullies, and something far more productive, I think. I gathered a family—my little cadre of ghouls—and led them as Primarch for decades before I was challenged and defeated by an usurper who was once my ward. He claims to value my input and keeps me around as a ‘voice of experience.’ But I am tired. My dusk awaits.”

Have you seen the civil engineer from up above come this way?

He sighs heavily. “Yes. Ecaterina, she is called. Our hunters found her soon after the exit to the sinkhole collapsed, then brought her here. With proper time to ripen, she would have made a tasty meal, but our Primarch seems to have other plans for her. And no, I’m not sure what those plans are. If she still lives, she’ll be in his den.”

How did the ghouls find their way into the tunnels beneath Grayce?

“The Primarch led us here. We had been stalking a pack of gauntlings—beasts who fed upon undeath. This makes the meat tastier and requires less time after death to age into deliciousness. Where they went, we could always find food. It was a good plan. They led us here, through caverns from the river, but then they turned on us and attacked. The fight caused a cave in, as you noted. Now that we’re here, under your town, our Primarch plots a way to settle in. A goal that I fear will inevitably put us in a clash against those above... but what do I know? I’m no longer in charge.”

Who is the Primarch?

“He is called Alendreu. He was a dungeon delver on the borders of Belkzen and Ustalav before joining our family. Always knew how to find the best food or prey underground and one of the strongest combatants I’d ever faced, and I was a bugbear. But his real strength has always been in planning. Long before he challenged me to lead our family, he was my best advisor. I knew long ago, it was only a matter of time before he took my place. And then, just a few months ago, he did. He’s the reason we’re here, under your homes, today.”

Were you the one who defaced the symbols of Pharasma here?

“Nope, but I’m glad they’re ruined. The Primarch destroyed them so that he and his minions could come and go without fear. I would have done it myself, but he’s the boss now. Let him deal with that sort of stuff, I say!”

Once the PCs have asked their questions, or as soon as the PCs ask him to describe what sorts of defenses and chamber layout they can expect beyond the doors, Krethark sighs in resignation as he picks up his sword and then puts himself between the PCs and the door to area @UUID[.2h5yLNynxsnsJkCK]{A11}, but what he does next depends on his attitude at this point in the encounter.

If the PCs had managed to make him friendly or helpful via Making an Impression, he lifts the makeshift bar from the door to let them pass, giving them the following final words of advice: “Be careful past these doors. Alendreu will be in the crypt he’s taken as a throne room along with your engineer. But before that, you’ll meet Carexilia and her lackeys. Carexilia has no love for Alendreu, especially now that he’s abandoned his plans to let that Ecaterina woman live. If Carexilia wasn’t planning to turn on him before, she is now.”

If he remains indifferent (or worse) or if the PCs Coerced him, Krethark’s patience finally wears out as he takes his stand between the PCs and the door. He tells them that it’d be best for them to return to the town above, and to report that their engineer is lost. If they persist, he nods in resignation and attacks.

In battle, Krethark tries to shove any obvious spellcasters down the stairs before jumping into combat with the largest of his foes. He seeks to bring down his foes one at a time, spreading fear with his sword as best he can. If he’s been forced into combat, he prioritizes his duty to guard the vault entrance, and fights until destroyed.

Reward

Krethark’s bastard sword is exceedingly ornate, with a scratched-out symbol of Iomedae on the pommel. From the description the PCs were given, this is Jakivi Rindix’s lost blade, Inheritor’s Kiss. If the PCs return this weapon to Jakivi, grant them 40 XP.

If the PCs convince Krethark to let them pass, they earn XP as if they’d defeated him in battle, but securing the blade from him requires combat, as the ghoul won’t give up “his sword” without a fight.

Prayer Chamber.name: Prayer Chamber
Prayer Chamber.text:
If not for the distant sound of music emanating from the golden double doors to the east, this prayer chamber of granite and marble would grasp silence like a shroud. To the north, a wide, shallow staircase leads up a few feet before being blocked by boulders and piles of ancient fallen brickwork and statuary. The room’s polished black granite floors still shine despite the age, and sculpted images in relief on the alabaster and granite walls depict scenes of battle dating back to the Shining Crusade. To the west, a broken statue of a warrior goddess lies beside the pedestal she once stood upon.

A PC who’s trained in Religion, or anyone who succeeds at a @Check[type:religion|dc:10|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Recall Knowledge, interprets the fragments of the broken statue to have once depicted Iomedae from the Shining Crusade era, before she became a goddess, but a critical success on that Religion check notes that, in fact, this statue once depicted Arazni, and that it was modified some years after its sculpting to depict Iomedae instead. The statue had been destroyed long before the ghouls arrived, yet another victim to neglect and the passage of time. If the PCs wish to restore this statue, they can do so, but it’ll take time and resources—see “Restoring the Mausoleum” at the end of this chapter.

The 15-foot-high ceiling causes every whisper to echo in the spartan chamber, but the sounds of fiddles and other string instruments from the ornate golden double doors to the north hide most sounds, causing all hearing-based Perception checks attempted in this room to gain a –1 circumstance penalty.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.BQIJAzrLVCvv2yQE] @UUID[Actor.o4ggs2JHTn1RwA7j]{Ghoul Stalkers x2}

Creatures: A trio of ghouls hunker down in the center of this chamber, arguing in loud whispers as to how best to deal with the occupants behind the golden doors. The one in charge is Carexilia, a ghoul with obvious elven features. As soon as they notice the PCs, she silences the others with a glare before turning to face the party with a mask of hunger splayed across her face.

If the PCs parted ways with Krethark peacefully and he opened the doors to admit them into the prayer chamber, Carexilia and her ghoulish companions are willing to parlay with the PCs, yet are initially @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fuG8dgthlDWfWjIA]{Indifferent} to them. If the PCs can make them friendly or helpful by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Making an Impression} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coercing} them, Carexilia reveals that she intends to overtake the Primarch and his guards, and asks the PCs to aid her in this task. She’d rather not give up Ecaterina, and if the PCs don’t mention the engineer in their discussion, Carexilia gleefully assumes that she gets to keep the delicious looking elf for an upcoming meal, which likely just delays a fight with her and the other dissidents. If the PCs do mention her, Carexilia begrudgingly allows them to leave with Ecaterina after the Primarch’s been defeated, but only if Carexilia’s been made @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful} will she consent to also letting the PCs leave with the treasure found in area @UUID[.TLMokELKdcgGMQom]{A12}.

If the PCs found Carexilia’s lost journal in area @UUID[JournalEntry.3JAT7L3gkSo6nBVw.JournalEntryPage.l9NTQyXqw9xjtC3X]{A4} and hand it over to her, the ghoul is delighted to have her missing property returned, and her attitude shifts one step closer toward helpful.

Carexilia and her two ghoul lackeys are quick to attack if Krethark did not let the PCs into the chamber, or if the PCs try and fail to improve their attitudes better than indifferent. Carexilia begins combat by casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4GE2ZdODgIQtg51c]{Darkness}, then attempts to engage lightly armored opponents from an advantageous position to make best use of her sneak attacks. She’s eager to spread her ghoul whispers to anyone she grabs onto, if only to entice them to eventually join her side. The other two ghouls engage with individual foes, prioritizing spellcasters before moving on to martial targets. If at all possible, they flank their opponents with Carexilia to impress their (hopefully) next Primarch. These ghouls have no choice but to fight to the bitter end.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.CFnc0oe61ddXRnZ7]

Although the statue of Arazni was destroyed long ago, a hidden stash of sacred tools remains tucked away behind a secret panel at the base of the pedestal the statue once stood upon. A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} this pedestal or the statue, or who spends at least 10 minutes Searching the room as a whole, can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:20||options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to notice the hidden panel. Within are two scrolls (a 3rd-rank scroll of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction} and a scroll of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.3x6eUCm17n6ROzUa]{Crisis of Faith}) and a channel protection amulet. If the PCs later take the time to rebuild this statue, they’ll automatically discover this hidden stash of treasure as part of that activity.

Reward

If the PCs recruit Carexilia and the other ghouls to aid in the conflict in area @UUID[.TLMokELKdcgGMQom]{A12}, grant the party 40 XP. If they manage later on to avoid a betrayal from Carexilia and leave the dungeon without fighting her or her two allies, grant them XP as if they’d defeated them in combat.

Primarch's Den.name: Primarch's Den
Primarch's Den.text:
This large round room has white granite floors with milled accents in burnished gold. The pale white walls stretch nearly fifteen feet in height, rising to a domed ceiling some twenty feet above. Six ornate stone sarcophagi are arranged around the room, divided by vases and plinths that display sculptures of the knights likely interred within. Above each sarcophagus, an image of the knight’s deeds in battle are sculpted into the white marble walls. One sarcophagus, just to the left of the couch on the northern wall, has been opened and the occupant removed, replaced by linens and pillows. A large round red and gold rug fills the center of the room, accentuating the lush oxblood-colored velvet couch and statue on the northern end of the room. The statue depicts a stern, but triumphant human warrior who overlooks the room like a protector.

The contents of the unopened sarcophagi have been left alone by the ghouls once they determined that the bodies within are little more than dusty bones barren of the rotten meat that they find so delicious. The souls of the knights buried here have long since been judged and moved on to the afterlife, leaving no haunting echo within, but the ghouls’ mere presence in the area has defiled the once sacred place. If the PCs wish to restore it, see the end of the chapter.

Encounter

Severe 3

@UUID[Actor.vSy35m79dshCwgL4] @UUID[Actor.o4ggs2JHTn1RwA7j]{Ghoul Stalkers x3} @UUID[Actor.XZgxBZE9hquKCnLR]

Creatures: The music that fills this room is provided by a trio of violin-playing ghouls loyal to Primarch Alendreu, who reclines with style atop the velvet couch. Ecaterina has been chained to the statue, her expression stony and defiant with an undercurrent of fear. As he notices the PCs, Alendreu sits up on the couch with a leer on his lips, then glances over to Ecaterina. “We have guests, my friend!” he exclaims as Ecaterina breathes an obvious sigh of relief at what she hopes are her rescuers arriving. “There are guests in my throne room!” Alendreu continues as he rises from the couch, at which point the three ghouls cease their violin playing to regard at their visitors with narrowed eyes. The three ghoul stalkers slink to the sides of the couch while the Primarch opens his arms wide in welcome, gives an unwholesome smile, and says, “Please come in. I am Alendreu, and you are guests here in my hall.” As he stands, he picks up a pair of thick-bladed orc necksplitter axes and smiles a hungry grin at his captive to make sure the menace in his voice was properly displayed.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seeks} Ecaterina and succeeds at a @Check[medicine|dc:18] check notes that she has several bloody wounds to her neck and shoulder, as well as a swollen ankle. None of these are life threatening by themselves, but her wounds could prove a larger issue if not treated soon.

Primarch Alendreu is a large, muscular orc ghoul who wears fashionable black leathers and violet dyed padded armor with gold accents. He speaks with the smug candor of a wealthy noble, and is cordial to the PCs, even if they’re accompanied by Carexilia and her ghouls. He at least suspects she’s been plotting to usurp him, and takes her presence with the PCs as proof.

Of course, the PCs are free to interrupt Alendreu’s grandstanding at any moment to attack him, but if they hold back long enough for him to finish introducing himself, they have a chance to keep him talking for a bit. Any PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:15|options:action:sense-motive|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive} can tell that the ghoul is enjoying the attention for the moment but fully intends to attack soon. Any PC who wishes to speak to Alendreu before then can choose to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce} Alendreu by attempting a @Check[deception|dc:22|options:action:lie|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret], @Check[diplomacy|dc:22|options:action:make-an-impression|name:PF2E.Actions.MakeAnImpression.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental], or @Check[intimidation|dc:22|options:action:coerce|name:PF2E.Actions.Coerce.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] check. On a success, a PC can Stride once to move into a more advantageous position in the room if they wish, and when combat begins, they can opt to use that same skill for initiative, but with a +2 circumstance bonus. If even one PC manages to keep Alendreu talking, you can use the opportunity to explain how the ghouls came to the tunnels or (possibly) caused the sinkhole if the PCs haven’t learned this information already. Alendreu can also speak to how, initially, the ghouls had intended to kill Ecaterina and eat her in a few days once she ripened, but that he decided to keep her alive for the moment to learn what he could about her knowledge of engineering (noting that “sometimes people forget things when they awaken as ghouls”), so that when the Whispering Tyrant makes his inevitable return to power, Alendreu will be ready to offer his new wisdom and skills to aid the lich.

Once you decide Alendreu’s had enough, give the players a chance to decide if they wish to attack. If they want to continue speaking, they’ll lose any circumstance bonuses to initiative they earned (but can still opt to roll initiative using the Charisma-based check they made) as Alendreu says, “But enough about that. I know why you think you’re here, but really? You’re just here to be food.” If the PCs let him get this far, he rolls Intimidation for initiative; otherwise, he rolls Perception.

Once combat begins, Alendreu targets the strongest looking PC in a roared challenge, leaping into melee with them to best use Double Slice. His ghoul minions harry spellcasters first—particularly any who use vitality spells to damage the ghouls. So long as Alendreu remains active, his ghouls fight to the death. If Alendreu is destroyed, any of the remaining ghouls panic and flee.

If Carexilia and her ghouls are here to provide aid to the PCs, they follow the party’s lead in battle, but if at any point Alendreu appears to be on his last leg, Carexilia eagerly tries to swoop in to deliver the destroying blow—moving in near Alendreu in a way that allows the ghoul primarch a chance to use a Reactive Strike against her.

If Carexilia is still alive at the end of the fight, any remaining ghoul stalkers immediately accept her as their new leader, and at her command, they immediately attack the PCs along with her. Only if the PCs managed to make her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v66R7FdOf11l94im]{Friendly} without Coercing her does she allow them to leave, alive, with Ecaterina—and only if they made her @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.v44P3WUcU1j0115l]{Helpful} will she allow them to loot Alendreu of his treasures. If Carexilia doesn’t betray the PCs, she’s pragmatic enough to know that the people of Grayce won’t abide ghouls living below them, and claims that she’ll gather the rest of the surviving ghouls and lead them out of the tunnels to somewhere far away from Grayce. Whether or not she’s earnest in this promise, or whether she simply finds deeper and more defensible tunnels below town to move into, is left to you to decide.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.8IMUvwd4lpuaNVrs]

Ecaterina’s belongings (other than the tattered fragments of her destroyed explorer’s clothing) lie in a heap on the ground to the side of the couch furthest from where she was kept chained up. This gear consists of a +1 dagger, a sterling engineer’s toolkit (treat as a sterling artisan’s toolkit that grants a +1 item bonus to Engineering Lore checks), a hooded lantern, a superb repair toolkit, and a writing set. If she’s rescued, Ecaterina gives the PCs her magic dagger as thanks.

Reward

If the PCs manage to rescue Ecaterina and get her back to Grayce, grant the PCs 80 XP.

Concluding the Adventure.name: Concluding the Adventure
Concluding the Adventure.text:
Once the PCs defeat the ghouls and free Ecaterina, returning to the surface is a simple task—even with the civil engineer’s broken ankle. She emphatically recommends not moving the rubble blocking the stairs up toward the graveyard from area @UUID[.2h5yLNynxsnsJkCK]{A11} if the PCs suggest it, but instead suggests reinforcing the blockage with mortar and brisk walls on the outside. She also notes with grave concern the leaking wall at area @UUID[.F28hpu3yHyq9l97E]{A8} as they pass by. Once back above, if the PCs didn’t learn the cause of the sinkhole, she can explain to the head council and Jakivi what caused the devastation.

Ecaterina comes up with two solid plans to keep any further incursions from coming up. The first—and easiest— plan is to close up and fully seal any remaining entrances to the tunnels from Grayce, and to destroy any remaining structures shoring up the tunnel walls. This would allow the Path’s waters to fill the tunnels and keep any ghouls, gremlins, or even the bear creatures from coming into the town. It would, however, require great effort to reinforce the foundations of most of the buildings in Grayce to prevent the sinkhole, and the lake that would form inside it, from claiming the town proper, not to mention the problems this plan causes with well water and irrigation for the fields.

The second option (and her preferred solution) is to send a team below, under guard, to reinforce the shoring (particularly in area @UUID[.F28hpu3yHyq9l97E]{A8}) and make more permanent structures to protect the substructure. The sinkhole should be filled in with dirt and stone quarried from the surrounding hills, and she suggests planting trees throughout the town square, noting that tree roots will further help to reinforce and strengthen the ground. The Synerina eagerly takes any advice the PCs have as well, but ultimately the choice they make will have little impact on the upcoming troubles in Grayce.

If the PCs don’t come up with the idea to restore the mausoleum on their own, Ecaterina mentions that this might help as well, since bolstering the spiritual defenses of the tunnels can certainly help just as much (if not more) in keeping the tunnels safe and free from monstrous infestations. See @UUID[.Og6H4tSPjkNE5hJP]{“Restoring the Mausoleum”} for more details on this longer-term project.

You can have Ecaterina decide to travel with the PCs on an upcoming adventure, although she won’t choose to do so while the situation below Grayce’s streets isn’t fully examined and reported upon to the authorities. Ecaterina isn’t a particularly potent combatant (she’s trained in unarmored defense and simple weapons only), but she can be a great help in traversing regions and areas where traps and other hazards are common. Alternatively, you can keep her in the background, and in the event the PCs are captured or defeated, she can repay the favor she owes them for her own survival by leading a rescue to get them out of danger at the very last minute.

Jakivi, in any event, is elated if the PCs manage to retrieve either the last word stone or his old blade, Inheritor’s Kiss. As he looks over his old weapon, he grimaces at the damage to the symbol of Iomedae on its pommel, but promises the sword that he will have it repaired promptly. If any of the PCs shows interest in the sword, he offers it to them as long as they promise it will join them in battle, since he suspects it wouldn’t have the chance to do so in his hand again. If presented with the stone, he introduces the PCs to his adopted wards, Nicco and Shorel Wesren (impressionable male and female human children). In a back room of the Ash Inn, he shows them how to retrieve their father’s memory from within, and thanks the PCs with rounds of drinks and promises of beds, meals, and drinks for all of them for at least a month.

Restoring the Mausoleum.name: Restoring the Mausoleum
Restoring the Mausoleum.text:
The old mausoleum the PCs explore in this adventure (consisting of areas A10–A12) date back centuries to the era of the Shining Crusade, when they were used not only to house the bodies of soldiers, but as hideouts for those seeking shelter from the advance of the Whispering Tyrant’s undead legions. This area, along with numerous other hidden sanctuaries, once bore potent wards to keep those hidden within from being discovered, but the passage of time and the blasphemous actions of intruders (most recently, the ghouls under Alendreu’s command) have eroded away these magical wards and divine protections.

While the work of shoring up the tunnels and filling in the sinkhole is mundane work best left to locals to undertake, the PCs might be uniquely situated to step in and provide additional work at restoring the mausoleum. If any of the PCs are worshippers of Pharasma, Iomedae, or Arazni, you should indicate to them that such a project could be undertaken by them and could well bolster the area’s spiritual protection against sinister influences as surely as the engineers’ work will at bolstering the tunnels from future physical collapses. Ecaterina (or another NPC of your choice) could suggest the same.

If the PCs wish to restore the mausoleum, they’ll need to undertake the following four activities. The first one must be completed first, but the remaining three can be completed in any order. Since these are all downtime activities, they can be excellent pursuits for the PCs in between adventures—they can even come back to working on the mausoleum later, and don’t have to complete all of these tasks before moving on to the next adventure in this book.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.IXuhShJXqH4Tw1cf]{Restore the Mausoleum}

  • Downtime
  • Manipulate

@Embed[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.IXuhShJXqH4Tw1cf inline]

The Disgraced Dollmaker.name: The Disgraced Dollmaker
The Disgraced Dollmaker.text:
When Thalleus Jongrim was 11 years old, he almost died. It was a fine summer day in Caliphas, and Thalleus had taken a makeshift raft to fish on Lake Encarthan. He’d watched the poorer children fish from time to time, but young Thalleus wasn’t very knowledgeable about watercraft and failed to notice the poor condition of his raft. When the vessel began to break apart, Thalleus panicked and became tangled in his fishing line. He floundered about helplessly before striking his head on a piece of debris, knocking himself unconscious.

Several minutes later, Thalleus awoke staring into the face of a passing fisherwoman, who had dived into the waters to save him. A devout Pharasmin, the fisherwoman assured Thalleus that the Lady of Graves had not yet called him to the Boneyard. Thalleus sputtered a thanks and made his way home, but in his heart, he knew that he had died and been brought back to life by some means he did not understand. From that moment on, Thalleus became fascinated with the transition between life and death.

Thalleus’s parents hired a tutor from the local church of Pharasma to answer their child’s endless questions, but it wasn’t long before Thalleus reached the limits of his teacher’s knowledge. As he grew older, Thalleus embarked upon his own research, delving into obscure occult and scientific tomes to expand his understanding further. Eventually, his parents paid to send him to the University of Lepidstadt. There, Thalleus learned about the cycle of the mortal soul and the fundamentals of life and consciousness.

But there was always more to discover. After several years of education, Thalleus realized his calling was to be an educator. The university board was intrigued by his field of expertise and hired him on as a professor. For decades, Professor Jongrim taught about the science of the soul, becoming a fixture at the school. But in between giving lectures and grading assignments, he made his own explorations into life after death. He shunned necromancy, as the old Pharasmin priests taught him, believing that there was a way to preserve a mortal soul without drawing the ire of the Lady of Graves. In a way, Thalleus discovered such a method, but his efforts led him down an arguably darker path.

Over 20 years ago, Thalleus learned about soulbound constructs—unliving forms animated by a fragment of a mortal soul—and the rituals needed to create them. While the process of making a soulbound construct requires a mortal soul, once the construct is completed, the soul can pass on to the afterlife as normal. In exchange, the soulbound construct has only a fraction of the original subject’s personality and almost none of their memories. Believing he could find a way around this limitation, Thalleus began experimenting with ways that a soulbound construct could accept nearly an entire soul, instead of only a fragment. Unfortunately, these experiments required actual souls. At first, Thalleus vowed to limit his experiments to willing subjects—usually those so ill they had no hope to live on any other way—but eventually he resorted to lying to volunteers about how fatal his experiments would be.

It took only a few years before Thalleus’s research was discovered. Rather than have the knowledge of his murders exposed to the world, the university quietly and unceremoniously dismissed him. Thalleus returned to Caliphas penniless and distraught, and several months later fell ill with an incurable disease of his own. Fearing that his death was fast approaching, Thalleus petitioned the local nobility for funding to build a home in the country, where he could live out the remainder of his days. Eventually, he was granted a property loan for a home a few miles north of the small town of Grayce. Thalleus didn’t inform his sponsors that he planned to find a way to transfer his soul into a more durable body—one made of wood and metal. So that the professor could keep the true purpose of the house a secret, multiple work crews labored in shifts to complete the construction, all of which returned to Caliphas soon thereafter.

Throughout the project, Thalleus had little contact with the people of Grayce beyond sporadic visits to town for supplies. Soon after the professor moved in, however, he began to advertise that he would take commissions for handmade dolls from the residents of Grayce and surrounding towns. After all, Thalleus needed the occasional influx of funds, as well as a cover story for his bulk orders of wood, cloth, and wire. Using the skills he’d honed over the years crafting soulbound constructs, Thalleus became known for his skills as a dollmaker, though his reputation as a recluse remained, as he hired no one from Grayce to assist him. To staff his workshop, Thalleus instead created special soulbound constructs known as automatic butlers—constructs that exhibit almost none of the donor soul’s personality—using soul focus gems he smuggled out of the university before he was dismissed.

To continue the work that would eventually save himself from death, Thalleus needed souls. He found them among the occasional travelers who stopped overnight in Grayce, and later from the refugees who fled to the town after Lastwall fell. Thalleus would quietly invite these people to stay in his house, then put them through deadly trials to prepare their souls for his experiments. If anyone asked about his guests’ whereabouts, Thalleus would claim the travelers had simply moved on.

Thalleus created many soul focus gems this way—some of which he installed into soulbound constructs—but his true aim continued to elude him. Meanwhile, his illness worsened, until he felt his life beginning to slip away around 2 years ago. In desperation, Thalleus attempted an occult ritual of his own creation to transfer his soul into an awaiting construct form. He died in the process, and as a result his soul fractured and inhabited the house’s many automatic butlers. Each butler took on a different aspect of Thalleus’s personality (displacing the soul fragment already in residence within the construct), although none had any memory of ever being Thalleus Jongrim.

Due to the remoteness of his house and his reclusive lifestyle, the people of Grayce have yet to discover that Thalleus has died. However, the professor’s old debts have finally come due.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
While the PCs were engaged in their earlier adventures, a royal decree from Caliphas arrived in Grayce. The decree states that Thalleus is years behind in payments on his property loan. As a result, Prince Aduard Ordranti III has requested the property be seized by town officials until a proper assessment can be completed. Synerina Leptinato (straightforward female human administrator 5), Grayce’s head councilor, takes the decree seriously and calls to meet with some of the most competent people she knows in town—namely, the PCs. They’ve had some successes in dealing with far more dangerous tasks, after all, so the head councilor is sure that they can handle this one.

One morning, the PCs are summoned to city hall, where Synerina tells them about the prince’s decree and shares what little she knows about Thalleus Jongrim. According to Synerina, Thalleus is an eccentric dollmaker from Caliphas who has lived outside Grayce for over a decade. Thalleus’s residence, colloquially known as the Doll House, was built specifically for him and is only a few miles away. Synerina tells the PCs that in addition to selling handcrafted dolls, Thalleus has occasionally taken in travelers and other itinerants. However, as far as she knows, no one has seen Thalleus for about 2 years.

Synerina asks the PCs to travel to the Doll House and speak with Thalleus Jongrim about his payments. She suspects that Thalleus has already fled the place, so if the PCs don’t find the dollmaker in residence, they should make a general assessment of the state of the property. They should also search for the house’s deed, as having it in hand will make it easier for the prince’s lawyers to claim ownership in lieu of the missing payments.

For this relatively simple task, the head councilor will pay the PCs a reward of 100 gp. With a sly wink, she also says that if Thalleus’s house has been abandoned, bandits have likely already looted the place of anything of value—a not-so-subtle suggestion that if the PCs happen to walk away with some of the professor’s belongings, no one will be the wiser.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:18] check or a @Check[grayce-lore|dc:16] check is familiar with Thalleus Jongrim’s reputation as a doll maker. His creations are of the highest quality, though Thalleus himself is known to be reclusive. On a critical success, the PC has heard rumors that some scandal forced Thalleus to leave Caliphas, though the details of the scandal are vague. Some say Thalleus had an illicit affair with a member of the royal court, while others claim he was a doctor who accidentally killed a patient while drinking. The truth, as the PCs will discover, is even stranger and more sinister.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Scenes

@UUID[Scene.tH5kmVlYOvALL7Re]{Dollmaker’s House} @UUID[Scene.nQAWDl5q7Fml9zvJ]{Dollmaker’s Basement}

You can find our provided maps for the dollmaker's house and basement in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

Shortly after the PCs depart Grayce for the Doll House, storm clouds gather in the sky overhead. The threat of rain is heralded by the occasional flash of lightning and peal of thunder. By the time the party reaches Thalleus’s house, a cold, hard rain begins to fall, soaking the PCs to the bone. Other than the inclement weather, the party arrives at the Doll House without incident.

Features of the Doll House

The interior of the Doll House is dark, and all doors are unlocked, except where noted. Ceilings are 8 feet high throughout.

Front Path.name: Front Path
Front Path.text:
A dirt path winds to the entrance of a rickety, two-story house partially hidden behind a stand of gnarled trees. Curtains are drawn across all the windows, though the front door is slightly ajar. A gust of wind causes some loose shutters to bang against the structure’s exterior.

The PCs can look around the grounds before entering the house, if they wish. The northern and eastern walls on the house’s first floor are a facade that presents a normal-looking abode, but the windows there don’t look into area @UUID[.iUA5BdUE3zGkzxWi]{A7}. If a character could move the curtains inside these windows, they would see nothing but wooden walls.

Approximately 60 feet to the east of the house is a locked trapdoor hidden beneath a patch of sod. A PC can discover the door with a successful @Check[perception|dc:23|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check, and it can be unlocked with three successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks. The trapdoor opens onto a corridor that eventually leads to area @UUID[.ssfKHc9bIFJtM6wj]{A17}. In the unlikely event the PCs discover the trapdoor, they might be able to bypass the encounters in the aboveground portions of the house, but they will have to backtrack and explore the rest of the area if they want to cleanse the Doll House of its haunting (see @UUID[.ssfKHc9bIFJtM6wj#putting-thalleus-to-rest]{Putting Thalleus to Rest}).

Scene Region

@UUID[Scene.tH5kmVlYOvALL7Re.Region.UgQgZdIOCBYtdPsZ]{Trapdoor Entrance}

For convenience, if the party discovers the hidden trapdoor, you can represent it by activating the Teleport Token behavior set up in the scene region marked "To A17" east of the house. You can open the region's configuration by clicking in the "Trapdoor Entrance" link above.

Keep in mind this trap door is actually 60 feet east of the house, which is not represented in the map.

Foyer.name: Foyer
Foyer.text:
The western wall of this entryway is decorated with a pair of oil paintings depicting two wooden dolls. One doll stands on a sunny beach dressed as a sailor in a bright blue shirt, while the other wears a pink ballerina’s tutu and poses on a stage. Neither doll has a face painted onto their smooth, featureless heads. Doorways lead north and east, while the front double door leads out to the south.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.4kc6sYSc56Q2KYTT.PlaylistSound.b4D2NNnV9r10gvnq]{Dollmaker's House}

As the party enters the Dollmaker's House, you can play this ambience sound we've provided.

To heighten the Doll House’s unsettling atmosphere, have each PC roll a @Check[perception] check whenever they return to this room. The character who gets the highest result notices that the dolls in the paintings have changed slightly: a head tilted in the opposite direction, an arm or leg moved to a different position, or a piece of clothing that seems more worn and tattered. These alterations are a symptom of the house’s haunting but are otherwise harmless.

Visitors who came to the Doll House were either customers looking to purchase one of Thalleus’s creations or weary travelers invited by the professor to spend the night, though the latter were usually taken captive. Either group would be greeted by the automatic butler Thalleus stationed here, which has remained in place even after the professor’s death. This construct is infused with the more dutiful aspects of Thalleus’s personality. It stands in the corner of the room just north of the eastern doorway, raising its head when the PCs enter.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.iICvyvPzfyJe4vzk]{Cockroach Swarm x2}

Creatures: The dutiful automatic butler isn’t a combatant in this encounter, but when it opens its mouth to welcome the PCs, a swarm of cockroaches that had been crawling around its interior comes boiling out. These hungry vermin are quickly joined by a second swarm that enters the foyer through the northern doorway. Each swarm fights until reduced to 5 Hit Points before fleeing through cracks in the floor and walls.

Automatic Butler: The automatic butler doesn’t recognize the threat posed by the swarms and repeats the following speech until a PC acknowledges it, after which the butler speaks more freely, as noted below.

“Welcome to the home and business of Professor Thalleus Jongrim. Here, the professor lovingly crafts all manner of dolls for lucky children to love and cherish. Won’t you take one home today?”

The dutiful automatic butler knows little about the rest of the house, as many of Thalleus’s memories were suppressed or splintered when the professor died. If asked about the deed to the house, the butler suggests the PCs begin their search in the library, directing them north. If the PCs ask about buying a doll, the butler instead points them toward the showroom to the east. The automatic butler doesn’t know anything about its own construction, although the PCs can attempt a @Check[arcana|dc:22|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[crafting|dc:22|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about it and learn some of the information found here. If the PCs ask the butler to accompany them as they explore the house, the construct explains that it isn’t allowed to leave the foyer.

When the PCs realize they must shut down all the automatic butlers to cleanse the house, they need only ask the dutiful automatic butler to stop operating. It complies without question, essentially destroying itself. As it does, the PCs see a ghostly wisp leave the now-inert mannequin. This wisp is the trapped fragment of Thalleus’s soul escaping to enjoy its final rest.

If the PCs attack the dutiful automatic butler, it doesn’t put up a fight. The characters can destroy it in a matter of moments, which has the same effect as if they had asked it to shut down.

Stairwell.name: Stairwell
Stairwell.text:
Doorways lead to the east and west at the bottom of these slightly crooked stairs. At least a dozen wood and cloth dolls sit on the steps, looking toward an oil painting hanging on the southern wall. The painting depicts a faceless wooden baby doll wearing a frilly bonnet and swaddling clothes.

The stairs lead up to area @UUID[.o7y3mILrkWJ8ZrqX]{A8}. The dolls on the steps are harmless and don’t impede the PCs’ progress, but their heads swivel slowly to watch the first PC to climb the stairs. Like the paintings in area @UUID[.ytaiJjfq4xTc22Ha]{A2}, the baby doll painting changes whenever the PCs return to this room. Each time, the baby seems to grow older—but not larger. Although the figure lacks a face, its “skin” develops wrinkles, and its clothes become more and more decrepit.

Doll Showroom.name: Doll Showroom
Doll Showroom.text:
This well-appointed room has seen better days, though someone has had the presence of mind to cover the two stuffed chairs against the southern wall with white sheets. A table, similarly covered, sits directly in front of the chairs. An empty stand that could support a small doll rests on the table. Against the northern wall are two cabinets packed with dolls made of all manner of materials. Each of the dolls watches over the room with small, dead eyes.

To support his experiments, Thalleus sold handcrafted dolls to customers who never suspected his other line of work. Sometimes, Thalleus would even take commissions to craft bespoke dolls, going over the details with the customer in this room, which served

as a sort of storefront. The two display cases are full of Thalleus’s handiwork. A simple posing armature used to stand on the table, but it has gone missing (see area @UUID[.o7y3mILrkWJ8ZrqX]{A8}).

A secret door to Thalleus’s workshop (area @UUID[.iUA5BdUE3zGkzxWi]{A7}) is located on the wall just north of the room’s entrance. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[type:perception|dc:20|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check can find the hidden switch that opens the door along the molding near the floor.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.N2oCj1LXgPalV9PI] @UUID[Actor.bdarrRaLjNmlYvNa]{Soulbound Doll x2}

Hazard: While the dolls in the northeastern cabinet are all mundane creations, the amount of suffering and void energy that was released when Thalleus died has caused the cabinet to become haunted. Once the haunt is activated, ghostly copies of the dolls attack living creatures in the room.

Creatures: Two soulbound dolls escaped from the house’s basement and now wait inside the northwestern cabinet for victims to torment. When the haunt rolls initiative, the soulbound dolls do so as well.

The dolls must spend their first action in the encounter clambering down from the shelves. They then advance menacingly on the PCs. Each soulbound doll has been made cruel through their creation and can cast a 2nd-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.wdA52JJnsuQWeyqz]{Harm} spell once per day. The soulbound dolls fight until destroyed.

False Hallway.name: False Hallway
False Hallway.text:
This hallway between the foyer and the library appears to end at a doorway to the east. In truth, the passage is part of an elaborate trap Thalleus set for visitors. The door at the end of the hall can’t be opened, though the knob turns. If the PCs ask the dutiful butler in area @UUID[.ytaiJjfq4xTc22Ha]{A2} what lies beyond the door, the butler claims (truthfully) that it doesn’t know.

Encounter

Trivial 3

@UUID[Actor.LvYs0VKdCwnmt98h]

Hazard: The floor in the east end of the hallway is designed to swing downward into a slide, depositing victims into area @UUID[.U1Z3WgcFaRlDVlHo]{A11}. Combined with the threats there, this becomes a moderate encounter. (Note that if three or more characters tumble into area A11 at once, the first of the characters automatically triggers the hazard there as soon as they arrive.)

Macro

@UUID[Macro.xWZkkFbRHtLs2DP0]{Reveal Piano Door}

If the characters fail to notice the trap and attempt to open the door, click on the above macro to toggle the state of the floor chute tile and play a sound effect!

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
Shelves straining beneath the weight of dozens of thick books line the eastern half of this cozy library. A desk in the northwestern corner is draped with a muslin sheet, as is a small table by the room’s only door. The table in the middle of the room is strewn with books, which are open to random pages.

Thalleus’s personal library is stocked with books about metaphysics, anatomy, religion, and occultism. He brought most of the books with him from Lepidstadt and has added to the collection since, though he keeps his most radical texts in his basement office (area @UUID[.oP9eBmUlMec6nD1x]{A15}). The books here aren’t organized in any particular order.

Automatic Butler: Thalleus installed an automatic butler in this room to help him catalog his many books and ensure that visitors didn’t walk away with anything too valuable or incriminating. Upon the professor’s death, the more studious side of his personality took up residence inside this construct. Since then, the construct has been focused on retrieving one of Thalleus’s notebooks from the shelves. The notebook has fallen behind some other books, however, making it difficult to find.

When the PCs enter the library, they find the automatic butler locked in a semi-confused state of repeated actions: moving a book from the shelves to the room’s main table, reading it for a few moments, then returning the book to the shelf. All the while, the butler mutters to itself, “Where is it? Where is it?” The construct doesn’t automatically notice the PCs entering the room and becomes startled if anyone makes their presence known. When this happens, read or paraphrase the following.

The finely dressed construct jumps a little in surprise. “Oh my!” it says in a cultured voice. “I didn’t notice you come in! But now that you’re here, perhaps you could help? The professor has asked me to retrieve a book, and I just can’t seem to find it!”

The studious automatic butler is so focused on its task that it assumes the PCs are guests, and thus it doesn’t question their arrival. It also doesn’t mind if the PCs start examining and reading the books. If the PCs attack the construct, it doesn’t defend itself and is quickly destroyed. If the PCs offer to look for the book, the butler gratefully accepts their help. If asked to describe what it’s looking for, the butler explains that Jongrim ordered it to retrieve one of his personal journals. As such, the book won’t have a title, and it will most likely be slimmer than the other volumes on the shelves. Unfortunately, the butler doesn’t know anything else about the sought-after book, though it is certain that it hasn’t found it yet.

Each PC who wants to search the library can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:20] check; a @Check[arcana|dc:20], @Check[occultism|dc:20], or @Check[religion|dc:20] check; or a @Check[library-lore|dc:16] check. The PCs can attempt a total of six skill checks, and they need to accumulate four successes (a critical success counts as two successes) to find the correct book. These checks mainly involve the PCs showing different books to the automatic butler, who rejects each one until the notebook is found.

The PC who achieves the fourth success spots a slim volume without a title wedged behind a larger tome about the history of dollmaking. The butler is ecstatic when it sees the notebook, crying “Yes! That’s what I’ve been looking for!” The construct then malfunctions from excitement, collapsing into a heap on the floor. When this happens, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check notices a faint ghostly form—the trapped portion of Thalleus’s soul—leave the automatic butler’s body. Once the butler collapses, no amount of prodding can get the construct to respond.

Encounter

Trivial 3

@UUID[Actor.dnP7hXNE1CuhT6Zt]

If the PCs don’t achieve four successes after six attempts, the automatic butler finds a book of occult treatises that, upon opening, suppresses the studious part of Jongrim’s personality. This causes the automatic butler to revert to its original demeanor. In a completely different and more monotone voice, the butler demands the “trespassers” leave the library immediately. If the PCs don’t comply, the automatic butler attacks.

The Notebook: Thalleus’s notebook is filled with pages of cramped handwriting and the occasional esoteric diagram. Any PC who flips through the notebook can determine that it was written by Professor Jongrim as a kind of diary. A PC who spends at least 30 minutes reading the entries discovers that the notebook details much of the backstory presented in the @UUID[.yEKYCCK9Q11rVseE]{Adventure Background}, including the professor’s eventual expulsion from the University of Lepidstadt. The diagrams focus on Thalleus’s early theories on soul transference, which seem dangerous and foolhardy to any character trained in Arcana, Occultism, or Religion.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.SrHjiqfeG5IqK9Xw]

Two tearaway paper dolls used as bookmarks fall out once the notebook is opened. The rest of the books aren’t particularly valuable, but altogether they can be sold for 30 gp.

Reward

For helping the automatic butler find the professor’s notebook, award the PCs 40 XP.

Doll Storage.name: Doll Storage
Doll Storage.text:
The northern wall of this dusty room is lined with shelves holding several dolls in various states of disrepair, from ones missing limbs to perfectly serviceable dolls whose clothes are simply a bit tattered or soiled. Two racks of clothes made for dolls have been pushed against the eastern wall, with a hand-cranked sewing machine on a table between them. A longer table occupies the center of the room, a few scraps of cloth scattered across its surface.

After fashioning dolls in his basement workshop (area @UUID[.6uAVoIuORZpshY13]{A16}), Thalleus would store the completed creations in this room, rotating them with the ones on display in area @UUID[.7mlYlo58cYvUYLdG]{A4}. Most the dolls kept here weren’t magical, as the professor retained the soulbound dolls for his research. This room was also used to store extra bits of clothing and dolls that needed repair (usually ones returned by a customer with a particularly rambunctious child). If these repairs could be affected quickly, Thalleus would do them here. Otherwise, he would return the doll to his workshop.

The secret door between this area and area @UUID[.7mlYlo58cYvUYLdG]{A4} is plainly visible from within this room. The secret door leading to the spiral staircase can be spotted with a successful @Check[perception|dc:22|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.WWtRJ5xPpByPE9FE]{Zombie Shamblers x4} @UUID[Actor.LU5gXvTWKZKB4OXL]

Creatures: Thalleus installed an automatic butler in this room in hopes that it would eventually learn to perform his more tedious repairs.

Upon his death, the more whimsical parts of the professor’s personality inhabited the butler, and it has spent the intervening months engaged in an endless “tea party” with the many dolls in the room. That is, until a gang of four burglars broke into the house several weeks ago. The burglars were killed by the soulbound dolls in area @UUID[.7mlYlo58cYvUYLdG]{A4}, who dragged their corpses into the storeroom.

The whimsical automatic butler has been treating these bodies as other dolls, dressing them in outfits and propping them up at the table. To make matters worse, the general level of void energy in the house slowly reanimated the corpses into zombies.

When the PCs enter the storeroom, they see what looks like four people standing at the long table. They wear brightly colored mismatched outfits and sway a little in place. Meanwhile, a wooden mannequin dressed in a fine black suit—the automatic butler—ambles toward the PCs, saying “Welcome, welcome! You’re just in time for dessert!” The butler then gestures toward the table. If the PCs refuse to approach, the butler becomes annoyed and pulls them toward the table, initiating combat. If any PCs stand by the table, the zombies notice them and turn to bite the newcomers. In either case, the party that didn’t initiate the fight joins in—the zombies because they sense a chance to feed on the living, and the whimsical automatic butler because the PCs are hurting its “guests.” They all fight until destroyed.

When the automatic butler is destroyed, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check notices a ghostly wisp leave the construct’s body. This is the trapped part of Thalleus’s soul passing on to the afterlife.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.RIG5um5oa8OaDOEG]

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:18|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check finds a floppy rag doll among the otherwise mundane dolls.

Upstairs Hallway.name: Upstairs Hallway
Upstairs Hallway.text:
If the PCs enter the upstairs hallway from the stairs, they hear the rhythmic thumping of wood against wood echoing from around the corner. A small triangular table stands in the corner of the hallway bend; on it is a single lit candle that emanates dim light in a 10-foot radius. From what the PCs know, there shouldn’t be anyone in the house to light a candle; its existence is another weird occult occurrence caused by Thalleus’s death.

When the PCs turn the corner, they see a 2-foot-tall posable armature (the one missing from area @UUID[.7mlYlo58cYvUYLdG]{A4}) repeatedly and methodically banging its little head against the door to area @UUID[.lUI43ZNScYcgvSWM]{A9}. If a PC approaches within 10 feet of the armature, the candle on the table suddenly snuffs out. The armature then scurries to the eastern end of the hallway, climbs the wall, and disappears through a hole in the ceiling. No amount of searching reveals where the armature went, though if you want to worry your players, it can turn up again elsewhere or reappear in its rightful place in area @UUID[.7mlYlo58cYvUYLdG]{A4}, now completely inanimate.

Bedroom.name: Bedroom
Bedroom.text:
The smell of musty death fills this modestly appointed bedroom, likely from the desiccated corpse lying on the once-plush bed. The corpse appears to have been propped up by several pillows, and a book lies open on its lap. A desk occupies the northwest corner of the room, while a wardrobe stands to the southwest. There are two doors in the eastern wall, with a third in the northern wall leading out.

The two eastern doors lead to a washroom and a closet, the latter of which contains several dark suits, as well as a secret door that can be discovered with a successful @Check[perception|dc:22|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The secret door opens onto a spiral staircase that goes all the way down to the basement, emerging in area @UUID[.6uAVoIuORZpshY13]{A16}. When Thalleus was still alive, he used these stairs to get to his underground workshop easily.

The corpse is, of course, that of Professor Thalleus Jongrim, who perished from his illness 2 years ago. As his life slipped away, Thalleus was in the middle of a ritual to transfer his soul to an automaton vessel he had prepared in his basement workshop (area @UUID[.6uAVoIuORZpshY13]{A16}). Thalleus died more suddenly than expected, however, so he didn’t quite finish the ritual. As a result, his soul and mind fractured as described @UUID[.ySjPxyRW6X2QlwyJ]{here}. Due to that same magical backlash, the book on Thalleus’s lap has been scoured of all useful knowledge of the ritual. A PC who scans through the pages and can read Requian makes out the word “soul” repeated over and over, but the surrounding text has been strangely blurred. The tome’s title, however, remains legible along its spine: Perambulations of the Immortal Soul.

Encounter

Severe 3

@UUID[Actor.GWTWKNMaKOecTDO3]{Death of the Dollmaker} @UUID[Actor.WPP72z4n7z7qTbkq]

Hazard: An event like Thalleus’s death leaves an occult mark on its surroundings. The very moment has been captured in a haunt fueled by residual spiritual energy.

Creature: In addition to creating a haunt in this room, Thalleus’s residual life energy animated his wardrobe. Located in the southwest corner of the room, the animated wardrobe lurches into action when the haunt rolls initiative. It fights until destroyed, using Thalleus’s clothes as tethers to keep PCs close enough to the bed to be damaged by the haunt.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.8a9nxC8sl4eypdUw]

Once the animated wardrobe has been defeated, PCs who search the construct find a sleeves of storage hanging inside it. The gaudy, colorful robe stands out amid Professor Jongrim’s otherwise dour, uninspiring clothing.

Secret Stairs.name: Secret Stairs
Secret Stairs.text: This hidden set of spiral stairs runs from the top floor of the house all the way down to the basement. All the secret doors leading into the staircase are clearly visible from the inside, and there is only a doorway at the bottom floor. The stairs are covered with dust, but the first time the PCs enter the staircase on any floor, they see footprints appearing in the dust—another side effect of the haunting created by Professor Thalleus’s death. If you like, these phantom footprints can help lead the players to a certain floor, or they can just be atmospheric.

Pit of Blades.name: Pit of Blades
Pit of Blades.text:
There are no obvious exits from this rectangular room with stone walls. The floor is packed dirt, and piles of bones have been pushed into the corners. Thin grooves are noticeable in most of the walls.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.4kc6sYSc56Q2KYTT.PlaylistSound.bNe6NF4agBxr3dDU]{Dollmaker's Basement}

As the party enters the Dollmaker's Basement, you can play this ambience sound.

This chamber lies directly beneath area @UUID[.iNlwBE8moEadgIQc]{A5} and is where creatures who trigger the trap in that room are deposited. The section of ceiling marked with a dotted line on the map is the underside of the false hallway’s chute. A PC can spot the closed chute with a successful @Check[perception|dc:23|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check, but it can’t be opened from this side.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:18|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the chamber finds the secret door in the northern wall.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.ZkqZwgQm9qmssVPe] @UUID[Actor.KH1GkazaI59zftst]{Crawling Hands x3}

Hazard: Unfortunately, the slide that dumps victims into this seemingly inescapable room isn’t the last of the PCs’ worries. A deadly trap is designed to kill everyone in the room, with sharp blades slicing out of three of the walls.

Creatures: Thalleus cleaned out the corpses in this room irregularly, believing that the soul of anyone killed by the trap wasn’t worthy to transfer into his creations. The bones are the remains of his last few victims, who slowly bled out after the blade trap chopped off their hands. These severed hands have since reanimated and now bide their time until more unfortunate victims arrive. One crawling hand emerges from each of the three piles of bones when the hazard rolls initiative. The crawling hands fight until destroyed, chasing down anyone who flees the room.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.C6CKd4Nu0Vbtai3C]{Toggle Pit of Blades}

As the party triggers the hazard, you can click on the above macro to reveal the serrated blades tile in the room and play a sound effect. You can click on it again to retract the blades and reveal them as needed, perhaps each time the hazard enters its routine!

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.j2202IijzPb3QoEM]

A PC who searches the piles of bones finds one of a pair of doubling rings on a bony finger; one of the crawling hands wears the matching ring.

Shifting Maze.name: Shifting Maze
Shifting Maze.text:
Plain wooden walls form a series of twisting passages, each indistinguishable from the others.

Victims who survived the pit of blades (area @UUID[.U1Z3WgcFaRlDVlHo]{A11}) usually found their way into this maze, the final step of the professor’s tempering process for their souls. Thalleus believed that a soul that had recently suffered hardship would be better suited for the transferal process. The winding, shifting nature of this maze, plus the many hazards toward which the victims were funneled, were all part of Thalleus’s attempt to create that suffering.

Invisible magical sensors hidden throughout the maze allowed Thalleus to monitor his victims from area @UUID[.R4mKMppRfwV3RMAl]{A13}, activating the traps when they entered certain areas and moving the walls around to further confuse them. When the PCs enter the maze, an automatic butler is likely at the console in area @UUID[.R4mKMppRfwV3RMAl]{A13}, ready to spring the traps and shift the walls. If the PCs defeat the construct before entering the maze (by reaching the basement via the secret stairs in area @UUID[.3oIK0368Vtkjzrru]{A10}), they should be able to discover the exit without having to deal with any traps or break down the maze’s walls.

The interior walls of the maze are made of wood panels. Though reasonably sturdy, the panels can be destroyed, allowing the PCs to move through the maze without needing to navigate its twists and turns. Each 5-foot section has Hardness 10 and 40 Hit Points (BT 20). The walls marked with an M are movable by someone operating the console in area @UUID[.R4mKMppRfwV3RMAl]{A13}.
