The movable walls begin in the configuration shown on the map, but they can be rotated into the positions marked with dotted lines. The movable walls are slightly thinner than the others and have only 30 Hit Points (BT 15). A PC can determine that a wall rotates by succeeding at a @Check[perception|dc:22] check, @Check[crafting|dc:20], or @Check[thievery|dc:20] check. Once a movable wall is discovered, a PC can fiddle with the wall’s rotating mechanism with a successful @Check[thievery|dc:22] check, essentially turning that wall into a door.

The secret doors leading out of the maze (one to the hallway that surrounds the maze and one to the maze’s control room) can each be discovered with a successful @Check[perception|dc:22|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check. Both doors are locked from inside the maze, requiring three successful @Check[thievery|dc:20|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks to open.

Maze Setup

Each yellow-tinted door represents a rotating wall. If opened, it will swing into position over a secret door that will automatically close, blocking vision and movement in that direction. If the wall needs to rotate again, you can close the yellow-tinted door or its invisible door counterpart, either action will return the wall to its initial position.

Additionally, since every 5-foot section of this maze can be destroyed, we have set them up as secret doors. If the characters break a 5-foot panel, you can open its corresponding secret door to reveal a tile for that broken panel, allowing the characters to pass through.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.MfR3AqSTAbTNqye7]{Trial by Flame} @UUID[Actor.06cbEhOcxDl0XqPu]{Trial by Ice} @UUID[Actor.RBXFsrHI3MwlDgRZ]{Trial by Poison}

Running the Maze: The cruel automatic butler operating the console in area @UUID[.R4mKMppRfwV3RMAl]{A13} watches the PCs’ progress through the maze, causing as much havoc and confusion as it can to continue the professor’s experiments. Assuming the PCs enter the maze from area @UUID[.U1Z3WgcFaRlDVlHo]{A11}, the automatic butler waits until they endure the trial by flame trap before rotating the westernmost movable wall. The butler then watches the PCs stumble through the southeastern part of the maze, rotating those walls at random intervals when the PCs aren’t looking to make the maze difficult to map. The PCs likely enter the trial by ice trap as they explore that corner of the maze. The automatic butler then rotates the northern wall to funnel the PCs toward the maze’s final trial.

There isn’t much the automatic butler can do if the PCs begin breaking down the maze walls. It continues to trigger the traps as normal but doesn’t rotate any of the walls.

Hazards: The maze contains three hazards that are triggered by the operator of the console in area @UUID[.R4mKMppRfwV3RMAl]{A13}. If the nearby magical sensor is disabled, the automatic butler can no longer see if the PCs are in range of the traps and chooses not to trigger them. The trial by flame trap is in the southwest portion of the maze. The trial by ice is in the southeast portion of the maze. The trial by poison trap is in the northeast portion of the maze.

Reward

For making their way through the maze and finding the secret door to the maze control room, award the PCs 40 XP.

Maze Control Room.name: Maze Control Room
Maze Control Room.text:
The main feature of this chamber is a large desk made of smooth wood and metal. Images of indistinguishable corridors float hazily in the many crystalline rectangles embedded in the center of the desk. A series of levers jut from the left side of the console face. Various diagrams and calculations have been chalked onto the walls, though time has rendered most of them unreadable. A door exits to the east.

This room contains the control console for the maze in area @UUID[.TSOT6YC7XTtwsUpj]{A12}. Invisible magical sensors situated in various points of the maze relay what they see to the console’s crystal windows. Each lever either rotates a wall of the maze to create confusion or triggers one of the maze’s hazards. Thalleus would use the walls in this chamber to take notes on subjects trapped in the maze, but his writing has faded over the years.

From this side, the secret door into area @UUID[.TSOT6YC7XTtwsUpj]{A12} is easy to spot. It can also be locked and unlocked from here. The butler stationed at the control console keeps the door locked at all times.

Encounter

Severe 3

@UUID[Actor.O5l94Emum5hWTiZ8] @UUID[Actor.rATBpWa62XUPnGZb]{Soulbound Dolls x2}

Creatures: Thalleus installed an automatic butler in this room to monitor the maze in case he was called away to deal with other victims. When the professor died, this construct absorbed a greater portion of his personality than the other butlers, though unfortunately those parts were among the cruelest and most uncaring facets of his mind. This automaton now delights in inflicting pain and suffering on others, especially those trapped in the maze it watches over. There haven’t been many victims in the past few years, however, so the cruel automatic butler has been directing its sadism toward two soulbound dolls once stored in area @UUID[.yscmlk1YElMj6vsX]{A14}. As a result of the butler’s cruelty, the dolls’ outfits are torn and tattered, and their limbs are rearranged into grotesque shapes. (This has no effects on their statistics.)

If the PCs survive the maze and enter this room through the secret door, the automatic butler becomes incensed and attacks, focusing its ire on any PC who disabled a hazard in area @UUID[.TSOT6YC7XTtwsUpj]{A12}. It occasionally makes a cutting comment about that PC’s performance, calling it “inadequate” or “subpar.” It orders the soulbound dolls to attack the other PCs, and they do so until destroyed. These rash soulbound dolls can cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.y6rAdMK6EFlV6U0t]{Breathe Fire} as their 2nd-rank spell.

When the cruel automatic butler is destroyed, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check notices a faint wisp of a ghostly form leave its remains. The wisp is the trapped part of Thalleus’s soul passing on to the afterlife.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.9V1pZoPmaf0E3XOM]

The crystalline “windows” embedded in the control console are valuable but highly fragile. Each can be pried free with a successful @Check[thievery|dc:20] check. On a failure or critical failure, the window shatters into shards of worthless crystal. Once removed from the console, the windows lose their magical properties. There are a total of eight windows, each worth 5 gp.

Gem Storage.name: Gem Storage
Gem Storage.text:
Gems and crystals of all shapes, sizes, and colors fill the shelves in this storage room. A thick layer of dust covers them all. Several rat skeletons dot the floor. A single door exits to the south.

Thalleus experimented with many different types of gems and crystals to house the fragments of souls for his constructs. Though they glisten in the light and appear beautiful, not all of them are valuable. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:16] or @Check[perception|dc:16] check can see that many of the gems are cheap glass replicas or common crystals. However, not all of them are worthless… or harmless.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.cfN3g0QmQ29AJEyI]

Hazard: With all the dangerous magic and necromantic science that Thalleus practiced in the house, his death unleashed waves of void energy throughout the building. Some of this energy was captured in four gems stored here, which the professor had already prepared to hold fragments of his victims’ souls. These gems now hunger to be filled and so reach out to grab any living creatures that enter the room. Over the years, the gems have killed several rats, but they have yet to be satiated. When the PCs enter the room, the gems awaken and wait for one of the characters to approach.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.2N3f0genDtOuzoRS]

A PC who is at least trained in Arcana or Occultism notices that one of the crystals is a fear gem.

Thalleus' Office.name: Thalleus' Office
Thalleus' Office.text:
This rectangular room has doors in the northern and southern walls, with a large desk scattered with papers in between. A chair that looks like it was once comfortable but is now covered in stains and dust sits behind the desk. Bookshelves line the eastern and western walls in the southern half of the room. Oil paintings of desolate landscapes hang on the other walls. A slightly sharp smell that irritates the eyes and nostrils fills the air.

Professor Jongrim constructed this room to be reminiscent of his office at the University of Lepidstadt, though the furniture is of lesser quality. One of the paintings shows an unidentifiable town on the shores of a calm lake; if a PC looks at the painting for more than a few moments, they feel the floor beneath them sway, as if they were standing on the deck of a ship in turbulent waters. The painting slowly changes to show a storm battering the town and causing massive waves on the lake.

The bookshelves hold tomes unfit for public display in the house’s library upstairs (area @UUID[.gh2XqRmZj7ipXARO]{A6}). A PC who succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:18], @Check[society|dc:18], or a @Check[library-lore|dc:16] check spots titles banned in several countries due to their focus on necromancy and soul-based magic. Thalleus’s copies of these texts are worn from repeated reading and contain notes scribbled in the margins. With enough time, a person studying these books could learn depraved rituals and techniques that corrupt the soul.

The papers on Thalleus’s desk are covered in a mishmash of occult symbols and semi-scientific diagrams. The desk also has several drawers, all of which are trapped.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.ixpeduV3MbwPC9oM] @UUID[Actor.r3EXyntNIazKf2gP]

Hazard: When the house was built, Thalleus installed a glass-lined chamber in the ceiling of this room as part of a devious trap to protect any secrets he had hidden within his desk. The glass chamber is divided into two parts: a reservoir filled with a powerful acid and a tank that holds a dangerous ooze. Triggering the trap causes two nozzles in the ceiling to begin spraying the acid, while a hatch opens to release the ooze. If a PC critically succeeds at finding the trap before it is triggered, they notice a series of switches on the underside of the desk that can be used to bypass the hazard. However, these switches must be flipped in an exact order or else the trap is triggered; this can be done with two consecutive successful @Check[thievery|dc:22] checks. Once the trap triggers, the switches can no longer bypass the trap.

If the trap is triggered, keep track of how many rounds it takes for the PCs to disable it. If the PCs want to rescue any of the desk’s documents from the acid (see Development), they can take an Interact action to grab a handful of them at random. Every three Interact actions used in this way counts as disabling the trap 1 round quicker.

Creature: The string slime released by the trap seeks out organic material to dissolve, which includes the PCs. If the ooze is split by slashing damage, the two separate slimes use their Tag Team ability as much as possible. The string slime fights until destroyed.

Development

The papers on top of the desk curl up and dissolve beneath the deluge of spraying acid, which also leaks into the desk’s interior to destroy everything within. However, if the PCs act fast enough, they can save some of the documents, a few of which are valuable.

Once the trap has been disabled, note how many rounds have passed since the hazard rolled initiative. (Remember that every three Interact actions the PCs take to rescue the papers reduces this total by 1.) If the PCs bypass the trap completely, the total is, of course, 0 rounds. If the total is 4 rounds or more, the PCs find only the deed to the house, slightly damaged but still readable. If the total is 2 or 3 rounds, they find the deed, as well as a scroll of enlarge (2nd rank). If the total is 1 round or fewer, the PCs find the deed, the scroll of enlarge, and a magic book that functions as runestone holding a +1 armor potency rune. They also find a ledger containing the names of all the travelers Thalleus kidnapped and killed. The list gives a small amount of solace to the families of the missing.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.qLnyDUClDNjiurBg]

In addition to the papers in Thalleus’s desk, the occult tomes on the bookshelves can be sold for a total of 50 gp.

Reward

If the PCs discover the list of names on the desk and deliver this information to Grayce, award the PCs 40 XP.

Soul Workshop.name: Soul Workshop
Soul Workshop.text:
This wide room contains several tables covered with occult paraphernalia, unidentifiable mechanisms caked in rust, shards of crystal, and pieces of wooden mannequins. Dried bloodstains are visible beneath the clutter on the two larger rectangular tables. A set of iron restraints is attached to the western table, while the eastern table supports a crude, human-sized mannequin, its construction not quite finished.

A brass contraption covered in dials and gauges stands against the southern wall. Rubber tubes lead from a canister to the back of a metal chair attached to the machine. Two-inch-long spikes and manacles on the chair’s arms and feet complete the picture of a most unusual torture device.

Doors lead west and north, while a wooden staircase spirals upward in the room’s northwest corner.

Professor Jongrim performed his most vile experiments in this room, using a custom device to extract soul fragments from his victims and install them in gems for his soulbound constructs. This soul-extracting device sits against the southern wall, and a PC can identify its use with a successful @Check[crafting|dc:18], @Check[occultism|dc:18], or @Check[religion|dc:18] check. For the machine to operate, a victim must be positioned (usually by force) in the chair, as the metal spikes plunge into the base of their skull. The manacles are then closed around the victim’s arms and legs to prevent escape. The device is then activated, vibrating the spikes at a specific frequency to draw out the victim’s soul, like extracting sap from a tree. Once extracted, the soul is transferred into a specially prepared gem placed in a socket in the front of the machine. The process kills the victim, of course, but it doesn’t fully trap the soul in the gem. Only a fragment of the soul enters the gem, allowing the rest of the victim’s soul to pass onto the afterlife, though this small blessing makes the overall process no less cruel.

The tables—the largest of which Thalleus would sometimes use to restrain other victims—are cluttered with the professor’s tools. Most of these tools have been damaged by time and through careless use by the room’s current inhabitants. The mannequin on the eastern table was meant to house Thalleus’s soul but is now useless. The spiral staircase leads to area @UUID[.iUA5BdUE3zGkzxWi]{A7}.

Encounter

Severe 3

@UUID[Actor.L2Nea3jwrjyijHFW] @UUID[Actor.VotlWUsFKdOrHWF6] @UUID[Actor.lFDYJOIp2knQ0IRY]

Creatures: Thalleus installed one of his first automatic butlers in this room to aid him in creating more. Upon the professor’s death, this automatic butler attracted the bitterest portions of his personality. Thalleus’s paranoia and hatred toward his fellow humans—especially the academics who exiled him from the university—have driven the construct to continue his research, albeit with less impressive results. Since the automatic butler doesn’t have all of Thalleus’s memories, it can’t replicate the process of creating more soulbound constructs. It hasn’t even had the chance to extract a soul fragment from a living being, a failure that has increased its bitterness tenfold. It takes this bitterness out on the PCs by attacking soon after they enter the chamber.

The butler’s negative emotions have coalesced into a malevolent shadow. When the PCs arrive, the shadow Hides beneath the eastern table, doing its best to remain unnoticed until it attacks. It focuses on the weakest PC while staying out of any magical light the party might be carrying. If the PCs defeat the automatic butler, the shadow retreats, rising through the chamber’s ceiling and fleeing the Doll House, never to be seen again. Otherwise, it fights until destroyed.

Finally, several months ago, a lone jinkin gremlin from below Grayce stumbled across the hidden entrance to the basement and became fascinated with both the automatic butler and Thalleus’s soul extraction device. Since then, the jinkin has served as the butler’s assistant, which mainly consists of being the target of the butler’s invectives. He hopes that the construct will eventually break down of its own accord so that he can loot it for scraps. The jinkin runs away if reduced to fewer than 5 Hit Points.

When the automatic butler is destroyed, a PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check notices the trapped part of Thalleus’s soul rising from the construct and passing on to the afterlife. If this is the fifth automatic butler the PCs have defeated, the departure of the final fragment of Thalleus’s soul ends the haunting of the Doll House, as described in @UUID[.ssfKHc9bIFJtM6wj#putting-thalleus-to-rest]{Putting Thalleus to Rest}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.t0YkbLjZl5eqDTwj]

The unfinished automaton’s face plate functions as a persona mask. Though mostly useless, enough of Thalleus’s tools can be salvaged to piece together a sterling artisan’s toolkit.

Basement Hallway.name: Basement Hallway
Basement Hallway.text:
A 10-foot-wide hallway runs the perimeter of the basement. Thalleus used the passage to travel between rooms, allowing him to remove dead bodies or collect living victims whose souls were primed to be extracted. The secret door to area @UUID[.TSOT6YC7XTtwsUpj]{A12} is obvious from the hallway and can be locked and unlocked from this side. A cramped passage in the southeastern corner leads to a trapdoor hidden in the ground roughly 60 feet east of the house (see area @UUID[.l5jZWu0mFv4B3nKt]{A1}).

Putting Thalleus to Rest

Even if the PCs make a beeline to Thalleus’s office and find the deed to the house, they’ve likely experienced several occult phenomena that suggest the property is haunted. While they weren’t told explicitly to clear out any ghosts, they might feel obligated to cleanse the building of Professor Jongrim’s lingering influence. Other characters might want to search the rest of the house for valuables, since they were given permission to take whatever they find. While doing so, they will be met with more occult phenomena, as well as any automatic butlers they haven’t yet encountered.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:22], @Check[religion|dc:22], or a @Check[spirit-lore|dc:20] check after entering the property understands that the house is haunted by a fractured spirit, likely that of Thalleus Jongrim. If the PCs witnessed a fragment of Thalleus’s soul escape a deactivated automatic butler, these DCs are reduced to 18 and 16, respectively. A PC who has spoken with at least two automatic butlers can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:18] check to realize that the constructs speak with the same voice. A PC who has made a successful check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about an automatic butler realizes this means the butlers contain fragments of the same soul—an almost impossible occurrence! Combined with the information found in area @UUID[.lUI43ZNScYcgvSWM]{A9}, the PCs can deduce that Thalleus’s soul fragmented into the automatic butlers when he died, and that those constructs must be destroyed or deactivated before the professor’s soul can truly begin its journey to the Boneyard.

There are five automatic butlers in the Doll House, in areas @UUID[.ytaiJjfq4xTc22Ha]{A2}, @UUID[JournalEntry.O3x6gtkglvPNr08r.JournalEntryPage.gh2XqRmZj7ipXARO]{A6}, @UUID[.iUA5BdUE3zGkzxWi]{A7}, @UUID[.R4mKMppRfwV3RMAl]{A13}, and @UUID[.6uAVoIuORZpshY13]{A16}. Each butler has a fragment of Thalleus’s soul trapped inside it. When the PCs destroy or deactivate all five automatic butlers (or simply when they decide to return to Grayce), proceed to @UUID[.14j0hqQddGe7ToqD]{Concluding the Adventure}.

Reward

For freeing all five portions of Thalleus’s soul, award the players 80 XP.

Concluding the Adventure.name: Concluding the Adventure
Concluding the Adventure.text:
When the PCs release the final fragment of Thalleus’s soul, read or paraphrase the following.

There is a release of tension in the air, as if the entire house had been waiting for years to exhale. Bits of shadow that clung tenaciously in the corners of rooms and behind doors suddenly seem less dark. The wallpaper and floors become less faded and scuffed. The creaks of settling joints and ungreased hinges sound less tortured and more like the result of an old house that hasn’t been maintained in a long while. Whatever occult presence cast a pall over the property is gone.

Releasing Thalleus’s soul permanently destroys the house’s haunts and ends any other minor supernatural effects. In addition, all the soulbound constructs and undead creatures within the house cease to be animated. The house is still in need of cleaning and repair (especially anywhere the PCs damaged things), but it is no longer haunted. Any mechanical traps or non-supernatural threats remain if the PCs decide to investigate unexplored areas of the house. However, those threats can be dealt with at the PCs’ leisure. The PCs might even want to rest overnight here!

The journey back to Grayce is uneventful, and if the house was cleansed, the usual clouds in Ustalav’s skies part momentarily to grant the PCs an hour of sunshine. Upon returning to town, the PCs can present the deed to Synerina and receive their promised reward of 100 gp. If the PCs fill her in on what happened in the house, the head councilor is shocked by the tale and insists that she (and the rest of the town) had no idea what the dollmaker had been up to. She thanks the PCs for putting the spirit of Thalleus Jongrim to rest and informs them that she will petition the prince for a greater reward for their trouble. In a few days’ time, she presents them with an additional 150 gp.

Sabotage!.name: Sabotage!
Sabotage!.text:
Father Wren, the owner of Grayce’s printing press and a priest of Zohls (the empyreal lord of determination, investigation, and truth), has had a great deal of bad luck lately. Forever practical, he’s avoided thinking about the constant failures and annoyances around the printing press as anything but random misfortune, even if it’s quite a bit and all at once. However, considering the context of the other stories he’s heard in town of similar misfortunes, he can no longer avoid the thought that Grayce is being actively sabotaged by some unknown party.

The aging publisher and spiritual leader hates involving outsiders in Grayce’s affairs, but he’s far too buried by his mounting deadlines to investigate himself. As a firm believer in truth, he’s looking for unbiased and trustworthy people who have the mettle to find and confront any miscreants involved. That is, if this is indeed more than simple bad luck.

Father Wren expects someone from a nearby village or a bored adolescent in Grayce to be the culprit. He’s not ruling out an organized effort by some unknown enemy of Grayce, but he is finding it hard to imagine that anyone has anything against the sleepy farming town. His own work following the teachings of Zohls has uncovered powerful diabolical enemies in the past, but this somewhat minor sabotage isn’t exactly the normal operating tactics of devils and their like. Regardless, he isn’t prepared for the true culprit behind these mechanical mishaps, a durtik gremlin by the name of Deeko.

Deeko loves nothing more than making dangerous devices of dubious quality. He created many clever clockwork toys and left them around the town, each implanted with a timer so that they would all malfunction or cause some sort of mayhem all at once, hoping the chaos riles up the townspeople. One of these devices was discovered by Krenvus Sang, a merchant of vintage goods and complex contraptions, though most others in town simply call him a “junk merchant.” From inspecting the device he found, he was able to determine that it was intentionally made to break in a spectacular fashion rather than just being poorly made. This discovery intrigued him, which led him to seek out more of the strange devices. He’d heard about others in town finding these devices and set out to track down as many as he could. He collected each of the toys, fixing them before anyone was hurt. He’s not sure if some passing inventor dropped their defective stock or where these devices came from, but he believes he’s solved the inherent issues in the mechanical devices and decided to sell many of these toys in his shop.

Deeko was crestfallen that not only did his big plan fail, depriving him of the screams from dozens of townspeople, but someone had the audacity to use their own mechanical skills to thwart him. To have his devices “fixed” and sold insulted Deeko and sent him into a rage. He’s decided the only way forward is vengeance upon Krenvus and the town that allowed this travesty. To aid in this new grand plan to defend his honor and cause even more trouble and destruction in Grayce, Deeko has recruited a larger crew of gremlins from the nearby hills and initiated his next plan: building tunnels underneath Grayce that will cause the entire town to collapse into the earth or slide into the river. If he’s lucky, he can pull off both results and watch it all happen.

Gremlins aren’t great diggers on their own, at least not on the scale he needed, so Deeko decided to build a fantastic new device to handle the labor of excavating the needed tunnels. As it’s larger and more demanding than a simple clockwork toy, building this digging machine required parts Deeko didn’t have. To handle this, he got his crew to steal the tools, materials, and equipment they require from the town above. While they take what they need, Deeko demands his crew play pranks on the town’s “inferior” machinery to further drive home his erratic “lesson.”

Deeko has dubbed his digging contraption as “the Dig Beast.” Makeshift as it is, the Dig Beast is taking much time to dig the tunnels. However, the final modifications are nearly complete, and if nothing is done, the gremlin’s twisted plot will actually come to pass. Fortunately, the pranks performed along the way have garnered attention and left a clear enough trail of evidence for the PCs to find and stop Deeko and his Dig Beast before he can collapse Grayce.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
This adventure assumes that most of the PCs are new in town and either passing through or came to Grayce intentionally after their previous adventure, quite likely dealing with umbral threats from Pathfinder Beginner Box: Secrets of the Star. Allow the PCs to explore the town and meet its residents, perhaps even take care of any business they need to do in town or simply just rest after their previous excitement. Once they’ve had a chance to do these things, get this adventure started.

Not long after arriving in town, Piotr Finch, an energetic young gnome whom Father Wren has hired as an errand boy, approaches the PCs during their downtime. If the PCs ask what role he plays, he boldly exclaims, “I’m an apprentice!” with a wide grin. He tells them the Father has urgent business to discuss with them at the printing press and they must come right away. He asks if they know where the Grayce Gazette is located, and if they haven’t seen the building yet, he gives directions and a description of the place (sturdy wooden building at the intersection of Ash Road and North Bend Road, just north of the Grayce Green Market). If asked for further details of what the publisher and priest wants, Piotr simply says, “I don’t know, but it’s got to be pretty bad for Father Wren to ask for help!” as he runs off to finish the next task on his long list of errands.

When the PCs arrive at the printing press, read or paraphrase the following.

The home of the Grayce Gazette is a disheveled mess of paper and machines. A few workers move at a frenzied pace. One is making constant checks and adjustments to the press and associated machinery while another pair examine the broadsheets being printed, scrutinizing each letter intensely. There are a few unlucky people trying to keep things clean and orderly, but the chaos churns faster than they can move. Despite the swirl of activity, one can see an order to things taking place.

Amid the chaos is a thin, gray-haired human man wearing simple brown robes marked with a few smudges of ink. He monitors the swirl of action with clasped hands, grunting directives like “Again!” or “Don’t put that there!” or “Hurry up! We must make up for the delay!” The aged man seems simultaneously exhausted and energized by the activity around him. As you enter, he seems to take notice of the visitors to this hectic scene.

“Oh, you are the adventurers in town. I see Piotr found you and you’ve agreed to at least hear me out,” he says while pushing spectacles up the bridge of his nose and grins. “Maybe we can finally sort out this mess!”

If the PCs took more than hour to arrive at the printing press after meeting Piotr, Father Wren asks them to wait a few minutes longer while he continues to direct his staff. He explains, “You took your time, so now I must take care of a few extra matters myself before we begin.”

If the PCs arrived promptly, Father Wren is impressed and says, “You’re all much more punctual than I had expected from adventurers. That is good. Very good.”

He motions for the PCs to follow him to his office in the corner of the building.

Father Wren’s office contrasts sharply with the working floor of the Gazette. This room is clean and orderly, with everything neatly placed where it belongs. A shelf filled with books covers the eastern wall. The mahogany desk, while well-used, still holds its luster, clearly being polished regularly.

The priest pulls a copy of a broadsheet and slaps it on the desk. “You see this disaster of a paper that almost went out?”

Any PC who examines the broadsheet and succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:14|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} immediately notices that many prices on the sheet are clearly wrong. The errant prices are either marked with the wrong denomination of coin (“Wheat per bushel: 5 gp,” for example) or the decimal point has been moved, making the products either ridiculously expensive or cheap (such as “Wool per sack: 2.4 gp”).

If no PC notices, Father Wren explains in exasperation that the broadsheet that almost went out this morning contained so many errors that it would have ruined the Grayce Gazette’s reputation.

He continues, pacing back and forth as he speaks.

“If this were just a matter of a mistake, I wouldn’t have called you here. But I can tell you that I check these myself every night with my most trustworthy and meticulous clerks. None of us found any of those errors. It seems that overnight someone must have snuck into the printing press and made the switch!” He stops pacing to drive the point home.

“And that’s simply the latest mishap we’ve dealt with. I thought my people were being sloppy, taking tools and leaving the press unmaintained. But they’ve never been this careless, and certainly they wouldn’t be doing this for long and still working here.” Father Wren sighs. “We’re being sabotaged!”

He sits down, taking off his spectacles then massaging the bridge of his nose. “What’s worse is that I don’t think it’s just us who is being sabotaged. All around town people have these mishaps with their tools and devices. The tollhouse and the drawbridge have both reported problems. I’ve heard even the junk merchant’s tools have gone missing!”

Normally I handle the affairs of Grayce internally. I don’t have much use for outsiders, no offense, but I’ve had no luck figuring out what’s going on and the problem seems beyond our ability to deal with it. I feel like outsiders would approach this without bias, and if you’re willing to, I’d like to trust you with this matter. I’m of course happy to pay you for your trouble—30 gold pieces if you can find out the identities of our saboteurs and prevent them from doing it again.

“To better understand what’s happening, you should talk to the some of the other people who’ve experienced technical difficulties in the last few weeks. Before we take any rash action, I’d like you to let me know your theories on who it is doing this and their reasons for doing it; I know adventurers are prone to fanciful thinking, but we need to focus on rational, sensible theories given the facts provided to us. I want culprits, not ghosts or children’s tales, do you understand?” Father Wren catches himself raising his voice. He clears his throat and finishes.

“Well, if you are going to take on this job, I’m sure you’ll have some questions for me. What else do you need to know about the situation?”

The PCs may have questions to ask. Some likely ones are answered below.

Who would be motivated to sabotage Grayce?

“There are always those who refuse to see progress. Those folks who don’t like the fact we have a functional printing press and that we use it for the public good certainly would want to slow us down. I can’t say I know who would have it out for our tinkerer, though.”

How long has this been going on?

“The oldest incident I can recall was about three weeks ago at the tollhouse, though I originally overlooked it because the tollkeeper Mariv is overly suspicious. I thought it was another of her overreactions.”

Do you suspect anyone?

“I suspect everyone and no one. Well, not exactly,” he grins. “I truly don’t think that anyone who lives in Grayce would do it, since it harms their livelihood, but it’s possible that it might just be bored children causing trouble. I also don’t think it’s travelers, since this has been going on for weeks and I’m not aware of anyone spending that long here in town.”

Do we have a deadline?

“As soon as you can! I can’t provide you with an exact time period, but I can tell you that the sabotage is escalating. I don’t want to find out how far they’re willing to go, and I certainly don’t want to risk another near catastrophe like we almost had today on next week’s broadsheet!”

If they decide to investigate other locations in town where these kinds of incidents have taken place, the PCs are going to want to know more about who to speak with at each location and why. To help with this, Father Wren has the following to say about each of them.

Printing Press (Yvette Molan) “I’m going to be the most useful person you can talk to, but I’m also the busiest. I’ll have you talk to Yvette, my machinist. She understands the machinery and our problems more than anyone other than me. She takes her time very seriously and so do I! She may seem brusque, but it’s just that she’s very busy and very focused and doesn’t like being interrupted. To be honest, I can relate, but other don’t see it the same. Don’t take up too much of her time. We have important work to do, and I’m hiring you so that Yvette can focus on that work.”

Chapel Drawbridge (Otto Vaunier) “Otto is an expert machinist with some unique and possibly conflicting views on machines. You might find it difficult to have the conversation you want with him at first, so be patient. You have to listen through some odd theories, but there’s usually a spark of cleverness beneath that. I’m too busy to have much patience with Otto myself, but hopefully you’ll have better luck.”

Tollhouse (Mariv Sonnal) “Mariv focuses on every detail, which is great for someone taking accounts of taxes and duties. However, sometimes I feel it’s to her detriment, as she constantly sees flaws and wrongdoing in everything all at once. After you talk with her, you’ll probably suspect the entire town of sabotage. Don’t take her too seriously, but do note her attention to detail.”

Vintage Gearworks (Krenvus Sang) “Quite frankly, I don’t understand the man. How much can some of that junk possibly be worth? Most of it isn’t even useful. While I don’t understand how Krenvus’ shop stays open, I do know one thing—Krenvus works magic with machines. If it has moving parts, he can repair it. He’s helped fix the printing press a time or two for us, though I can’t say I liked the price. I don’t understand why he doesn’t put his skills to better use, but some riddles are meant to remain unsolved, I suppose.”

Once Father Wren answers their questions and tells the PCs whom to talk to, they can then start their investigation. If they spend too much time with questions and conversation, he starts trying to usher them out to get started. “There’s no time to waste! These saboteurs aren’t going to just stop on their own.”

If the PCs are from Grayce, they might take on mission without asking about payment, but if the PCs do ask, Father Wren promises 30 gp each if they can find out what is happening and stop the sabotage.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
In this part of the adventure, the PCs collect clues by talking to each of the NPCs who have experienced problems. They use those clues for attempts to deduce the general reason and identity of the saboteurs.

The PCs can investigate the different locations in any order. Each location listed in the investigation is presented in isolation, so if the PCs have visited some of the other sites, feel free to incorporate what they’ve learned previously to give more context to the clues they find in subsequent locations. In some cases, this can reinforce commonalities in the events, while in others it has the potential to lead the PCs astray if they get too wrapped up in the wrong details.

After each encounter with an NPC, a single PC can attempt one of the activities below to deduce the identity of the saboteur or the reason for the sabotage. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid} actions can assist on this roll. When the party has achieved a success or critical success for both identity and motive, they can speak to Father Wren regarding their conclusions.

Deduce Saboteur's Identity

You put together the clues you have and deduce the general nature of the saboteur's identity.

Skill Checks: @Check[crafting|dc:23|options:deduce-saboteurs-identity] @Check[nature|dc:23|options:deduce-saboteurs-identity] @Check[society|dc:23|options:deduce-saboteurs-identity]

Critical Success Gremlins delight in just this kind of random, almost gleeful, sabotage. The party receives a +1 circumstance bonus to all Recall Knowledge checks pertaining to gremlins for the rest of the adventure.

Success You understand that the saboteur is creating mischief in the way you’d expect from only a few creatures—fey mischief-makers would cause such careless chaos.

Failure You fail to connect the clues in a coherent way.

Critical Failure Your conjecture further muddies the water about who the saboteurs could be. The next check the party attempts to deduce the saboteur’s identity takes a –1 circumstance penalty.

Effects

@UUID[Item.f3bpUqkoagfOvLDd]{Gremlin Recall Knowledge} @UUID[Item.Ast8W7cfe0YP4Vpj]{Saboteur's Identity Penalty}

If the party gets a critical success on this activity, you can drag the Gremlin Recall Knowledge effect onto their character sheets or tokens to grant them a toggleable bonus for their Recall Knowledge checks.

Alternatively, if they get a critical failure, you can drag the Saboteur's Identity Penalty effect onto the character next attempting this activity. This will automate their penalty for one of the above checks.

Deduce Saboteur's Motive

You use the evidence you find to solve the riddle of the saboteur’s motive.

Skill Checks: @Check[crafting|dc:23|options:deduce-saboteurs-motive] @Check[deception|dc:23|options:deduce-saboteurs-motive] @Check[perception|dc:23|options:deduce-saboteurs-motive]

  • Critical Success The saboteurs are seeking revenge, but that’s not all. They are using the stolen parts and tools to build something for that revenge. The party receives a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative in all encounters for the rest of this adventure.

  • Success The evidence makes it clear that the saboteurs are seeking revenge on the town for some reason and are likely planning something big.

  • Failure The saboteur’s motives remain ambiguous and muddled.

  • Critical Failure What you think about the saboteur’s motive is not only not helpful, but also actively distracting. The next check the party makes to deduce the saboteur’s motives takes a –1 circumstance penalty.

Effects

@UUID[Item.hIBBV2sHFXLQsUWj]{Saboteur's Motive Initiative} @UUID[Item.O9cUn5tlmcoycslo]{Saboteur's Motive Penalty}

If the party gets a critical success on this activity, you can drag the Saboteur's Motive Initiative effect onto their character sheets or tokens to automate this initiative bonus.

Alternatively, if they get a critical failure, you can drag the Saboteur's Motive Penalty effect onto the character next attempting this activity. This will automate their penalty for one of the above checks.

Each time the PCs investigate one of the sites and talk to the NPC there, they lower the skill checks DC for both Deduce Saboteur’s Identity and Deduce Saboteur’s Motive by 2. If the PCs visit all four sites, they are automatically able to deduce the clues as if they achieved a success for each activity.

The party can still look for clues and visit the remaining sites after they have successfully deduced the identity and motive. If they do this, treat them as if they had critically succeeded in both activities.

The default time of each investigation is about 2 hours, including travel time and searching around. Unless they get distracted or waste time, the PCs should be able to investigate all sites in a day or two. If they take longer than a day, Father Wren sends Piotr to find them and remind them of the mission’s urgency. The youngster playfully chides, “Father Wren says time’s a tick-tocking! You better hurry up!”

Reward

Each investigation site’s reward is 75 XP. If the PCs succeed at both checks before they visit all sites, they gain the reward XP and reduced skill check DC as if they visited the remaining sites.

Printing Press.name: Printing Press
Printing Press.text:
Things are even more chaotic after Father Wren discovered the mistakes in the morning, and everyone’s even more rushed and hurried trying to make up for the time lost. Yvette (focused female nephilim human machinist 3) is not in the main shop when the PCs look for her, and they must ask around the Gazette to find her. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:13|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Seek or @Check[diplomacy|dc:13|options:action:gather-information|name:PF2E.Actions.GatherInformation.Title|traits:exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.plBGdZhqq5JBl1D8]{Gather Information} learns that she is outside in the shed doing some tool maintenance. If the PCs seem intent on bothering her in the shed, other workers let them know this might not be the best time because Yvette is extremely particular about her scheduled projects. If pressed on what time they should come back, the workers shrug, remarking that Yvette sometimes gets absorbed in her work for unknown periods of time. If the PCs attempt to wait, Yvette spends the rest of the day on her personal project, an anti-tampering device for the printing press. If consulted, Father Wren tells the PCs to do whatever it takes to get the info they need, but also to be careful around Yvette, adding “If you are interrupting a project of hers, steel yourself!”

If the PCs force the discussion early and talk to Yvette in the shed, read or paraphrase the following.

The shed door is partially open. Inside is an umber-skinned woman in a short-sleeved shirt hunched over delicate machinery on her workbench. Her hair is closely braided to her head, and she wears goggles with magnifying loupes flipped. Without turning or pausing, she speaks.

“I’m sure that somewhere, someone, somehow informed you that the penalty for interrupting me in the middle of my shop time is grounds for a swift and miserable death?”

Yvette gives her warning to the PCs, then ignores them to focus on her work. Getting her attention requires the PCs to attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:15|options:action:make-an-impression,target:yvette|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression} or @Check[deception|dc:15|options:action:lie,target:yvette|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie}, or a @Check[type:crafting|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge,target:yvette|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}. Critical successes on any of those checks result in Yvette being particularly helpful, giving the PCs a +1 circumstance bonus to the @UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW.JournalEntryPage.4iMnk44TCz0uxVOJ]{deduction activities}. Any PC who attempts an Intimidation check gets her attention, but not in a good way. She turns to the PC attempting to Intimidate her and says, “I’m not the one you should try that with, friend.” Any subsequent checks to interact with Yvette from that PC take a –2 circumstance penalty. Each PC can attempt two checks before Yvette gets frustrated and makes of show of pretending they don’t exist for the rest of the day. If a PC critically fails a check, Yvette ignores that character for the rest of the day.

Effects

@UUID[Item.N1QoG8XukhDVQ7Yc]{Saboteur Deduction Bonus} @UUID[Item.BwjihI13l4ifZvvG]{Yvette Penalty}

If the party critically succeeds at getting Yvette's attention, you can apply the Saboteur Deduction Bonus effect onto the character making the next deduction check.

If they attempted to intimidate Yvette, you can apply the resulting penalty by applying the Yvette Penalty effect.

Yvette is currently working on an anti-tampering device to protect the printing press from sabotage. On her workbench is the prototype for what she calls “press locks,” which can be placed on type blocks and the other components of the printing press, preventing anyone from adjusting or changing the components until they are unlocked. Any PC who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} recognizes the purpose of what the machinist is building.

Once they have her attention, Yvette impatiently asks the characters what they need and spares a few moments to discuss matters with them. She wants to build the press locks to protect the printing press, but she also wants the matter resolved.

A PC who offers to help with the press locks can do so with a successful @Check[crafting|dc:16|options:action:craft|traits:manipulate] check to Craft. This impresses Yvette and convinces her to offer her aid in analyzing any clues the PCs uncover, reducing the DCs of all @UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW.JournalEntryPage.4iMnk44TCz0uxVOJ#deduce-saboteurs-identity]{Deduce Saboteur’s Identity} or @UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW.JournalEntryPage.4iMnk44TCz0uxVOJ#deduce-saboteurs-motive]{Deduce Saboteur’s Motive} by 1 so long as the PCs consult her. If the PCs help with her crafting, she’s always willing to put down what she’s doing to consult with the PCs if they return later.

Below are some questions the PCs may ask.

How has the printing press been tampered with?

“What’s interesting is that most of the incidents we’ve had recently just seemed like mistakes—a screw loose on the plate so the ink pressed uneven, misaligned movable type—things that could be accounted for by people simply making a mistake, only unusual for the fact that Father Wren is so strict about it that it never happens! But matters have quickly changed, and now the press is being changed. Father Wren already told you about how our movable type got rearranged, but a week ago our hand crank was completely disassembled! It’s like whoever is doing this is learning the machines as they go.”

Has anything gone missing?

“Yes. But weirdly enough, nothing unique to the press. If it were a rival press, which there isn’t anywhere nearby, I’d expect the culprits to focus on the components we need to do our work. Instead, it’s been a lot of small gears and washers. Oh yeah, and some boards and a bag of nails have gone missing out of the shed.”

Who do you think it is?

“I want to say it’s kids pulling pranks, but I don’t think any kid in Grayce can pull off elaborate pranks like the ones we’ve been seeing. Also, I don’t see why they’d care about altering the listed prices. That pranking goes directly to harm us, and I don’t think any of the locals are that malicious. They’re just bored, mostly.”

“Plus,” she adds, “Father Wren locks up the shop at night, so anyone getting in to rearrange the type blocks or mess with the press has either stolen the key or is picking the door’s lock and getting in. I don’t really see bored youth going to that kind of trouble. But then, who is willing and skilled enough for that?”

Yvette answers some questions but is eager to finish her work and uses any lulls in conversation to make her way back to it.

Looking Around the Gazette.name: Looking Around the Gazette
Looking Around the Gazette.text:
PCs can look around the Grayce Gazette on their own as long as they don’t get in the way. Each PC can attempt a single @Check[perception|dc:15|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Seek or a @Check[crafting|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}, or a @Check[engineering-lore|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Recall Knowledge.

For each successful check, the group notices one of the following clues. A critical success means the group notices two of the following:

  • In the pile of papers scattered around is a detailed drawing of the printing press’ type block. In a childish scrawl in Sakvroth next to the diagram, it says “Mess this up.”

  • Several nuts and bolts that clearly don’t fit the printing press or any device in the Gazette are scattered on the floor.

  • It looks like some of areas of the printing press have been gnawed on while other areas look like they were scratched with a knife or dagger.

  • There is a strange draft coming from the roof. Examination of the area reveals someone made a small patch of removable roof just big enough for a creature of size Small to squeeze through.

If the PCs find at least two clues, each PC gains a +1 circumstance bonus to their next @UUID[.4iMnk44TCz0uxVOJ#deduce-saboteurs-identity]{Deduce Saboteur} check.

Effect

@UUID[Item.N1QoG8XukhDVQ7Yc]{Saboteur Deduction Bonus}

You can automate the aforementioned bonus by applying this effect on the character attempting the next Deduce Saboteur check.

Reward

For speaking with Yvette and looking around the Gazette for clues, award each PC 75 XP.

Chapel Bridge.name: Chapel Bridge
Chapel Bridge.text:
When characters arrive at the Chapel Bridge, read or paraphrase the following.

The Path River winds sleepily around the southern edge of Grayce. Allowing entrance to Grayce from across the river is a wooden drawbridge attached to a stone chapel.

Inside the wide entranceway leading into the chapel, you see a gaunt man with mangy gray and white hair with his ear pressed against the drawbridge crank. His eyes are shut as he waits reverently for something to happen.

The man next to the crank is Otto Vaunier (superstitious male human caretaker 1), the caretaker of the chapel and the drawbridge. He maintains and operates the drawbridge on his own. (Despite having had several apprentices over the years, most haven’t stuck around for even a year.)

When the PCs speak to him, he looks up from his activity and stares at them intensely.

“The spirits trapped in the drawbridge are very angry today, friends… they want to join Pharasma, not have their souls trapped in this wretched frame of gears and stone. Is this what you’d want to be trapped in for your afterlife? I surely think not.” The man rubs his hair and then shrugs.

“Ah well, there’s not much I can do for it other than try to ease its comfort and make this existence a little more bearable. What can I help you with? Did you come here to hear the anguished cries of the dead?”

Otto is a faithful worshipper of Pharasma who believes that mechanisms and machines operate by trapping the spirits of the dead in them. He used to dismantle machinery around town to “free their spirits” but after much trouble he decided to use his natural affinity for machines to tend them instead. He refers to it as “easing their suffering.”

He wants to talk to the PCs about the souls trapped in the machines, starting with “Borden,” the spirit Otto believes is trapped in the drawbridge mechanisms. Attempts to get substantive information from him fail automatically until he exhaustively explains all his theories. It takes roughly 2 hours for him to do so, as he enumerates all the machine spirits in town that he’s “befriended.”

Characters can speed this up by enthusiastically engaging with him in conversation (this requires a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:14|options:action:make-an-impression|name:PF2E.Actions.MakeAnImpression.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression} or @Check[deception|dc:14|options:action:lie|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|options:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] Deception check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie}), debating his beliefs (@Check[religion|dc:16|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[crafting|dc:16|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}) or framing the problems occurring in town as a threat to the machine spirits (@Check[deception|dc:14|options:action:lie|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|options:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check to Lie). A success reduces the time to 1 hour, and a critical success reduces it to about 10 minutes. Each PC can attempt one check during Otto’s lecture. A critical failure adds an hour to the time, as Otto feels the need to go into more detail and be more clear since the PCs obviously don’t understand.

When Otto talks to the PCs about the incidents, he describes the incident about a week ago.

“When you say ‘sabotage,’ it’s so funny to me! It makes me chuckle inside, knowing that only I can tell what the spirits want! It’s lonely but it fills me with a glowing bit of pride. But the closest thing to what you think it is might be the day a week ago where the bridge clearly was tired of people walking over it and boats passing under. Just exhausted, it was. So, I needed to raise it at the normal time for ships to pass, and it refused. I pleaded and pleaded, and it just said, ‘no, Otto.’“

But then I figured Borden must be feeling a bit worn down, so I went and checked. Borden wasn’t just worn down, he was upset! Look at how he ground down these gears!”

Otto digs into an overflowing basket of parts and retrieves a large bronze gear full of scratches and gouges.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:14|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Recall Knowledge reveals the scratches and gouges come from claws and teeth.

If the PCs ask about any other strange occurrences a the Chapel Bridge, Otto also complains about having to replace his shovel blades—or entire shovels—repeatedly over the last month. He tells the PCs that overnight the blades keep being removed from the shaft of the shovel and taken, meaning he can’t reliably engage in his hobby of “burying” dismantled machines so they can rest.

Looking Around the Chapel Bridge.name: Looking Around the Chapel Bridge
Looking Around the Chapel Bridge.text:
Characters can investigate the drawbridge mechanism and surrounding area on their own or they can bring Otto with them to answer more questions. He’s always happy to talk. The PCs can perform their investigation with successful @Check[crafting|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[nature|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}, or @Check[perception|dc:15|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek}. For each successful check, the group notices one of the following clues. A critical success means the group notices two of the following:

  • Otto has wooden trays of old devices that he’s disassembled that are ready for burial, but many of these are missing bolts, grommets, gears, and screws.

  • Disturbed earth around the tower, as if someone had done some digging and aborted the process.

  • In a corner is a brief comment etched in Sakvroth by one of Deeko’s henchman. Any PC who knows Sakvroth understands that it says, “This place is going DOWN.”

  • There is a dagger lying on the ground, left behind by a careless jinkin. The dagger is crudely made and meant for small hands.

If the PCs find at least two clues, they each get a +1 circumstance bonus to their next @UUID[.4iMnk44TCz0uxVOJ#deduce-saboteurs-identity]{Deduce Saboteur} check.

Effect

@UUID[Item.N1QoG8XukhDVQ7Yc]{Saboteur Deduction Bonus}

You can automate the aforementioned bonus by applying this effect on the character attempting the next Deduce Saboteur check.

Reward

For speaking with Otto and looking around the Chapel Bridge for clues, award each PC 75 XP.

Grayce Tollhouse.name: Grayce Tollhouse
Grayce Tollhouse.text:
The tollhouse sits near the Gravedocks. It is a stout building with wide windows on the first of its two floors. Standing beside the open door, looking out over the activity at the docks‚ is a prim woman in a high-necked dress. She scrutinizes you as you approach.

“Judging by the looks of you, you are those people Father Wren asked to look into all the vandalism the town has seen lately.” She gestures inside the tollhouse as she turns inside the building.

“Please, come in. I have thoughts about all this.”

Mariv Sonnal (prim female human toll collector 2) has reams of papers on her desk of “suspicious” people she has noticed around town. She tells the PCs that she fears this conspiracy against the industry of the town runs deep, “Sometimes I fear Father Wren himself knows more than he lets on. Secretive, that one. I can’t quite puzzle him out.” A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:13|options:action:sense-motive|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive} or @Check[society|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} reveals that this is Mariv’s unchecked anxiety and paranoia speaking and is not representative of reality.

Mariv also tells the PCs about the machinery malfunction that happened here around two weeks ago. The master scale in the tollhouse was damaged and rendered incapable of taking measurements. This halted operations at the tollhouse for almost an entire day while it was fixed. During that time, boat traffic was held up at the docks, leading to harbormaster Ulaptisk Nannocurt coming over to see what was going on and yelling at Mariv to get things moving so no one’s stuck at the dock after the bridge closes for the night. If asked about that, Mariv remarks “Krenvus really saved me that day! He made the bolts custom just from taking measurements.” It became clear to Mariv that there was foul play when Krenvus told her the fulcrum had several bolts missing, disconnecting it from the weighing platform.

While discussing the events, Mariv brings up a handful of people in Grayce as members of a conspiracy to slow advancement and growth of the town. (These people are innocent, of course. They’re just older people who prefer the town a little less industrialized.) If a PC entertains these theories and talks to Mariv as they investigate on their own, they glean useful information nested in the conspiratorial information with a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:18|options:action:make-an-impression|name:PF2E.Actions.MakeAnImpression.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression} or @Check[society|dc:18|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to Recall Knowledge. A PC who succeeds at one of these checks gains a +2 circumstance bonus on one check made while @UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW.JournalEntryPage.Kf5nilLwHn9Ti7sW]{looking around the tollhouse}.

Effect

@UUID[Item.ezcNlkMta79tBBkg]{Tollhouse Investigation Bonus}

If any PC benefits from the aforementioned bonus, you can apply this effect to them to automate it.

Looking Around the Tollhouse.name: Looking Around the Tollhouse
Looking Around the Tollhouse.text:
The PCs can investigate the tollhouse area on their own, though Mariv follows them around to keep an eye on them and offer unsolicited advice and theories. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge,looking-around-the-tollhouse|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[society|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge,looking-around-the-tollhouse|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}, or @Check[perception|dc:15|options:action:seek,looking-around-the-tollhouse|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} reveals one of the clues. A critical success reveals two.

  • Damage around the fulcrum included claw marks and bite impressions.

  • Many of the weights used in the weight pans for measuring are missing.

  • Behind the tollhouse in a dried mud patch is a diminutive humanoid footprint.

  • The shaft of a shovel lies near a bush outside. The blade has been broken off. This is one of Otto’s missing shovels.

If the PCs find at least two clues, they each get a +1 circumstance bonus to their next @UUID[.4iMnk44TCz0uxVOJ#deduce-saboteurs-identity]{Deduce Saboteur} check.

Effect

@UUID[Item.N1QoG8XukhDVQ7Yc]{Saboteur Deduction Bonus}

You can automate the aforementioned bonus by applying this effect on the character attempting the next Deduce Saboteur check.

Reward

For speaking with Mariv and looking around the tollhouse for clues, award each PC 75 XP.

Vintage Gearworks.name: Vintage Gearworks
Vintage Gearworks.text:
When the PCs enter Vintage Gearworks, read or paraphrase the following:

This small shop is a bewildering splendor of complex devices of every size and purpose; shelves overflow with windup creatures like soldiers, tortoises, and dragons. Repeating crossbows and strange-looking weapons hang on the walls. Among the recognizable items are pieces of machinery which defy easy explanation.

A man in a bronze pinstriped vest emerges from behind a pile of equipment with a wrench in his hand. On the wall directly behind him is a large sign in bold bronze letters that says, “No Refunds of any Kind.”

“Welcome to Vintage Gearworks! You look like the type who needs some sort of… complex solution for your complex problems! That happens to be my specialty, so please don’t worry. My devices can help you find friends or dispense with your enemies! Just tell me what you need!”

He gives the welcoming smile of a practiced salesman.

Krenvus Sang (creative male human inventor 4) is always looking for customers. Even though he is worried about all the sabotage and what it could mean for his business, he focuses initially on selling items to the PCs. He begins by offering deals on several uncommon items (he calls them his “favorite items for people of discerning tastes”) for a deep discount: a gnome flickmace for 2 gp, a repeating heavy crossbow for 10 gp, and an arbalest for 4 gp. If it appears to be too good to be true, that’s because it is—each of the items has a chance to malfunction when used. Each time the item is used to make a Strike, the wielder must succeed at a DC 4 Flat Check. On a failure, the item malfunctions, and the Strike fails. No repairs are needed for future Strikes after a malfunction, but the flat check is always required. Repairing these items requires materials equal in cost to the difference from Krenvus’ price to the market value of the item and a successful @Check[crafting|dc:14|options:action:repair|name:PF2E.Actions.Repair.Title|traits:exploration,manipulate] check to Repair. Krenvus stresses highly his “no refund” policy when selling these items.

He offers some more common items at a “friends of the store” discount: a shortbow, a crossbow, and a hand crossbow, each for 25 sp. The discount is lighter, but these devices operate as they are supposed to. He’ll offer a deal on all three for 7 gp.

If the PCs buy something here, Krenvus is immediately helpful. If the PCs buy one of his “discerning tastes” items he is extra talkative and helpful, granting them a +1 circumstance bonus to checks to @UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW.JournalEntryPage.jWD5QHKyAuU8ETfd]{look around the store}. If the PCs don’t buy anything and mock his wares, Krenvus is hurt and a little defensive. It takes a few minutes to get him to be give useful information or allow the PCs to look around the store.

Merchant

@UUID[Actor.g6JU4Nui6G0uiu62]{Vintage Gearworks}

We have provided a merchant actor for Vintage Gearworks which you may drop onto the canvas, allowing your players to open its sheet by double-clicking on its token. From there, they can drag and drop items from the merchant's sheet to their own character sheets to purchase an item.

The gnome flickmace, repeating heavy crossbow, and arbalest found in this merchant actor are automated to send a reminder note with the necessary flat check when a Strike is made with them.

Effect

@UUID[Item.VeDOIKv4ZlTER2xY]{Gearworks Investigation Bonus}

If the PCs buy something, apply this effect to them to automate their bonus to look around the store.

Krenvus feels the saboteur must be some rival inventor from another town, because his tools have been going missing. The inventor often misplaces an item, but ten days ago his copper hammer, a can of grease, three chisels, and a leather bag all went missing. That frustrated him and slowed down his repairs for a few days. He remarks, “I had to go over to Yvette’s shed, and she’s never going to let me hear the end of it!”

While upset that his things have gone missing and worried that the situation might escalate unless the perpetrators are caught, he readily admits that he’s personally benefited from this spate of sabotage. Folks in town have come to him to have their machines repaired. If accused of being the culprit so that he could make some coin fixing the broken machines, he stands aghast at the accusation. “How dare you! I would never intentionally break something of someone else’s just to make some coin. That’s... that’s just not right! I am a craftsman!” he shouts, and then continues in a smaller voice, “Even if people don’t really ‘get’ the things I make.”

Looking Around Vintage Gearworks.name: Looking Around Vintage Gearworks
Looking Around Vintage Gearworks.text:
Once they’ve talked to Krenvus and gained his favor, the PCs can investigate Vintage Gearworks on their own. While they search, Krenvus tells them that if they break something, they’ve bought it. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge,looking-around-vintage-gearworks|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[nature|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} or @Check[perception|dc:15|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} reveals one of these clues. A critical success reveals two.

  • One of the soldier windup toys appears to be rigged to strike someone, dealing a small amount of damage. Krenvus notes he would never do that to a children’s toy, so that must be something else the saboteurs rigged.

  • The tools reported missing would be used for precision crafting work.

  • Krenvus’ workshop has a small barrel in the corner marked “bottled lightning” and there are only three empty flasks. The inventor confirms that he thought he had a lot more and is surprised to see his supply exhausted.

  • Several of the items in the shop have been gnawed on by small but sharp teeth. The pattern appears humanoid.

If the PCs find at least two clues, they each get a +1 circumstance bonus to their next @UUID[.4iMnk44TCz0uxVOJ#deduce-saboteurs-identity]{Deduce Saboteur} check.

Effect

@UUID[Item.N1QoG8XukhDVQ7Yc]{Saboteur Deduction Bonus}

You can automate the aforementioned bonus by applying this effect on the character attempting the next Deduce Saboteur check.

Reward

For speaking with Krenvus and looking around his shop for clues, award each PC 75 XP.

Putting it All Together.name: Putting it All Together
Putting it All Together.text:
Once the PCs have a good sense of the saboteurs’ identity and motivation, it’s time to tell Father Wren their theories. If the investigation takes longer than two days, the priest sends Piotr to bring them over for another conversation in which he insists that they hurry up.

Father Wren is not pleased to hear any talk about gremlins. At first he insists it’s just adventurer nonsense or repeated superstition (perhaps suggesting that Otto’s influence has gotten to them). He’s a smart man and knows about gremlins and their predilection for wrecking machinery, but he’s simply never heard of them being in this part of Ustalav, much less in town. Father Wren ultimately relents after hearing or seeing some evidence (such as the claw and tooth marks on the other machines or the small footprint in the mud near the tollhouse), and he finds a mischief motivation easy to believe; it explains the “malice and randomness” of the sabotage he and others are experiencing.

Doubts aside, Father Wren believes the PCs to be ready for the most important step: doing something about this! The priest wants the culprits found and stopped quickly. He asks the PCs what they plan to do next. Before they leave the Gazette’s office, the priest would like a rudimentary plan for how they’ll find the captors.

Characters who are trained in Society understand that the saboteurs must be close by to access the sites and leave without being noticed or seen. They also know it’s likely the saboteurs do their work late at night. Father Wren accepts most plans, though he urges expediency.

Finding the Culprits.name: Finding the Culprits
Finding the Culprits.text:
The PCs can take two likely approaches: Search around town for the saboteurs or determine the most likely place they’ll strike again and stake that place out.

For the former plan, it takes two days to investigate the clues. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:15|options:action:gather-information|name:PF2E.Actions.GatherInformation.Title|traits:exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.plBGdZhqq5JBl1D8]{Gather Information}, @Check[stealth|dc:15|options:action:hide|traits:secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.XMcnh4cSI32tljXa]{Hide}, @Check[crafting|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] or @Check[nature|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge}, or @Check[survival|dc:15|options:action:track|name:PF2E.Actions.Track.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Track} speeds up this investigation. If at least half of the PCs succeed at one of the checks, it takes only a day to find the culprits. Critical successes count as two successes, and critical failures remove one success.

If they only take one day, the PCs deduce that Vintage Gearworks will be targeted at night. Krenvus is happy to let them stake out his shop, and even offers the PCs his @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.awtacA9swoKxH8fY]{Lucky Copper Coin} in hopes they can resolve this.

If the PCs take the full two days, they realize the target just as Vintage Gearworks is being broken into.

If the party chooses to stake out a location without having succeeded at the above checks, they can deduce the right place to stake out with a successful secret @Check[crafting|dc:17|traits:secret|options:deduce-location], @Check[nature|dc:17|traits:secret|options:deduce-location], or @Check[thievery|dc:17|traits:secret|options:deduce-location] check. If they achieved a critical success on either Deduce Saboteur’s Identity or Deduce Saboteur’s Motive, they get a +1 circumstance bonus to this roll. If they achieved critical successes on both, they get a +2 circumstance bonus to the roll.

A success leads that PC to stake out Vintage Gearworks, and they’re given the lucky copper coin as above. A failure doesn’t reveal where they should go, but the PCs can still choose any site. If they choose the Gazette, it leads directly to @UUID[.d5JtQQPebTDZ5D4f]{Battle at the Gazette} and the PCs get a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls. A critical failure leads that PC to stake out the tollhouse, where nothing happens all night. If the PCs have competing results, they should decide how to proceed.

Effect

@UUID[Item.GHvYFoljKPzIycHU]{Deduce Location}

Use this effect to automate the party's bonus to deduce the stake out location, if necessary.

If they stake out Vintage Gearworks, shortly after nightfall they hear giggling and banging noises. Some of Deeko’s henchmen are out to get a few more tools and smash more toys. Should the PCs approach, they’ll see a group of four diminutive figures stealing and breaking some of Krenvus’ repaired toys. This is a group of mitflits that Deeko sends to steal things for him. They notice the PCs immediately and make a run for their base, the entrance to which is nearby the Gazette’s office.

If the PCs give chase, have each PC attempt a @Check[acrobatics|dc:15], @Check[athletics|dc:15], or @Check[survival|dc:15] check. If at least half of the PCs succeed, they stay close enough to the gremlins to keep the pressure on them. When they turn around and make a stand in the Gazette’s office, the PCs each get a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative roll during Battle at the Gazette. Critical successes count as two successes, and critical failures remove one success from the total. If every PC critically fails, they are still able to follow the obvious trail of broken toys to the shop, but they take a –1 circumstance penalty to initiative against the prepared but cornered fey.

If they weren’t staking out the right place the first night or don’t go to the Vintage Gearworks when they realize it will be targeted again, Father Wren gets nervous and insists that they stake out the printing press the second night, leading into the Battle at the Gazette.

Reward

Krenvus gives the PCs his lucky copper coin if they stake out his shop.

Adapting to Players

It’s possible that the players have their characters take a path different than described here. That’s fine, and part of the fun of roleplaying games! Don’t spend too much time trying to force them into the printing press; if they have a clever plan that lets them get the drop on the thieves, you can have the @UUID[.d5JtQQPebTDZ5D4f]{Battle at the Gazette} there. If they manage to capture or trap the gremlins, give them an XP award as if they had fought them.

Battle at the Gazette.name: Battle at the Gazette
Battle at the Gazette.text:
Scene

@UUID[Scene.aW5sGJibg583T6qf]{The Grayce Gazette}

You can find our provided map for the Grayce Gazette in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

If the PCs start the battle at the end of the chase, read or paraphrase the following.

The tiny saboteurs sprint down the unlit roads of Grayce, eventually darting into the Grayce Gazette, whose doors are unexpectedly open. Once there, they get halfway inside before they spin around, drawing their short swords to make a stand.

If the PCs are staking out the Gazette, the mitflits attempt to sneak in through a hole they’ve cut in the roof (they keep a patch over it to hide their handiwork). If any PCs are inside the Gazette, read the following.

In rapid succession, three things happen: Moonlight peeks in through the roof of building, a rope unfurls from the roof, and four tiny figures slide down the rope into the building.

Upon noticing they have company, one of the figures says “Um…oops?” as the group draws their weapons.

Effects

@UUID[Item.2SkGy5VVpzvQefYT]{Battle Initiative Bonus} @UUID[Item.JXUXABO1c4X5RBtd]{Battle Initiative Penalty}

Depending on the party's actions in @UUID[.lGPaqlgcv16odHbp]{Finding the Culprits}, they might have a bonus or penalty to their initiative in the following encounter. Use these effects to automate whichever modifier applies.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.7nuZgjdKgHZik7UO]{Mitflit Thieves x4}

Creatures: The four mitflits have been sent by Deeko to get the last component needed to greatly increase the Dig Beast’s efficiency. They’ve mostly gotten tired of Deeko’s project, but knowing they are near the end of it has made this group enthusiastic and eager to complete it. The crew fights until only one of them is left standing. That survivor quickly surrenders.

Interrogating the Mitflits: Any survivors initially refuse to reveal information about the big plan.
