A PC who succeeds at a @Check[deception|dc:15|options:action:lie|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie} or @Check[intimidation|dc:15|options:action:coerce|name:PF2E.Actions.Coerce.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce} gets the fey to reveal their given task: Get the last part their boss Deeko needs to exact his revenge on the town.

The mitflits don’t really know what he wants revenge for, but they can tell the PCs how he plans to get revenge—make Grayce collapse into a huge hole. Deeko has been sending them to get parts to complete his big digging machine, which he calls “the Dig Beast.” It’s already begun digging, but he needs this part to “make it faster. Really a lot super faster.”

If the PCs promise to let them leave (they are happy to abandon Deeko’s weird project), the survivors tell the PCs about a hidden entrance located in a bush close to the Gazette that leads to the underground dig site.

Finding Deeko’s Dig: If there are no survivors or the PCs can’t get the remaining mitflits to talk, they find on one of the mitflits a piece of paper containing a detailed, meticulously drawn picture of the piece they were sent to steal. In childish handwriting next to the picture is a message: “Bring this back to the hole outside the press building.” Deeko makes these notes to ensure that the mitflits steal the right items, a common problem when they first started building the Dig Beast. On the back of this note is a sketchily drawn map of the town. The group of gremlins finds the layout of Grayce a little confusing and they commonly get lost on their thieving incursions, so they created this map to help them find their way. The map highlights where the entrance to the dig site is, and the PCs can use this note to determine its location. Without the map, they find the well-hidden entrance after an hour of searching, but all gremlins now have a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls, since their friends are taking so long.

Overview (6DJb).name: Overview
Overview (6DJb).text:
Scene

@UUID[Scene.7sZrHoO5cGEYPUgJ]{The Dig Site}

You can find our provided map for the Dig Site in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

The entrance to the underground site of the dig is a hole near a set of bushes near the Grayce Gazette. A grass-covered wooden hatch conceals the hole. A wooden ladder of dubious construction descends 15 feet into the ground.

The dig site is not lit, as the gremlins possess darkvision. Unless noted otherwise, the ceilings are about 10 feet high. Deeko has not supported the tunnels or other openings well, meaning they are prone to collapse. They are especially dangerous for non-gremlins who pass through, since the tunnels are suffused with unluck from the pugwampis in the area. Every area marked A2 includes the unlucky collapsing tunnels hazard.

Deeko taught the gremlins here Common as a part of his elaborate plan to further taunt the townspeople and ensure they understand his machinations when the time finally comes.

Effect

@UUID[Item.9yurWcX4mxp8qe8X]{Gremlin Initiative Bonus}

If the party fails to find the mitflit's map in @UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW.JournalEntryPage.d5JtQQPebTDZ5D4f]{Battle at the Gazette} and take too long to arrive at the Dig Site as a result, all gremlins here gain a +1 circumstance bonus to initiative. Drag this effect onto any gremlin tokens to automate this bonus.

Entrance.name: Entrance
Entrance.text:
It seems that half of Grayce’s trash has somehow ended up in this recently excavated area. Old food and discarded gear are strewn around haphazardly, piled in a few corners but also generously spread over the center of the room itself. In the northern wall are two small tunnels about two feet in diameter. Opposite them is a similar tunnel on the southern wall. A larger tunnel exits to the east.

Encounter

Low 2

@UUID[Actor.RgwOPXmjTh8AGWkt]{Guard Rats x3}

Creatures: This area is home to three especially large and vicious giant rats that Deeko initially planned to use to enact his tunneling plot. Deeko soon learned that the rats were neither efficient diggers nor were they easy to train and use for his purposes. He decided to let the rats be useful in other ways, to act as guards in case any non-gremlins started snooping around. The rats come sniffing out of the tunnels shortly after the PCs arrive. Deeko’s crew knows to give them food and to quickly run past them. If a PC offers the rats food, they eat it for 2 rounds before attacking the adventurers, looking for a larger meal. They don’t follow if the PCs move into area @UUID[.hSkQYvUsnv2RIvi8]{A3} while they are eating.

Unlucky Collapsing Tunnels.name: Unlucky Collapsing Tunnels
Unlucky Collapsing Tunnels.text:
Deeko knows that he’s supposed to support tunnels and caves as he builds them, but Deeko also knows he intends to collapse these walls in on themselves. Not intending to work against his own plans, he’s provided minimal support for the tunnel ceilings, just enough for his crew to maneuver around. Unfortunately for non-gremlins, the pugwampis’ unluck auras have suffused the area, making the tunnels more likely to collapse when a creature who isn’t part of the crew traverses them. Each spot marked A2 on the map represents a place where the PCs must navigate this hazard.

Encounter

Trivial 2

@UUID[Actor.b1W2rT4jjiRmCqXL]

Alerting Others: Whenever a tunnel collapse is triggered, the inhabitants of nearby rooms are alerted, giving them time to set up an ambush or to be prepared for the PCs when they approach.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.wk2DzvyILgq2h6Yw]{Collapse Tunnels}

We've provided a handy tool to easily locate each unlucky tunnel and trigger it to collapse. To use it, simply run the macro linked above!

Reward

When the PCs successfully navigate a collapsing tunnel, award them 20 XP each.

Salvage Processing.name: Salvage Processing
Salvage Processing.text:
Large piles of collected junk and rubble line these walls. In the center of the southern alcove is a mound containing tools as well as scraps of wood, broken pottery, copper, and iron. A broken bench forms a makeshift barrier for the alcove.

This is an area where the mitflits process the salvage they get for Deeko. After a few unfortunate incidents where they didn’t get Deeko the proper item, the mitflits take their time comparing what they got to the description or picture that Deeko provided them with. Anything they aren’t sure about they leave here and tell Deeko they weren’t able to locate it.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.kkAllKGsVCZVGFpf]{Mitflits x2} @UUID[Actor.aeOzCBpwnUVcpqxI] @UUID[Actor.6wPW2dvpt86Ou6bL]

Creatures: A group of mitflits and their pugwampi “commander” are here waiting for the previous group that the PCs encountered. They are nervous, but they’re doing their best to keep themselves occupied by playing games with the swarm of rats they’ve befriended. Each mitflit takes a piece of food out of their pouch and throws it in a different area of the chamber to see which one the rat swarm goes after, thus determining which mitflit is the rats’ favorite.

If alerted, the gremlins will position themselves behind the desk, fighting from there while the swarm attacks the PCs. Otherwise, the gremlins and the rat swarm are in the center of the room when the PCs approach. The gremlins attempt to flee if one of them is killed.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.Ty9dFIoIJ8Yx4lmz]

In the pile of materials in the southern alcove, the adventurers find a mechanical torch and two oils of potency.

Break Room.name: Break Room
Break Room.text:
This cavern reeks of rotten food and moist soil. Large outcroppings of stone jut out of the dirt walls, providing more support than the flimsy metal rods placed in the corners of the carved-out space. A large tunnel forks into two smaller tunnels in the north of the room, while another tunnel winds to the west.

The jinkin and pugwampi diggers that Deeko originally brought on to do the digging for his grand plan use this room to take a break. Once Deeko learned how slow the gremlins are at digging, he’s mostly been using the Dig Beast, leaving these workers bored and hungry for mischief.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.qJmbUbWxfNf2xuXo]{Jinkin Foremen x2} @UUID[Actor.aeOzCBpwnUVcpqxI]{Pugwampi Digger}

Creatures: The two jinkins here were supposed to supervise the others, but with little to do, they are only “supervising” one of their pugwampi diggers. The jinkins are pretending to play a game with Harrow cards that the pugwampi stole, but they don’t know the rules and are merely berating their co-worker at random intervals and playing hands that don’t do anything. When the PCs get their attention, they eagerly join the fight. The jinkin won’t retreat, but the pugwampi will do their best to escape to area @UUID[.7BYiGiXLG444nFq8]{A5} once the jinkin are defeated.

If captured, neither of the jinkin can be made to confess anything useful, but the pugwampi pleads for the PCs to let them go, playing innocent with pleas of “They made me do it!” If the PCs let the pugwampi go, the scared gremlin warns them about the “Not-Dig-Beast” saying, “it doesn’t dig, it just hurts things.” The pugwampi then leaves the tunnels and flees Grayce, sick of this whole endeavor.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.mXcCZxiVsAMRpXTE]

Besides the filthy and incomplete deck of Harrow cards, the PCs find a tiny pouch packed with 25 sp tucked underneath a makeshift table. On the ground next to it is a pair of purple embroidered charlatan’s gloves the jinkins hadn’t gotten around to cursing yet and misplaced.

Junk Room.name: Junk Room
Junk Room.text:
Three large heaps of organic and inorganic trash take the role of support beams in this room. The western wall is mold-encrusted stone, while the eastern wall is mostly packed dirt. In the center of the room is a large pit, about 10 feet wide and just as deep. Tunnels leave this room from the north and the south.

This room is where the crew keeps their trash, though lately they have been putting little effort into it maintaining a clean environment. The pit in the room is 10 feet deep and is full of broken glass and shards of scrap metal; anyone falling in this pit takes an additional 1d6 piercing damage (for a total of @Damage[1d6[piercing],5[bludgeoning]|options:fall-damage|shortLabel|name:Junk Pit] falling damage).

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.nPlMWJjZvq8hH03P]{Jinkin Digging Crew x2}

Creatures: There are two burly (by gremlin standards) jinkin diggers here, hiding from the foremen. They have been digging the hole to make themselves look busy and to play a prank on the their bosses that will hopefully get them to leave the pair alone for good.

If the PCs trigger a tunnel collapse or make excessive noise (a fight in area @UUID[.imHOBp2WA4IsoY1i]{A4} is insufficient as they assume it’s the foremen causing trouble with the other crew and getting what’s coming to them), the diggers try to hide behind the large heaps of trash and push the PCs in. During the fight, the diggers attempt to shove opponents into the pit. They pair up and attack the least armored foes they can reach. They don’t retreat but also don’t chase escaping PCs.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.8c6AcOrx9TQRAhsU]

One of the diggers has a +1 dogslicer on him. In the trash is a consumed aeon stone and a tarnished silver drinking stein with several semiprecious stones inlaid in the shape of a raven. Once cleaned, it is worth 4 gp.

Failed Experiment.name: Failed Experiment
Failed Experiment.text:
The northern stone wall of this large cavern has large gouges in it that look like scars. Small amounts of rubble rim the wall where a strange wooden cart sits. A thick wooden post juts out from the back of the cart; connected to the post is a horizontal beam with three additional wooden prongs, making a shape that resembles a fork. What appear to be shovel blades are attached to each of the prongs by chains. A makeshift engine is attached to the post from the cart’s undercarriage.

The cavern has two exits to the south and opposing exits to the west and east.

Encounter

Low 2

@UUID[Actor.g7KYjnRII2x1b2Er]

This is the Deeko’s first attempt at creating a digging machine. The flail approach he took is not particularly effective for digging; it only excelled in injuring his crew. Frustrated but unwilling to dismantle his work, he left it in this chamber.

The jinkins thought it would be fun to curse the machine and make it chase the crew around. They did too good of a job cursing the machine, and now the crew only enters this room when they must, running by and hoping not to get caught by the whirling machine.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.0cn5sf1K5Umrrl8Q]

In the rubble near the cart’s starting position are two scrolls of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dINQzhqGmIsqGMUY]{Mending}.

Deeko's Workshop.name: Deeko's Workshop
Deeko's Workshop.text:
This cavern has been outfitted into an extensive, if unconventional, workshop. Outcroppings of rock are used as hooks to hang tools from, and crates full of tools, fasteners, and scraps sit atop large worktables of bolted-together scrap. A paper takes up most of the eastern worktable, its corners held down by machine parts. There are several old clockwork toys and weapons on the western worktable.

There are several oil puddles in the room, making a trail that leads to the southern cave exit from where a loud grinding and breaking noise emanates.

This is Deeko’s workshop, where he makes his devious devices and builds his prized creation—the Dig Beast. He’s been working furiously to get the Dig Beast operational, to the exclusion of all else. Deeko is possessed by his scheme and is currently operating his device in @UUID[.bk2HsVLYtpq5xM94]{A8}.

The paper on the worktable is a schematic of the Dig Beast. If the PCs take a look at it, read or paraphrase the following.

The careful detail of the schematic and the childlike scrawl of the words contrast each other on the page. The schematic details a wooden cart with large wheels wedged in between an impractically large engine and a large rolling drum with a several arrays of shovel blades attached to it.

Any character trained in Crafting realizes that this machine is barely operational (and certainly not practical).

Encounter

Low 2

@UUID[Actor.P7o55s94mfHBsNBu] @UUID[Actor.ECe2DkOgSSqXHBqv]

Creatures: Deeko left a pugwampi guard and his dog here to make sure no one interrupts his work. The pugwampi doesn’t want to be here but is scared to go into area @UUID[.WjSgJsyicsSOnPhi]{A6} because of the “Not-Dig-Beast.” The guard puts up resistance when the PCs enter but is hesitant to cause trouble and only fights if cornered. If the PCs demonstrate that it’s safe to enter area @UUID[.WjSgJsyicsSOnPhi]{A6}, the guard and his dog happily leave and travel far from Grayce. If forced to fight, the guard surrenders if his dog goes down or he is reduced to half of his Hit Points. If the PCs ask about Deeko, the guard tells them, “He’s a durtik, so he has the big brain! He’s doing big things! But… now he’s boring and all the mischief he promised us is nowhere.”

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.Ps7jPVtQKYgJTC4F]

On the table scattered among the toys and other weapons are flutterback windup wings.

Dig Site.name: Dig Site
Dig Site.text:
This enormous cavern is all newly dug, though it’s hard to tell the main direction in which the digging has taken place. To the south, east, and west are mounds of dirt where the stone was punctured and tunnels were started. Water drips from several places along the southern edge of the room.

Oil slicks dot the rocky floor, forming a trail that leads to an impossible-looking machine: a large wooden cart with scraps of metal ornamentally lashed to it, with a large engine attached to the rear and an iron rolling drum with shovel blade “teeth.” The machine is tearing up the southern wall, kicking up dirt and stone with the jagged drum.

Atop this device is a small creature with mottled gray and green skin and a tuft of white hair on his head and a long wispy white beard. He’s trying to control the machine but is having a difficult time getting it to go in a consistent direction. The creature hollers and it’s hard to note whether the sounds express joy or frustration.

The PCs can enter the room about 30 feet before the machine spins Deeko around and he notices them. When this happens, read or paraphrase the following.

The machine whips the rider around and he suddenly takes notice of his new visitors.

“Oh, so Grayce sends defenders of its shameful ways! I can happily crush you along with the rest of them!”

Encounter

Severe 2

@UUID[Actor.LxhDVR5SdzIpM2HK] @UUID[Actor.KTCbS1jKAl0alIoK]

Creatures: Deeko is all too happy to monologue with the PCs before entering combat. He’s proud of what he’s made and thinks his plan to collapse Grayce’s foundation and break the town is something worth being lauded over. Some questions the PCs might ask follow.

What did Grayce do to you?

“It’s simple! I left my great pranking toys around the town, expecting them to be picked up and all go off at once, causing ‘oopsies’ for everyone. I would dance to the sounds of a prank choir! But… I waited, and nothing. Your junk man, he found them and fixed them. How dare he? Where is professional courtesy and respect?”

What are you planning to do?

“The only reasonable thing to do when a professional is disgraced! I am going to cause Grayce to collapse under the weight of its own arrogance!”

Isn’t that a bit extreme?

“Clearly you have no pride in your work, or you’d be able to relate to my pain.”

After a bit of chatter and monologue, Deeko exclaims, “You are interrupting my work!” and starts a fight. The Dig Beast is charged up with cursed energy from Deeko and some of the jinkins, so it can operate on its own. The durtik shoots at range from atop it, targeting characters using ranged attacks or spellcasters.

Convincing Deeko: Deeko is too caught up in his plan to consider stopping, and he can’t be talked down initially. His little toy contraption plan failed and this escalation is the only balm that will soothe his hatred for Grayce.

Deeko fights furiously and to the death for his plan, or at least he intends to until things go even further astray. A PC can attempt to persuade Deeko to do change course in his actions and pursue something else. If the Dig Beast is destroyed or Deeko is reduced to 10 or fewer Hit Points, a PC can use an action to attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:20] or @Check[intimidation|dc:20] check. If successful, Deeko promises to mend his ways and leave Grayce. Deeko will likely get into trouble in some other place and might be a character the PCs run into again.

Concluding the Adventure.name: Concluding the Adventure
Concluding the Adventure.text:
Father Wren is happy to have the spate of sabotage end, but he insists on proof that there were actual gremlins involved. When provided this proof, he shakes his head, mutters something about the world getting stranger and stranger, and then asks the PCs to limit who they tell about this. The priest fears people in town might panic if they knew a pack of gremlins were digging holes to sink the entire town. He does encourage them to follow up with the people they talked to earlier in the adventure to let them know the problem is resolved. He thinks if anyone should know the truth, it should be those who were affected the most. He pays the PCs 30 gp each as promised and in appreciation he also offers them a few items that he no longer uses. He gives the party a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.RgNBGpBc9G2yw1C2]{Crafter’s Eyepiece} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.eurAnvH8bK0ZctOR]{Bracers of Missile Deflection}.

Krenvus Sang: If the PCs let Krenvus know what happened, he expresses relief that the sabotage troubles are over but he also expresses sadness that the interesting source of useful but broken items to fix is no longer available. He offers to do any repairs the players might need in the future.

Yvette Molan: Following up with Yvette, the mechanic nods sagely and throws herself back into her work, telling the PCs: “The only gremlins here are my never-ending deadlines!”

Otto Vaunier: If told about the gremlins, Otto interprets them as escaped machine spirits seeking revenge on the town, no matter how the PCs attempt to explain it. He finds comfort that the spirits are gone but also sees this as further proof that machinery in town is causing problems. “The machines will have their revenge on us one day,” he says.

Mariv Sonnal: “This goes deeper than I thought, but I admit I’m surprised it’s gremlins and not part of some greater plan,” Mariv responds when told about Deeko and his crew. The toll collector pulls out her journal and starts making notes, submitting the PCs to rapid-fire questioning to gather more information to sate her curiosity.

Temple of the Unlit Star.name: Temple of the Unlit Star
Temple of the Unlit Star.text:
Being a Game Master

As the Game Master, you get to work with all the other players to see how the story of the adventure unfolds. While they’ll each play their individual heroes, you’ll assume the role of all the monsters, villagers, and other characters that they encounter. You decide how those people and monsters act, what they do in combat, and what intriguing clues they might give to the heroes. You’ll also describe each area the heroes explore so the other players can imagine the setting and decide how their heroes respond to what’s going on around them. These are the tools you use to help shape the story with the other players.

It’s important to remember that you’re not playing against the other players. This is a game where everyone wins if everyone has a fun time. Monsters are meant to be defeated, and treasure is there to be found. Try to make the players feel like they’ve earned their success without being too tough on the heroes they’re playing.

The First Adventure

If you’re the Game Master and you want to play with your friends right now, start with this adventure. It walks you and the other players through how to play, giving you a chance to learn together.

This adventure is designed to be played by four 1st-level heroes, but it will work for two or three heroes with only a few slight adjustments. Each player can build their own hero, or pick one of the pregenerated heroes included in this module.

Using a Pregenerated Hero

If any of your players wishes to use one of the Pregenerated Heroes, navigate to the folder containing them inside the "Temple of the Unlit Star" folder in the actors tab of your right sidebar. You can bring up the right-click menu on any of the characters and then click on "Configure Ownership" to give a player ownership over that character.

Give the players 10–15 minutes to look over their character sheets so they can learn how their characters work. During this time, you should read through the @UUID[.fGXZ88z1Zhy2qgRE]{introduction} and @UUID[.4gbSE10YHvpHCQQu]{first encounter} pages to get ready to run them.

Running This Adventure

“Temple of the Unlit Star” is designed to teach new Game Masters and players how to play Pathfinder. Each section of the adventure will teach new concepts as you need them, adding more and more to the game. Meanwhile, the other players each have an entire hero to roleplay as, learning how to use their abilities and how to succeed in the dangerous world they find themselves exploring.

This adventure, like most published adventures, is presented as a series of areas to explore and challenges to face. Each one is tied to a location on the map of the dungeon and coded with a number. The dungeon in this adventure consists of two levels.

As the game proceeds, the players can move their tokens around the map as they explore the dungeon. Whenever the heroes enter a new area of the map, refer to the section in this book that corresponds to the number on the map. Each entry begins with a brief introduction so you know what to expect, followed by text set in brown for you to read aloud. The rest of the area’s text includes all the information you need about what the heroes will come across in this area. This text contains spoilers for the room—it gives you information about the challenges the heroes face as they explore the area. If the area includes combat, traps, hazards, or treasure, the rules for those are in this journal or linked for you to easily access.

As they move through the temple’s levels, the players will use their heroes’ skills and abilities to explore the area and overcome its obstacles. It’s likely they’ll have questions and try actions that aren’t covered by the rules presented here. As the GM, you get to make up the answers and decide what happens, but always try to be fair, and remember that the goal of the game is for everyone to have a fun time. You should encourage the heroes to try new things as they learn, but don’t forget that, as new adventurers, their heroes’ abilities are limited.

If the players get stuck or confused about what to do next, you can give them a few hints or ideas to get them started, like “Do you want to open the door?” or “Who wants to look for hidden treasure?” Remember that this is their first game, too, and they will have more fun if everyone is participating.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
Once everyone is ready to begin, start by reading the text block below to set the scene.

You are all young travelers with dreams of becoming adventurers. The life of an adventurer is one of excitement, riches, and most of all, danger! You’ve left your home in search of an opportunity and are now traveling along the Path River in the eerie nation of Ustalav. The river’s route has led you past the small village of Grayce, perhaps the very village you came from originally! Regardless of where you began your journey, you soon find yourself in a small marshland along the river’s edge.

While you can’t explain it, you get a feeling that something is amiss within the marsh. It’s almost as if you hear an inexplicable voice calling you deeper into the area. Despite your initial reservations, you know that this is your opportunity for adventure! You continue to follow the voice that may or may not be calling to you and eventually stumble upon the ruins of a large stone building. The ruins consist of two chambers: an entryway and a larger chamber with several pedestals surrounding an altar at its center. The image of a large butterfly is carved into the altar and almost appears to glow with starlight. The pedestals each seem to have a weapon or other item like a staff resting upon them, as well as a parcel wrapped in leather.

The pedestals draw your attention and you enter the chamber. As you do, the ground beneath your feet begins to rumble. An earthquake! Before you can react, the floor beneath you falls away and you watch as the pedestals and altar are swallowed up by a massive sinkhole. As you try to escape, the sinkhole grows larger and you fall into the darkness below!

Scene

@UUID[Scene.CXf8roZuSpOaAJjx]{Temple of the Unlit Star}

After reading this introduction, you can find the Temple of the Unlit Star scene on the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar (the map icon). Right-click it to bring up the context menu, and click the "Activate" option. You can then place the party's tokens in area @UUID[.4gbSE10YHvpHCQQu]{A1}, where the lift has collapsed into this lower floor. Once all the tokens are placed, go to @UUID[.4gbSE10YHvpHCQQu]{A1}.

The first floor of the temple introduces a number of challenges for your heroes to overcome. As they explore, they’ll find that they’re in a temple to Desna that’s been sunk deep into the earth by a dark force, and their only hope of returning to the surface lies in reforging a mystical artifact. The heroes will have to explore the first floor to recover the artifact’s shattered pieces before fighting a powerful guardian and making their way to the temple’s next floor!

Crashed Lift.name: Crashed Lift
Crashed Lift.text:
Pulling yourselves to your feet, you find yourselves in a cylindrical room. The rubble from the earthquake has lodged overhead, the grinding boulders forming a makeshift ceiling about ten feet high. The faintest bits of light filter through, but the surface is impossibly far away. You’re trapped deep underground.

Go around the table and ask each player the first thing they want their hero to do. As each player describes their action, allow them to move their token around this area, but don’t let them leave this first room just yet.

In the chaos of the fall, the player characters’ gear was dislodged from their packs and scattered around the room, requiring them to take a moment to collect it all; this is a good opportunity to encourage the players to look over the gear lists on their character sheets and take stock of what’s available to them. As they collect their things, have the players introduce their heroes with their name, ancestry, background, and class, along with any other details about their character they want to share. Players might want to describe what their hero looks like, what kind of gear they carry, and maybe a bit about their personality.

After each hero has had a chance to introduce themselves and collect their respective equipment, the rubble shifts above their heads as giant centipedes, attracted by the earthquake, emerge to attack! Read the following out loud.

A loud scratching begins to echo through the chamber. By what little light is in this room, you see a mass of skittering legs making their way through cracks in the ceiling. Three enormous centipedes climb down the walls with surprising speed. The moment they reach the sunken floor, they begin to rush toward you, their mandibles snapping!

The First Combat

Low 1

@UUID[Actor.NRBgcu0LkXXp8mtp]{Giant Centipedes x3}

The heroes are now in combat with three giant centipedes. In combat, each player takes turns and follows specific rules about what they can and can’t do.

The giant centipedes’ statistics are can be viewed by clicking on the giant centipedes' link in the block above, as well as by double-clicking their tokens on the map.

The centipedes act on instinct, without thought for advanced tactics. On their turn, each centipede moves toward a different hero and attacks. If a hero falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, the centipede moves to the next nearest and attacks. Driven by hunger, the centipedes will attack until slain or incapacitated.

Combat and Initiative

Once you've located the giant centipede tokens in the map, you can start your first combat as follows:

  • Reveal the centipede tokens on the map by selecting them, right-clicking on one, and clicking "Toggle Visibility State."

  • Drag select the tokens for the centipedes and the heroes. Right click one of them, and choose "Toggle Combat State."

  • This will create an encounter and add your tokens to the combat tracker. You can quickly roll initiative for all the centipedes by clicking the "Roll NPCs" button, which is the second button at the top of the initiative tracker.

  • You can then allow each player to roll initiative for their hero, either by clicking the die next to their hero's name on the tracker or from their character sheets.

As a tip, if you right click on the "Encounters" tab icon (the crossed swords) on your right sidebar. This will pop out the encounter tracker and let you position it wherever you'd like while being able to keep the chat as your active sidebar tab.

Striking and Armor Class

When a creature uses the Strike action to make an attack, first pick a target within the reach (or range) of your Strike. Then, you can hover over a token and press 'T' on your keyboard to designate it as a target. You can also click the targeting button on the token menu.

To attack using the giant centipedes' Mandibles Strike, open its character sheet by clicking on the giant centipedes' token. Under the Attacks section, you can click on the "Strike (+6)" button in the Attacks section of the sheet listed below the Mandibles attack. This will open a dialog box asking if there are any modifiers that need to be applied. Since we have none, you may simply click "Roll (+6)" to confirm.

As long as a target is set, the system will compare your result to the target's AC automatically, and you will be able to see it in the chat, along with buttons to roll the resulting damage, if any. It even takes into account things like flanking! This automation can save a lot of time for the GM, but it's always worth checking to make sure you didn't forget a modifier from something like cover.

If you roll a 20 on the die, or the total is at least 10 more than the target's Armor Class, it’s a critical hit! These deal twice as much damage and are marked green in the chat card.

To roll damage, click the "Damage" button in the same chat card that showed the result of your Strike (or "Critical" if the attack as a critical hit). Once the damage appears in the chat log, you can select the token affected and click the appropriate button beneath the damage total to apply the damage.

Experience Points

For starting their heroic journey, give each hero 20 XP. For defeating the giant centipedes, give each hero 60 XP

After Combat

Once one side is defeated or flees, you can stop tracking actions and the heroes no longer need to act in order. Instead, go around the table and ask the players what the heroes would like to do next. When the players decide to explore beyond this room, proceed to @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.on1towphTAWHfcAX]{A2}.

Shadowed Balcony.name: Shadowed Balcony
Shadowed Balcony.text:
This long balcony will give your players a chance to experience combat in a more open environment than the cramped area that they started in. You’ll need two umbral gnome scout pawns from the box. When the heroes enter this area, read or paraphrase the following.

The creaking of the door echoes off the walls of this long balcony as you enter. Lightly glowing mushrooms under two rows of cracked stone pews cast the room in a pale blue light, though it fails to penetrate a curtain of darkness to the east, which ripples like oil. At the distant end of the balcony, a fire flickers, two creatures dancing about it.

This room appears to be a balcony of some kind, though whatever the balcony is meant to view is obscured by a shadow veil. This is one of several manifestations of a foul darkness hanging over this temple that the heroes will encounter. The veil blocks all light and passage. If a hero falls into the shadow (or attempts to enter it), they experience a complete void of senses and a sensation of vertigo before they are ejected from it a moment later, returning to the space they entered from. As the heroes progress through the temple, they’ll find ways to cross these veils, but they are unable to at the moment.

When the heroes enter the balcony, the umbral gnomes are on the other side at the indicated location, cooking around a fire. The combination of the fire and the glowing mushrooms basks the balcony in a dim light. Give the heroes a moment to look around the area as they enter, but roll initiative immediately thereafter—the gnomes attack as soon as they hear the door loudly creak open.

Umbral Gnome Fight

Trivial 1

@UUID[Actor.a9Zlz4FINRa6imky]{Weak Umbral Gnome Scout x2}

This fight uses the same rules as the fight against the centipedes, but the larger area means range and positioning will come into play—the @UUID[Actor.a9Zlz4FINRa6imky]{umbral gnomes} at the other end of the balcony will pelt the heroes with sling bullets, and the heroes will need to either respond with ranged attacks and spells or quickly close the gap to engage the gnomes in melee.

The heroes might try to reason with the gnomes to reach a peaceful solution, but sadly, that won’t be possible. Heroes who take time to study the gnomes notice a darkness filling their eyes and extending through their veins, signs that they’ve been completely overtaken by whatever evil permeates this temple. The gnomes fight until they are slain or incapacitated.

Ranged Combat

Unlike the previous area, this balcony is large, and the heroes and the umbral gnomes start on opposite sides. This means that the heroes (and their enemies) will need to either attack at range or spend some actions Striding into melee range. The umbral gnomes in this room prefer to attack using their slings, which allows them to make a ranged Strike.

Unlike a melee Strike, the gnomes don’t have to be adjacent to a hero to target them with a ranged Strike—they can target a hero anywhere in the room, though if the target is outside their 50-foot range increment, they’ll do so with a –2 penalty. Otherwise, a ranged Strike works just like a melee Strike. Choose a target for the umbral gnome to attack by hovering over that target's token and pressing "T" on your keyboard, click on the "Strike (+7)" button under the Sling attack in the Attacks section of the umbral gnome's sheet. The umbral gnomes’ slings have reload 1, which means that after they make a sling Strike, they cannot attack with their sling again until they have spent 1 action to reload it. If the heroes move into melee range against the gnomes, the gnomes will attempt to attack with their sickles instead.

Experience Points

For defeating the gnomes, give each hero 40 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

Once combat is finished, the heroes might have a chance to look around the balcony. Further examination of the stone pews reveals that each has a drawer under the seat with a hymnal in it. Though all of the books have long since been consumed by mold and decay, it is clear that this is a temple and has been here, undisturbed, for some time.

The Malfunctioning Lift.name: The Malfunctioning Lift
The Malfunctioning Lift.text:
After making their way through the shadowed balcony, the heroes can pass through the door on the other side. Once the first hero has entered the room, read the following aloud.

The solid stone floor creaks and bounces ever so slightly as you enter. This cylindrical room is a counterpart to the room you first came to your senses in, but in a much better state of repair, with silver etchings of constellations covering the walls. A stone panel sits in the center of the room, dust covering magical runes and inlaid on its clockwork mechanisms.

This room is one of two lifts used to move up to the balcony. While this room isn’t totally collapsed, the magical controls needed to operate the lift have been damaged. A triangular silver crystal rests on a pedestal in the center of a stone panel, pulsing with a faint magical light. Three large, dull runes are inscribed around the crystal, linked to it by magical inscriptions in silver ink, though each inscription is partially scuffed out. On the side of the panel is a hand crank and several delicate brass gears, some of which are dented and missing.

Skill Checks

Combat won’t get the heroes past the broken lift—instead, they’ll need to use their skills, attempting skill checks to investigate and repair the mechanism so they can descend. When a character attempts a skill check, they can open their character sheet, go to the skills tab (the "open hand" icon) and click on the appropriate skill. Compare the total to the Difficulty Class (or DC) of the task to determine whether or not they succeed. As with attack rolls, characters can get critical successes and critical failures on skill checks.

For this challenge, the heroes can attempt to either delicately repair or tinker with the gears using @Check[crafting|dc:15] or @Check[thievery|dc:15] skill checks, wrench the mechanisms back on track or crank the lift manually with an @Check[athletics|dc:15] check, or repair the magical runic circle using an @Check[arcana|dc:15] or @Check[occultism|dc:15] check. Have each hero roll one check of their choice.

Critical Success (The die roll was a 20 or the total was 25 or more.) The hero is especially effective at repairing the lift—silver light flows from the crystal and lights up two runes.

Success (The result of the check was 15 or more.) The hero makes some progress in repairing the lift, lighting up one rune.

Failure (The result of the check is less than 15.) The hero’s efforts fail to make any headway. There is no change to the runes’ light.

Critical Failure (The die roll was a 1 or the total was 5 or less.) The hero damages the lift’s mechanism! One rune’s light goes out.

Skills and Checks

You may have noticed that the skill checks above are actually buttons! Clicking one while you have a token selected will use that creature's statistics to resolve the check, comparing it with the listed DC—in this case, a DC of 15. The resulting chat card will take into account the selected token's modifiers and calculate the degree of success automatically.

Of course, ideally, you'd want your players to be able to roll that check. While you can still ask for the appropriate skill check and compare the result to the DC yourself, another option is to press the speech bubble icon on the right side of the check button. This will post the button to chat without sharing any of the GM-only text that surrounds it, allowing your players to easily roll their skill checks without risk of spoilers!

Track how many of the lift’s runes the party can light up. If the party can light up all three runes, they successfully repair the lift—go to the “Success” heading below! If they didn’t light up all the runes they can attempt additional checks until they do. However, if they get a critical failure while none of the runes are lit up, then read the “Failure” entry below instead.

Success

If the heroes light up all three lights, they successfully repair the panel! Read the following as the heroes ride the lift down to the ground floor.

As the final light shines, the sounds of grinding stone echo throughout the lift. The door disappears as the floor descends, rotating clockwise. After half a minute, the platform reaches a lower level, a new door leading out into a darkened hallway.

From here, the heroes can proceed deeper into the temple, entering area A4. Having repaired the control mechanism, the heroes can also return to the balcony by riding the lift back up, as long as the magical crystal remains on the pedestal.

Failure

If the heroes have none of the three lights lit up and get a critical failure, they fail to repair the panel and in fact cause it to malfunction. They’ll still make it down to the rest of the temple, but the trip will be a bit less smooth than they might like. Read or paraphrase the following:

The control fizzles as all three light comes on briefly—before the runes spark and burn out in a crackle that smells of ozone. With a lurch, the floor drops out, crashing against the sides of the lift shaft before smashing into the ground in a cloud of dust.

As the floor falls, roll @Damage[1d6[bludgeoning]|shortLabel|options:fall-damage] to determine how much bludgeoning damage the heroes take as the floor hits the ground. After they pick themselves up, they can proceed deeper into the temple. If the heroes wish to return to the balcony, they’ll need to climb up the rubble in the lift shaft, which they can do with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:15] check. When attempting the check to climb up the shaft, a failure results in a lack of progress, while a critical failure causes a hero fall from the wall and take another @Damage[1d6[bludgeoning]|options:fall-damage] damage.

Experience Points

Once the heroes have all made it down (one way or another), give each hero 80 XP for plying their skills to repair the lift.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.3cCSoQqrsGZMvSXt]

The crystal on the pedestal is a star shard, one of several fragments of a powerful magical crystal, the unlit star, which the heroes will find (and reforge) later in this temple. Though this shard has enough magic in it to operate this small lift, it has no other abilities by itself. Heroes who succeed at a @Check[arcana|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:secret], @Check[nature|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:secret], @Check[occultism|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:secret], or @Check[religion|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} learn that the shard is but one fragment of a broken magical crystal, which contains a small fraction of light-based magic and power, but no other information.

The heroes might choose to take the star shard from the lift mechanism for safekeeping. If they don’t, you can always give them a light reminder of the shard once they gain the unlit star later in the temple, since they’ll eventually need it to progress.

The South Hallway.name: The South Hallway
The South Hallway.text:
As the heroes emerge from the lift, they’ll find themselves on the main floor of the temple. Get the magnetic skink pawns from the box, but don’t place them on the map just yet. Read or paraphrase the following

In the dim light streaming from the lift room, you see a short hallway stretching out from the lift, the stone tiles covered with ages of dust. A set of doors is visible to the south, and a hall to the north. To the east, another curtain of darkness ripples ominously. The air hangs still as death.

This hallway simply connects some of the southern rooms of the temple, but the shadow veil blocks passage further to the east. As the heroes enter the hall, two magnetic skinks climb down from the walls. The metal attached to their bodies scrapes against the wall and fill the hallway with a horrid scratching! The heroes and the skinks should roll Perception for initiative.

Skink Fight

Low 1

@UUID[Actor.yb3ZUPctOGz3yQTS]{Magnetic Skink x2}

This fight with the skinks will begin to introduce monsters with more advanced abilities. The magnetic skinks scamper forward to attack the closest hero. The magnetic skinks should attempt to position themselves so that when they use their Launch Metal ability, they catch multiple heroes at once, and they’ll each wait to use their Launch Metal to try to affect as many heroes as possible. After using Launch Metal, a skink uses its Unsteadying Magnetism on a nearby target wearing or holding metal, and then moves in to bite them with their jaws attack. The magnetic skinks fight to the death.

Creature Abilities

Monsters have special abilities just like the heroes do. Some of these require the monster to use its actions, while others are passive (they’re always on and don’t require any particular action from the monster). If the ability has an action icon next to it, that’s how many actions it takes for the monster to use, and if it doesn’t, then that ability is always in effect.

Saving Throws and Conditions

There’s more ways to attack a target than by swinging a sword at it, so AC isn’t the only defense that a creature (or one of the players’ heroes) has—creatures also have three types of saving throws: a Fortitude save, typically for physically resisting an effect through the strength of your body (like the unsteadying magnetism of these skinks, or a poison or disease); a Reflex save for dodging away from falling debris or avoiding explosions and other bursts of damage; and a Will save for resisting effects that target the mind or soul, like intense fear or mind-addling magic.

Abilities that call for a saving throw will say which of the three saving throws they require, as well as a DC. When a hero is subjected to one of these abilities, they roll a d20 and then add the relevant modifier. As with attack rolls and skill checks, characters can get critical successes and critical failures on saving throws, with effects depending on the outcome. Many damaging abilities that use saving throws use a basic saving throw, which has the following outcomes:

Critical Success You take no damage from the effect.

Success You take half the listed damage from the effect.

Failure You take the full damage listed from the effect.

Critical Failure You take double the listed damage from the effect.

Special Abilities and Recharge

The skinks have two different abilities that make use of saving throws. The first is their Launch Metal ability, which can damage multiple creatures in an area. In this case, it can harm anyone adjacent to the skink. When a skink uses the ability, you can click on the ability on its sheet to expand its description, and then click on speech bubble next to the ability's Reflex saving throw. This will send the saving throw to chat, and you can ask any hero standing next to the skink to click on it to roll their Reflex saving throw. It’s also possible that the other skink will need to attempt the saving throw if it’s nearby! Once everyone has given their result, you can roll the damage for the ability. Effects like Launch Metal that can affect multiple creatures at once only require a single damage roll. Once you have the damage result, you can determine the final damage for each creature by using the results noted for basic saving throws above. If the result is 25 or higher, or they roll a 20 on the die, that’s a critical success and they take no damage. A result of 15 to 24 causes the creature to take half of the damage. A result of 6 to 14 causes the creature to take the full amount of damage. Finally, a result of 5 or lower, or rolling a 1 on the die, is a critical failure, and the creature takes double the damage you rolled. It’s possible for each hero to get a different result and take a different amount of damage.

While this is a powerful attack, a magnetic skink can’t use it continually. Once it uses the ability, the skink will be unable to use it again until the ability recharges. When the skink uses Launch Metal, roll 1d4—the ability will take that many full rounds to recharge (so if you roll a 1, it won’t be able to use Launch Metal next round, but it will be able to the round after that). This may be a good chance for the heroes to attack!

The Unsteadying Magnetism ability also requires a saving throw, but this doesn’t have varying results. Instead, the results are binary: the hero is either affected or they’re not. If they succeed on their saving throw, nothing happens. If they fail, the hero gains a condition, a special effect that adjusts the recipient’s statistics for as long as it remains. When a skink uses Unsteadying Magnetism, they target a hero within 20 feet (4 squares) and that hero must attempt a Fortitude saving throw by rolling a d20 and adding their Fortitude. If the result is equal to or greater than 15, they resist the Unsteadying Magnetism fully, but if the result is lower, the magnetic pull temporarily disorients the hero, giving them the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} condition until the skink’s next turn—this means they are slow to react to threats, so they take a –2 circumstance penalty to their Armor Class.

Experience Points

For defeating the magnetic skinks, give each hero 60 XP.

Lavatory.name: Lavatory
Lavatory.text:
This room is easy to see from the south hallway. When the heroes open the door, read the following aloud.

This lavatory contains two small basins for hand washing, as well as four simple stalls. A brass mirror hangs above the basins, though it is covered in dust, and a cupboard creaks at the end of the hall. The room is tidy, though it has obviously been unused in years, if not longer.

This is a simple lavatory. While this is a quieter room without any combats or major skill challenges, that doesn’t mean that the heroes can’t learn about their environment from exploring. Give the heroes a chance to search through this room. Some discoveries are below. Once they’ve found all the discoveries, feel free to explain that there isn’t anything else of note within the room.

  • Basins: A hero who examines the basins find a simple enchantment around the rim. Touching their hands to the bowl causes it to fill with pure water. A hero who succeeds at a @Check[arcana|dc:10|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[nature|dc:10|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], @Check[religion|dc:10|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret], or @Check[occultism|dc:10|options:action:identify-magic|name:PF2E.Actions.IdentifyMagic.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret]check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.eReSHVEPCsdkSL4G]{Identify Magic} recognizes that the bowls can produce more than enough water to supply the heroes with drinking water each day.

  • @UUID[Actor.tcsctXOG5Or6uxjD]{Cupboard:} The cupboard contains dust cloths, soap, and various cleaning supplies, including a few glass bottles. Though most have gone bad, there are 2 bottles of perfumed oils, which function as pints of oil. The heroes might have use for these later.

  • Mirror: The mirror is covered with a thick layer of dust. The first time the dust is wiped away, it reveals, for the briefest of moments, a face surrounded by shadows, with two smoking red orbs for eyes. The face fades in an instant, likely leaving the hero who wiped the mirror wondering if it was just their imagination.

  • Stalls: The stalls are tidy and featureless, though the third stall’s door is jammed shut and can’t be opened without a hero succeeding at a @Check[type:athletics|dc:10|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check. Inside is a small handwritten notebook. If a hero spends 10 minutes flipping through it, they find it is a simple to-do list and journal written by a “Brother Celluan.” The journal details, over several days, his fear of a wave of undead that has been making their way closer to the temple. On the back page is also a short number of lines written in Elven—heroes who can speak this language identify it as a short, heartfelt, and somewhat clumsily written love poem toward a woman named “Eina.”

Experience Points

For each discovery a hero finds, give all heroes 20 XP (a maximum of 80 XP).

Storage Rooms.name: Storage Rooms
Storage Rooms.text:
These rooms flank the hallway and can be easily opened. When the heroes open the first of the two rooms, read the following.

The wooden shelves lining these walls still stand, though barely, with cloth, crates, and barrels packed neatly around and beneath them. The smell of rot permeates the air.

Simple Trap

Trivial 1

@UUID[Actor.2XOgNOupUBGr6K6S]{Falling Shelves}

The first of the two rooms contains a simple hazard—the rickety shelves are in danger of collapsing!

When the heroes first enter this room, ask each player to roll a @Check[perception|dc:20] check. If anyone gets a result of 20 or higher, they notice that the shelves are badly compromised and in danger of toppling over. If they know the trap is there, a hero can attempt a @Check[athletics|dc:18] or @Check[thievery|dc:18] skill check, allowing them to either brace the shelves up or carefully take items from them. If they succeed, they disable the hazard and can interact with the shelves normally. If they fail, they can keep trying until they manage to disable it, but if they critically fail, they trigger the hazard and the shelves collapse, rolling a melee Strike against all heroes in the room. If any of these Strikes are critical hits, they deal double damage, just like any Strike. Afterward, the hazard poses no further harm, and the heroes can continue their exploration.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.6fnmsyDNkEihBx1k]{Collapse Shelves}

If the shelves collapse, use this macro to send them toppling down and play a sound effect.

Experience Points

Regardless of whether the heroes disable or trigger the hazard, give them each 20 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.3Aezm4RpFZWKqc7z] @UUID[Actor.Gpf1Kvqtem4MIX7e]

Though many of the items on the shelves have rotted away or gone bad, the heroes can find a flask of holy water and an elixir of life. If they fail to prevent the shelves from toppling over, both of these liquids dash against the floor, becoming unsalvageable.

The shelves in the second room are in much better repair. Here, the heroes easily find another elixir of life, as well as several sets of frayed priestly robes.

Worship Hall.name: Worship Hall
Worship Hall.text:
This room is the main hall of the temple, although foul undead have taken up residence in its once-holy halls. Take three skeleton guard pawns and one zombie shambler pawn from the box. When the heroes approach the ornate door to this area, have them roll a @Check[perception|dc:12] check; if any hero gets a 12 or higher, let the heroes know that they can hear a scraping sound from the other side of the door. When they enter, read the following:

Four stone columns surround a central dais marked with a butterfly. To the east, before the dais, stands a small altar with a dull stone sitting upon it. As you enter, four pairs of empty eye sockets turn hungrily to you, within heads at various states of decay. The living dead begin lurching toward you, their moans filling the air.

Undead Fight

Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.trchDxbDR2TiPMxT]{Skeleton Guards x3} @UUID[Actor.Xo4IGzw28hivgMmM]{Zombie Shambler}

Like for the other fights, first ask the players to roll Perception for initiative. The skeletons and zombie both roll Perception for initiative.

The heroes may find this to be a difficult fight. If they need to retreat and regroup, the undead do not pursue them out of this room.

Immunities, Weaknesses, Resistances

These undead have special rules that affect how they take damage. Both types of undead have immunities that prevent certain types of damage and abilities from affecting them. They aren’t affected by anything with the mental trait, they don’t take poison or bleed damage, and they can’t fall unconscious—even from effects with the nonlethal trait.

Skeletons have resistances that reduce the amount of damage they take from certain damage types. Each time a skeleton takes damage of a type listed in its Resistances entry, reduce the amount of damage it takes by the number after the type.

For example, if a hero hits a skeleton with a greatsword Strike and would deal 8 slashing damage, the skeleton would take only 3 damage, because its bones are resistant to slashing damage and reduce the damage by the listed value of 5.

The zombie also has weaknesses, which work in the opposite way. Whenever the zombie takes any damage of the listed types, increase the damage it takes by the number listed after it. For that same hero’s greatsword Strike that dealt 8 damage, the zombie would take 13 damage instead, because of the zombie’s weakness to slashing damage! The zombie has one more special ability called slow that represents their ponderous, staggering movements. A zombie can use only 2 actions on its turn each round instead of 3, and can’t use reactions at all!

"IWR" Automation

As you deal any of the damage types listed in the above explanation, you will find that immunities, weaknesses, and resistances are automatically calculated by the system! Whenever you see an information icon next to a "damage taken" message, you can hover over that icon to get a breakdown of what damage types were affected by this automation.

Heroes may find out about these weaknesses and resistances by observing combat. Describe the players attacks in ways that might let them pick up on this information, like “Your flames dance along the skeleton’s ribs, but the dry bones seem like they’re barely affected by your magic!” or “Your sword slashes through the zombie’s belly with barely any resistance, the wet flesh tearing even more than you expected!” Heroes can take an action to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about one of the undead in the room by attempting a @Check[religion|dc:13|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check; on a success, they learn about one of its immunities, weakness, or resistances (player’s choice), and on a critical success, they learn about two.

After the Fight

After the fight, the heroes can look around the room and investigate the altar. Upon it sits a dull crystal with a silver inscription, which reads, “Our precious unlit star, to shine in the darkest night.” The crystal seems like it should have eight points, but all but one are broken off, with rough seams at each missing point. The heroes can attempt a @Check[religion|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to attempt to Recall Knowledge, with the following results.

Critical Success As success, and they also learn that the Temple of the Unlit Star mysteriously vanished overnight many years ago. It is said that in times of great need, the magic of the temple’s artifact could lift the entire building into the heavens to protect it and its inhabitants from harm.

Success The Zenith Temple was a temple to Desna, the goddess of the stars, dreams, and travelers, formed to give aid to travelers crossing the haunted lands of Ustalav. The temple was also known as the Temple of the Unlit Star. Enshrined within the temple was the unlit star, a powerful artifact of the faith said to transform heroic will into light that could banish any shadow.

Failure The hero recalls nothing.

When a hero touches the crystal, the unlit star, it flares with silver light, illuminating the worship hall. If any undead are still in the hall when this happens, they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} for 1 round as they are dazed by the artifact’s holy light. The light dispels the shadow veil to the west, allowing the heroes to see into room @UUID[.on1towphTAWHfcAX]{A2}, the balcony, which overlooks this hall.

The light also causes the stone dais in the middle of the floor to levitate slightly off the ground—this is another magical lift, similar to the one leading down from the balcony. If the hero holding the unlit star stands on the lift, they can command the lift to rise… however, if they do so, the lift only raises a foot or so into the air before sinking back down. In its broken state, the unlit star does not have enough magic to convey the heroes higher into the temple. High in the air, beyond the reach of the unlit star’s light, shadows still cover the ceiling of the worship hall.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.3cPOh10GOQGBphGp]{Open Lift Manager}

We have set up a scene region for the lift that will let the players move their characters to the second floor when they move into the lift. To enable the lift for the second floor, use the Open Lift Manager macro above! From there, when a character moves onto the lift, they'll be prompted to move to an enabled floor.

The Unlit Star

@UUID[Actor.O7g2Z5VqnSqG9X1m]{Altar}

We have provided items for the unlit star and star shards to help you keep track of the heroes' progress. You'll find these items in the loot actor that is both linked in this block's header, as well as placed on the map's altar. You can reveal the loot actor's token and let the player whose hero will carry the unlit star drag the items to their inventory.

Experience Points

For defeating the undead and discovering the unlit star, give the heroes each 120 XP.

The Path Forward

Progressing up to the next level of the temple will require the heroes to reforge the unlit star, they’ll need the power of four star shards (see the box, below), located on this floor. When the heroes gain the unlit star, it already has one shard, possibly cluing them in to the need to reforge the artifact. The remaining star shards are located in the following areas:

  • @UUID[.D3L0mmk6HHkPbzPk]{A3. The Malfunctioning Lift}

  • @UUID[.gpZh5vEFO7QAsRZx]{A9. Hag Grotto}

  • @UUID[.eO5YfwgLIx7Rg41L]{A14. Crypt}

Your players can choose to continue through the temple by continuing north from the worship hall and progressing clockwise, or by backtracking to the south hallway, using the unlit star to dispel the shadow veil there, and then progressing counterclockwise. Either way will work, so let the players take charge of their adventure!

When the heroes have the four star shards they need and are ready to return to the worship hall to ride the lift, go to @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.wAbHx8wcQ4hn3r0h]{Finishing the First Floor} so they can face the final challenge on this floor.

The Unlit Star

From this point in the adventure on, the heroes have possession of the unlit star. Though shattered into several star shards, the crystal remains a powerful magical relic. Have the players choose a party member to carry the unlit star. The bearer of the unlit star can spend an action to command it to shine magical light in a 30-foot radius, or to command it to dim its light. Any shadow veils on this floor can be dispelled by the light of the unlit star.

As the party progresses through the temple, they can find and return the shattered fragments of the unlit star. Using an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pvQ5rY2zrtPI614F]{Interact} action to hold a star shard to the unlit star causes the two to rejoin in a flash of silver light.

Ruined Rooms.name: Ruined Rooms
Ruined Rooms.text:
This area can be entered from the worship hall to the south or through the closet connected to the flooded passageway to the north. Regardless of how the heroes enter, read the following when they do.

Debris litters this large room. Remnants of broken shelves and other storage suggests this chamber once held a variety of items, though nothing of use appears to remain. A large closet stands in the northern part of the room, with part of its floor crumbled away to reveal a pool of water.

Butterfly Fight

Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.g9RxHRpIK4GFFjQv]{Ferrous Butterflies x2}

A pair of ferrous butterflies have taken to resting in this chamber, building a nest among the debris. The butterflies spend most of their time hanging from the ceiling and fly down to fend off any intruders to the room. When the heroes enter, the butterflies unleash a metallic screech to try to scare them away. If that doesn’t work, the butterflies fly down to attack the heroes. They don’t chase the heroes out of the room, but will otherwise fight to the death to defend their nest.

Persistent Damage

Whenever a ferrous butterfly hits a hero, it leaves bleeding wounds! This deals persistent damage, a special type of damage that doesn’t happen right away.

Instead, that hero takes 1 bleed damage at the end of their turn (not the butterfly’s turn). The hero can then attempt a flat check (roll a d20 without adding anything) to see if the bleeding stops—if the result is a 15 or higher, the wound coagulates! If not, they’ll take the damage again at the end of their next turn (taking 1 additional point of damage), and then roll a new flat check. This happens at the end of every turn until the bleeding ends.

There are other actions a hero can use to help them. A hero can spend a two-action activity to attempt to stanch the bleeding. If they do, they can roll a flat check right away, before they take the damage, as described above. The bleeding also stops if a hero is restored to their maximum HP by magic or other means.

Experience Points

For defeating the ferrous butterflies, give the heroes each 80 XP.

Hag Grotto.name: Hag Grotto
Hag Grotto.text:
This room can be entered from either the west or the south, but either way requires a quick traversal underwater. The small pools of water in rooms @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.UCPjxy60QH6YKddM]{A8} and @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.WDt6XE2cQ9gNXPN4]{A10} connect to this chamber beneath the temple walls. The heroes don’t need to swim to enter this room—simply crouching beneath the partially sunken walls is enough to enter. Regardless of how the heroes enter, read or paraphrase the following when they do.

Knee-deep water and a constant dripping sound fills the cavern, as does a strange song. On an island in the middle of the cavern rests a woman, brushing her hair in a faded mirror. Looking closer, you notice her comb is made unmistakably of human bones. The woman has an eel’s long, thin teeth, an anglerfish’s translucent skin, and an octopus’s tentacles instead of legs. Broken chairs, jewelry boxes, vanities, and similar furniture are piled haphazardly about her, and atop the tallest stack sits a shining piece of crystal.

When the Temple of the Unlit Star was sunk into the earth, the northern wing suffered heavy damages, with some rooms collapsing entirely and being flooded with water from a nearby river. Through cracks deep underwater, a nearby sea hag, Shulzara, slipped in, called in part by the sinister magic now permeating the temple. Over several weeks, Shulzara preyed on what few priests remained, killing them and raiding the temple for beautiful objects to hoard in her grotto.

Shulzara was able to abscond with one of the star shards , which sits atop her tower of broken furniture, stolen baubles and clean-picked bones. The PCs may try to bargain with her for the star shard, but Shulzara has no intention of trading, especially once she notices the PCs have the unlit star—why bargain when she could simply take the artifact from their bodies?

Fight with Shulzara the Sea Hag

Low 1

@UUID[Actor.1IfAjRfF1ro6DMLo]{Shulzara}

As soon as Shulzara notices the heroes, she mentally prepares for battle, eager to add the unlit star and the PCs’ various trinkets and equipment (not to mention their skulls) to her collection. Before she attacks, she asks the PCs a few questions about themselves, mostly focusing on how they got into the temple and whether they’ve found any other star shards. She refuses to share much about herself, preferring to keep the focus on the heroes. After a few questions, Shulzara grows bored and finally attacks.

She uses Perception to roll initiative, but any heroes who wish can choose to use Athletics for their initiative roll instead, representing their brief swim into the chamber.

Difficult Terrain

The water-filled squares in this room aren’t deep enough to require swimming, but it’s still difficult terrain, which is particularly hard to move through. Moving into a square of difficult terrain costs an extra 5 feet of movement, and a creature can’t @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.UHpkTuCtyaPqiCAB]{Step} into a square of difficult terrain. These squares are not difficult terrain for the sea hag, whose amphibious nature means she’s well accustomed to the terrain.

Difficult Terrain Automation

You may have noticed the water-filled squares on the scene are marked. That corresponds to a scene region, which are areas on the map that can have special behaviors. In this case, when a token moves through a square within the region, it counts as difficult terrain, calculating and displaying the movement and action costs for you and your players.

Unique Enemy NPCs and Spellcasters

Some unique NPC (non-player characters) may have different motivations and abilities than typical members of their ancestry or training, or even have unique abilities altogether. In Shulzara’s case, she can cast arcane magic just like a sorcerer. The spells Shulzara can cast are listed in her stat block. She has three 1st-rank spell slots, so she can cast up to three 1st-rank spells during the fight, deciding what spell she wants to cast each time—it can be the same spell three times, each spell once, or any other combination. She also has some cantrips, which do not cost spells slots to cast.

On Shulzara’s first turn, she spends two actions to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4koZzrnMXhhosn0D]{Fear} on the hero that looks the physically toughest, hoping to shake them up or even make them flee from her. She uses @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.jfVCuOpzC6mUrf6f]{Hydraulic Push} to deal damage and push back the first target to close the distance to her island. If too many heroes bunch up on the larger outcropping to the west, she’ll cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.yAiSNmz39qXOIlco]{Mud Pit} on it to transform it into even more difficult terrain. Since she loves her collected baubles, she will never cast mud pit on her own island. When Shulzara runs out of spell slots, she’ll use @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IxhGEKl63R4QBvkj]{Frostbite} to attack. If she has extra actions after casting a spell, she’ll use them to Stride away, slash with her claws, or cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.TVKNbcgTee19PXZR]{Shield} for some extra defense.

Lastly, Shulzara has a hag’s innate resistant to magic. If she ever has to roll a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, she has a +1 status bonus to the roll.

Experience Points

For defeating Shulzara, give the heroes each 60 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.tGGBLpdxNHF7hOoU]

Atop Shulzara’s tower of broken furniture is a star shard, which glows softly in response to the unlit star’s proximity. Shulzara’s grotto is also full of stolen items—while most are rusted, tarnished, or covered in muck, the heroes do find some items of value: a set of pearl earrings worth 5 gp, a helix-shaped pendant worth 3 gp, and a piece of parchment in an ornate case. The piece of parchment is a scroll of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gKKqvLohtrSJj3BM]{Force Barrage}. A bard or sorcerer can use this scroll to cast the spell force barrage without expending a spell slot or even having it prepared. The process of casting the spell from the scroll causes the scroll to burn up in a harmless flash of silver fire, so it can be used only once.

Clinic.name: Clinic
Clinic.text:
This room was originally used as an infirmary, but is now in a shambles. The heroes can enter this room from the south or via the waterway that connects to the flooded chamber to the north. Regardless of how the heroes enter, read the following when they do.

A pair of beds and a few empty shelves along the walls are the main features of note in this chamber. A mass of debris and litter lies in the northwestern corner. The scraps and junk scattered about and collected in one corner suggest that this room was once an infirmary of sorts. In the northeastern corner, the floor has fallen away and left a large opening filled with water.

Rat Fight

Low 1

@UUID[Actor.iIJPJcDT8wlJ8z5M]{Giant Rats x3}

A trio of large rats spend most of their time in this chamber, hiding among the pile of detritus in the northwest corner. They’ve transformed the pile into a nest for themselves and are resting inside when the heroes arrive.

As the heroes move through the room, the rats stir and emerge from their nest to hiss at the heroes. If the heroes aren’t immediately scared away, the rats move in to attack. The rats prefer to stay near their nest and don’t chase the heroes out of this room, but otherwise fight to the death.

Experience Points

For defeating the rats, give the heroes each 60 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.Lb5KsvtYBKYUGkiI]

If the heroes search the room, they don’t immediately find anything of note. If they decide to search the nest, there is a chance they find something helpful. Heroes who search the nest can attempt a @Check[type:perception|dc:15] check. On a success, they find a pair of healing potions among the various bits of junk the rats have collected. On a critical success, they find a third healing potion.

Training Hall.name: Training Hall
Training Hall.text:
The residents of the temple made use of this magically-enhanced training room for exercise and combat training. Read the following when the heroes enter the room.

Large mats line the floor of this large chamber, each bearing years of wear. Three wooden training dummies stand at the far end of the room. Countless cuts and bits of chipped wood on the dummies suggest hours upon hours of combat training. A thin aura of shadow surrounds each of the dummies and a small bronze plaque on the wall above them reads, “Please remember to dismiss the magical partners after your training!”

The dummies are each magically enchanted with the power to produce shadowy apparitions to be used as part of training. A hero who casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic} within the room can detect the presence of magic, hinting at the possibility of the heroes affecting the room’s magic as noted in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.Ef9BtdLyhbCpZtNw#training-magic]{"Training Magic"} . The dummies are still active from when the temple first sank, as the guards that were training in here evacuated without deactivating them. The magic doesn’t immediately activate when the heroes enter, however. Once a hero moves within 10 feet of any of the dummies, the shadow magic around the dummies resumes and creates a set of corporeal apparitions that fight the heroes.

Orc Apparition Fight

Low 1

@UUID[Actor.YReM6QbqwUz3UTP7]{Orc Scrappers x2}

Once one of the heroes is within 10 feet of a dummy, two shadowy apparitions resembling orcs appear. These orcs are solid projections and can harm the heroes like any other danger in the temple. Immediately after they appear, the orcs give a slight bow of respect and then attack.

The magic in the room prevents the apparitions from leaving and the apparitions disappear if the heroes leave the room for longer than 1 minute. Until the heroes defeat the orc apparitions or turn off the magic creating them, they continue to appear whenever the heroes return to the room.

Once an apparition has been reduced to 0 Hit Points, it’s destroyed and doesn’t reappear later.

Training Magic

The room’s magic allows the heroes to manipulate the parameters of their training. While they won’t be able to learn about the specific nuances of the magic without spending weeks or even months studying the room, the heroes do have an opportunity to make some notable changes to the fight against the orc apparitions.

A hero trained in either @Check[arcana|dc:16|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], @Check[nature|dc:16|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], @Check[occultism|dc:16|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], or @Check[religion|dc:16|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] can learn more about the room’s magic by spending an action to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} and rolling their relevant skill against a DC 16.
