If a hero attempts this check while the apparitions are active, the DC is 12 instead (@Check[arcana|dc:12|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], @Check[nature|dc:12|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], @Check[occultism|dc:12|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], or @Check[religion|dc:12|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret]). On a success, the hero determines not only that magic in the room is creating the apparitions, but also that the magic can be manipulated to affect the apparitions.

With this knowledge in hand, the heroes can manipulate the room’s magic. To do so, a hero has to be adjacent to one of the training dummies and then spend an action to either roll an @Check[arcana|dc:15], @Check[nature|dc:15], @Check[occultism|dc:15], @Check[religion|dc:15], or @Check[thievery|dc:15] check. With a success, the hero is able to adjust the orcs to fight with their “safe” technique. In this case, all of the orcs’ attacks become nonlethal. If a hero is reduced to 0 Hit Points by a nonlethal attack, they are simply knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}. The apparitions ignore unconscious creatures, as well as anyone obviously attempting to move an unconscious creature to safety.

Once the orcs have switched to their “safe” technique, the heroes can use further actions to dismiss the apparitions. Doing so requires an additional action, using the same skills and DC listed above. On a success, the hero dismisses one of the two apparitions. One more success dismisses the remaining apparition. If a hero critically succeeds at the check to dismiss an apparition, they dismiss both at once instead. Unfortunately, the method to reactivate or create new apparitions requires much further study, so there aren’t any immediate ways to fight additional apparitions once the orcs are defeated or dismissed.

Experience Points

For defeating the orcs, give the heroes each 60 XP. If the heroes were able to end the training session and dismiss one or both of the apparitions, give them each an additional 20 XP.

Music Room.name: Music Room
Music Room.text:
The hall outside this room is blocked with rubble. Luckily, this chamber connects to the library to the south, but finding the secret passage between the two rooms requires the heroes to solve a puzzle. Read the following aloud when the heroes enter the room.

A large piano sits in the southern end of this chamber, with several pieces of sheet music and a small note placed on its music rack. Two of the piano’s keys have been colored gold, separating a section of five others—three white keys and two black—from the rest of the board. A large stone pew rests along the northern wall, directly across from the piano.

Players who search the piano find a note that reads “Don’t forget the musical order! The sheets help!” as well as five sheets of music. The sheets each contain the music for a different song. The songs are “Call of the Two Ravens,” “Eastern Midnight, Fifth Movement,” “First Passage of the Moon Through the Central Sky,” “Snow Moth’s Fourth Aria,” and “Third Sonata of the Western Stars.” Anyone that casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic} in the room senses the presence of magic.

The puzzle in this room is connected to the piano and a magically infused melody. The five demarcated keys are the only ones capable of playing the magical melody and the sheet music provides a hint for the correct tune to play to solve the puzzle. The names of the songs hint at which key to press and the correct order. If a hero succeeds at a @Check[type:performance|dc:15] check, they’re able to deduce that the numbers in the titles hint at the order to press keys. On a critical success, the hero also deduces that the locations and directions in the title hint at the placement of a given key.

Each song title references either white or black in its description, suggesting the song’s associated key. Thus, “First Passage of the Moon Through the Central Sky” refers to the white key (moon), located in the middle (central sky), and that it should be played first. Following this logic, it’s possible to determine the order to press the keys, though finding the placement of two of the keys requires some further deduction as not all of the titles include a direction or location. The correct order is the middle white key, then the left black key, the left white key, the right white key, and finally the right black key.

Determining the correct order of the keys in this way could prove difficult for players. If a player declares they wish to simply brute force the solution by pressing every combination of five keys until they solve it, they’re free to do so. Taking this route only takes about 10 minutes of continuous work.

Once the keys are pressed in the correct order, the piano slowly levitates a few feet away from the wall and reveals a now-obvious doorway that connects to room @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.29TF3ZneQ53rqk54]{A13}. The door to the other room is unlocked, allowing anyone to pass through. If the heroes play any keys on the piano after this happens, the secret door closes and the piano returns to its original position.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.sLEleGaGH9QBTdH1]{Reveal Piano Door}

If your players solve the puzzle, use the linked macro to move the piano and reveal the secret door behind it!

Experience Points

Sometimes challenges take the form of puzzles or other non-combat situations! If the heroes solve the puzzle, award them each 80 XP. If the heroes already solved the puzzle in the @UUID[.29TF3ZneQ53rqk54]{library}, they don’t receive the XP for the puzzle in the music room.

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
The hall outside this room is blocked with rubble. Luckily, this chamber connects to the music room to the north, but finding the secret passage between the two rooms requires the heroes to solve a puzzle. Read the following aloud when the heroes enter the room.

Large bookshelves line the walls of this room. A small bronze plaque is built into the top of each bookshelf, with each plaque depicting a simplified diagram of the phases of the moon: new moon, quarter moon, full moon, and a second quarter moon. A large desk and chair are located within the center of the chamber, with several notes and open books strewn across the desk.

Players who search the room notice several important details. First, each of the plaques has a specific phase of the moon specially embossed to make that particular phase stand out: new moon on the northern bookshelf, first quarter to the east, full moon to the south, and third quarter to the west. Second, they see that the spine of each book also bears one of the four phases. Finally, one of the notes on the desk explains that “the magic in the bookshelves is finally appropriately attuned,” though it doesn’t give further details. If anyone casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic} in this chamber, they sense the presence of magic.

To solve the puzzle, the heroes must place all of the books on the bookshelf with the matching highlighted phase of the moon. That is, all of the books with the new moon on the spine must be on the northern bookshelf, and so on. While this might be obvious to some players, other players might want a hint. Anyone looking to determine more about the puzzle can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:12] check. On a success, that hero notices that the majority of the books are on their respective shelf (new moon books to the north, etc.), but a few books are out of place.

Moving the books on to the correct shelf is a simple matter and takes 5 minutes of work. Moving all of the books between the shelves isn’t enough, however. The three books on the desk are also part of the solution and must be placed onto the shelves as well. Once all of the books are in the right place, the plaques on the shelves begin to glow with starlight and the northern shelf levitates slightly and moves away from the wall, revealing a secret doorway that connects to room @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.agPGqPwF3lCrves6]{A12}. The door to the other room is obvious and unlocked, allowing anyone to pass through. If the heroes remove one of the books from the shelf after this happens, the secret door closes and the bookshelf returns to its original position.

Experience Points

If the heroes solve the puzzle, award them each 80 XP. If the heroes already solved the puzzle in the @UUID[.agPGqPwF3lCrves6]{music room}, they don’t receive the XP for the puzzle in the library.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.BQRi0vuJjpGQHENU]{Reveal Library Door}

Use the Reveal Library Door macro if your players solve the puzzle to move the bookshelf and reveal the secret door behind it!

Crypt.name: Crypt
Crypt.text:
The temple residents would keep their dead in this room, but the vile energies that sunk the temple have brought corruption and undeath to the bodies within. The door to this room is normally locked with a magical seal, but the magic of the unlit star breaks the seal and allows the heroes to enter. When they do, read the following.

This large chamber houses several simple coffins, some of which have their lids removed or broken. A multitude of sections of the wall bear carved words, each a prayer for a restful death. The putrid stench of death hangs in the air.

Ghoul Fight

Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.iLkQt8A99nQWUI8k]{Ghoul Stalkers x2}

Some of the corpses here have returned in undeath as ghouls}, vile undead that retain their intelligence from their living days. The pair of ghouls were unable to leave the chamber due to the seal and eventually resigned themselves to their coffins. When the heroes enter, the sound of their arrival stirs the ghouls to rise from their coffins and attack. The ghouls have to spend 1 action in combat to climb out of their coffins, but they otherwise are free to move as they please. The magical seal on the room prevents the ghouls from leaving the room, but they otherwise fight viciously until reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Flanking

The ghouls here have a bit more tactical instincts than the undead found in the worship room, and will attempt to move into a flanking position to gain an edge. The ghouls will try to stand on opposite sides of a single hero, flanking them and giving them the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} condition (which applies a –2 circumstance penalty to AC) against all melee attacks made by the flanking ghouls.

The ghouls have a special ability called sneak attack that lets them deal an extra 1d4 damage each time they hit a hero with the off-guard condition. A hero can stop being flanked on their turn by moving away from the ghouls, or if one of the ghouls flanking them is reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Flanking Automation

The system can automatically determine if you are flanking a target. You can verify this by pressing the "Alt" key on your keyboard while targeting an enemy token. If they are flanked, you will see a line labeled "Flanking" connecting your token to the token flanking with you.

Once you roll your Strike, the off-guard condition from flanking will be taken into account, which may automatically activate certain abilities such as the ghoul stalker's sneak attack!

Experience Points

For defeating the ghouls, give the heroes each 80 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.z6oc76wOV9CeFM3C]

Within the coffin in the far back corner of the room is a star shard, which glows softly if the unlit star is within 30 feet. A PC can notice faint light shining through the slightly ajar seam of the coffin with a successful @Check[perception|dc:15] check. Also within the coffin is a magical +1 dagger. This is a +1 weapon, which means that attack rolls with the dagger gain an additional +1 item bonus!

Finishing the First Floor.name: Finishing the First Floor
Finishing the First Floor.text:
Once the heroes have returned the four star shards on this floor to the unlit star, they can return to the @UUID[.SxFJiKuH1ZUUOrR4]{worship hall} and attempt to use the crystal’s magic to progress to the second floor. Warn the heroes that such an overt display of power is likely to rouse whatever evils might yet linger on this floor and that they should prepare for a fight. If your heroes could use a rest, they can find safety in one of the rooms they’ve cleared out, which will allow them to heal up and regain any spell slots or daily abilities they’ve spent. If your heroes haven’t found the healing items in the clinic or storerooms yet, you could consider giving them a gentle suggestion that there might be helpful supplies elsewhere in the temple if it feels appropriate to your group’s dynamics.

Once the heroes have steeled themselves and returned to the worship hall with the unlit star in hand, read or paraphrase the following.

As you touch the unlit star to the dais, silver magic traces around the circle, building in power. Suddenly, a column of light erupts upward, piercing the shadows and revealing the ceiling of the worship hall. The ceiling is covered in a mural of an elven woman with four butterfly wings and wearing a dress the color of twilight—the goddess Desna—hanging stars in the night sky. As the crystal’s light chases the shadows from the room, they gather to a single, inky black point on the ceiling. Leathery wings burst forth from the pit of shadow, giving way to the shape of an enormous bat. The creature screeches as it surges forth to attack you!

The partially restored unlit star has returned light to the first floor of the temple, but the darkness that lurks here has responded in kind, sending forth a guardian shadow bat to get rid of the heroes and prevent them from cleansing any more of the temple! Roll initiative using Perception for the shadow bat.

Shadow Bat Fight

Low 1

@UUID[Actor.TUkD3aBPIQVux8aP]{Shadow Bat}

The shadow bat will likely prove a challenging fight for the heroes, but with some teamwork and luck, they just might stand a chance. The shadow bat has been ordered to guard the entrance to the second floor, not to hunt the heroes down, so if they need to retreat and regroup, they can do so safely.

Special Attacks

Much like the magnetic skinks earlier, the shadow bat is capable of spending 2 of its actions to release a powerful Screeching Gust attack that deals damage to all creatures in a cone, starting from its space. Anyone caught in this screeching must roll a basic Reflex save against a DC of 16.

As with all basic saves, a creature takes no damage on a critical success, half damage on a success, full damage on a failure, and double damage on a critical failure. You’ll roll damage only once and determine how much damage everyone takes based on their saving throw. This ability also requires the bat to recharge and rolling 1d4 determines how many rounds are required for the recharge. The bat becomes particularly vulnerable while recharging, which gives the heroes a great opportunity to retaliate!

Moving Ahead

With the shadow bat defeated, the heroes are free to take the lift up to the temple’s second floor. Like before, the hero carrying the unlit star can command the lift to rise. If the heroes haven’t reattached the star shards to the unlit star yet, the lift only rises slightly in the air before floating back down. The unlit star doesn’t have enough power, even with the other star shards in proximity. The heroes must attach the shards if they wish to activate the lift, though doing so might not be immediately obvious to the heroes yet. Luckily, the hero carrying the unlit star receives a feeling from the artifact itself suggesting that the hero needs to attach additional star shards to help rebuild the artifact. As noted earlier, attaching a star shard requires an Interact action to fully reconnect the two.

Once the three shards have been reattached, the lift can finally take the heroes up to the @UUID[.cDB7IwpCub6CVbBF]{second level}. The heroes can also return to the first level at any time by making use of the lift.

Experience Points

For defeating the shadow bat and taking the lift up to the next floor, give the heroes each 120 XP.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
The challenges in the second level of the temple are more dangerous than the first. The heroes are free to explore the area as they see fit, though a few doors are locked or jammed, and require additional effort to enter. Specifically, they a need a key for the head priest’s quarters in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.dv7x8m3mV1Hfldgc]{B9} (the key is located in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.GHK4A7OTDnjcBlTK]{B2c}), they need to force open the door to the meeting room in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.2Xjn200JX7vr3VLO]{B5}, and they need to find some way to unlock the Vault in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.PsskQ4Es8jIArlxf]{B10}.

Reaching the Roof

Much like with the first floor, the lift can take the heroes up to the temple’s roof where they can finally escape and return home. Just like before, the unlit star lacks the power to take the lift any higher. If the heroes wish to progress up to the next level, they’ll need to locate the three star shards found on the second floor. These star shards are located in the following areas:

  • @UUID[.2Xjn200JX7vr3VLO]{B5. Meeting Room}

  • @UUID[.mRCuKpU9Td4YeXVK]{B7. Refectory}

  • @UUID[.dv7x8m3mV1Hfldgc]{B9. Head Priest’s Quarters}

Worship Hall (qzVx).name: Worship Hall
Worship Hall (qzVx).text:
Much like the hall on the first floor, this chamber was used for worship and important ceremonies. Read the following when the heroes enter the worship hall for the first time.

The central dais marked with a butterfly sits flush with the floor in this room. A pair of stone columns remain intact in the eastern portion of the room, with rubble and debris occupying much of the northern and northeastern sections of the room. A massive stone has fallen in the northwestern corner. The northeastern wall has partially collapsed, revealing several destroyed sleeping chambers. Beyond the ruined portions, three sets of door lead out of this room, one to the north, one to the south, and one to the east. A feeling of unease hangs here, but nothing of note appears to be the cause.

The first time the heroes enter this room, they’re free to explore as they wish. The doors to the north and south lead out to a hallway and the garden in @UUID[.plAAJpus1YSPP4rr]{B8} respectively. While the eastern door would normally connect to another hallway, another collapsed boulder is blocking access beyond the doors. Initially, the heroes can safely move through this room without issue. Once they have collected the three star shards on this floor, the vile energies that flow through the temple cause another creature to appear and attack the heroes. Before they’re able to make use of the lift to head up to the roof, run the heroes through the fight with the gargoyle as noted in @UUID[.pyLWP3WII4lppGqd#gargoyle-fight]{Gargoyle Fight}.

Dormitories.name: Dormitories
Dormitories.text:
The temple’s residents would sleep in these rooms. The chambers are simple, each containing a bed, a small footlocker beneath the bed, and a simple wooden shelf on the wall. The heroes can search each of the chambers and find additional contents in a given room as noted below.

  • @UUID[Actor.fBXLRrqVUTtUu4ua]{B2a:} A religious symbol of Desna—a butterfly whose wings are marked with a sun, moon, and stars—rests on the shelf. The footlocker contains 3 gold pieces, 8 silver pieces, and a simple book with a variety of prayers and songs in honor of Desna.

  • @UUID[Actor.5ij4EekgGXHxQrP0]{B2b:} The footlocker in this room is locked. A hero can unlock it by using @Check[thievery|dc:15|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock}. Unlocking the container requires a total of 2 successes. Alternatively, a hero can break the lock off with single successful @Check[athletics|dc:18|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check. Inside the footlocker are a 2 gold pieces and 5 silver pieces, as well as a pendant of the occult.

  • B2c: A pair of giant flies have crawled into this room and attack anyone that opens the door, as noted in Fly Fight.

  • @UUID[Actor.xN4htA6RTcBwdhci]{B2d:} This room appears to have nothing of note, but if a hero succeeds at a @Check[type:perception|dc:16] check, they notice a derelict parchment between two books on the shelf. The parchment is in fact a scroll of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gKKqvLohtrSJj3BM]{Force Barrage} as noted by a faint scribbling on the back of the parchment.

Fly Fight

Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.t8mDlH0ELLKtm7WG]{Giant Flies x2}

Two giant flies have taken residence in this bedroom, occasionally leaving through a small crack in the western wall to go find something to eat, but generally returning shortly thereafter.

The assumption is that the flies are in this room when the heroes open the door, but you might decide that the flies return while the heroes are searching the room to catch them unawares! Once the flies attack, they begin to pursue the heroes wherever they go in hopes of acquiring a big meal.

The flies focus their attacks on the smaller heroes, which might be someone who is shorter like a halfling or with a slighter build like a spellcaster. Each fly focuses on a different hero. They lack the instincts to fight with any obvious tactics. The flies are relentless and will chase the heroes beyond this room. If the heroes need to escape from the flies, they can facilitate their own escape by making use of the doors to trap the pests in a room. The flies lack any kind of preservation instincts and fight to the death.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.XjPJDJb51bQXt6i6]

Once the flies are gone, the heroes can discover that the footlocker in area B2c sits wide open. Inside is a fine silk pouch which is in fact a spacious pouch. Inside the pouch are two items. The first is a wayfinder. The other is a simple brass key. This spare key once held by a high priest is magically attuned to the door to the head priest’s chambers (room @UUID[.dv7x8m3mV1Hfldgc]{B9}) and is the only way to unlock that door.

Experience Points

For defeating the flies and finding the key to the head priest’s chambers, give the heroes each 100 XP.

Ruined Dormitories.name: Ruined Dormitories
Ruined Dormitories.text:
The walls of these dormitories collapsed as the Zenith Temple sunk and now lie in ruins. Read the following when the heroes explore this area.

The walls of these three rooms have collapsed, creating a large opening that connects all the chambers. Rubble and debris cover the floors and the remnants of what once were comfortable beds.

There isn’t much for the heroes to find in this room, as most interesting objects were destroyed in the collapse. As with the other dormitories, each room contained a bed, footlocker, and shelf. The only @UUID[Actor.ODm0fUJodomosIdg]{intact footlocker} is the one in the central room, but it’s currently buried beneath a pile of rubble. Noticing the footlocker requires a hero to succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:18] check. Once they notice the footlocker, the heroes can spend several minutes digging through the rubble to reach it. Inside are two vials of holy water that remained intact.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.8aR2tZ0R4fly7J9G]{Reveal Footlocker}

If your players dig through the rubble and reach the footlocker, you can use this macro to move the rubble out of the way!

Washroom.name: Washroom
Washroom.text:
The heroes can access this room from the hallway with ease. When they enter, read the following.

This washroom contains several stalls, a pair of hand washing basins, and a large tub. The basins are scattered with shards of glass, which obviously came from the broken mirror on the wall above the basins. Water flows out of a spout into the tub at an irregular rate; short sprays followed by several moments of nothing before the flow resumes.

Much like the lavatory on the first floor, the temple’s residents used this room to bathe and freshen up. The hand washing basins can also magically produce water, though the heroes would want to clear the broken glass before using it. The tub uses a similar magic to produce water, but the temple’s sinking has caused the magic to malfunction and produce water at irregular intervals.

Water Scamp Fight

Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.QN9Zv9l71Q1E9bCR]{Water Scamps x2}

When the magic that produces water for the tub malfunctioned, it also summoned two elementals known as water scamps. The scamps are currently unable to leave this room as they’ve been unable to determine how to use the doors, so they’ve been spending their time in the tub and enjoying what little sprays of water they receive. When the heroes enter, the scared scamps begin to fly around the room in a panic and attack the heroes.

As they fight, the scamps make use of their acid breath to harm the heroes. A scamp will do its best to avoid harming their fellow scamp with the acid breath. Otherwise, the scamp claws at whichever hero is closest. If none of the heroes are blocking the open doors, one of the scamps attempts to fly out of the room out into the hall instead.

Once outside, the scamp will try to find somewhere else to hide, favoring rooms where there are obvious obstacles or terrain to hide behind. The scamp won’t open any door, but will fly into rooms where doors are left open. If the heroes return to a room where the scamp is hiding, the scamp will panic again and attack with its acid breath before trying to run away once more. The second scamp remains in the washroom, as it’s too frightened to leave. The panicked scamps fight until slain, though the PCs might be able to return the scamps to their original home by repairing the magic on the tub as noted in “Repairing the Magic” below.

Repairing the Magic

The basins’ and tub’s magic connects to a magical plane known as the Plane of Water. The malfunction on the tub’s magic accidentally summoned the scamps in addition to the water it produces. If the heroes can repair the magic, the scamps would be returned to the Plane of Water to live free and safe lives once more. While the fact that the magic is malfunctioning might be obvious at a glance, repairing it takes a bit more work.

A hero that is adjacent to a basin or tub can spend an action to repair the magic by attempting a @Check[arcana|dc:18], @Check[nature|dc:18], @Check[occultism|dc:18], @Check[religion|dc:18], or @Check[thievery|dc:18] check. On a success, a hero fixes the water producing function, returning it to normal, but the scamps remain in the temple. The hero can tell that there is still some kind of malfunction with the magic, even if the water is working normally. They can attempt the check again, and on a success, the scamps are returned home. A critical success on the initial check repairs the water and immediately sends the scamps home. A critical failure on the initial check causes a powerful spray of water that hits the hero for @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage. A critical failure on the second check causes the water to malfunction once more, returning it to the same state it was when the heroes initially entered.

Experience Points

For slaying the scamps, give the heroes each 80 XP. If the heroes were able to send the scamps back to the Plane of Water, give them each 120 XP instead.

Meeting Room.name: Meeting Room
Meeting Room.text:
The door to this room is unlocked, but is stuck due to the webbing inside. When the heroes approach this door, some obvious webbing pokes out from the edges of the door, between the frame. It should quickly become apparent that the door isn’t budging. A hero who attempts a @Check[type:athletics|dc:16|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check can force the door open and access the room beyond. Otherwise, the heroes can spend 10 minutes cutting away at the webbing around the door to eventually clear the way. Once the heroes head inside, read the following.

Masses of webbing fill the entirety of this room. At its center, a large stone table lies crushed beneath a massive chunk of rubble. A large hole in the ceiling thirty feet above marks the space the rubble once occupied and allows light to pour in from outside. The table’s shattered remnants remain relatively contained due to the amount of webbing that encase it. Piles of bones lie scattered throughout the room, with some caught up along the walls among the webs.

While the room is covered in webs, it doesn’t hamper the heroes’ movement across the floor in any way. The webbing grows particularly thick higher up, however, and makes it near impossible for the heroes to climb up toward the ceiling. The spiders are able to navigate these webs without issues, but the heroes would need to spend hours cutting away or burning the webs to clear a path to the ceiling. The walls lack any obvious handholds and climbing along them requires a successful @Check[athletics|dc:30|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move] check, which is unfeasible for the heroes.

If the heroes wish to stand on the table’s remains, they can do so as part of their typical Stride. As they move, they can reduce their total movement by 5 feet (as if they moved into another space) to represent the effort required to clamber onto the table. Once on the table, they can move normally or even jump down without any further effort or issue. The spiders are able to move across the table without any additional movement cost, thanks to their massive legs.

Spider Fight

Low 1

@UUID[Actor.A4VgQIHsqJKssQOM]{Giant Spiders x2}

A pair of mated spiders have taken residence in this room. They’ve made their home and use the hole in the ceiling as an exit so they can hunt. The spiders would occasionally traverse the temple and hunt the remaining priests. The bones about the room are the remains of these priests. When the heroes enter, both spiders descend down from the walls and attack. The spiders keep their distance, using their web on the heroes. They then move in to attack any webbed heroes, or they retaliate once the heroes have closed in.

One spider has an obvious, supernatural pattern reminiscent of stars. This spider recovered a star shard from one of the priests it hunted. While the spider doesn’t understand what that shard is, the shard’s magic has drawn the spider to it and the spider guards the shard ferociously. The shard’s magic has since transformed the spider, leading to the strange pattern on its body. The other spider flees once it’s reduced to 5 Hit Points or fewer. If it begins its turn with few Hit Points, it spends all of its turn trying to climb up the wall and reach the opening in the ceiling 30 feet away. Once it does, it flees the temple and doesn’t return. The star-patterned spider fights to the death in this room in an attempt to guard the star shard.

Experience Points

If the heroes slay both spiders, or slay one and cause the other to flee, give them each 80 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.mhksEj6dhO30cZqr] @UUID[Actor.bupuT5qBWcFK6oPG]{Priest Remains}

The star shard in this room is contained in a small pouch of webbing several feet off the ground in the far back corner. The proximity of the unlit star causes the shard to glow, making it obvious to the heroes. Cutting down the webbing to get at the shard is a simple matter and only takes a minute of work.

If the heroes search the room further, they can find the mostly intact remains of a priest by succeeding at a @Check[perception|dc:16] check. While this priest is unfortunately dead and wasted away to bones, his clothing is relatively intact and among his garments are a set of +1 handwraps of mighty blows. These handwraps improve the accuracy of unarmed attacks, such as fist attacks, and grant a +1 bonus to unarmed attack rolls. These handwraps are particularly useful for monk characters.

Central Hallway.name: Central Hallway
Central Hallway.text: This hallway is generally straightforward, save for the massive boulder that occupies the central branch to the west. This boulder fell during the temple’s sinking and now blocks access to the worship hall in @UUID[.3ZpSTHqTS1EfqzVx]{B1}. The boulder fully prevents movement through this part of the hall, even for smaller creatures. The boulder is also too heavy to move, even if all of the heroes work together. For the moment, this limits movement through the upper floor.

Refectory.name: Refectory
Refectory.text:
This room includes both the temple’s kitchen and a dining area for the temple’s residents. When the heroes enter, read the following aloud.

Two long dining tables occupy the southern half of this large room. A multitude of plates and cutlery cover the tables. A small kitchen area takes up the northern portion of the room, separated by a short wall. The kitchen includes a small stove built against the partition and a pair of hanging cauldrons. Like the dining tables, the kitchen is littered with cooking tools and cookware.

Encounter

Severe 1

@UUID[Actor.r2uJWK5Vz7lJpfux]{String Slimes x2}

The temple residents fled during their meal as the head priest unleashed his attack on the temple, leaving the room in the state that it is now. When the heroes enter the room, they hear a strange slurping and sloshing in the southern end of the room. This sounds comes from a pair of young string slimes that crept in here by squeezing in through a few small holes in the temple’s outer walls. These slimy creatures tend to mindlessly travel places in search of food, but are now stuck and unable to return to the outside world. The slimes have eaten what rotting scraps of food were left in the room and continue to move about, searching for more food. The slimes quickly notice the heroes as they enter the room and lunge forth to attack, believing the heroes to be their next meal.

Speaking With Brother Celluan

Once the heroes have dealt with the slimes, things change within the room. A voice calls out to the heroes, thanking them for dealing with those pests and noting that they can come grab their meals in a moment. Looking to the north, the heroes see that a figure has manifested in the kitchen.

The figure is the ghost of Brother Celluan, a priest that perished during the attack on the temple. Brother Celluan typically cooked meals for his fellow priests during his life and his spirit remained connected to the kitchen even after his death. He doesn’t have any harmful intent and any attempts to attack pass through his incorporeal body harmlessly. (Celluan overlooks these attacks, passing them off as innocent attempts to protect oneself without malice.)

After he notifies the heroes that he’s working on preparing a meal for them, Brother Celluan invites the party to the kitchen to speak with him while he cooks. The heroes likely have questions for Brother Celluan and he’s a generally forthcoming individual. A number of likely questions and Celluan’s responses are included below.

Who are you?

“My name is Brother Celluan. I am one of the priests in this temple. I’ve been acting as the temple’s cook for many years now, so I’m sure it’s no surprise to find me here.”

Do you know you’re a ghost?

“You don’t say!” Celluan inspects his hands for a moment before returning to his cooking. “Yes, I’m well aware of my current condition. I know little about ghosts, but my general understanding is that a ghost is connected to a place important to them. I spent much time in this kitchen, so I guess I understand why I’m still here now.” If the heroes ask Celluan about helping him move on or end his time as a ghost, he avoids the topic, focusing on his cooking instead. The heroes have an opportunity to help with this, but can learn more information from Celluan as noted in @UUID[.#winning-over-celluan]{Winning Over Celluan}.

What is this place?

“This is the Temple of the Unlit Star, a holy site dedicated to Desna. My fellow faithful and I tended to an important relic that was kept here. This relic kept the temple safe from outside forces and was the centerpiece of many holy rituals.”

Do you mean this relic? The heroes can present the unlit star and the various star shards they’ve collected so far to Celluan. “Ah, the unlit star! It’s managed to survive! I thought it was lost forever after the attack on the temple. It looks incomplete, though. The star has eight points and what you have here is obviously lacking a few. Well, if you’ve a few pieces of the star, surely the rest are still around somewhere. You could rebuild the star.”

What happened to this temple?

Celluan appears to hesitate before answering this question. “In the days before my death, a number of undead creatures started to make their way toward the temple. It was unlike anything I’ve seen before. The shambling dead, skeletal creatures, and shadowy beings began to circle the temple. While I’m aware that such things exist beyond the temple walls, the defenses here would typically keep such things at bay and even actively repel them; they wouldn’t dare approach the temple before. Eventually, though, the undead were able to break into the temple and attacked us, slaughtering myself and the rest of the priests here. I awoke sometime later in this state, though it seems like quite some time has passed since the attack and my return as a ghost.” The heroes can try to pry more about the temple’s history as noted in @UUID[.#winning-over-celluan]{Winning Over Celluan}.

Is this your journal?

If the heroes present the journal from area A5, Celluan’s eyes widen in recognition. “Yes! That’s mine. You didn’t read it, did you?” His face takes on an obvious blush, even in his ghostly state. “You know what, it doesn’t matter. Sister Eina is long gone and knowing that I had love in my heart while I lived isn’t anything to be ashamed about. In fact, I wish to thank you for helping me see that.” When the heroes present the journal to Celluan, the act earns his respect and grants the heroes a bonus to their checks to win him over, as noted in @UUID[.#winning-over-celluan]{Winning Over Celluan}, below.

How do we get out of here?

“I fear that I don’t know for sure. I can’t leave this chamber in my state, but I have an idea. If you’re able to reactivate the lift in the worship hall on this floor, it should take you to the roof. From there, the failsafes can be deactivated, returning the temple to the surface.”

Winning Over Celluan

Brother Celluan is withholding some information from the heroes, more so out of shame than any malice or attempt to deceive. While the heroes speak with him, they might get a sense that Celluan isn’t entirely forthcoming. If any heroes seem suspicious, they can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:14|options:action:sense-motive] check to read Celluan’s face as he answers questions. With a successful roll, the hero recognizes that Celluan is holding back some information.

Confronting Celluan about this causes him to become even more reserved, but the heroes have a few means of getting him to open up. A success on any of the following skills will get Celluan to divulge more. If the heroes presented Celluan’s journal to him, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to these checks as Celluan is more endeared to them.

@Check[diplomacy|dc:15]: The heroes can attempt to be polite and discerning with Celluan, most likely explaining that they’re in need of help and anything else he can share might be useful.

@Check[intimidation|dc:17]: Pressing Celluan can be effective, especially if the heroes make note that withholding information is not of much use to him in his ghostly state.

@Check[religion|dc:13]: Celluan is particularly influenced by appeals to his faith. The heroes can make note that they’re trying to protect the temple or rid the temple of whatever evils are at play within, which can lead Celluan to open up.

If the heroes fail a given check, they can attempt one of the remaining checks. Failing all three skill checks causes Celluan to close off and note that he’s no longer in a talking mood. He refuses to share any further information at this point, though he’s willing to repeat any of the answers to the questions on the previous page, if the heroes need reminded.

If the heroes succeed at one of the above checks, Celluan proceeds to share more information, as noted below.

Lukahn: “Before you travel any further, I think you should know the cause of the troubles within the temple. Shortly before my death, I saw that the head priest—a man by the name of Lukahn—took the unlit star and did something with it. I couldn’t quite tell what he did, but it felt like a corrupting presence. I think it was his doing that caused the undead to attack the temple.

“I didn’t sit idly by, though. Just as the undead were making their way into the temple, I rushed to the rooftop where the star was kept and broke it up into the fragments you see now. Lukahn tried to stop me, but it seemed that Desna interfered and caused one of the fragments to shoot into Lukahn and pin him against the orrery on the rooftop. I’m not sure what happened, but Lukahn seemed to be unable to follow me after that, so I fled back into the temple.

“I then handed the pieces off to the other priests so they could hide them from Lukahn. As they scattered to do so, I looked back to the rooftop. Lukahn transformed into a creature made of shadow, possibly due to the very same corruption he caused to the temple. It was a sad sight, but I didn’t stick around to witness what happened to him next. I returned to the temple to help where I could, eventually meeting my death. I’m not sure what exactly Lukahn did that day, but whatever it was, the darkness he brought to the temple is still around. I believe that restoring the star will help put an end to it.”

Celluan the Ghost: “I didn’t expect to become a ghost, but I guess I’m not surprised by it. I loved my time here. I loved my fellow priests. I loved Desna. It’s that love that urged me to track down the unlit star and try to keep it safe by breaking it up. I’ve heard that ghosts stick around due to unfinished business. I don’t think that cooking more meals is my unfinished business. If you were able to help rebuild the star and liberate it from Lukahn’s evil grasp, I think I would finally find peace and be able to move on.”

Star Shard: “Before you go, take a look beneath that pot. In my final moments, I hid a piece of the star beneath it. I would have tried to find a better hiding spot for it, but I recall it being hard to make competent decisions in my final moments. Take the shard and put an end to Lukahn’s wickedness!”

Brother Celluan has no further information to offer. Beyond the above information, he has trouble recalling much about his time in the temple and is completely unaware of anything that happened after his death. He is genuinely regretful he can’t offer more information or leave the room to offer his help. He wishes the heroes well once they leave the room and reminds them to return to this room if they need a place to rest.

Experience Points

For defeating the slimes and speaking with Brother Celluan, give the heroes each 160 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.G2Wwf0LJVaiu1fln]

One of the star shards is in this room, immediately available for the heroes to claim. It might be some time before the heroes decide to search the room, however, as they might spend some time speaking with Celluan. It’s possible that the heroes learn of the shard’s location from Celluan directly. If they don’t it’s not much work for them to locate the shard. So long as the heroes take some time to intentionally search the room, they eventually locate the shard beneath one of the pots in the kitchen, as it’s assumed they make attempts to do more than a cursory search.

If the heroes never take the time to search the room, this shard eventually makes itself known to the heroes. If they collect all the remaining shards and still haven’t found this piece, the shard is much more obvious next time the heroes return to the room. By this point, the unlit star is almost fully restored and the shard “wants” to be found. It glows with bright light and causes the pot to rattle, drawing the heroes’ attention.

Garden.name: Garden
Garden.text:
This room is a simple garden that the temple’s inhabitants used to grow local produce, as well as a place to keep several insects. Read the following when the heroes enter the room.

A pale green light fills this chamber, emanating from a mass of glowing mushrooms growing on and around a tree at the far end. A pair of tables hold several potted plants, each clearly dried and wilted. A large glass box reminiscent of a greenhouse stands in the corner opposite the tree. Inside are several more potted plants, each appearing healthy and green. Dozens of butterflies and moths flit about within the greenhouse.

Shadow Twigjacks

Severe 1

@UUID[Actor.iqQspEn4uxv0wVwb]{Shadow Twigjacks x2}

While this room might seem inconspicuous when the heroes first arrive, there are still dangers inside that they’ll need to face!

The corruption within the temple has transformed a pair of the potted plants into creatures called twigjacks. The twigjacks now consider this room their home and will defend it against any intruders, including the heroes.

The twigjacks begin this encounter @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}. Ask each player to tell you their Perception DC: their Perception + 10. Then roll Stealth from the twigjacks' sheets. If the total is equal to or higher than the highest Perception DC from the heroes, the heroes don’t notice the twigjacks before they attack—the room looks like it’s empty!

Don’t reveal the tokens on the map until the twigjacks attack or move down from the shelves, or until a hero moves through the room and up to the tree. But if any hero’s Perception DC is higher than the total of the twigjack’s Stealth check, the twigjacks are spotted! You can reveal their tokens.

Either way, ask the players to roll initiative, using Perception unless a hero was hiding. Use the total from the twigjacks’ Stealth check for their initiative. If any heroes have their turn before the twigjacks but the twigjacks successfully hid themselves, the heroes know there are foes nearby, but they don’t know where—they’ll have to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} to find their enemies.

Rolling Behind the Screen

This is a situation where you may want to keep the players in the dark about the twigjacks' Stealth results. If so, when you roll Stealth with the twigjacks and the roll dialog pops up, you can change the Roll Mode dropdown from "Public as User" to "Private to Gamemasters" to hide the result from your players.

Retroactive Initiative

You may have noticed that you'll need to use the twigjacks' previously rolled Stealth check as their initiative. Instead of rolling new initiatives and editing them to match the old rolls, here is what you can do:

Create an encounter, adding the players and twigjacks to the tracker as normal. Then, you can go to the chat and look for the results of the twigjacks' Stealth checks, then click the crossed swords icon to the right of each result on the chat to set their initiative as that result!

If a twigjack’s turn starts while they’re hidden, they fire a splinter at a hero. That character has the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} condition against the attack, which gives them a –2 circumstance penalty to AC. After this ranged Strike, the twigjack is no longer hidden (set the twigjack’s pawn on the map if you haven’t already), and the fight then proceeds normally.

A Friend Among Plants

After the fight, the heroes have a moment to catch their breath. Soon after, they hear a rustling from the tree at the far end of the room. They see what at first appears to be a mushroom moving down along the tree’s trunk, but it quickly becomes clear it’s actually a living fungus with a somewhat humanoid shape. This is a leshy by the name of Gorkie. As she climbs down from the tree, Gorkie lets out a croaky and somewhat high-pitched laugh. Gorkie then proceeds to introduce herself. Read the following as she does.

“Hee-hee, well done all of you. You did well in ridding the garden of those menaces. Gorkie saw you fight and Gorkie knows you’re all very strong. I think that you might need Gorkie’s help, so let me know if you wish to buy some magic to help with more fighting!” Gorkie produces several vials of liquid and a pair of scrolls. “Gorkie takes gold and silver from anywhere, so don’t worry!”

Gorkie is a traveling merchant who found herself in this room some time ago. Now that things in the room are safe, she’s back to business as usual. The heroes might have some questions for her. The following are some common questions and responses.

Who are you?

“I am Gorkie. I’m a leshy and a most exceptional merchant. See my wares!”

How did you get here?

“Gorkie heard some commotion a while back and came to investigate. I was drawn to the garden as this commotion was happening. Soon, there were shadow creatures and undead all around so I hid in the tree. I saw other mushrooms and felt safe. After some time, Gorkie tried to come down, but those shadowy plants were here, so I hid again. I went to sleep for some time and now here you are, waking me up in time to buy good items!”

You managed to stay safe in here?

“Yes! This tree and fungus are magical. Gorkie can tell they have a blessing and that kept the shadow plants away. The same blessing keeps the plants and moths over there alive. The blessing likes butterflies and moths, I think! This blessing has probably rubbed off on these potions, so now is the best time to buy!”

Are you going to leave now?

“Gorkie not ready to leave yet. I can feel a bad feeling outside of this room, so it’s best to stay here for now. If the bad feeling goes away, then I think I can leave. Make sure to buy something before I go!”

You have things for sale?

“Gorkie does! I have potions and special water and some magic contained within parchment. I can show you!”

Gorkie doesn’t know too much else about the temple. She’s willing to let the heroes stay in the garden to rest, but does continue to occasionally pester them to buy something. If the heroes do decide to rest here, they find themselves overwhelmed with a feeling of peace, thanks to Desna’s blessing on the garden. Before they sleep or leave, the heroes feel a compulsion to open the door to the greenhouse. When they do, the butterflies and moths fly into the greater room and occasionally land on the heroes, almost as if thanking them for releasing them. The butterflies and moths never leave this area, even if the doors are left open. With the insects released, the heroes can get a more restful sleep and they recover an additional 5 Hit Points if they take a period of rest in this room, thanks to Desna’s blessing.

Gorkie's Wares

If the heroes wish to buy something from Gorkie, she’s eager to share all about her items. She has the following for sale.

  • 3 healing potions (4 gp each)

  • 2 holy waters (3 gp each)

  • 1 scroll of concordant choir (3 gp)

  • 1 scroll of thunderstrike (3 gp)

Gorkie explains what each item does, as noted in the Magic Items section. The heroes can trade with Gorkie at any time and they’re free to come back at later times to make more purchases from her.

Some heroes might attempt to convince Gorkie to offer a discount or even give away her wares for free. A hero that wishes to do so can attempt a @Check[diplomacy|dc:16], @Check[nature|dc:16], or @Check[performance|dc:16] skill check. On a success, Gorkie admits she likes the heroes and she’s been trying to sell these items for some time, so she’s okay with getting less of a profit if it means she can go find new wares. She offers the heroes a discount of 1 gp for all items in this case. If the heroes critically succeed at any of these checks, she is particularly won over. She gives the heroes one of the healing potions for free and then also offers them the 1 gp discount. She’s not willing to give any further discounts, though, no matter how much the heroes try to convince her, stating it would be bad business to sell her wares for anything less.

Merchant Actor

@UUID[Actor.CqrpFjHNo259QhkO]

We have provided a merchant actor for Gorkie's Wares which you can find on the map as a hidden token. If you reveal the token, your players can open the sheet by double-clicking on it. From there, they can drag and drop items from the merchant's sheet to their own character sheets to purchase an item.

If Gorkie offers the heroes a discount, you can edit an item's sheet inside the provided merchant actor and lower its price accordingly, or add a gold piece back to your players' inventories for each item they purchase.

Experience Points

For defeating the shadow twigjacks and speaking with Gorkie, give the heroes each 160 XP.

Head Priest's Quarters.name: Head Priest's Quarters
Head Priest's Quarters.text:
This chamber belonged to the head priest and offers the heroes a glimpse at the wickedness that befell the temple. The door to this room is magically locked and the heroes need the key from B3c to unlock the door. Unlike other locked doors on this floor, the magic on this door is beyond what the heroes are capable of disabling and they must use the key to open the door. Attempts at unlocking the door without the key are met with a repelling magic that pushes the heroes away. Once the heroes enter the room, read the following aloud.

This chamber is a spacious bedroom with a bed along one wall, a bookshelf along the other, and a small tub opposite the entryway. The room is in a state of disarray with bedding thrown on the floor and several torn books strewn about the shelf. Strange, black claw marks scar the floor and walls. Two rotting, human corpses lie in the center of the room, each bearing similar marks.

Lukahn, the head priest stayed in this room during the temple’s heyday, but the chamber became a place of death. As he took over the temple in an attempt to claim the power of the unlit star, other priests broke the relic into several pieces and attempted to hide them. Two priests came into this chamber while it was open and hid, but found themselves unable to escape due to the magical lock on the door. Soon, a shadow entered the room, slaughtered the priests, and left their corpses here. The corpses have sat in this room, resonating with unholy energies ever since.

Undead Priest Fight

Moderate 1

@UUID[Actor.TciT0K3eNqiTyxsr]{Crawling Hands x2} @UUID[Actor.7c0XJLfVKw8EMmKy]{Severed Head} @UUID[Actor.Xo4IGzw28hivgMmM]{Zombie Shambler}

The corpses in the room rise to meet the heroes once they enter, animated by the unholy energies within them.

The shadow that slayed these priests is long gone, but they still have an effect on the corpses. The torn body of one priest rises in parts, rather than wholly intact undead, becoming a pair of crawling hands and a disembodied head.

The second priest remains relatively intact and rises as a zombie. The hands, still full of rage toward the head priest, crawl toward obvious spellcasters in an attempt to stifle any further summoning.

The severed head attempts to bite anyone that comes close to its former body, and the zombie lumbers toward the first person to enter the room. These undead fight until destroyed.

Experience Points

For defeating the undead within the room, give the heroes each 80 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.j3YF9u4dRH98QE8p]

Once the heroes have dispatched the undead, they’re free to search the chamber. While most of the things that remain here are of little monetary value and mostly relate to Desna’s faith, there are two items of note. One of the books is a prayer book to Desna that grants a +1 item bonus to Religion checks related to Desna. The other is a star shard, which lies beneath the bed. One of the priests had this shard on their person when they entered this room. The shard fell from the priest’s hand in their dying moments. While locating the star shard would normally require a bit of searching, it becomes very noticeable for the heroes as it begins to glow once the unlit star is in the room.

Vault.name: Vault
Vault.text:
The temple’s sacristy also served as a general vault for the temple. In addition to housing the items that priests and worshippers would need most for their practices, the vault held other items of value that the temple’s residents collected over the years. The door to the vault is magically locked and the heroes will need to put in some effort to get inside. When they approach this room, read the following.

A pair of beautifully engraved doors stand at this end of the hall. The doors are covered in meticulously carved stars, forming the constellations of the heavens, gilded in such a way that they seem to move with every shifting view. In the center, the handles form the two halves of a prismatic butterfly, its thorax composing a complex locking mechanism.

The high priests of this temple made use of a magical phrase to unlock the vault, but the phrase has been long lost with the residents’ deaths. The only option for the heroes to enter the vault now is to disable the magical lock on the door. The heroes have main two options: either use physical means via Thievery or magically disable the lock through either Arcana, Nature, Occultism or Religion. The heroes can use a combination of any of these skills to successfully unlock the door. Due to the magical nature of the lock, unlocking it with a magical skill will prove easier and any hero trained in one of the four magic-related skills (listed above) becomes aware of this fact if they study the lock.

Due to the complexities of the lock, it will take 3 total successes to unlock the door (with a Critical Success counting as 2 success). These successes can be from any of the skills used. A critical failure on any of the checks causes some kind of mishap that reduces the heroes’ total successes by 1, requiring additional successes to make up for the loss. Worshippers of Desna have a +2 circumstance bonus to any of these checks, as their faith helps guide them. Heroes that attempt to physically pick the lock can do so with a @Check[thievery|dc:18|options:unlocking-vault] check. Heroes that interact with the magic of the door can do so with an @Check[arcana|dc:16|options:unlocking-vault], @Check[nature|dc:16|options:unlocking-vault], or @Check[occultism|dc:16|options:unlocking-vault] check. Due to the divine magic used to create the lock, attempting a @Check[religion|dc:14|options:unlocking-vault] check is even easier.

Using Automation Effects

@UUID[Item.8YM1bIack1RLHena]{Faithful Guidance}

An effect is a handy tool that allows you to automate modifiers, temporary Hit Points, and more—typically with a duration. Effects are applied by drag-and-dropping them onto a character's sheet or token.

In this case, if any of the heroes worship @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.deities.Item.JgqH3BhuEuA4Zyqs]{Desna}, you can drag the effect linked in the header, as described, which will automatically apply a +2 circumstance bonus when rolling their checks using any of the check buttons above.

Once the heroes open the doors, they gain access to the simple vault within. The counters lining both walls are worn with age and covered in dust, though they were clearly once cared for and well organized. Each drawer and cabinet bears a faded label on the front and everything within seems to have a designated place, even if the vials and boxes along the counters seem to be empty.

Experience Points

For unlocking the vault, give the heroes each 40 XP.

Treasure and Discovery

@UUID[Actor.vPi3ie3e3RK0sSJa] @UUID[Actor.3b8QSdOhYWCvewb7] @UUID[Actor.HvdiTiKEUDbgDzic]{Cabinet}

If the heroes make their way inside, they’re free to search the room. Their search immediately turns up a drawer labeled “Medical Supplies” along the right wall. Inside this drawer are two healing potions and one elixir of life. A separate drawer labeled “Spare Keys” is also immediately obvious, though this drawer is stuck and requires a successful @Check[athletics|dc:17|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check to open up. Inside is a skeleton key that the head priests would occasionally give out to trusted subordinates. In addition to the magical properties of the key, this key can unlock and relock the door to the vault. The rest of the key drawer has impressions of other keys that were once here, but have since become lost.

A hero who searches further can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:16] check to look around. On a success, that hero finds a +1 shortsword located in a lower cabinet. Additionally, if the hero critically succeeds on the check to search, they find another drawer that seems to have been wedged shut. By pulling it open with negligible force, they find inside a 1st-rank scroll of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.TFitdEOpQC4SzKQQ]{Runic Weapon}. A bard or sorcerer can use this scroll to cast the spell runic weapon without expending a spell slot or even having it prepared. The rest of the vault’s contents are either items of little value, damaged beyond repair, or in an otherwise unusable state.

Finishing the Second Floor.name: Finishing the Second Floor

Overview (avqy).name: Overview
Overview (avqy).text: The roof of the temple contains only a single challenge: the corrupted phantom of Head Priest Lukahn, roused from his decades-long fugue by the heroes’ actions. If the heroes can defeat him and reclaim the last shard of the unlit star from his heart, they’ll be able to break the long-standing curse on the Zenith Temple and return to the surface.

C1. Star and Shadow.name: C1. Star and Shadow
C1. Star and Shadow.text:
The lift takes the heroes up to the roof. Read the following as they reach the roof.

The lift continues up past the second floor, eventually stopping as it becomes flush with the temple’s rooftop. Across the rooftop stands a rusting metal structure made of metallic rings and orbs: an orrery. From within the orrery emerges a rolling shadow. The shadow is formless at first, but soon coalesces into the shape of a human man made mostly of darkness. His face moves through a variety of emotions from anguish to despair to anger and then finally joy. He then looks up at you.

“I don’t know who you trespassers are, but I am pleased to see you. You see, you’ve reclaimed the shards of that blasted crystal. That same crystal has kept me bound to this rooftop for centuries and I’ve been unable to return to the lower portions of the temple to reclaim them. Now that you’ve brought them to me, I shall be able to liberate myself and unleash the power of shadow upon the world!” A small glimmer of light appears within the man’s shadow body: a star shard! “First I will claim your lives and then I will claim those shards for myself!” He lifts his hands above his head, creating a mass of shadowy arms around himself and the edges of the rooftop. This is the time to stand against his wicked shadows!

Encounter

Extreme 1

@UUID[Actor.YYhD00fbaYCHjrDn]{Shadow Priest Lukahn} @UUID[Actor.DZsWmzBEY8LsoF0H]{Shadow Walls}

The fight against Lukahn is the most complex one yet. In addition to facing off against the head priest, the heroes must also contend with the magical hazard he has created. Lukahn keeps his distance from the heroes, using his magic or his shadow blast attack to attack them from afar. If any heroes engage with him directly, he flies away to try to keep his distance from them, resorting only to using his shadow hand when he’s cornered. Lukahn has no other desire than to be free from this temple, so he fights until he’s utterly destroyed.

Since Lukahn’s body is mostly shadow, attacking him isn’t as effective as attacking the creatures within the temple. Any attacks or spells have their damage reduced by his resistance, unless they deal force, spirit, or vitality damage.

Most of the heroes’ weapons are not magical, so the resistance is doubled against these attacks. However, when Lukahn or the heroes are in light, the weapons are considered magical, so this resistance isn’t doubled. Thankfully, the unlit star can provide constant light and help the heroes with their attacks. If the heroes are able to place the artifact into the orrery as noted in @UUID[.BzuY4GJBo2CIcXkV#the-orrery-of-light]{The Orrery of Light}, they’ll be able to gain even further advantages.

The hazard here takes the form of several walls of grasping shadows, as seen on the map for this area. The hazard is complex, which means it works like a monster. It rolls Stealth for its initiative and has a turn in initiative like any monster. On its turn, the shadow walls attempt to harm the heroes. The exact effects are different each round and target random parts of the room. The hazard’s Routine entry describes how this works.

Overcoming the Hazard

The heroes can overcome this hazard in a variety of ways. Once the encounter begins, the heroes can try to disable the shadow walls by disrupting the magic creating them. Doing so requires the heroes to stand adjacent to one of the four walls and attempt one of the checks listed in the shadow walls’ Disable entry. The hero must spend 2 actions to attempt the DC 20 skill check. On a success, that wall is banished away.

The heroes can also physically destroy the walls by attacking them individually (using the AC and Hit Points in the hazard’s stat block). The walls, being made of shadow, have Hardness which represents the fact that attacks are less effective compared to attacking a creature. Each time a hero hits a wall, subtract this number from the damage roll before reducing the given wall’s Hit Points. Once three walls have been banished, whether the heroes have disabled or destroyed them, the hazard stops working entirely as the magic creating the walls has been disrupted.

The Orrery of Light

The structure on roof is a magical orrery that the temple’s priests used to perform magical rituals at key times throughout the year. The unlit star was the centerpiece to the orrery and its magical power source. When Lukahn took over the temple, he did so at the orrery and corrupted the energies within to doom the temple. If the heroes are able to bring the unlit star to the orrery, they’ll be able to restore the device to almost full power and use its magic to severely hamper Lukahn.

The hero carrying the unlit star can attempt to return the artifacts’ various pieces to specific segments of the orrery to reactivate the device. Doing so requires the hero to stand adjacent to the orrery and make use of the Restore the Orrery special activity.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.4JohOQpxHFTNBLa6]{Restore the Orrery} 2

  • Concentrate
  • Manipulate

@Embed[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.4JohOQpxHFTNBLa6 inline]

Custom Action

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.adventure-specific-actions.Item.4JohOQpxHFTNBLa6]{Restore the Orrery}

Much like the Diminish Shadow action in @UUID[JournalEntry.jvzuMC2WQpJNJQzW.JournalEntryPage.pyLWP3WII4lppGqd]{Finishing the Second Floor}, you can drag the Restore the Orrery action linked above onto the token of the hero holding the unlit star.

As the heroes return pieces to the orrery, it begins to activate, slowly spinning at first, but growing faster as more pieces are restored. The orrery provides additional benefits based on the number of pieces the heroes have returned.

  • 0–1: No initial benefit.

  • 2–3: The orrery begins to glow, filling the entire rooftop with light. This light makes it easier for the heroes to harm Lukahn as his Light Vulnerability is constantly triggered.

  • 4–5: The orrery glows brighter, its magic dampening the effects of the shadow walls. If they’re still active, the bonus for their ranged Strikes becomes +8 instead of +10, and the DCs to avoid damage become DC 13 instead of DC 15. This is in addition to the benefit above.

  • 6–7: The orrery glows with the light of the full moon. The shadow walls are instantly banished, disabling the hazard once and for all. Additionally, the light hampers Lukahn even further. He takes a –1 status penalty to all checks and DCs for the duration of the combat. This reduces the bonus on his attack rolls, skill checks, AC, and DCs for his spells.

Experience Points

Once the heroes defeat Lukahn, banish the shadow walls, and return the unlit star to the Orrery of Light, they each gain 160 XP.

Wrapping Up.name: Wrapping Up
Wrapping Up.text:
Once the heroes defeat Lukahn, the head priest lets out an anguished wail. With his final cry, his body fades away, leaving behind the final star shard. At this point, the heroes are free to claim the piece and reunite it with the rest of the unlit star. If a hero still carries the unlit star, they’ll be able to reattach the shard to the rest of the artifact as normal. Once the unlit star is fully restored, it begins to slowly float toward the orrery. It then phases through the center orb and magically embeds itself into the center of the orrery. If the heroes placed shards of the unlit star into the orrery during combat, they receive a powerful feeling suggesting they must place the remaining shards into the orrery. Once they do, the pieces reunite within the center orb and become the complete unlit star.

Regardless of how the unlit star makes its way into the orrery, once it’s inside, the orrery begins to turn at a constant rhythm and the Zenith Temple starts to rise back toward its original location. The cavern that the temple had fallen into begins to open up, as if by the will of Desna herself. The opening reveals the night sky above. A multitude of stars welcome the heroes back to the surface. The temple begins to shake as it rises up out of the sink hole. This continues for several moments until eventually the entire temple has returned to the surface, rising above the marsh. The heroes can see the ruined chambers they originally entered at the start of the adventure. They now stand over the place where their adventure began, transformed into true heroes ready for even greater adventures! If they search the temple, they’ll find that Gorkie has left to sell her wares elsewhere and Brother Celluan has moved on to finish his journey into the afterlife.

Over the coming weeks, news of the heroes’ exploits travel all across the region, and soon they receive opportunities for more adventuring work. Such adventures are up to you, the GM, to determine. However, if you're looking to get started right away, the Troubles in Grayce anthology included in this module has six adventures ready for you and your group. These adventures take place within the same haunted nation of Ustalav, can serve as direct sequels to this story, and your players can use the same heroes they used for this adventure!

The Path River Peeler.name: The Path River Peeler
The Path River Peeler.text:
The high banks of the Path River are riddled with natural cave systems that, since ancient times, have been sites of spiritual importance to the peoples of Ustalav, Lastwall, and Belkzen. Grayce itself grew up around one such site, a shrine to the goddess Pharasma, but in other locations more sinister forces held sway. Centuries ago, a coven of hags gathered in a cave along a stretch of the Path River known today as the Shivering Bluffs. There, the hags made pacts with entities from beyond the Universe, including—or so it is rumored—the Netherworld. During the Shining Crusade, the forces of the Knights of Ozem scattered this coven, but the hags’ shadow still looms over the region.

Though many of the tales regarding the Shivering Bluffs are nothing but superstition, the area’s reputation for danger is well deserved. Few people visit the Bluffs, making them a haven for wild animals, and in the cave where the coven of hags once gathered, a tear in the fabric of reality occasionally allows even stranger creatures to pass through. The most infamous of these creatures is the Path River Peeler. Descriptions of the Peeler vary, but all agree it is an otherworldly monster that preys on the flocks of sheep that graze along the Bluffs’ fertile, eastern slopes. While sightings of the Peeler ebb and wane—sometimes whole generations pass without a single attack—in recent weeks the monster has become increasingly active. This, combined with other strange happenings that have occurred in Grayce of late, has put the entire town on edge.

One of Grayce’s least popular residents, a changeling named Damarys (spiteful female changeling witch 3), has seized this opportunity to stir up trouble in town. Abandoned as an infant on the doorstep of the temple of Grandmother Crow, Damarys has long felt like an outsider among the people of Grayce. This alienation grew stronger shortly after her 12th birthday, when voices claiming to be the spirits of the hags banished centuries before led Damarys to the Shivering Bluffs. There, in the darkest of the caves, the voices promised Damarys that if she were to bring ill fortune to the town of Grayce, one day a portal to her home—her true home—would be opened.

Excited by the thought of leaving Grayce behind, Damarys moved from the temple where she’d been raised to the countryside. Here, she could keep to herself and earn her living as a shepherd while remaining close to the Shivering Bluffs. She visited the hags’ cave often, and several weeks ago she noticed a thin crack forming in one of the cavern’s walls. On the chill wind that blew from the fissure, Damarys once again heard the whispers of the hags promising to bring her home. That night, Damarys awoke to find a monstrous creature crouched above her bed: a thing that seemed part monkey and part bat, but which walked upright like a human. The creature did no harm to Damarys, but the very next day, fresh reports of Grayce’s local cryptid, the Path River Peeler, began.

Damarys senses that her otherworldly patrons are about to make good on their promise. The crack from which the Peeler emerged grows wider, and Damarys believes that if she can keep the cryptid safe, a doorway to the Netherworld will be opened for her. In the meantime, she hopes to cause as much misery in Grayce as possible, exacting revenge for both herself and the voices she’s come to think of as her true family.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
The adventure begins shortly after the PCs arrive in Grayce from their previous adventures. Give the PCs a chance to take care of any business they might have and to get a feel for the town, describing the settlement’s general layout and its more notable landmarks. Then—perhaps as the PCs are purchasing supplies at Grayce General Goods or securing rooms at the Ash Inn or Riverbend Tavern & Inn—they’re approached by Albin Derkensoor (old and hardy male human rancher 3). Albin is in his sixties, and his family moved to Grayce when he was still a child. Normally, Albin’s eyes twinkle with cheer, but today his wrinkled face is a mask of worry.

“Folks have been saying there’s adventurers in town, and by the looks of you, they’re right. If that’s true, I could surely use your help. I’ll buy you a drink and tell you all about it, if you’re interested.”

Assuming the PCs agree to hear Albin’s story, he directs them to the Sing-A-Long Bar. As he does, attempt a secret @Check[perception|dc:12|options:action:sense-motive|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|traits:secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive} for each of the PCs. Any character who succeeds notes that while the people of Grayce clearly recognize Albin, they seem to be giving him the cold shoulder, casting suspicious looks in his direction, or even outright turning their backs on him.

Albin endures this treatment silently and, when they arrive at the tavern, motions for the PCs to take a seat in a quiet corner (a rarity for this establishment once night falls). Once everyone is settled, he begins.

“Three nights ago, round about midnight, I was awakened by the worst sound I’ve heard in all my years. It was some sort of beast—of that I’m sure—but the cry it made was more like a laugh than a growl. A low chuckle, from deep in the throat, but louder than a peal of thunder.

“The sound was still echoing off the hills when my sheep began to scream. I rushed outside to find Euphis, my ranch hand, standing inside their pen hollering and beating on a shield. Once he’d calmed down, Euphis said he’d seen a monster bearing down on the flock. He managed to scare the thing off, but not before getting a good look at it. It was taller than you or me, even hunched over, and had eyes that burned like torches in the moonlight. The Path River Peeler, he swears it was.”

At this point, Albin holds up his calloused hands. “Now, Euphis is brave for certain, and I’d never question his word. But he’s not the brightest guy. I can’t say for sure what he saw. All I know is that my sheep are too frightened to graze their normal pastures. And I can’t forget that laugh.” Albin shakes his head. “If that thing wasn’t the Peeler, it was something just as bad, or worse.”

The PCs probably have questions about Albin’s story. Some likely inquiries, as well as Albin’s answers, follow.

What’s the Path River Peeler?

At this, Albin smiles nervously. “A story told to scare the children, or so I thought until three days ago. Supposedly, it haunts the hills just north of town. No one agrees what the creature is, and truth be told, no one’s claimed to have seen it since I was young. But with all the trouble in town recently, word about what Euphis saw has spread.”

Trouble? Like what?

Well, that sinkhole, for one! It opened a week before my sheep got all stirred up. I don’t know what a hole in the ground has to do with the Peeler, but anything out of the ordinary makes folk nervous in these parts. And frightened people start making connections where there’s none to be had.” (In this, Albin is correct: the sinkhole has nothing to do with the Path River Peeler, though it does play a part in other adventures in this anthology, such as “Sabotage!” and “They Hunger Below.”)

Why’s everyone giving you the cold shoulder?

“I can’t say I blame them,” Albin sighs. “If it was the Peeler Euphis saw, then maybe a curse has befallen me. Some say the Peeler brings pestilence with it, too. If that’s true, and my sheep have been infected, I couldn’t ask anyone to join my flock with theirs, not until this trouble’s been sorted out.”

What can we do to help?

A look of determination settles on Albin’s face. “Find the Peeler—or whatever that creature was—and put it down. You can come to my place to look for tracks, but I’d start here in town if I were you. Maybe someone knows something about the Peeler—or has even seen the beast themselves and are just too scared to speak up.”

Can we talk to Euphis about his experience?

“Well, of course you can. If you decide to help me out and take on this task, you can come by the farm and ask Euphis as much as you want.
