I told you everything he already told me, but he might remember some other helpful clue if asked the right questions.” Albin pauses for a moment and knits his brown slightly before continuing. “Like I told you, he’s a good guy, but a bit naive. I only ask that you are kind to him. He’s been through a lot.”

Albin isn’t wealthy, but he offers the party a total of 40 gp as a reward for tracking down the Path River Peeler. He also says the PCs are welcome to stay at his ranch until the matter’s settled. If the PCs agree, Albin heads home to prepare space for them to settle in once their investigations in town are finished.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Following Albin’s advice, the PCs can canvas Grayce for more information about the Path River Peeler, perhaps starting with the other patrons in the Sing-A-Long. As the PCs ask around, they quickly discover that while everyone in town has a story about the Peeler, most are little more than fairy tales passed down from parents or grandparents. No one living in Grayce today claims to have seen the monster firsthand—except, of course, Albin’s ranch hand @UUID[.fn2aQCd7IhNhi5Hp]{Euphis}.

For every 30 minutes the PCs spend asking about the Path River Peeler, one of them can attempt a @Check[type:diplomacy|dc:15|options:action:gather-information|name:PF2E.Actions.GatherInformation.Title|traits:exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.plBGdZhqq5JBl1D8]{Gather Information}. Because current knowledge of the Peeler is only speculation, even on a failed check the PCs should learn one or more of the rumors listed in the Rumors in Grayce sidebar. On a success, the PCs are directed to one of the three more substantive leads listed below. On a critical success to Gather Information, the PCs learn about two of these leads rather than just one.

  • @UUID[.rF3wUQ3CgljTpjiZ]{Jarelle Quaine}, a ranger who patrols the pastures north of Grayce, is well respected in town. All agree that if anyone has solid information about the Peeler, it’s her.

  • @UUID[.v154AQMmOMoSLYzG]{Titus Horvat} is a retired farmer turned amateur cryptozoologist and has been stirring up fears by telling wild stories about the Peeler.

  • @UUID[.HqUQ2tiUCZkhtyNX]{Damarys} is a shepherd who lives alone in a cottage just an hour’s walk from Albin’s ranch. No one in town has anything nice to say about Damarys, and more than one person is certain she has something to do with the Peeler’s sudden reappearance.

The PCs can follow up the leads in any order, and Jarelle, Titus, and Damarys might direct the party to each other if the PCs don’t discover all the leads themselves.

Rumors in Grayce

As the PCs ask around for information about the Path River Peeler, they hear no end of stories about the monster. It seems everyone in Grayce has a friend or relative who’s spotted the Peeler along a lonely road one night, though no one claims to have seen the beast themselves. What’s more, little tragedies like a child taking ill, random accidents, and even poor weather are often blamed on the Peeler, with no evidence to support the claim. Most describe the Peeler as a black-furred, bat-faced monster that walks upright, but the details vary from person to person.

The PCs might hear any of the following rumors during their investigation. As none of these claims are entirely true (and are some outright fabrications), the PCs don’t need to learn any of them to continue the adventure.

  • The Path River Peeler earns its name from the state in which it leaves its victims, who are often found stripped entirely of skin. It preys mostly on sheep but has also been known to hunt other animals—and people.

  • The monster hates loud noises. Singing at full volume is a surefire way to keep the beast at bay.

  • The Peeler lives in a cave somewhere in the Shivering Bluffs north of town. It retreats there every morning, lest the sun’s rays burn it to cinders.

  • If you see a patch of dark fungus, that’s a sign the Peeler has passed that way recently.

  • Nothing can harm the Path River Peeler, save fire.

  • The Path River Peeler is a devil summoned to the Universe by a coven of hags centuries ago. Though the hags are long gone, the Peeler still haunts the Shivering Bluffs, waiting for a chance to avenge its masters.

Jarelle and Phara Quaine.name: Jarelle and Phara Quaine
Jarelle and Phara Quaine.text:
Jarelle Quaine (upstanding female human ranger 1) has lived in Grayce her entire life and is well liked by nearly everyone in town. She’s especially respected by the shepherds who graze their flocks outside of town, as Jarelle regularly patrols the pastures to keep them free of wolves and other predators. When her parents both died several years ago, Jarelle was thrust into the role of sole caregiver for her younger sister, Phara (troublemaking female human teenager 0). Since then, the two have lived together in a cottage a few minutes outside of town.

When the PCs arrive, they find Jarelle busy oiling her bow, while Phara lounges in the branches of a nearby tree with one leg dangling and swinging back and forth, looking bored. As the PCs approach, Phara clambers from the tree and greets the party with an excited grin, eager to have new and interesting people to talk to. She peppers them with questions (“Are you adventurers?” “What monsters have you killed?” “Can you show me some magic?”), but it’s not long before Jarelle intervenes to ask the PCs their business.

If the PCs question Jarelle about the Path River Peeler, the young ranger nods matter-of-factly. Jarelle doesn’t typically take tall tales seriously, but she’s heard enough stories about the Peeler that she believes the monster’s not entirely a myth. She’s never seen the Peeler—and suspects that most people who claim to haven’t either—but she knows the wildness around Grayce is full of creatures far stranger than the wolves or occasional kobold or bugbear she encounters on her forays. To that end, she’s been keeping an eye out for the Peeler, but she also believes one shouldn’t go out of one’s way to look for trouble. “In my experience,” she says, “Trouble finds you soon enough. No reason to rush it.”

Though Jarelle believes Grayce’s best course of action is to simply wait and hope the Peeler moves on (like it always has for as long as people have been seeing the creature in these parts), she agrees to show the PCs her maps of the surrounding area and help them identify the best place to stake out the beast. All the while, Phara continues to interrupt, asking the PCs what they think the Peeler is, how they plan to kill it, and whether she can accompany them on their “Peeler hunt.”

Any PC can help Jarelle study her maps by succeeding at a @Check[survival|dc:16] or @Check[scouting-lore|dc:14] check. Another PC can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid} the check by making a successful @Check[deception|dc:15], @Check[diplomacy|dc:15], or @Check[performance|dc:15] check to distract Phara during the meeting. Even on a failure, Jarelle suggests a location where the PCs could start their hunt, but on a success, the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks made to overcome the obstacles in @UUID[.UT0yM9V79tZ3Ikbq]{Event 2: Countryside Chase}, as their familiarity with the area gives them an edge.

As the PCs prepare to leave, Phara asks if she can come with when they kill the Peeler. At this, Jarelle puts her foot down: Though she’s certain her sister will make a fine ranger herself someday, she’s still too young to be hunting monsters, even accompanied by the PCs. Phara opens her mouth as if to protest but grudgingly accepts her older sister’s decision—at least for now. The PCs will meet Phara again when she disguises herself as the Path River Peeler during @UUID[.UT0yM9V79tZ3Ikbq]{Event 2}.

Reward

For helping Jarelle identify the best place to stake out the Peeler, grant the PCs 20 XP.

Titus Horvat.name: Titus Horvat
Titus Horvat.text:
Titus Horvat (credulous nonbinary human cryptozoologist 2) was a struggling farmer when they received a surprise inheritance from their uncle, a professor of biology at the University of Lepidstadt. The estate included a modest library, as well as hundreds of their uncle’s journals, each filled with sketches of unusual creatures that had been dissected at the university. Their imagination inflamed by these images, Titus immediately retired from farming to pursue a new career as an amateur cryptozoologist. They figured they didn’t need to tend the fields and be at the whim of the weather now that they’re set up from the inheritance, and they might as well put all these books and notes to use. Though most people in Grayce consider Titus eccentric, the reemergence of the Path River Peeler has lent them an air of credibility. For their part, Titus is basking in their newfound celebrity, delivering impromptu lectures about the Peeler in their home for fellow townspeople or engaging in long conversations at the market if someone brings up the Peeler.

When the PCs arrive at Titus’s house in town, they assume the PCs have come to question them about the Peeler. They invite the PCs inside, directing the party to a parlor where the bulk of their late uncle’s library is on display. Titus can tell the PCs any of the stories detailed in the Rumors in Grayce sidebar. If the PCs offer their own theory as to what the Peeler might be, Titus latches onto the idea, bending over backwards to incorporate the PC’s suggestion into their own wild speculations. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:14|options:action:sense-motive|name:PF2E.Actions.SenseMotive.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1xRFPTFtWtGJ9ELw]{Sense Motive} recognizes that, while Titus might share their uncle’s enthusiasm for biology, but they have the perspective of a superstitious farmer, not a scientist.

PCs looking for reliable, hard facts about the Peeler must study the books and journals Titus has laid out in their parlor. A PC can study the books by making a @Check[academia-lore|dc:16], @Check[nature|dc:16], or @Check[occultism|dc:16] check. A PC can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid} on the check by succeeding at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:14|options:action:aid|name:PF2E.Actions.Aid.Title] check either to enlist Titus’s help or simply keep the former farmer busy. On a failure, the PCs uncover plenty of information about cryptids like the Peeler but learn nothing specific about the Peeler itself. Treat a successful check as if the character had succeeded on a check to Recall Knowledge about the Peeler. For example, you might tell the players that the Peeler is inured to cold, or that the monster dislikes loud noises.

Reward

For studying Titus’s collection of books and journals, award the PCs 20 XP.

Damarys.name: Damarys
Damarys.text:
Ever since she was abandoned on the doorstep of the town’s temple to Andoletta, Damarys has been a thorn in Grayce’s side. Though Andoletta’s priests endeavored to raise her with love and attention, Damarys has always kept her distance from her community. She prefers to be left alone and goes out of her way to ensure she isn’t around when the town is looking for volunteers. When she does interact with others, it’s usually to make a biting criticism. More often, she simply lurks on the fringes of gatherings, fixing her fellow townspeople with a scornful stare. Infuriatingly, Damarys learned from a young age to always follow the rules just enough to avoid punishment. As a result, though everyone in town dislikes Damarys, no one can point to concrete proof of the mischief she’s suspected of.

Damarys’s cottage lies a few miles east of Grayce and roughly an hour’s walk north of Albin Derkensoor’s ranch. When the PCs arrive there, Damarys has just returned home from grazing her modest flock of sheep. She is a woman in her late 20s with a somewhat wild look, thanks to her patchwork clothes and the mismatched color of her eyes. Her tousled hair is woven with rodent skulls, iron nails, and other baubles, and her shepherd’s crook is made of willow wood: a lone holdover from her time spent at Andoletta’s temple. Damarys acknowledges the party’s approach with an unwelcoming nod.

Unlike the party’s other two leads (or anyone else in Grayce), Damarys has seen the Path River Peeler firsthand, but she’s not inclined to share what she knows. She believes that once the Peeler has finished its current killing spree, the monster will return to the Netherworld, allowing her to slip back through the rift alongside it. If a band of do-gooding adventurers kills the Peeler before then, she’ll miss her chance and be stuck in Grayce forever.

Despite her initial reluctance to speak with the party, clever PCs can play on Damarys’s contempt for the people of Grayce and trick her into revealing some information about the Peeler. Damarys is confident she’ll soon be leaving Grayce behind, and in the meantime feels the townspeople deserve whatever misery the Peeler brings. A PC can get Damarys talking with a successful @Check[deception|dc:21] check. Alternatively, a character can break the ice by noting either her occult baubles or her shepherd’s crook with a successful @Check[occultism|dc:18] or @Check[religion|dc:18] check, respectively.

Once she gets started, Damarys’s disdain for the people of Grayce reveals itself. “They’re no better than these sheep,” Damarys says, “Dumb animals clamoring for safety, blind to the wonders that fill the Universe and worlds beyond.” If asked if she’s seen the Peeler, Damarys smirks. “Oh yes. Its touch carries with it the chill of the Netherworld. The Peeler will return home soon enough, but until then, you—and everyone else in Grayce—would be best to stay out of its way.”

At some point during the conversation with Damarys, make a secret @Check[perception|dc:17|traits:secret] check for each of the PCs. Any character who succeeds spots a flicker of movement as a tiny figure, its body seemingly made of twisted brambles, scuttles into the nearby bushes. The creature is named Mocking-Vain, a minor fey spirit that serves Damarys. If asked about the creature, Damarys simply nods. “As I said, the world outside of Grayce is filled with wonders—and terrors.” A character who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:14|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} identifies Mocking-Vain as a sprigjack.

Development

Damarys can share as much—or as little—information about the Path River Peeler as you’d like, but keep in mind that Damarys is only a bit more well-informed about magical matters than some of the PCs might be. Much of what she “knows” about the Peeler is speculation fueled by her hopes of leaving Grayce behind.

The PCs should leave the meeting with Damarys with the suspicion that she knows more about the Path River Peeler than she lets on. Throughout the encounter, she’s careful not to lie, instead smiling enigmatically if the PCs ask her a question she doesn’t want to answer. Though she might hint that the Peeler makes its lair somewhere in the Shivering Bluffs, she won’t reveal the exact location of the hags’ old cavern, Hag Hollow. If the PCs attack her, Damarys cowers and claims (truthfully, at this point) that she’s done nothing wrong. She fights back only if she feels her life’s in danger; if this occurs, Mocking-Vain also leaps to her defense. See area @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11} of Hag Hollow for statistics for both Damarys and Mocking-Vain, if needed.

Regardless of the outcome of the meeting, Damarys doesn’t want the PCs poking about in her business. That night, she sends the party a warning (see @UUID[.8qaR66FyblF61ift]{Event 1: Grisly Delivery}), then retreats to Hag Hollow to alert her allies there.

Reward

For meeting with Damarys, reward the party 20 XP.

Albin's Ranch.name: Albin's Ranch
Albin's Ranch.text:
Having finished their preliminary investigation, the PCs can head to Albin Derkensoor’s ranch. When they arrive, Albin greets the party accompanied by his ranch hand, Euphis (superstitious male human laborer 0). Albin shows the PCs to the rooms he’s prepared for them in the main building, then gives them free rein of the rest of the grounds. If the characters seem uncertain about how to begin, Albin suggests two avenues of investigation: searching the sheep’s pen for clues and interviewing Euphis about the night he saw the Peeler.

Searching the Pen: Albin has been a successful rancher for decades, and even though he now leaves most of the work to hired hands, his flock of sheep remains several dozen strong. Albin’s sheep appear healthy, but the animals are clearly spooked, huddling together in one corner of the pen and bleating excitably as the PCs approach. A PC can attempt to calm the sheep by making a @Check[nature|dc:14|options:action:command-an-animal] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.q9nbyIF0PEBqMtYe]{Command an Animal}. On a success, the sheep settle and return to moving about the pen, though they still clearly avoid one end of the wooden enclosure.

A PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the pen can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:14|options:action:search|traits:secret] check. On a success, the character finds a set of unusual tracks in one corner of the pen. (If the PCs calmed the sheep, the tracks are in the area the flock continues to avoid. PCs who Search that area notice the tracks automatically.) The tracks are of a creature that walks upright like a human, but with long, thin toes like those of a primate.

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[stealth|dc:22|options:action:track|name:PF2E.Actions.Track.Title|traits:secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Track} can follow the trail to the bottom of a 20-foot-high cliff about a mile north of Albin’s ranch (in the general direction of the Shivering Bluffs). The tracks disappear at this point, suggesting that the creature scrambled up the cliff on the way to wherever it was headed.

No matter how hard the characters search, they lose the Peeler’s trail here, though a character who makes a successful @Check[perception|dc:14] check discovers a growth of unusual black fungus nearby. The finger-like growths are cold to the touch and if harvested dissolve to oily slime within minutes. A character who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:21|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} identifies the growths as barrow claw, an extremely rare fungus said to be native to the Netherworld. (The Path River Peeler unknowingly deposited the barrow claw spores here on its flight from Albin’s ranch to Hag Hollow.)

Interviewing Euphis: Euphis is a kind-hearted human man in his late 20s, but his overactive imagination often leads to naivety. He’s worked for Albin for several years now, though he maintains vague hopes of becoming a soldier, or perhaps an adventurer like the PCs. He even keeps a battered shield and wooden sword beside his bed in one of the ranch’s outbuildings. On the night of the Peeler’s visit, Euphis was awakened to the sound of the sheep screaming in their pen. Grabbing his sword and shield, Euphis rushed to the yard and spotted the Peeler silhouetted in the moonlight. He began shouting and banging on his shield, driving off the Peeler with his racket before the monster could turns its attention on him.

Euphis caught only a brief glance of the Peeler, and his memories are confused by his active imagination. He variously describes the Peeler as a vampire, a bat-faced demon, and an ape-like creature akin to a black-furred yeti. Sorting out what Euphis really saw requires a @Check[diplomacy|dc:14] check. On a success, the PCs confirm the following.

  • The Peeler walked upright and was covered with bristly black fur. It had weirdly long fingers and saucer-like eyes that reflected the moonlight.

  • The Peeler clearly intending to harm the sheep, but when Euphis banged on his shield, the creature clasped its oversized ears and fled.

  • A chill lingered in the air even after the Peeler retreated, leaving Euphis shivering for several minutes. (In fairness, Euphis’s shivering was likely more due to fear than the chill.)

If the PCs happen to ask Euphis about Damarys, he knows the woman well, as the two of them shared their childhood at Andoletta’s temple. Like most people in town, Euphis doesn’t like Damarys, going so far as to accuse her of practicing sinister magics. Euphis recounts one night when they were teenagers, where he followed Damarys as she stole her way to the Shivering Bluffs. Once she spotted him, she turned into a raven and took flight. (Like many of his memories, Damarys’s transformation is a product of Euphis’s overactive imagination, though the seed of the story remains true.) If pressed, Euphis can tell a dozen more stories about times Damarys was mean to him or picked on him.

Development

There’s nothing more to be discovered at the ranch. As the stake-out spot Jarelle identified is a day’s walk away, Albin suggests the PCs rest for the night before heading out the next morning.

Reward

For investigating Albin’s ranch, grant the party 20 XP. Reward the PCs an additional 20 XP if they discover and correctly identify the barrow claw fungus.

Grisly Delivery.name: Grisly Delivery
Grisly Delivery.text:
Whether the PCs rest at Albin’s ranch or somewhere back in town, that night they receive an unsettling delivery. If the characters think to set a watch, whichever PC is awake at midnight can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:14] check. On a success, they hear a shuffling noise outside their door, followed by the sound of receding footsteps. A character who rushes to the door arrives in time to spot a hooded figure retreating into the night.

A PC can run down the fleeing figure by succeeding at a @Check[acrobatics|dc:16] or @Check[athletics|dc:16] check. On a failure, Euphis tackles the figure in the yard instead (if the PCs are resting in town, a different bystander waylays the figure). Once their hood is removed, the figure is revealed to be a local youth named Lev Urada (stubborn male human punk 0). Lev snarls and struggles to escape but eventually relents, knowing he’s been caught.

Outside the PCs’ door lies a halfling-sized bundle wrapped in a heavy blanket. Unwrapping the bundle reveals a freshly peeled sheepskin, still wet with blood. This grisly delivery is from Damarys, who gave Lev a few coins to deliver the package in hopes of dissuading the party from further investigations.

Lev fears and idolizes Damarys in equal measure. The PCs must succeed at a @Check[intimidation|dc:14|options:action:coerce|name:PF2E.Actions.Coerce.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce} him into revealing where he got the sheepskin. If the PCs bring the matter to the town guard, the authorities are sympathetic but admit there’s not much they can do: Unless the PCs can prove Damarys stole the sheep from which the skin was taken, she hasn’t broken any law. If the PCs head to Damarys’s cottage to confront her there, they find her cottage empty, though the skinless body of the sheep (which was, indeed, was taken from her own flock) hangs from a tree out back.

Reward

Award the party 20 XP for discovering the source of the bloody sheepskin, either by interrogating Lev or by visiting Damarys’s cottage.

Shivering Bluffs.name: Shivering Bluffs
Shivering Bluffs.text:
A hard-beaten livestock path winds its way through the hills east of Grayce to the location Jarelle identified as the most likely place to encounter the Path River Peeler. Local shepherds graze their flocks here, but they’ve been avoiding the area in recent days due to everyone being on edge about the Peeler sightings. Walking there (either from Grayce or Albin’s ranch) takes most of the day. Along the way, the PCs pass by pastures where the sheep of Grayce graze, but other than the occasional meeting with a shepherd and their flock, the journey is uneventful. Once they arrive, the PCs can make camp atop the hill Jarelle identified, giving them a clear view of the surrounding countryside­—and a beautiful sunset.

A few hours after sunset, the silence is broken by an unnerving cackle that echoes across the hills. As the PCs search for the laughter’s source, each of them can attempt a @Check[type:perception|dc:14|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek}. Any character who succeeds spots a dark figure near a copse of trees a few hundred yards from their campsite. The night is too dark to make out many details, but the figure seems to be covered in animal fur, though it stands upright like a humanoid. As soon as the PCs move in its direction, the figure bolts and disappears into the trees.

Countryside Chase.name: Countryside Chase
Countryside Chase.text:
The figure the PCs spotted is Jarelle’s sister, Phara, who has dressed up in a homemade Peeler costume for a bit of fun at the party’s expense. Chasing down Phara uses the chase rules found @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.journals.JournalEntry.S55aqwWIzpQRFhcq.JournalEntryPage.HSg7h1jm5oASbXao]{here}. Phara starts the chase one obstacle ahead of the PCs and moves at a pace of one obstacle each round. The chase ends when the PCs catch up to Phara, or once Phara reaches the chase’s final obstacle. Remember that if the PCs successfully helped Jarelle identify this location, each of them gains a +1 circumstance bonus to checks made to overcome obstacles during the chase.

Effect

@UUID[Item.jM2lWQ6JUFaZkHHt]{Countryside Familiarity}

If the PCs gain the +1 circumstance bonus for this chase from helping Jarelle, you can apply this effect to each party member to automate it. As long as the skill checks presented below are used, this effect's bonus will be toggled on automatically.

Keep Pace

Obstacle 2

Chase Points 3; Overcome @Check[acrobatics|dc:12|options:countryside-chase|name:Keep Pace] or @Check[athletics|dc:12|options:countryside-chase|name:Keep Pace] to maintain pace with the fleeing figure, @Check[perception|dc:12|options:countryside-chase|name:Keep Pace] to keep the figure in sight

The shadowy figure breaks away, threatening to escape into the night. As the PCs bound down the hillside, they must watch their footing to avoid a nasty tumble.

Overgrown Forest

Obstacle 2

Chase Points 2; Overcome @Check[perception|dc:16|options:countryside-chase|name:Overgrown Forest] to avoid becoming lost in the lightless woods, @Check[survival|dc:12|options:countryside-chase|name:Overgrown Forest] to spot the clearest route through the vegetation

The copse of trees at the bottom of the hill is overgrown with briars.

Crossing the Gully

Obstacle 2

Chase Points 2; Overcome @Check[acrobatics|dc:12|options:countryside-chase|name:Crossing the Gully] to use the fallen tree like a balance beam, @Check[athletics|dc:16|options:countryside-chase|name:Crossing the Gully] to leap across the gully

Rainwater from the bluffs has cut a gully through this part of the woods. An uprooted tree spans the gap.

Find the Trail

Obstacle 2

Chase Points 3; Overcome @Check[survival|dc:12|options:countryside-chase|name:Find the Trail] to pick up the figure’s trail, @Check[perception|dc:16|options:countryside-chase|name:Find the Trail] to spot a tuft of fur left behind from Phara’s costume

As the PCs emerge from the forest, they find themselves at the foot of the Shivering Bluffs. Picking up the figure’s trail from here requires keen eyes.

If the PCs catch up with Phara, she begs for mercy as soon as the characters unmask her. She admits to stitching together the Peeler costume from the odd animal pelts, then hiding in the nearby trees to wait for the PCs to arrive. She only wanted to have a little fun, she explains, and can’t suppress a mischievous grin when she recalls the chase. “You should’ve seen the looks on all your faces!”

If the PCs fail to catch Phara, they instead find her costume a short distance from the entrance to Hag Hollow, where she discarded it before heading back to town. In this case, the figure’s identity remains a mystery, though at your discretion Phara might admit to the prank later, after the PCs return to town.

Development

Regardless of when (or if) the PCs catch up to Phara, moments after the chase ends, another cackle pierces the night. Unlike the laughter they heard previously, the PCs are certain no mortal could reproduce this sound. In fact, the laughter is the otherworldly cry of the real Path River Peeler, returning to its lair after another successful hunt. If the PCs caught up with Phara at the Find the Trail obstacle, the sound comes from just over the nearest hill. Otherwise, the laughter continues long enough to lead the PCs to the entrance of Hag Hollow (area @UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.u2WXLRV9GycOpTPM]{A1}).

If Phara is with the PCs when they hear the Peeler’s cry, her eyes go wide at the sound. Assuming the PCs send her home while they investigate the laughter’s source, Phara readily agrees, this time without a hint of protest.

Reward

Award the PCs 60 XP if they successfully chase down Phara.

Overview (MlWG).name: Overview
Overview (MlWG).text:
Hag Hollow is just one of the many natural cave systems that riddle the bluffs along the Path River. After the hags that once inhabited the caverns were driven away, the site sat empty for centuries, until Damarys’s voices led her to the location. Since then, Damarys has visited Hag Hollow regularly, enjoying the solitude the caves afford. A few years ago, a tribe of kobolds called the Shiverscales also happened upon the caves. At first, Damarys disliked the Shiverscales, but she agreed to let them stay after they promised to guard the caverns in her absence. The fact that the Shiverscales have come to regard the Path River Peeler as a sort of patron spirit has only endeared the kobolds to her further.

In addition to Damarys and the Shiverscales, two other groups of creatures inhabit Hag Hollow. The first is a band of sprigjacks lead by Damarys’s minion Mocking-Vain. The sprigjacks actually predate Damarys’s arrival at Hag Hollow, though they’ve since accepted the reclusive woman as the true holder of the caves. The second group is a pair of fungus leshies drawn by the barrow claw fungus that infests the caverns. Though the Shiverscales, the sprigjacks, and the leshies are all loyal to Damarys (and, through her, the Path River Peeler), the three groups generally avoid each other. None of them have ever crossed the chasm (area @UUID[.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5}) that separates their lairs from the deepest parts of the caverns (areas @UUID[.Ko6VaK8YonCisnAN]{A10}–@UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}).

Of course, the Path River Peeler also lives within Hag Hollow. Every generation or so, the rift in area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12} opens wide enough for the Peeler to enter the Universe. During these times, the Peeler haunts the countryside until the rift begins to close again, at which point the monster returns home to the Netherworld. While in the Universe, the Peeler usually comes and goes from Hag Hollow via a second tunnel that opens onto the surface about a half mile away (see area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}).

Hag Hollow Features

Hag Hollow is a natural cave system with walls and floors worn smooth by centuries of inhabitance. Unless noted otherwise, the ceilings of the caverns are 10 feet high, while those of passageways are 7 feet high. All areas are unlit, except for area @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11}, where Damarys’s campfire fills the area with dim light. The temperature throughout the caverns is unnaturally cold—not quite enough to freeze skin, but cold enough to frost one’s breath.

When the PCs arrive, Damarys is in area @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11}, having retreated to the caverns shortly after the PCs visited her. If the PCs didn’t meet with Damarys, she’s still in @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11}, but none of the inhabitants of Hag Hollow are on alert for intruders. In this case, you might decide to give the PCs a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative until the party’s presence in the caverns becomes obvious.

Scene

@UUID[Scene.AIIwIbRO0qPJ6SPQ]{Hag Hollow}

You can find our provided map for Hag Hollow in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

Effect

@UUID[Item.7GWHHv1FDKQTiMHO]{Surprise Visit}

If you decide to give the PCs the aforementioned circumstance bonus to initiative, you can apply this effect to them. Don't forget to remove it once their presence becomes obvious!

Approach.name: Approach
Approach.text:
A footpath winds its way to the base of a cliff before disappearing into a low, dark cave. Boulders and thorny bushes line the path.

Though the Path River Peeler typically enters Hag Hollow from another direction (see area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}), this entrance is where both Damarys and the Shiverscale kobolds come and go from the caves. The brush, boulders, and shape of the cliff face explain why Hag Hollow has remained largely unexplored for centuries; from any distance of more than 100 feet or so, the entrance is entirely unnoticeable.

Encounter

Low 2

@UUID[Actor.TElwkEGZy1zgwoVg]{Sprigjacks x4}

Creatures: A group of four sprigjacks—subordinates of Damarys’s minion Mocking-Vain—lurk in the bushes just outside the entrance to the caves. The sprigjacks wait until the PCs approach the cave entrance before leaping from the thorns to attack.

Trapped Entrance.name: Trapped Entrance
Trapped Entrance.text:
Inside the cliff face, the footpath continues, snaking between walls of smooth but natural stone.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.4kc6sYSc56Q2KYTT.PlaylistSound.XOdbzjAFdhh4dBQN]{Hag Hollow}

As the party enters Hag Hollow, you can play this ambience sound.

Encounter

Trivial 2

@UUID[Actor.johVX4cgmJXlyIh7]{Spiked Walls x2} @UUID[Actor.u7kT6j1uCZGVDeyr]{Crumbrunk}

Hazards: At the two points marked on the map, {tripwires} span the tunnel low to the ground. If the PCs notice the wires, they can step over them easily. Otherwise, passing through either area causes a lattice of tree branches and wooden spikes to snap shut across the passageway.

Creature: The area where the tunnel widens is used as an impromptu workshop by @UUID[Actor.u7kT6j1uCZGVDeyr]{Crumbrunk}, a mischievous jinkin whom the Shiverscale kobolds grudgingly adopted after Crumbrunk was exiled from his own gremlin clan.

The Shiverscales don’t particularly like Crumbrunk, but they admit his traps are even more clever than the ones they could build themselves. If the PCs trigger his spiked wall traps, Crumbrunk crouches behind the boulder in the center of his workshop and peppers characters who are caught in the trapped section of the tunnel with blowgun darts. The boulder grants Crumbrunk standard cover, or greater cover if he uses the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ust1jJSCZQUhBZIz]{Take Cover} action.

Spiked Walls

The traps described above have been implemented as opened secret doors. If a character triggers any of the tripwires, you can click on the secret door to swing its spiked wall closed.

As described in the hazard's sheet, the characters are able to use an Interact action to temporarily push the wall open, so you can open and close these two secret doors as needed.

Development

If the PCs avoid or overcome his spiked wall traps, Crumbrunk shouts to alert the kobolds to the northwest. If alerted, the Shiverscales don’t come to Crumbrunk’s aid, but rather position themselves to ambush the characters when they arrive in area @UUID[.0LnR3wuDr6Vftntt]{A3}.

If captured, Crumbrunk can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerced} into telling the PCs more about Hag Hollow, including information about its current inhabitants and the general layout of the caverns. If asked about his own history, Crumbrunk explains his fellow gremlins cast him out after one of his traps malfunctioned and injured their leader. The PCs might encounter these gremlins in @UUID[JournalEntry.aPeBj20dAAiIHelW]{“Sabotage!”}, also in this adventure anthology.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.n8ZzGfII83v07YVQ]

Crumbrunk’s trap making tools function as an artisan’s toolkit worth 4 gp. Among the scattered tools is a thin glass vial that contains a lesser antidote.

Communal Cave.name: Communal Cave
Communal Cave.text:
This cavern is shaped roughly like a figure eight, with two smaller, circular caves joined in the center of the area. Pillars of natural stone stretch from floor to ceiling in each of these smaller caves. The ground near the base of the pillars is crowded with straw pallets, bedrolls, and the remnants of campfires. In the northern cave, rough stairs rise to the north, while another set of steps rises westward from the southern area. Tunnels stretch to the east from both the northern and southern caves.

The rank-and-file members of the Shiverscale tribe gather in this area. Their leader Zurkurk (area @UUID[.MSBwuZS2h79nNNtf]{A7}) occasionally visits to address them; otherwise, the kobolds spend their time sleeping, eating, or harassing Crumbrunk in area @UUID[.3Yz7wzrYSmukQjUp]{A2}.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.TpIuWrGVSvhqQ1e3]{Shiverscale Kobold ×4}

Creatures: Four shiverscale kobolds are in this area when the PCs arrive at Hag Hollow. If they hear sounds of combat in area @UUID[.3Yz7wzrYSmukQjUp]{A2}, two kobolds each hide behind the pillars to the north and south, ambushing the PCs as they enter the cave. The kobolds consider this a brilliant “pincer maneuver,” but they haven’t thought the tactic through. If any of them rolls a critical failure with their crossbow and at least one of their allies in the opposite cave is a possible target, roll a @Check[flat|dc:15]. On a failure, the bolt hits another kobold.

Development

Loud noises in this area alert the tribe’s gecko wrangler, Zoti, in area @UUID[.hQcK73p7jr2f9Hqc]{A4}, as well as Zurkurk’s bodyguards in area @UUID[.jmQwNpWjNv4IK5MB]{A6}. Neither group comes to investigate the sounds, but they prepare themselves for battle, as described in those areas.

Treasure

In addition to their weapons and armor, one of the kobolds has hidden a pouch containing seven agates worth 1 gp beneath their bedroll.

Gecko Grotto.name: Gecko Grotto
Gecko Grotto.text:
This oval-shaped grotto reeks of animal waste. In the southern wall, a recessed shelf appears to have been adapted as a sleeping space. The cavern’s floor drops into a chasm to the northwest.

Encounter

Low 2

@UUID[Actor.8EwWPFAi4K8Qdymk] @UUID[Actor.e8009N7Dav655oDg]

Zoti, the Shiverscales’ gecko wrangler, has used her seniority to take over this cavern as her living space. She spends most of her time here training her giant gecko, Big Eye, but as the tribe’s eldest member, she occasionally visits area @UUID[.MSBwuZS2h79nNNtf]{A7} to advise her son, Zurkurk.

Creatures: If she hears sounds of combat in area @UUID[.0LnR3wuDr6Vftntt]{A3}, Zoti sends Big Eye to the ceiling just above the cavern’s entrance and prepares herself for battle. Otherwise, Zoti rests in the alcove in the southern wall and must spend her first turn gathering up her spear and shield. Meanwhile, Big Eye clings to the stone just beneath the lip of the chasm to the northwest.

Development

Characters standing near the ledge to the northwest see the entrance to another cave (area @UUID[.Ko6VaK8YonCisnAN]{A10}) on the far side of the chasm. The chasm is 15 feet wide at this point, but the party could cross the distance using a grappling hook and rope or by constructing a bridge using the materials in area @UUID[.NhnZZjsLGUrOMiL5]{A8}. The chasm’s walls have a Climb DC of 15 (@Check[athletics|dc:15|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move]). See area @UUID[.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5} for a full description of the chasm.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.RYYgsVkxMWWuWzAz]

Zoti’s sleeping shelf is filled with heavy winter blankets and foul-smelling animal furs. Beneath the assorted bedding is a gecko potion.

Chasm of Echoes.name: Chasm of Echoes
Chasm of Echoes.text:
A chasm winds through the center of this cavern like a lazy river. In most places, the chasm is twenty feet across, though it narrows to half that distance in some spaces. Forty feet above the chasm’s floor, a ledge of natural stone wraps around the cavern’s eastern end, forming a walkway that connects the chasm’s northern and southern sides. The cavern’s ceiling rises another twenty feet above this ledge, its soaring vault transforming even the slightest sound made in the cavern into a chorus of echoes.

Due to the echoes, creatures in this area take a –2 circumstance penalty to Stealth checks made to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.VMozDqMMuK5kpoX4]{Sneak} and gain weakness 2 to sonic damage.

This cavern serves as a natural barrier between the areas to the south and the caves used by the coven of hags centuries ago (areas @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11}–@UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}). Only Damarys crosses the chasm regularly, walking along the ledge at the east end of the cavern. The Shiverscale kobolds are too frightened to venture past the chasm, and the Path River Peeler dislikes the echoes the cavern’s high ceiling creates. (If the PCs retreat here during the encounter with the Peeler in area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}, the monster pursues them as far as the ledge south of area @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11}, but no further.)

Navigating the Chasm: Depending on where the PCs enter this area, they should be able to see several exits from the chamber, including the tunnels to areas @UUID[.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5}, @UUID[.aXzSUJJbFbqrUhaJ]{A9}, @UUID[.Ko6VaK8YonCisnAN]{A10}, and @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11}. The mouth of a wide cavern overlooks the chasm at area @UUID[.hQcK73p7jr2f9Hqc]{A4}. Finally, a cramped tunnel opens onto the chasm’s floor from area @UUID[.NhnZZjsLGUrOMiL5]{A8}. This opening is hidden from the ledge, but characters on the ground can find it with a successful @Check[type:perception|dc:14|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search}.

Though it is barely 5 feet wide, the natural ledge that circles the cavern is stable, save for the 10-foot-square section outside the tunnel to area @UUID[.0LnR3wuDr6Vftntt]{A3}. See the Hazard section below for details about this unstable overlook.

The ledge south of area @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11} is only 10 feet from the ledge on the opposite side of the chasm, meaning characters could conceivably Leap the gap. Alternatively, the party can cross the distance using a grappling hook and rope or by constructing a bridge using the materials in area @UUID[.NhnZZjsLGUrOMiL5]{A8}. Of course, the PCs could also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climb} down the cavern’s walls, cross the bottom of the chasm on foot, and Climb up the opposite side. The chasm’s walls have a Climb DC of 15 (@Check[athletics|dc:15|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move]).

Macro

@UUID[Macro.RvN1HeCjwJFj287x]{Craft Bridge}

If the party constructs a bridge using the materials in area A8, you can run this macro to place a bridge tile in the chasm!

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.CltT4PlhmoStdhc7]{Unstable Overlook} @UUID[Actor.EfQoNdBj3GMeQ4vK]{Skeletal Ogre}

Hazard: The jinkin Crumbrunk (area @UUID[.3Yz7wzrYSmukQjUp]{A2}) has prepared this natural ledge to collapse. Though the Shiverscales and Damarys know how to avoid the weakened area, the PCs might not be so lucky.

Creatures: A few decades ago, a wandering ogre discovered Hag Hollow but slipped and fell as he edged along the chasm’s ledge. The ogre’s remains—animated by the presence of the rift to the Netherworld in area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}—patrols the chasm’s floor.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.MfMrUF8w7jmFURsj]{Collapse Ledge}

As the party moves into the overlook, you can run this macro to cause the ledge to collapse if triggered.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.yFNhBZIlPVJwMUVv]

The cavern’s floor is littered with rubble and other debris the Shiverscale kobolds have tossed into the chasm. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:14|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to Search through the trash discovers a silver bangle, once worn by the ogre as an earring, worth 5 gp.

Bodyguard Cave.name: Bodyguard Cave
Bodyguard Cave.text:
This cave is empty, save for a pair of straw pallets against the southern wall.

When not accompanying Zurkurk, two elite Shiverscale kobolds named Kar and Rikka rest or care for their weapons in this area.

Encounter

Low 2

@UUID[Actor.0vdtv3nZwZIP1i0G]{Kar} @UUID[Actor.57XSqifwStDCqWK6]{Rikka}

Creatures: If they hear sounds of combat in area @UUID[.0LnR3wuDr6Vftntt]{A3}, Kar and Rikka ready their crossbows and prepare to ambush the PCs as they enter, using Stealth for initiative.

Development

Noise here alerts Zurkurk in area @UUID[.MSBwuZS2h79nNNtf]{A7.} Unless the PCs are very quiet, the kobold chieftain comes to investigate after 3 rounds. If he does, this becomes a Severe encounter.

Zurkurk's Cave.name: Zurkurk's Cave
Zurkurk's Cave.text:
Three column-like formations of limestone support the twenty-foot-high ceiling of this cavern. Crude paintings of kobolds kneeling before a towering, demon-like figure decorate the cavern’s walls. A tattered curtain separates the main space from an alcove in the cavern’s southwest corner.

The leader of the Shiverscales, a kobold cavern mage named Zurkurk, led his tribe to the Shivering Bluffs several years ago. When they encountered Damarys in Hag Hollow, Zurkurk arranged a truce by swearing his tribe’s allegiance to the changeling. Zurkurk’s true loyalty, however, lies with the Path River Peeler. Though he’s only seen the monster once or twice, Zurkurk is convinced the Peeler is a devil from Hell and hopes one day to bargain with the fiend for magical power. In the meantime, he spends his days painting fanciful depictions of the Peeler on the walls.

Cave Paintings: Zurkurk’s paintings don’t give the PCs a much clearer picture of the Peeler than the descriptions they collected back in Grayce. In these images, the Peeler is an ape-like creature with black claws that stretch nearly to its feet. If the scale of Zurkurk’s paintings could be trusted, the Peeler would stand nearly 20 feet tall—however, this is more a product of the kobold’s reverence for the creature, rather than an accurate representation of its size. (While far taller than a kobold, the Peeler is only about 6 feet tall.)

One detail Zurkurk managed to capture across all the paintings are the Peeler’s unusual, oversized ears. Insightful PCs might take this as another clue that the Peeler is sensitive to loud noises.

Encounter

Low 2

@UUID[Actor.wN11zf2bN04vFx6Q]{Zurkurk}

Creature: If the PCs haven’t encountered him elsewhere, they find the kobold here working on his latest painting on the cavern’s southern wall. If hard pressed, @UUID[Actor.wN11zf2bN04vFx6Q]{Zurkurk} casts invisibility on himself and flees up the passage to area @UUID[.aXzSUJJbFbqrUhaJ]{A9}, hoping his pursuers tumble into the pit trap in area @UUID[.NhnZZjsLGUrOMiL5]{A8}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.cykFxZ6qqOrFIDxC]

The alcove behind the curtain to the southwest conceals Zurkurk’s sleeping space. Blankets and animal pelts crowd the alcove. A shelf carved into the wall holds Zurkurk’s collection of brushes and paints, as well the entirety of the Shiverscales’ wealth: a pouch containing 80 sp and 32 gp, a collection of four minor healing potions, and an ivory walrus tusk worth 10 gp.

Snake Pit.name: Snake Pit
Snake Pit.text:
The tunnel turns at a nearly 90 degree angle as it leads toward the lair of dangerous fungus leshies. This bend is a perfect spot to set a trap for any potential invaders.

Encounter

Trivial 2

@UUID[Actor.BHq5wpQU8hQEke8D] @UUID[Actor.AJ5LuNMVPLCydryP]

Hazard: Crumbrunk, the jinkin trap maker from area @UUID[.3Yz7wzrYSmukQjUp]{A2}, recently dug a pit trap in the middle of this passageway. The Shiverscales and Damarys avoid the trap by sliding wooden planks across the pit. Stacks of these 10-foot-long planks rest against the walls to the east and west of the pit.

Creature: A giant viper lives at the bottom of the pit. Crumbrunk occasionally harvests the viper’s venom, which the jinkin uses to coat his blowgun darts. The viper attacks any creature that falls into the pit.

Crawlway

A tunnel with a low ceiling at the lowest part of this area slopes downwards 20 feet to the bottom of the chasm in area @UUID[.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5}. Medium or smaller creatures must @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Tj055UcNm6UEgtCg]{Crawl} down the passage and larger creatures must @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeeze}. This end of the tunnel is obvious, but characters in the chasm must succeed at a @Check[type:perception|dc:14|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} to notice it.

Development

With 10 minutes of work and a successful @Check[crafting|dc:16] check, a PC can use the wooden planks to build a bridge across the chasm in area @UUID[.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5}.

Macros

@UUID[Macro.lZVNElmjWQTYfoFv]{Trigger Pit} @UUID[Macro.RvN1HeCjwJFj287x]{Craft Bridge}

If the party triggers the hidden pit, run the Trigger Pit macro to reveal the trap!

As mention earlier, the party can construct a bridge using the materials here to cross the chasm in A5. If so, you can run the Craft Bridge macro to place a bridge tile in the chasm!

Leshy Lair.name: Leshy Lair
Leshy Lair.text:
The air inside this cave is even colder than elsewhere in the caverns. Black fungi shaped eerily like human fingers grow along the southern wall. A tunnel leads into the cave from the west, while a set of natural stairs turns sharply to the north.

The fungus is identical to what the PCs might have discovered while following the Peeler’s trail from Albin Derkensoor’s ranch. A character who succeeds at a @Check[type:nature|dc:21|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} can identify the fungus as barrow claw. The fungus is cold to the touch and quickly dissolves into oily slime if harvested. If allowed to spread, barrow claw can be a blight to crops, but it is otherwise harmless to animals and other creatures.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.UKSULD0e3gfanx1T]{Barrow Claw Leshies x2}

Creatures: When the rift from the Netherworld opened in area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}, the Path River Peeler unknowingly transported spores of barrow claw fungus here. The spores found purchase along the southern wall and eventually drew a pair of fungus leshies to the area. When the PCs enter the cave, the leshies have used their Change Shape ability to blend into the patches of barrow claw.

The leshies remain in their fungus form unless the PCs disturb the barrow claw, at which point they return to their true shapes and attack. The leshies fight to the death, but they don’t pursue characters who flee beyond the cavern.

Hidden Cave.name: Hidden Cave
Hidden Cave.text:
The entrance to this cave is hidden from most parts of area @UUID[.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5}, although creatures standing at the westernmost end of the ledge above the chasm can see it, as can creatures in area @UUID[.hQcK73p7jr2f9Hqc]{A4}. The PCs can reach the cave by shimmying across the chasm or by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climbing} the chasm’s walls, as described in area @UUID[JournalEntry.m9RHhYLLlsOypqar.JournalEntryPage.P2glT6Gpn3poXFxD]{A5}.

Nearly a century ago, a brave (but somewhat hapless) human swashbuckler named Klerran Keel discovered Hag Hollow and decided to explore the caverns. He made camp in this out-of-the-way cave, but before going to sleep he blew his bugle across the chasm, tickled by the echoes the call made. The racket disturbed the Path River Peeler, who crept into the hidden cave and killed Klerran while he slept.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.5QfO6h7sFpCOVsl1]

If the PCs make their way into the cave, they discover Klerran’s bones in a heap against the northern wall. Bloodstains on Klerran’s buckler suggest the man died of violence, though his rapier still rests inside its sheath nearby. Klerran’s pack has mostly rotted away, but among the scraps of leather the PCs can turn up his fateful bugle (a virtuoso musical instrument), as well as a vagabond’s teapot.

Development

A PC who blows Klerran’s bugle when they encounter the Path River Peeler in area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12} gains a +1 item bonus on Intimidation checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize} the monster.

Reward

Award the PCs 60 XP if they discover Klerran’s remains.

Coven Cave.name: Coven Cave
Coven Cave.text:
The walls of this cavern rise to form a dome nearly twenty feet above the cavern’s floor. Six pillars made of natural stone—but spaced too evenly to have occurred by chance—form a ring in the center of the space. Scratched into the cavern’s walls are hundreds of strange symbols; while some are simple stick figures, others seem to bear occult significance.

Beneath the carvings grow patches of black fungus shaped like human fingers. A tunnel leads into the area from the southeast, while a set of natural stone stairs exits downward to the east.

In centuries past, the hags that once inhabited Hag Hollow gathered in this cave to commune with one another and share foul magics. This includes the original ritual they used to open the portal to the Netherworld in area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}. The voices Damarys hears are loudest here, and this is where she often comes when she visits the Shivering Bluffs. The pillars in the center of the cave were indeed shaped by magic, though they have no magical properties now. The black fungus is barrow claw, identical to the patches the PCs might have encountered in area @UUID[.aXzSUJJbFbqrUhaJ]{A9} or near @UUID[.fn2aQCd7IhNhi5Hp]{Albin’s ranch}.

Encounter

Moderate 2

@UUID[Actor.ipKDFMBbBuJHYlEa] @UUID[Actor.2wJUY9zDyB4ligT0]

Creatures: Once she finished with the sheepskin Lev Urada delivered to the party in @UUID[.8qaR66FyblF61ift]{Event 1}, Damarys headed to the Shivering Bluffs just in case the PCs found their way to Hag Hollow. When the PCs arrive, she stands beside a campfire inside the ring of pillars, while Mocking-Vain lurks in the shadows nearby.

Damarys believes (correctly) that if the PCs kill the Path River Peeler, the rift to the Netherworld will be closed forever. As a result, she tries to prevent the party from entering area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}. She gives the PCs one last chance to head back to Grayce. She starts off defiant, telling them that the caves are hers and they are intruding on her property, thinking that appealing to possessions might gain some traction with the adventurers. If they don’t listen to that approach, she pleads for them to leave, saying that her destiny is in these caves and the PCs are ruining her chance at destiny. If that approach doesn’t seem to work, she offers to tell them everything she knows about Hag Hollow, the Path River Peeler, and her supposed role in all this. She hopes they will be reasonable and understand things from her perspective, but by this point thinks its probably hopeless for them to understand. If they continue to refuse to leave, she attacks, opening combat by casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.CQb8HtQ1BPeZmu9h]{Stupefy} on the most likely spellcasters.

Carvings

The symbols on the walls were carved over generations by the hags who once inhabited the caverns. Most of the symbols are meaningless, but a character who studies the carvings for 10 minutes and succeeds at a @Check[occultism|dc:15] or @Check[arcana|dc:18], @Check[nature|dc:18], or @Check[religion|dc:18] check gains a +1 circumstance bonus on checks made to seal the nether rift hazard in area @UUID[.VGTidrWapVfro0IO]{A12}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.ofC0v29PmX5baPTx]

Among the carvings is a stylized image of a cat that any character trained in Occultism recognizes as an ancient symbol of protection. The image is etched into the wall, but the characters can chip it away with a minute of work. Once separated from the stone, the symbol functions as a jade cat talisman.

In addition to her armor and weapons, Damarys wears a ring of sigils.

Nether Rift.name: Nether Rift
Nether Rift.text:
The ceiling of this cavern is 20 feet high. The area is dark, but a crooked line of blue light glows in the middle of the northern wall. The light emanates from the rift to the Netherworld in that area and is visible from either entrance to the cave.

A layer of crystalline frost covers every surface of this oddly shaped cavern. The source of the frost is obvious: a chill breeze blows from a scar in the middle of the cavern’s northern wall, filling the area with gently drifting snowflakes. The fissure is only a thumb’s width across, but a pale blue light glows within it, visible even in the darkness.

Patches of black fungus, each roughly ten feet in diameter, grow throughout the cavern. Steps lead up into the area from the west, while another set of stairs rises to the east.

Working together, the hags that once inhabited Hag Hollow created this portal to the Netherworld. The portal opens infrequently—sometimes remaining shut for a decade or more—but when it does, the Path River Peeler finds its way into the Universe. Once it arrives, the Peeler hunts the area along the Path River until some unnamed force bids it to return, at which point the portal widens enough for the Peeler to pass back through it. Damarys hopes to accompany the Peeler the next time this occurs, but for now she must wait, as the Path River Peeler’s hunger remains unsated.

Encounter

Severe 2

@UUID[Actor.65OzVr2FfL0mX3Qy] @UUID[Actor.Adb41RiAbn5Xv4f3]

Creature: Shortly after the PCs enter the area, a deep, ominous cackle (identical to the one the characters heard outside Hag Hollow) echoes down the stairwell to the east. Moments later, the Path River Peeler emerges, having just returned from its most recent hunt. Clutched within the monster’s claws is the body of a sheep—not flayed entirely of skin but certainly ravaged and still dripping with fresh blood. When it notices the PCs, the Peeler tosses the carcass aside and unleashes its Otherworldly Cry.

In combat, the Peeler makes claw Strikes against the closest PC. If the characters successfully @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize} it, the Peeler uses its Flight Response reaction to scuttle up the cavern’s walls. It then uses Blood Run Cold against the PC that Demoralized it before returning to melee. The Peeler is immune to the effects of the nether rift hazard.

Hazard: When the Peeler appears, a gust of icy wind blasts from the portal to the Netherworld. The gust causes the temperature in the cavern to drop even further; in response, the barrow claw fungi throughout the area release their spores.

Development

If the PCs kill the Path River Peeler, the rift to the Netherworld snaps shut, leaving behind no evidence that it was ever there. If the PCs disable the hazard before the Peeler is defeated, the monster howls in rage as its connection to the Netherworld is severed. Until the portal is opened again (an event that won’t occur until long after the adventure has ended), the Peeler becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} and gains weakness 5 to all damage except cold.

The tunnel from which the Peeler entered meanders for about half a mile before opening onto the surface. Unless you want to expand the adventure by introducing additional encounter areas, this secondary entrance to Hag Hollow is unremarkable.

Effects

@UUID[Item.1tXJtcyVdGjhiltE]{Severed Netherworld Connection} @UUID[Item.k31hZrblNMSbmzym]{Carvings Knowledge}

Any character who successfully studied the @UUID[.pluGGQDzhHfgUI03]{A11} carvings can use the Carvings Knowledge effect to gain their circumstance bonus on checks to disable the Nether Rift.

If the Nether Rift is disabled before the Peeler is defeated, as described in the Development block above, you can apply the Severed Netherworld Connection effect to automate the Peeler's clumsy condition and weakness.

Concluding the Adventure.name: Concluding the Adventure
Concluding the Adventure.text:
Having defeated the Path River Peeler and closing the rift to the Netherworld, the PCs can return to Grayce as heroes. If they think to bring the Peeler with them, a crowd of townspeople quickly gathers to gawk at the alien-looking corpse. Titus Horvat, the farmer turned cryptozoologist, even offers the party a sum of 60 gp in exchange for the beast. Despite Titus’s best efforts to preserve its remains, the Peeler’s flesh rots unnaturally fast over the next few days, though the monster’s skeleton remains on display in their parlor for years to come.

As for Damarys, no one in Grayce celebrates her death, but her reluctance to help anyone but herself means she’s not missed. Her body is buried with little ceremony in the town’s smaller, new graveyard. The question of whether Damarys’s voices were only in her head, or if they truly were the whispers of the hags, remains unanswered. Perhaps one or more of the hags escaped extinction by fleeing through the rift and still plots revenge from their new home in the Netherworld. It’s possible Larmine, from the adventure @UUID[JournalEntry.wzqJL0YgefgczTx0]{“Sweet Tooth”}, was drawn to the area due to this strong presence and past hag activity, and she might not be the last hag to visit and prey upon the area!

Sweet Tooth.name: Sweet Tooth
Sweet Tooth.text:
Dalmira’s Bakery, a local institution that’s been providing Grayce with its breads and cakes for the better part of a decade, is under new management. Three months ago, customers arrived at the usual opening time to discover Dalmira nowhere to be found, leaving nothing but a note tacked to the door that she’d had a family emergency in Caliphas and would be gone “for some time.” Not to worry, though—her cousin Larmine would be arriving the next day to continue operations.

And arrive Larmine did, making the transition as smooth as could be expected on such short notice. Some even consider the new management a marked improvement over the old, as Larmine carries more sweets than Dalmira did, and many swear that her rolls are far softer and more fragrant. She even gives out spare treats to children, making her very popular with her neighbors. A few traditionalists still grumble, of course, but overall the townsfolk have been quite happy with the greater selection.

This, however, is only because no one knows Larmine’s secret: she’s actually a sweet hag drawn in by past hag activity in the region, who has been quietly preying on river travelers so as not to alert the general population. Her scheme first began when she broke into the gristmill down the river from Grayce and captured its owners, the Daswoorens, an older dwarven couple who have been processing grain in the region for decades. Larmine then stalked and abducted Dalmira when she was alone, leaving the note to excuse her absence before spiriting the baker away to the mill. She then changed her shape into that of a helpful cousin and reopened the bakery the next morning. So far, her schemes have gone unnoticed and three boats of travelers have fallen victim to her plots, but even she knows it’s only a matter of time before Grayce’s residents grow wise to her scheme and find a way to fight back.

Getting Started.name: Getting Started
Getting Started.text:
This adventure begins in the Grayce town square during a bustling market day. Read or paraphrase the following to set the scene.

The shops open bright and early on market day, some flinging wide the doors to their buildings and drawing back the windows that face the town square, others coming in from further afield to set up stalls along the cobblestone streets at the heart of the village. Soon, customers flood in from all corners of Grayce and beyond, building into a bustling crowd of shoppers, gawkers, and the occasional street minstrel plying their trade.

At the fountain in the center of town, a spritely blonde aiuvarin girl stands on the edge of the basin with a plum in each hand, waving them over her head as she shouts, “Market day special, two plums, three copper, get ‘em while they last!” A basket of the fruits sits at her feet, a sign propped against them proclaiming their provenance from “Fingael Farm Fruits.”

Outside Dalmira’s Bakery, its current proprietor—not Dalmira, but her cousin, a plump middle-aged human woman with a warm smile—weaves her way through the tables, delivering orders of fresh bread and fluffy cakes to the eager diners. She shares a conspiratorial wink with a passing child, then slips a cookie from the pocket of her apron and passes it into their waiting hands before slipping back into her shop tending to the customers waiting at the counter.

On a nearby corner, a stout dwarven tinker rattles the pots in his wagon as he pulls it up to an empty patch and begins setting up shop. Before long, locals come by to examine the cookware for sale, or to bring their dented pots for repairs.

In every direction, the marketplace of Grayce unfolds, and the air is dense with the chatter of the crowds.

By this point in their adventures, the PCs have likely garnered a reputation as problem-solvers. That’s why the local sheriff, Jindel Macroi (perspicacious female human sheriff 6), has requested that they attend today’s market as a bit of extra security, just in case she needs some extra help on hand to manage the crowd and the many unfamiliar faces it contains. Luckily, her precaution appears to be just that, as the day proceeds without incident. Jindel accompanies the PCs on a relaxed stroll through the bustling market, and is in the midst of saying (with relief) that everything appears to be going smoothly when she’s approached by a concerned citizen.

A small hand catches Jindel’s wrist, stopping her in mid-stride. “Beggin’ your pardon, Sheriff, but I need to ask. Have you heard from the Daswoorens of late? Has anyone?”

The speaker is a gnome dressed in worn leathers, a bow across their back and leaves strategically tucked among their forest-green hair. Jindel frowns down at them thoughtfully. “The millers? Can’t say I have. Why?”

“I was out by the gristmill this morning, heard something mighty strange—the wheel, making a real ruckus. Arvent wouldn’t ever let it carry on like that.” The hunter fidgets, their expression growing deeper with concern. “Saw some things, too. I ain’t an expert, but… it looked like bugbears. And nobody I’ve talked to has seen the Daswoorens in weeks. I… I think something bad’s going on down there.”

Sergei (astute nonbinary gnome hunter 3) is a bit solitary for a gnome, but known to be cautious, steady, and reliable—not the sort to spin tall tales. Jindel takes their words into consideration for a moment before turning to the PCs and asking them to investigate the claim (assuming the PCs don’t volunteer their services first). Below is some additional information, in the form of questions the PCs might ask and their potential answers.

Who are the Daswoorens?

Jindel answers. “Arvent and Monnery Daswooren run the gristmill a few miles downriver from town. It’s honestly not unusual for people not to see them; they tend to keep to themselves. You might want to ask around a bit before going to bother them. Arvent’s sister lives in town. You could ask her, though they haven’t gotten along for a while. And I think the girl who delivers the grain just came into town from her route. Elida.”

What makes you think there’s bugbears?

Sergei shrugs. “Tracks. Hair, caught in the branches. A bad smell. I’m not an expert, though. I can show you on the map where the hunting trails are. Then you could see for yourself.”

Why didn’t you go to the mill yourself?

Sergei holds up their hands in self-defense. “I’m a hunter, mate, not a fighter. I can handle some rabbits or a stag, but bugbears? If it was them, I’d be a goner, and then there’d be nobody to report back. I hope I’m wrong, but my gut says I’m not.”

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
The PCs don’t have a strict time limit for their investigation, though the sheriff encourages them to set off by the following morning. This provides the PCs at least 6 hours to Gather Information or perform other preparations before daylight wanes, shops begin closing, and people return home for dinner. Beyond this, there are several key NPCs the PCs might question, and while failing to engage with them doesn’t thwart the PCs’ sleuthing, it does have a small impact on their @UUID[.X9kctv9AMUZlOjIQ]{XP story award}.

In addition to the investigation locations detailed on the following pages, which can be done in any order, the PCs might wish to follow Jindel’s suggestion and ask around the market for more information. Doing so nets them a bit of information on the Daswoorens, along with a broad range of local gossip. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[grayce-lore|dc:13|options:action:gather-information|name:PF2E.Actions.GatherInformation.Title|traits:exploration,secret] check, a @Check[diplomacy|dc:16|options:action:gather-information|name:PF2E.Actions.GatherInformation.Title|traits:exploration,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.plBGdZhqq5JBl1D8]{Gather Information}, or a @Check[society|dc:17|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} hears or recalls a fact they don’t already know from the list below. On a critical success, the PC receives two facts, while a PC who critically fails hears a false rumor of your own invention.

  • The gristmill downriver from town has been there for the better part of a century, built by Arvent Daswooren’s father. Arvent and his wife Monnery took over the business just under forty years ago, after his father passed away from illness.

  • Kirnac Tinsmith, the traveling tinker, got into a mighty brawl at the Ash Inn’s tavern last time he was in town. It ended with him thrown out and banned from the building. Jakivi Rindix (cordial male human innkeeper 4) claims it all happened because Kirnac got overly drunk and belligerent, but Kirnac’s been telling anyone who’ll listen that Jakivi stiffed him on the bill for a set of tableware.

  • People have been raving about the improvement in sweets selection and in the taste of the bread available at Dalmira’s Bakery ever since its current proprietor, Larmine, took over three months ago. Some folks think being too loud about the preference is in bad taste, however, given the way Dalmira had to rush out of town so suddenly to deal with an unexpected family illness in Caliphas.

  • The gristmill was never really meant to be lived in—when Arvent’s father was alive, the family lived in town and took the grain to and from the mill themselves, meeting the farmers in the market and the merchants at the docks. But Arvent and Monnery moved out to the mill for good around fifteen years ago, after Arvent had a falling out with his sister Orivana.

  • Old man Fingael’s sent his granddaughter Anais into town to hawk fruits from their orchard for years, but over the past few months their offerings have withered down from a full cart to a single basket. The townsfolk have started to whisper that either the trees or Fingael are getting sick, leaving Anais to make ends meet on her own. (This rumor is untrue—the farm’s stock is mostly going to a new, lucrative contract with a greengrocer in Anactoria. But Anais is more than happy to let it spread because she’s coming into town to earn some pocket money, and more sympathy nets her extra sales.)

  • No one in town’s really sure what happened to cause the falling out between Arvent and Orivana Daswooren, but the two siblings are still infamously bitter about it to this day. Monnery comes into town once every other month or so for shopping, and she’ll usually check in with Orivana when she does, but so far as anyone knows Arvent and his sister haven’t spoken for over a decade.

Cartwright's Clues.name: Cartwright's Clues
Cartwright's Clues.text:
The PCs can find Elida Cartwright (guarded female halfling cart driver 3) outside the Apple Tree Stables, where she’s in the midst of scrubbing down the larger of her two stubborn old mules. The small but sturdy cart she uses to run deliveries of mail and merchants’ goods to and from the town waits nearby, and the other mule is inside the stable lazily chewing hay.

Elida has been out of town doing her job the last few weeks and thus has no context for who the PCs are or why they’d be approaching her out of the blue. The mule she’s grooming shows even less patience than she does, using the halfling’s distraction to snag a mouthful of her hair and start chewing before she scolds the animal into letting go. Getting Elida to speak in anything more than short, guarded sentences requires a PC to succeed at a @Check[diplomacy|dc:22|options:action:make-an-impression|name:PF2E.Actions.MakeAnImpression.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression}, the DC of which can be reduced by 2 for each of the following actions a PC takes:

  • Repair the broken wheel on Elida’s cart with either a 2nd-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.dINQzhqGmIsqGMUY]{Mending} spell or a successful @Check[crafting|dc:15] check.

  • Calm her ornery mule with a successful @Check[nature|dc:16|options:action:command-an-animal|traits:auditory,concentrate] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.q9nbyIF0PEBqMtYe]{Command an Animal}, and then help her finish giving it a bath.

The Diplomacy check to Make an Impression can be attempted multiple times if necessary, but after 3 failed attempts Elida gets frustrated and storms off, refusing to speak with the PCs at all.

If they win her over, Elida confirms for the PCs that she has a standing contract with the Daswoorens to transport grain from the farmers who come in for the market to the gristmill, and then take the finished flour from the gristmill to the various business in town, the docks, or the nearby towns as needed. Thing is, it’s a seasonal contract, and she hasn’t been to the mill since last year because the farmers won’t start bringing in the wheat harvest for another month yet. She shrugs off any rumors the PCs have heard about the couple, saying that their business is none of hers, and describes them as “nice enough” and “her kind of people,” meaning they keep things professional and don’t waste time on small talk.

If the PCs mention why they’re asking after the Daswoorens, or if they ask Elida if she’s seen anything unusual on the roads out of town, she thinks for a moment before mentioning that, over the last few months, there have been a handful of merchants who have seemingly disappeared somewhere on the river between Grayce and Caliphas. The latest is actually a friend of hers, an aiuvarin named Taynor Belziz, whom she said goodbye to in Grayce with plans to meet up for drinks in Caliphas two weeks later, but they never showed up. Elida doesn’t think the two points are related, but the gristmill is built onto the river, so feels it was worth bringing up.

Family Drama.name: Family Drama
Family Drama.text:
Arvent Daswooren’s sister, Orivana Daswooren (stubborn female dwarf gardener 3) can be found in her home, a humble cottage with a lush garden and dedicated greenhouse. When the PCs arrive, she answers the door with her gardening apron still on, having just finished washing the dirt from her hands after a long day’s work.

The mention of her brother makes her scowl, and a PC (any PC) must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:15|options:damaging-effect] save to catch the door before she slams it in their face; if all PCs fail the Reflex save and someone critically fails, that PC takes @Damage[1d4[bludgeoning]] damage as the door is slammed on their fingers. If nobody manages to keep the door open, convincing her to open it again to continue the conversation requires a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:16] check. The lock on the door is poor (requiring two successful @Check[thievery|dc:15|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks to pick or a successful @Check[athletics|dc:18|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open}), but forcing a conversation in this way causes all DCs to interact with Orivana going forward to increase by 5.

Once she’s been convinced to speak with them, getting Orivana to talk about her brother specifically requires the PCs to succeed at a second @Check[type:diplomacy|dc:18] check; this DC can be lowered by –2 if the PCs mention Monnery while trying to persuade her. If the PCs succeed, Orivana goes quiet for a while, then heaves a sigh, tells the PCs to hold on a moment, and disappears into her cottage. She returns a moment later.

Orivana reappears cradling a cinnamon-colored ferret in one arm. “This here’s Carrot,” she says, scratching the creature behind the ear as it tries to hide its face in her chest. “He’s Monnery’s baby. Comes from the same litter as my Rex. She’d bring him over to play. And this…” She holds up an old, tarnished silver ring with an emerald the size of a walnut. “This is the reason my brother and I haven’t spoken for fifteen years.

“Our mother left me this. I don’t have much use for jewelry, so it stayed with Dad’s things out at the mill, until Arvent started renovating the place to put in an apartment. Somewhere along the way it went missing. I was sure he’d sold it. I’ve never been so mad.” She rolls it between her fingers so the gem sparkles in the light. “Imagine my surprise when Carrot turned up, all on his own, dirty and shaking and huddled in my greenhouse for warmth… wearing this on a ribbon around his neck.

“I don’t know what this means. I just know my brother’s too damn proud to not come rub this in my face... if he could.”

In fact, Arvent dispatched Carrot and the ring as a desperate cry for help, hoping the wily mustelid would eventually find Orivana. If a PC can communicate with animals, they can question Carrot. He’s braggadocious about his myriad exploits since leaving the mill, and the PC regularly needs to praise his bravery, distract him with cooked chicken, or remind him of their questions in order to keep him focused. He knows that big, hairy people (the bugbears) attacked the mill, so he hid in Arvent’s beard while the dwarves were marched to the basement. Arvent tied the emerald ring to Carrot’s neck before releasing the ferret, hoping it might seek help.

The Hunter's Trail.name: The Hunter's Trail
The Hunter's Trail.text:
