Sergei can give the PCs directions to the hunting trail where they found their clues, but they decline any request to tag along; they don’t want to influence the investigation and would just get in the way if there really is danger. Following the unmarked trail takes an hour of hiking and a successful @Check[survival|dc:15] check. On a failure, the PCs take a wrong turn along the way and wind up stumbling into a thicket of blackberries; they take @Damage[1d4[piercing]|name:Thicket of Blackberries] damage from the thorns, and are then able to untangle themselves and find their way back onto the trail.

While following the trail, the PCs can attempt a @Check[nature|dc:14] check, @Check[survival|dc:16] check, or @Check[perception|dc:18] check to find the clues Sergei mentioned that hint at bugbears in the area. A PC who succeeds at the Nature check finds tufts of coarse brown fur caught in the branches along the trail, while those who get a critical success can identify the fur as coming from bugbears. A PC who succeeds on the Survival check finds tracks in the dirt and mud belonging to an unknown number of bipedal creatures with claw-like toenails and at least one other, Large-sized creature whose footprints are otherwise nearly human; on a critical success, the PC can identify these tracks as belonging to at least two, possibly three bugbears and one ogre.

Each PC who succeeds at the Perception check finds a different handmade bead scattered somewhere on the ground, while one who rolls a critical success finds half a dozen of them. The beads are a mix of glass and clay, all different shapes and sizes, and all extremely colorful. There’s no context for where they might’ve come from here, but the PCs will learn their origin when they meet Zini in area @UUID[.hOamDxpAMcCjfw63]{A2}.

PCs who can communicate with local flora or fauna might poll these unlikely witnesses. Plants report that about six people marched this way; most of them walked softly and stepped around plants, but the big one crushed whatever it stepped on—including tearing down some low-hanging elm branches that now allows more sunlight to reach the undergrowth, much to the latter’s appreciation. Local squirrels and birds saw a goblin, about 3–6 hairy goblins (they squabble about the numbers), and a giant person walk this way. The giant pushed the small goblin into a tree trunk, and little rocks (the beads, which animals were sad to discover weren’t edible) fell off the scared goblin. If a PC communicating with the woodland creatures bribes them with a suitable snack or improves their attitude with a @Check[diplomacy|dc:11] check, the animals are willing to guide the PCs toward where the humanoids went, traveling as far as the next encounter and granting the PCs the benefits of the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kV3XM0YJeS2KCSOb]{Scouting} exploration activity for the @UUID[.X9kctv9AMUZlOjIQ]{upcoming encounter} with the sticky toffee hound.

Sticky-Sweet and Strange.name: Sticky-Sweet and Strange
Sticky-Sweet and Strange.text:
Scene

@UUID[Scene.qHhbUrZGBnIPWy4Z]{Hunting Trails}

You can find our provided map for hunting trails in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

As their final clue in the area, the party discovers a smaller path branching off of the hunting trails where the ground and low-hanging shrubs are stained with traces of a sweet-smelling, viscous, red-brown liquid so dark its larger collections look black. A character trained in Cooking Lore or who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:12] check recognizes the liquid as black treacle, a dark sugar syrup similar to molasses. Any one PC can lead the rest of the party in following the short trail with either a @Check[cooking-lore|dc:15] check, a @Check[survival|dc:15] check, or a @Check[stealth|dc:18] check, applying any food-related bonuses granted by the hounds’ Sticky Paws ability. a success on either makes the creature below off-guard for the first round of the combat to follow.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.MsELMjof55g0TOoB]

Creature: At the end of the trail, the PCs find the creature that created it, a sweet-smelling ooze creature with a texture somewhere between gelatin and a very moist cake, which has been molded into the rough shape of a small hunting dog. Larmine created these sticky toffee fey hounds to be her companions and guardians, but this one got separated from the pack trailing her bugbear hench-goons and was unable to find its way back to the village, let alone the bakery.

Recognizing the PCs only as creatures that are not its master, the sticky toffee hound attacks them on sight and fights until destroyed.

Reward

In addition to the XP for defeating the sticky toffee hound, the PCs earn 40 XP for speaking to Orivana, 40 XP for speaking to Elida, and 60 XP for completing their investigations both in town and on the hunting trails.

Overview (UT79).name: Overview
Overview (UT79).text:
Scene

@UUID[Scene.m0166cBxEwCHOtUN]{The Gristmill}

You can find our provided map for the gristmill in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

The gristmill built by Arvent Daswooren’s father and now run by him and his wife is located about three hours out of town along a winding dirt road, on the far bank of the Path River. It’s currently occupied by a gang of bugbears who work for Larmine in exchange for getting to keep the worldly goods of the victims they snatch for her.

The scheme works like this: Back in Grayce, Larmine selects her targets from among the travelers passing through the village by riverboat, targeting small craft traveling downriver with no more than three people aboard. She presents her chosen targets with the “parting gift” of an incredibly fragrant lavender and rosemary sweet roll. Her bugbear minions can pick up the distinct scent of this treat—even on the breath of someone who ate it hours earlier—from half a mile away. When they do, they quickly inform their leader, Aezar (greedy female ogre glutton 5), who attacks the unfortunate boat with a grapple as it passes by the mill’s deck, dragging it to shore while the bugbears wade into the water to capture their intended victims.

So far, the bugbears have captured three boats for the sweet hag this way, with all but one of the passengers having already met their unfortunate ends. The most recent captive, Taynor, has been kept alive because Larmine deemed them “too scrawny” to make a proper meal and tasked the bugbears with “fattening them up.” They’re imprisoned in the gristmill’s basement alongside the mill’s owners—who survive because the bugbears otherwise wouldn’t know how to run or fix the mill—and Dalmira, who Larmine intends to coerce future letters out of until she can convincingly take permanent ownership of the bakery.

The gristmill is a single-story wooden building with an elevated stone foundation built securely into the high banks of the Path River. Its single story stands 20 feet tall, with a few small, square windows in each wall. All of its doors are made of wood and are unlocked unless otherwise indicated.

Out Front.name: Out Front
Out Front.text:
From the outside, there seems to be nothing amiss about the humble gristmill waiting at the river’s edge. The large wooden wheel still turns with the flow of the water, and smoke rises from the stone chimney, smelling faintly of burnt meat. A wooden deck runs along the river next to the mill, with a small walkway jutting out from it over the flume of the waterwheel to ease the effort of repairs or the danger of unsticking debris lodged in the slats.

The PCs approach this area from the north, arriving either along an old road that passes by through the woods or a path along the river. So long as they don’t linger in the open too long, getting up to the building without being seen by the guards (Creatures, below) is a relatively simple matter; they have time to plan their strategy before they approach. There are no visible entrances on the north side of the building. The loud creaking and splashing of the waterwheel are clearly audible even from across the river; a PC who succeeds at a @Check[survival|dc:12] check observes from a distance that the noise is more than loud enough to cover the sounds of an approach (or even combat, if the combatants avoid battle cries and stifle any calls of alarm).

The double doors leading into area @UUID[.uPuCD3pjMsDWfrhD]{A5} are used for moving goods from wagons into and out the mill; they stand 5 feet above ground level (ideal for shoveling grain from the wagon bed to the room’s floor) and are currently barred from the inside. While these doors can be forced open (Hardness 10, 40 HP, BT 20), a PC can determine by softly testing the doors that doing so would be prohibitively loud. The door leading to area @UUID[.hOamDxpAMcCjfw63]{A2} stands at the top of a short flight of wooden stairs and is unlocked.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.9cBuzDV8seJqhNKJ]{Bugbear Prowler x2}

Creatures: Two bugbear prowlers stand guard outside the gristmill as the PCs approach. One paces the ground with an irritable scowl, her restless steps pausing just short of the deck, while the other sits on the stairs leading to the mill’s entrance door, picking his teeth. Both have strict orders to apprehend anyone who spots them or gets too close to the mill, but they haven’t actually seen anyone during their several days’ worth of watch shifts. As a result, they’re bored, easily distracted by suspicious sounds, and itching for a fight. The PCs can take advantage of this by luring one or both guards to area A1a with a @Check[deception|dc:15] check. If the two are separated this way, the noise of the waterwheel covers up the sounds of combat enough that the other bugbear struggles to hear the fighting. At the end of each combat round, the bugbear can attempt a @Check[perception|dc:25|traits:secret] check to hear combat and join the following round. After each round, the DC decreases by 2, and the bugbear becomes curious enough to investigate after 4 rounds, even if they didn’t hear anything suspicious.

At the start of their second turn in combat, a bugbear prowler uses a free action to roar a warning of the attack to their companions in area @UUID[JournalEntry.wzqJL0YgefgczTx0.JournalEntryPage.uPuCD3pjMsDWfrhD]{A5}. If they’ve been lured into area A1a, however, the noise of the waterwheel covers up that sound and prevents it from alerting the rest of the gang to the PCs’ incursion.

Entry Hall.name: Entry Hall
Entry Hall.text:
The front hall is made of the same plain local wood as the building’s exterior. Its only decor are several spiderwebs nestled far outside a dwarven housekeeper’s reach as well as a moth-eaten old runner carpet that looks like it gets cleaned maybe once a decade. Plain wooden doors lead to the north, south, and west, and a number of wooden barrels occupy the eastern wall.

A Friend in Beads: When they first enter the hall, any PCs who succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:16] check notice a sprinkling of two or three small, colorful beads scattered across the wooden floor. The beads are much like those the party might have found along the @UUID[JournalEntry.wzqJL0YgefgczTx0.JournalEntryPage.GiBbTQeAxCiJYOrW]{hunting trails} and lead to a pair of wooden barrels set against the wall; PCs who succeed at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check hear a faint rattling noise from inside one of these barrels as they approach.

When they look into the barrel marked Z on the map, read or paraphrase the following.

At the bottom of the barrel lies the withered remains of a few sad, dry pickles and the even sadder form of a huddled goblin, her knees pulled tight to her chest with trembling arms. The colorful, mismatched beads clumsily sewn onto her tattered clothing rattle together as she looks up with a gasp and bursts into tears.

“I’m sorry! I’m sorry! I didn’t mean to burn the grub again! Please, please don’t pull my ears no more!”

Zini (browbeaten female goblin scavenger 1) lived with a small migrant tribe of her fellow goblins until about a month ago, when she had the bad luck to be snatched up by the bugbear gang while foraging in the local woods. The bugbears forced Zini to “join” their gang because they enjoy keeping someone around to bully into doing the chores at the mill. They get even more enjoyment out of picking on the poor goblin when Zini inevitably fumbles the chores struggling with tools built for “longshanks.”

The PCs can calm Zini down by speaking to her in soothing tones, or simply by not taking hostile actions towards her for five minutes until she realizes they’re not going to hurt her. Zini’s attitude towards the PCs starts off as unfriendly—out of fear more than genuine dislike—but she can be quickly brought around with successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:17|options:action:make-an-impression|name:PF2E.Actions.MakeAnImpression.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,exploration,linguistic,mental] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression}, by presenting her with some of the lost beads (her favorite things), or by promising to help her escape her bugbear captors. The latter two actions each raise Zini’s attitude by one step.

If Zini is made at least friendly, she can be convinced to tell the PCs about her history with the bugbears as detailed above, as well as explain why she was in the barrel—she was hiding from the gang’s lieutenant, Grizzle (area @UUID[.uPuCD3pjMsDWfrhD]{A5}), after burning the food she’d been ordered to cook in the kitchen (area @UUID[.lUZ3NqXMPsozRzoi]{A3}).

If made helpful, Zini eagerly answers all questions the PCs might have about the bugbears and their role in Larmine’s scheme. Zini knows everything laid out in the gristmill introduction section, except that she doesn’t know “the boss lady’s” name, where in town she’s hiding, or who she’s disguised as. She can tell the PCs that there are (or were) four bugbears total in the gang—including Grizzle, who’s “meaner and sneakier than the other three”—plus their ogre leader Aezar, who Zini describes with a shudder. “I stays away from her. She wants to grind up my bones to make bread. She says so.”

Whether she’s asked or not, a helpful Zini also makes sure to tell the PCs about the prisoners the gang keeps in the basement and the magical trap placed on its trap door (see area @UUID[.lUZ3NqXMPsozRzoi]{A3}), though she doesn’t know the prisoners’ names nor precisely how said trap works. She warns the PCs that they’ll need three “gummy-gums” (colorful, fist-sized gumdrops) to unlock the spell, or it’ll “turn them into gingery-bread.” She doesn’t know where the “gummy-gums” are kept, except that the bugbears probably have them, but she can show the PCs the hazard they unlock in area @UUID[.lUZ3NqXMPsozRzoi]{A3} if her explanation proves too limited on its own.

Zini plans to hide in her barrel until the PCs finish their business at the mill. That said, Zini does accompany the PCs on their explorations if asked, but she avoids combat and hides from enemies except in especially dire circumstances. She makes an exception for Grizzle or Aezar, as she’s been mulling over clever insults she wants to use against them but has never dared voice before now. Against these foes, she uses her Pent-Up Taunt and might launch a sling bullet or two before seeking cover.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.vkcVkap2wr529Q2w]

The barrels Zini isn’t hiding in used to contain food, but have been emptied by the bugbears in the months they’ve occupied that mill. All that remains is a single feather step stone that Grizzle didn’t realize was magical when it slipped out of his pocket.

Reward

The PCs earn 60 XP for befriending Zini.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
The kitchen of the gristmill’s meager living quarters is humble, but cozy. To the south, a table and some chairs have been shoved out of a small dining nook and a rug has been tossed aside to reveal a trap door with a heavy iron ring on its face. In the northeast corner stands an iron stove, its oven door hanging partially ajar and its stovepipe connected to the stone fireplace beside it. Over a low fire in the hearth, the blackened contents of a large cast-iron pot send a steady trail of smoke up the chimney. A straw-stuffed ice box sits along the east wall.

The pot contains the charred remains of Zini’s rat and venison stew. It’s unsalvageable.

The stove and its oven are cold, but if the PCs think to check inside, they find the latter to still be filled with ashes. By carefully sifting through these ashes, a PC can uncover a number of small, delicate bone fragments. With a successful @Check[medicine|dc:16] or @Check[survival|dc:16] check, a PC identifies the fragments as belonging to a gnome; these are all that remain of one of Larmine’s earliest victims.

The door to area @UUID[.bUbp2ZsSSuQW9mh5]{A4} is locked, both with a simple lock built into the door (three successful @Check[thievery|dc:20|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks to pick) and a larger average padlock the bugbears latched onto a recently-installed hasp (four successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks to pick). Aezar keeps the keys to both locks on her in area @UUID[.nqnTCkhJfsMtiOWR]{A6}.

The trap door (marked T on the map) leads to the basement, where the bugbear gang have imprisoned the Daswoorens, Dalmira, and Taynor on Larmine’s orders. Before the PCs can free them, however, they’ll have to deal with the nasty spell Larmine’s placed to thwart meddling outsiders.

Encounter

Low 3

@UUID[Actor.GSuvWPIpA8DbJV3S]

Hazard: The trap door and the floor around it are adorned with a pair of interlocking magic circles drawn with what appears to be royal icing, though it resists being smudged, eaten, washed away, or otherwise disturbed in any fashion. The three “keys” to deactivate its hazard take the form of equally durable gumdrops the size of a human fist; Larmine figured that if the bugbears or Aezar were stubborn or foolish enough to try to swallow one anyway, they deserved to choke on it. One of each of these gumdrops can be found on Grizzle in area @UUID[.uPuCD3pjMsDWfrhD]{A5}, on Aezar in area @UUID[.nqnTCkhJfsMtiOWR]{A6}, and in Aezar’s gluttonous hoard in area @UUID[.bUbp2ZsSSuQW9mh5]{A4}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.8qae17Web4UI0xfZ]

Among the bone fragments in the oven’s ashes, the PCs can find a ventriloquist’s ring.

The icebox is almost entirely empty save for a single glass bottle containing a fizzy, unnaturally blue-tinted potion. The bottle has a tag tied to its neck which reads, “In case of” with a drawing of a gingerbread man on the front and “drink me” on the back. This sickeningly sweet potion undoes the transformation effects of the Bittersweet Surprise; Larmine left a single dose with the bugbear gang after one of them accidentally set the trap off while drunk.

Development

When the PCs disable the Bittersweet Surprise, they’re able to enter the basement below the gristmill and rescue the people imprisoned there. Proceed to @UUID[.2REZqxhdIEiheE8x]{Answers in the Basement}.

Reward

The PCs earn 60 XP when they disable the Bittersweet Surprise and enter the basement.

What if they Eat the Gingerbread?

Players will sometimes choose to have their characters do obviously unwise things just to see what will happen. If a player expresses interest in tasting part of a PC’s body that has been transformed into gingerbread by the Bittersweet Surprise, gently remind them that, while the transformation can be undone with either the potion in the icebox or the 2nd-rank spell @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}, the healing magic required to regrow body parts, such as the 7th-rank spell @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.2Vkd1IxylPceUAAF]{Regenerate}, is far outside the level range covered by the adventures in this book and unlikely to be available, let alone affordable, for a long time to come. If they persist anyway, it will be a valuable learning experience.

Eaten portions of a creature’s body cannot be restored by the methods that would otherwise undo the transformation and result in the associated negative penalties persisting indefinitely, though at your discretion they might be reduced or negated with an appropriate assistive item.

Miller's Bedroom.name: Miller's Bedroom
Miller's Bedroom.text:
This once-cozy bedroom for two has been ransacked, its sturdy dwarven-made bed cracked down the middle and homemade quilts shredded by bugbear teeth and claws. Broken travelers’ trunks and emptied rucksacks fill the corners, their contents piled in a heap below a large crack in the wall across from the door.

The bugbears broke the bed here shortly after they took control of the mill, mostly out of spite.

Aezar put a fist through the wall between this room and the main mill chamber so she could pile the most valuable loot from the gang’s victims into a gluttonous hoard only she could reach. A Small or smaller creature could @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeeze} through this gap to get to area @UUID[.nqnTCkhJfsMtiOWR]{A6}, but it’s too small for anything larger to pass through.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.x9D0Bd36AcNsuhkK]

The most important thing the PCs find among the pile of stolen goods is a rich purple gumdrop the size of a human fist—one of the three keys required to disable the hazard in area A3. The room also contains a soft purple dancing scarf decorated with silver bells, a mage’s hat in the form of a fashionable leather tri-corner, two potency crystal talismans, a crying angel pendant talisman, a lesser potion of retaliation (fire), and a beacon shot arrow, along with 472 gp distributed among multiple coin purses.

Beyond that, the hoard is a jumble of random (mostly spoiled) sweets that Larmine has given Aezar, as well as a collection of bones sourced from a wide variety of birds, mammals, and humanoids.

Supply Storage.name: Supply Storage
Supply Storage.text:
Several large wooden crates line the walls of this chamber, some standing open and others stacked two or three high. A set of wide doors used for unloading grain into carts fill the south wall.

Passing glimpses into the crates that stand open reveal them to contain empty sacks waiting to be filled with flour or meal, replacement parts for the water wheel, and other supplies necessary to keep the mill in working order.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.ZE9FyzukpIR0wi5H] @UUID[Actor.9LRcg8nt5eoVMYjm]

Creatures: Grizzle (mean male bugbear tormentor 3), the gang’s second-in-command, has been relaxing in here with the most vicious of the bugbear prowlers, though what they’re up to depends on how the PCs chose to handle the guards in area @UUID[.1CBdS3czEKgPtA7M]{A1}. If the party was able to sneak up on the guards or use the noise of the waterwheel to their advantage to cover up the sounds of their attack, the bugbears are lounging around on the floor getting drunk and are completely unprepared for a fight; they start the combat @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} and must draw their weapons before they can attack.

If, however, the guards were able to alert the mill to the coming attack as detailed in area @UUID[.1CBdS3czEKgPtA7M]{A1}, then Grizzle and his companion have already concealed themselves among the crates and lie in wait to ambush the PCs. In this case, they roll Stealth for their Initiative and begin the combat @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.IJBhCReCEeRwfaQa]

Tucked among and behind the crates are piles of torn cloth, tangled ropes, and broken planks with nails still embedded inside; the shattered remains of the three boats the gang had previously attacked as part of Larmine’s scheme, destroyed and stashed here by Aezar to cover up their foul deeds. Among these remains, the PCs can find some of the cargo the bugbears were allowed to claim for themselves.

Grizzle carries 43 gp, along with a small velvet sack containing a bright red gumdrop the size of a human fist. This gumdrop is one of the keys to the hazard blocking the trap door in area @UUID[.lUZ3NqXMPsozRzoi]{A3}.

Mill Room.name: Mill Room
Mill Room.text:
The bugbears’ ogre leader, Aezar, claimed this room as her personal domain in part because it’s the largest chamber in the mill and in part because she’s fascinated by the millstones used for grinding. She spends whatever time she’s not sleeping or eating in here feeding things like tree branches and planks torn out of the floor between the stones to watch them get ground up. This regular abuse is a major strain on the wheel’s machinery and the source of the noise that alerted Sergei to the mill’s occupation.

Aezar’s favorite thing to grind is bones. The bones come from a variety of places—the fish and game the gang hunt for their daily meals and some unfortunate birds Aezar snatches on her rare ventures outside, mostly, though she has gotten the occasional scrap from Larmine off their shared victims.

Aezar put her fist through the wooden wall between this room and the bedroom so she could reach the gluttonous hoard she was building up in area @UUID[.bUbp2ZsSSuQW9mh5]{A4} without having to leave the comfort of her chosen lair. The rules for passing through described in that area also apply from this direction.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.TwrwjR9OPZTDyVZB]

Creature: The PCs find Aezar squatting near the grindstones, watching them crush a stick into sawdust. She gets excited upon spotting the PCs, as she won’t have to share the spoils with Larmine this time and will finally get a chance to try something she’s been wanting to experiment with: making bread out of “bone flour.”

Treasure

Aezar carries a few things in mismatched pouches tied to a makeshift rope belt around her waist. One such pouch contains 72 gp. Another holds only a forest green gumdrop the size of human fist—one of the three keys to the hazard in area @UUID[.lUZ3NqXMPsozRzoi]{A3}.

One small, tattered pouch also dangles from a worn leather cord around her neck. Inside, the PCs find a large, morbidly-designed piece of peppermint hard candy the size and shape of (as well as bearing markings resembling) a human eyeball. This is actually a sweet hag’s eye belonging to Larmine. A PC who examines the eye using @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.gpzpAAAJ1Lza2JVl]{Detect Magic} realizes that its magical effect is currently active; the hag is watching them right now. Immediately after this revelation, or within minutes of the PCs removing the eye from its sack (whichever comes first), Larmine triggers the Meltaway Mint activation. Back in town, she begins locking down the bakery for a fight, knowing that her scheme has been revealed.

Answers in the Basement.name: Answers in the Basement
Answers in the Basement.text:
Once the PCs defeat Grizzle and Aezar, they should be able to locate the three gumdrop keys they need to disable the hazard in area @UUID[.lUZ3NqXMPsozRzoi]{A3} and enter the basement. This area has no map as no combat is expected here. Read or paraphrase the following.

Light spills down a short flight of wooden stairs into a dark basement lit only by the sputtering stubs of a few candles and two tiny, high-set windows. Heavy creaking and grinding noises echo off the damp stone walls; at the far side, the gears and shaft of the waterwheel partially extend into this lower level. It smells of the river, fresh water soaking the stone of the walls and the unfinished, packed earth of the floor, though the heavy aromas of mud and moisture don’t quite cover up those of filth, waste, and oddly sweet sickness from the four humanoid forms huddled among the shadows.

This basement is mostly intended to provide extra storage and a space to access the waterwheel’s gearworks for repairs, but the bugbear gang has also been using it as a holding cell to contain the four prisoners Larmine ordered them to keep an eye on: the missing miller couple, Arvent and Monnery Daswooren (industrious male and female dwarf millers 3); the rightful owner of Dalmira’s Bakery, Dalmira Eranhal (hardworking female human baker 2); and the most recent victim of Larmine’s scheme with the bugbears, Taynor Belziz (frightened agender aiuvarin human merchant 3).

The three locals are physically unharmed, but are dirty and fatigued from the months they’ve been locked away down here, especially as they haven’t been given proper food; Larmine’s been giving them nothing but sweets from her stolen bakery. Taynor is a bit healthier, seeing as they’ve only been down here a week, but they’re nursing a half-healed head wound from their capture and several body bruises they’ve received since their arrival, thanks to the bugbears’ efforts to force-feed them on Larmine’s orders.

All four are grateful for their rescue and do their best to answer the PCs’ questions.

Dalmira? What are you doing here?

“I’ve been here since the start, same as the Daswoorens. There’s a sweet hag running my bakery! That’s how she’s finding her targets, and slipping them the bun the bugbears use as a signal. She threatened to eat me next unless I kept writing the letters telling everyone I was okay.”

Wait—You mean Larmine isn’t your cousin?

“I don’t even have a cousin! She’s a people-eating monster. She locked Arvent and Monnery up in their own home, then jumped me while I was going in before dawn to open up the bakery. She brought the bugbears in to guard us and took over my shop so she could use it to find people the town wouldn’t miss.”

Arvent, you sent your sister a ring?

Monnery sighs in relief. “He made it! Thank goodness. I was afraid he’d get eaten by something.”

Arvent, in turn, scoffs, though his tone holds more regret than vitriol. “I told Vana I didn’t sell it. We found it down here, on the floor. Must’ve fallen out of its case while we were moving Dad’s old stuff.”

“The bugbears didn’t know I had Carrot with me.” Monnery explains. “We sent him out one of the windows. We wanted to send a message too, but there’s nothing to write with down here, and if we waited until we got some, we were worried they’d decide to eat one of us. It was a long shot, but we had to try.”

Are you all okay? Do you need help getting back to town?

Taynor groans, holding their stomach. “I never want to see another sweet bun as long as I live. But I’m not going to be eaten by a hag so, it’s a better ending than I thought I was getting.”

Dalmira rubs their back soothingly and assures the PCs, “We’ll see them back to town safely. Just please—you have to get that hag out of my shop, before she hurts anyone else.”

Zini also chooses to travel back to town with the rescued prisoners, rather than accompany the PCs into the danger that awaits them at @UUID[.6sLA7HYgKbxiT7sf]{Dalmira’s Bakery}.

Reward

Award the PCs 60 XP for rescuing the kidnapped townsfolk.

Overview (T7sf).name: Overview
Overview (T7sf).text:
Scene

@UUID[Scene.zldGHQyZFXcUosBU]{Dalmira’s Bakery}

You can find our provided map for Dalmira's bakery in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

By the time the PCs get back to town, the market day is over. With the exception of taverns, most of the shops and stands have closed, including the bakery. Thanks to her sweet hag’s eye, Larmine knows the party is coming. She’s locked down the bakery and secured herself with magical defenses, hoping to take out and consume the meddling heroes as revenge for ruining her schemes before she flees.

Outside.name: Outside
Outside.text:
Dalmira’s Bakery stands quiet under the faint glow of an evening sky, its tables empty and its wide windows dark. A painted “Closed” sign decorated with carved bread loaves hangs on a hook between the double front doors.

The front doors have been locked with a simple lock, which requires two successful @Check[thievery|dc:20|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks to pick, and have also been barred from the inside. The check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} the doors is a @Check[athletics|dc:23|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check if the lock hasn’t been picked, and a @Check[athletics|dc:18|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check if it has.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.3isJhl2RNoYeYSSV]{Animated Silverware Swarm x2} @UUID[Actor.ybkelAOtSIA06fnj]{Animated Broom x2}

Creatures: As the PCs cross to reach the bakery doors, the silverware adorning the tables suddenly rises up in two animated swarms, accompanied by a pair of brooms that were leaning against the bakery wall as though waiting to be used. These enchanted animated objects are Larmine’s first line of defense now that she knows her secret is out; they’re all completely mindless and cannot be reasoned with. They fight until destroyed.

Shopfront.name: Shopfront
Shopfront.text:
The main interior of the bakery is roughly divided by a wooden counter running down the center. When the bakery is open, customers are generally restricted to the front of the shop, where shelves and tables present a display of the goods for sale, while the space behind the counter is for employees only. It is currently lit by dim light through the wide windows at the front of the store. The PCs don’t initially have a chance to look around, however, as they’re set upon as soon as they enter the building by Larmine’s “guard dogs,” a trio of her sticky toffee hounds.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.4kc6sYSc56Q2KYTT.PlaylistSound.2zzCvivgs13V0A9c]{Bakery}

As the party enters the Dalmira's Bakery, you can play this ambience sound.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.MsELMjof55g0TOoB]{Sticky Toffee Hounds x3}

Creatures: Unlike the lone instance the PCs fought before, these three hounds fight in a pack, attempting to drive the PCs back out the door of the shop or, barring that, at least keep them from going behind the counter, as that’s the only way to access the door to the kitchen where Larmine is making her final stand. The sticky toffee hounds are completely loyal to their sweet hag creator and fight until destroyed.

Development

Once the sticky toffee guard dogs have been dealt with, the PCs have a chance to catch their breath and search area B2 if they like, or they can head straight for the door to the kitchen (@UUID[.31C7UWPV0e7fbDhV]{B3}) and their final confrontation with Larmine. Either path takes them past the hazard in area @UUID[.2WaGn72XcX2nnbUF]{B2c}, but the boons to be uncovered in @UUID[.2qb1ny92ZGxfaBh2]{B2a} and @UUID[.AZoKtgxgA7n9GZOR]{B2b} are up to them to discover.

Window Display.name: Window Display
Window Display.text:
An array of fresh breads and pastries are laid out over a gingham tablecloth, arranged to form a fetching display in the wide bakery window.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.KRLjSAprH0orGxCW]

In her hurry to secure the bakery for the PCs’ arrival, Larmine accidentally mixed some alchemically-infused pastries in with the goods on display. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[alchemy-lore|dc:14] or @Check[cooking-lore|dc:14] check, or a @Check[crafting|dc:18] check, can identify the following from the irregularities in their scent and coloration—two chocolate croissants infused with moderate bestial mutagens, a bearclaw that acts as a moderate juggernaut mutagen, and a pinwheel whose sun-dried tomatoes have been replaced with poisonous belladonna.

Oven.name: Oven
Oven.text:
Unlike most of the building, the wall here is constructed of masonry with a solid stone foundation, offering added support to both the wood of the surrounding structure and the large cast-iron oven that’s been set inside. A stack of firewood and an iron poker rest on the floor beside it, and a pair of quilted mitts hang from a peg on the nearby wall.

The oven is cold and empty when the PCs initially find it. Since they’re not in combat, they can take their time to open its heavy iron door without needing to make a skill check. The PCs don’t need to be professional bakers to tell that this industrial-sized oven is more than large enough for a Medium-sized creature to crawl—or be forced—inside, and that there is a second door on the opposite side, opening into the kitchen on the other side of the wall. This second door is latched and cannot be opened from this side, so the PCs can’t use this route to reach area @UUID[.31C7UWPV0e7fbDhV]{B3}; they can, however, fill the bottom of the oven with some of the firewood and light it using either the provided flint, a matchstick, or any basic fire-producing cantrip. Doing so will provide them optional strategy to make use of in their fight against Larmine; see @UUID[.31C7UWPV0e7fbDhV]{Potential Advantage}.

If the PCs take the time to light the oven, be sure to inform them as they’re closing the door that it’s already growing warm to the touch, as a hint that they should consider grabbing the nearby oven mitt. This will allow them to make full use of the oven’s advantage, should they choose to take it.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.ViriVeeOgSNIxMSW]{Light Oven}

If the characters light the oven, click on the macro above to activate the oven's tiles and ambient sound. You can use the macro again to turn off the oven.

Enticing Display.name: Enticing Display
Enticing Display.text:
A variety of iced cakes, chocolate-dipped cookies, and delectable pastries remain on display within this wood-and-glass display case. The divine scent of spun sugar and fresh fruit wafts from its open back side.

Encounter

Moderate 3

@UUID[Actor.XLNW0J4gjcrk8oJL]

Hazard: The treats in the display are, in fact, Larmine’s last line of defense against her expected intruders. Because it’s out in the open rather than being hidden, it uses Deception for both concealment and Initiative rather than Stealth.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.V17qw1xEEWPNcj2T]{Break Display Case}

If the characters defeat the Enchanted Sweets hazard by destroying the case, click on the macro above to shatter it.

Kitchen (bDhV).name: Kitchen
Kitchen (bDhV).text:
In the bakery’s kitchen, the PCs at last come face-to-face with the culprit behind the disappearances, who has dropped her human disguise to reveal her true sticky sweet form.

Two more gooey toffee hounds stand, growling, between the open kitchen door and their master, now in her true form. Gone is the kind face and warm smile of the kindly baker. In their place, Larmine resembles a drippy mass of sticky chocolate taffy, stretched into the rough shape of a human woman, her hair in whipping cords of licorice and her peppermint eyes narrowed in fury.

“You meddling brats!” she shrieks, in a voice that would be syrupy if it wasn’t screeching. “You’ve ruined everything! I had a good thing going here, even if I had to put up with those wretched bugbears. I’ll render your fat down to shortening for this!”

Encounter

Severe 3

@UUID[Actor.6ZDTclOqh9zXftLU]{Larmine} @UUID[Actor.MsELMjof55g0TOoB]{Toffee Hound x2} @UUID[Actor.TKrZNNfYOnpxQzfK]{Spitting Hot Candy Pot} @UUID[Actor.sTLLeVohXDezulem]{Hot Oven}

Creatures: Larmine begins the fight in the south-west corner, positioning her sticky toffee hounds between herself and the PCs. She uses @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.tlSE7Ly8vi1Dgddv]{Laughing Fit}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.PjhUmyKnq6K5uDby]{Shrink}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4gBIw4IDrSfFHik4]{Daze} from a distance in an attempt to make the party more vulnerable for her hounds, and lashes out at any who get close with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.DYdvMZ8G2LiSLVWw]{Spider Sting} and her candy cane claws. She keeps her distance from the stove to avoid getting caught in the aftermath should her candy pot be broken by the PCs.

Hazard: At the start of combat, Larmine snaps her fingers, stoking the stove’s flames and setting off the Spitting Hot Candy Pot hazard to make the PCs’ job even harder.

Potential Advantage: If the PCs lit the oven in area @UUID[JournalEntry.wzqJL0YgefgczTx0.JournalEntryPage.AZoKtgxgA7n9GZOR]{B2b}, the Hot Oven simple hazard is available during their combat with Larmine. At the beginning of combat, the heavy iron door is closed and Larmine is positioned between it and the party. Clever PCs can take advantage of this hazard by reaching the door, opening it with an Interact action and a @Check[athletics|dc:18] check, and then maneuvering Larmine or her hounds inside using the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shove} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.lOE4yjUnETTdaf2T]{Reposition} actions. Once the door is opened, however, Larmine becomes aware of the hazard’s existence and might choose to use it against the PCs if they don’t get her first.

Concluding the Adventure.name: Concluding the Adventure
Concluding the Adventure.text:
With Larmine and the last of her hounds defeated, the PCs can report the results of their investigation to Jindel. They find her in the sheriff’s office with Zini and the kidnapping victims, who did indeed make it back to town safely and immediately sought out the sheriff to let her know what was going on.

Dalmira is relieved to be back home, even if her bakery does need to close for a few weeks to scrub toffee out of the floorboards (and potentially deep-clean the oven). She’s a little miffed when she hears people preferred the sweet hag’s goods to her own and decides to take the opportunity to rework her recipes a bit. In the meantime, she hires Zini on as an assistant, giving the goblin a room to live in above the shop until someone can get ahold of her tribe.

Arvent and Monnery seek out Orivana (and Carrot), spending a few weeks in the latter’s guest room while they recover from their ordeal. Things remain a bit awkward between the siblings, but when they reunite for the first time in fifteen years, Orivana pulls her brother into a stiff hug and mutters that she’s glad he didn’t get himself eaten.

When Elida hears that Taynor’s been found, she immediately drags them out for the drinks they owe her and gives them a friendly hard time about their newfound disgust for sweets. It doesn’t really hide how grateful she is that her friend, at least, did not end up as the sweet hag’s final victim.

Baking in Grayce: Even with Zini’s assistance, there’s a lot to clean up in the bakery—to say nothing of all the food preparation needed to feed Grayce! Dalmira extends an open invitation to any PCs with shopkeeping or cooking experience, offering to hire them on as seasonal help at a generous wage. This provides all of the PCs indefinite access to 3rd- and 4th-level @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.QyzlsLrqM0EEwd7j]{Earn Income} tasks using skills like Cooking Lore, Crafting, Labor Lore, and potentially other Lore skills at the GM’s discretion. The bakery’s well-kept tools grant such PCs a +1 circumstance bonus to their checks to Earn Income.

Finally, if any PCs show potential as bakers, Dalmira shares several of her own recipes, such as the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.cngyxKY271mvKySQ]{Cinnamon Nostalgia Bun}. She also develops a new recipe to commemorate the PCs’ victory: the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.ZY0XGD1LFFSh3VNO]{Hagbane Biscuit}. She bakes an extra hagbane biscuit for the PCs that she wraps carefully to preserve it for whatever adventures the PCs face ahead.

Treasure

As thanks, Jindel awards the PCs 250 gp.

The Count of Petals.name: The Count of Petals
The Count of Petals.text:
Vampire activity is rampant in the Ustalavic county of Caliphas, but the people of Grayce take pride in the fact that they haven’t had a vampire in their town for generations. They practice their disdain for vampires by hanging garlic over doorways, displaying religious symbols prominently, and tacking small oval mirrors to posts throughout town. Thus, when vampire hunter Garren Shirvolt arrived in Grayce claiming to be on the trail of a vampire called the Count of Petals, the locals were skeptical, but hoped that Garren would at least make a few purchases before giving up and deciding to move on.

Despite Grayce’s skepticism, the Count of Petals is real and not far away. Seven years ago, Petr von Arkenbrand, the heir of an Ustalavic noble family known for both their rose gardens and the red rose petals adorning their family crest, became a vampire. His transformation was a result of a tragic encounter with an ancient bloodsucker who turned him against his will. As a newly created vampire, Petr struggled at first with the loss of his humanity, doing his best to deny his new, unsettling appetites. This “weakness” led Petr’s vampiric peers to mockingly dub him the Count of Petals—a name that eventually became his undead alter ego, once he finally gave in to his monstrous urges, becoming a deadly hunter of the living.

Ironically, Petr’s actions as the Count of Petals drew the ire of the vampires who once mocked him. After killing a mortal under the protection of a powerful vampire family, Petr was captured, stuffed into a casket, and driven south through the countryside, across Grayce’s Chapel Bridge and into the Gravelands. There, he was left in a crumbling, abandoned castle, essentially banished from Ustalav. Ever since, Petr has has ruled over his ruined domain, seething over what he regards to be a great injustice—and plotting his revenge.

Garren Shirvolt, the vampire hunter who recently passed through Grayce, has a personal grudge against the Count of Petals. The murder that lead to the Count’s exile took the life of Garren’s lifelong partner, a human woman named Lorain. Driven by vengeance, Garren searched for years for the vampire who had stolen his love from him, but the Count’s exile to a remote castle made it nearly impossible for Garren to track him down. Only recently did Garren uncover a clue leading him to Grayce. He rode into town three days ago, stayed overnight, and then headed south across the Chapel Bridge into the Gravelands, determined to find and destroy the vampire who took his partner’s life.

A Dire Warning.name: A Dire Warning
A Dire Warning.text:
The adventure begins a day or two after the PCs finish their previous adventure. While they are out and about in town, a commotion in the town square catches their attention. Read or paraphrase the following to get the adventure started.

A terrified scream pierces the relative quiet of people going about their business. “A harpy!” one of the townspeople yells. “It flew from across the river!” And sure enough, a winged creature resembling a cross between a bird and a human sweeps across the town square. The ragged creature hovers above the terrified crowd with a look of disgust on her face before releasing a wet, leather sack from her grip. The parcel plummets to the ground with the sound of a ripe fruit being stepped on, causing the startled crowd to jump back.

“Grayce! You’re dead—all of you!” the creature proclaims before turning in the air with a single, powerful beat of her wings.

The townspeople stare in horror as the sack falls open and a man’s head—his mouth still open in a silent scream—rolls out. With an audible gasp, the crowd retreats a few steps. After a few moments of awkward silence, a priest breaks from the crowd and speaks.

“I’ve seen this man before. He’s the vampire hunter who rode through town a few days ago!”

The priest’s name is Sancovel Durantine (pragmatic female aiuvarin priest of Pharasma 8). If the PCs hesitate to step up and deal with the new threat, Sancovel approaches them, knowing that they’ve successfully handled other recent problems. Sancovel explains that the vampire hunter’s name was Garren Shirvolt and that he passed through Grayce three days ago. She’s worried that Grayce has been marked for vengeance, as the vampires Garren went after obviously think he was sent from town. For this reason, she asks that the PCs finish what Garren started.

Sancovel doesn’t know exactly where Garren was headed, other than that he went into the Gravelands looking for a vampire he called the Count of Petals. She suggests the PCs ask around for information about where Garren might have went after leaving Grayce.

On the Clock

The harpy’s threat gives the party’s mission a sense of urgency. If the PCs are slow to react, the count’s flying allies—the harpy, the gargoyles, and the giant bats—escalate their attacks on the town. They might start by killing livestock and spreading fear among the townsfolk. As the situation worsens, the minions could kidnap one of the town’s council members to use as leverage. The count might also summon other vicious creatures from the Gravelands to join his cause, sending them to menace Grayce until the PCs take action.

Asking Around.name: Asking Around
Asking Around.text:
To find out where Garren Shirvolt headed after leaving Grayce, the PCs need only ask around town for a few hours. Unless you wish to complicate matters with red herrings and the like, the investigation doesn’t require any skill checks, only time. Sancovel confirms that she saw Garren crossing the Chapel Bridge and continuing southwest into the Gravelands three days ago. Before he left town, Garren did a bit of shopping at Grayce General Goods, suggesting that the store is a good place to start the search.

Grayce General Goods: Shortly after his arrival in Grayce, Garren spoke with @UUID[Actor.ESURU33xyLebJb9I]{Denval Troben} (warm male dwarf merchant 3) at the general store. Denval remembers that Garren purchased a braid of garlic and asked for directions to the town’s smithy and inn. Garren was polite enough, but from their brief exchange Denval got the impression that he was a man who had suffered from some great tragedy.

The Riverbend Inn: After speaking with Denval, Garren went to the Riverbend Inn and inquired @UUID[Actor.rk26tOBkdO3YhaBL]{Jabric Roshin} (attentive male aiuvarin innkeeper 3) about a ruined castle in the Gravelands: the Herald’s Hold. Once Jabric admitted that he knew nothing about the place, Garren retired to his room, not emerging again until the next morning.

Sang’s Smithy: Garren checked out at the break of dawn and stopped by Sang’s Smithy, where @UUID[Actor.YmLtIdJHzVM4hiQb]{Krenvus Sang} (creative male human blacksmith 4) sold him some silver-tipped arrows and a sturdy hammer. Garren didn’t mention anything about his business in town, but Krenvus saw Jindel Macroi (perspicacious female human sheriff 6) stop him as he was riding toward the Chapel Bridge.

@UUID[Actor.L5QFgAu5iTTuy3co]{Jindel Macroi}: When the sheriff asked Garren about what business he had in Grayce, she learned the hunter was pursuing a vampire he called the Count of Petals. According to Garren, the Count resided in the ruins of the Herald’s Hold, a castle in the Gravelands a few hours southwest of town. Garren scribbled Jindel’s general directions to the place in a journal before continuing on. As he left, Jindel noted that Garren carried an elegant sword in an ornate scabbard and wore religious symbols of Pharasma, Iomedae, and Andoletta.

If the PCs ask, Jindel is happy to give the party directions to the Herald’s Hold, the same ones she shared with Garren just a few days previous.

Reward

For learning the location of the ruined castle where Garren was headed, award each PC 10 XP.

Overview.name: Overview
Overview.text:
Scene

@UUID[Scene.AqtFKmFqQmCbYoOu]{Gnarled Path}

You can find our provided map for the path into the Gravelands in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar. Both the @UUID[.crbqPqVTDQ0xzNtG]{Wolves by Day} and @UUID[.61H4dcB5L8D2jaIQ]{Shadows by Night} events can be run on this map, and we have provided placed tokens for whichever encounter your players face.

Having discovered Garren Shirvolt’s intended destination, the PCs can set out on their journey. Like the vampire hunter before them, they must head south across the Chapel Bridge into the Gravelands. When the PCs arrive at the bridge, they are met again by Sancovel, who asks them what they discovered about Garren. Upon hearing that the PCs intend to head for the Herald’s Hold, Sancovel mentions that if there really is a vampire in the castle, it would be safer to enter during the day. See the Day and Night sidebar for more information on how the time of day affects the flow of the adventure.

The distance to the Herald’s Hold from Grayce is about 10 miles, a journey that takes 4 hours for a typical party with a Speed of 25 feet. Almost as soon as the PCs cross the river, a pall settles over the landscape. A strange chill fills the air, and as the PCs travel, they pass abandoned farmsteads, with fallow fields and outbuildings on the verge of collapse. Apart from the weeds, scraggly trees, and odd carrion bird, the countryside is devoid of life, and yet the PCs have the undeniable feeling that something unseen observes their progress through the Gravelands, a malevolent presence lurking in the shadows just beyond the edges of their vision.

At some point during their journey to the Herald’s Hold, the PCs must contend with a group of hostile denizens of the Gravelands. If the PCs are traveling by day, proceed to @UUID[.crbqPqVTDQ0xzNtG]{Event 1.} If they’re traveling by night, proceed to @UUID[.61H4dcB5L8D2jaIQ]{Event 2}.

Day and Night

Because daylight is deadly to vampires and also affects how some of the other creatures in the castle behave, it’s crucial to track the time of day during this adventure. You can assume that there are approximately 12 hours of daylight in a day. The PCs should consider starting their journey at first light to avoid exploring the castle at night. Alternatively, they might time their departure from Grayce to arrive at the castle at dawn, giving them a full day to explore. Individual area descriptions detail how the castle’s inhabitants behave differently during the day and night. For example, at night, the count and some of his allies gather in the great hall (area @UUID[JournalEntry.xiLOxiL2uVSICHbL.JournalEntryPage.zm9GYwWrV1XD30DP]{A10}) for a feast, as detailed in that area’s description.

Wolves by Day.name: Wolves by Day
Wolves by Day.text:
The PCs are only a few miles outside of Grayce when the wind picks up, growing stronger with every minute that passes. The branches of a leafless tree sway ominously, and as the PCs pass, a flock of crows bursts into flight with a chorus of startled cawing. Shortly after, a thunderstorm rolls in, darkening the skies. A flash of lightning reveals the silhouette of a lone wolf sitting atop a low hill near the side of the road approximately 200 feet behind the PCs. The wolf answers the peal of thunder with a long, eerie howl.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.x7Aa4Tvr9eBaHryF]{Warg} @UUID[Actor.BN5Lb6IsQ9Wyu3rL]{Wolves x4}

Creatures: The lone wolf is actually a warg, but its howl attracts regular wolves, which arrive shortly thereafter to menace the PCs. It is not immediately obvious that the creatures present a danger, but upon hearing the warg’s howl, any character who succeeds at a @Check[nature|dc:17] check understands the howl was a hunting call.

The wolves reach the PCs’ initial location 3 rounds later, so if the howl made the PCs suspicious, they have some time to prepare for combat or attempt to hide.

Small trees beside the road provide standard cover, while large trees and clusters of trees provide greater cover. The wolves’ scent ability alerts them to the presence of prey in the area, but not their exact location. If the wolves can’t locate any PC after 3 rounds of searching, they lose interest and run back into the countryside.

Reward

If the PCs successfully hide from the wolves instead of fighting them, award them XP as if they had defeated the creatures in combat.

Shadows by Night.name: Shadows by Night
Shadows by Night.text:
If anything, the Gravelands seem even more desolate at night than they do during the day. The temperature drops even further, turning breath to frost and amplifying the sound of every footstep. The fact that the moon fills the area with dim light is a small blessing, but the silhouettes of shadow created by the glow seem to reach out to the PCs as they travel, attempting to clutch at them with long, dark claws.

A few hours into their journey, ask each PC to make a @Check[perception] check. Whichever character achieves the highest result notices a pair of shadowy, humanoid-shaped figures following them on the road from several hundred feet behind. If the party stops, the figures do as well, picking up the trail again as soon as the PCs resume their journey.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.VotlWUsFKdOrHWF6]{Shadows x2}

Creatures: The figures are actually shadows, undead creatures from the Netherworld drawn to the void energy that permeates the Gravelands. Each PC can attempt a @Check[occultism|dc:17] (trained) or @Check[religion|dc:17] (trained) check to protect the party with incantations and prayers, or a @Check[intimidation|dc:19] check to order the shadows to leave the party alone. In place of a skill check, a PC can attempt a @Check[will|dc:20] saving throw to steady their resolve. A critical success on any check counts as two successes. If the PCs achieve more successes than failures, the shadows disappear into the countryside. Otherwise, the shadows continue following the PCs for several minutes before closing the distance to attack.

Reward

f the PCs successfully convince the shadows to back down, award them XP as if they had defeated the creatures in combat.

Overview (R6Kz).name: Overview
Overview (R6Kz).text:
Scene

@UUID[Scene.Tceul7Epr4A29l1j]{Herald’s Hold}

You can find our provided map for Herald's Hold in the "Scenes" tab on your right sidebar.

After a grueling trek through the monster-infested Gravelands, the PCs arrive at an overgrown path (area @UUID[.fdORBkuM7MqdBLUF]{A1}) leading to the castle where the Count of Petals now resides. Originally, Herald’s Hold was built to defend against the forces of the Whispering Tyrant, providing shelter for a local noble family and a military unit that patrolled the surrounding area. As the keep’s strategic importance grew, an outer wall was constructed, complete with a gatehouse and a bell tower. The bell tower served to call local farmers to Iomedaean services in the castle’s chapel and to warn them of enemy movements.

During the fall of Lastwall, the castle’s defenders were overwhelmed by a relentless undead horde. Despite their valiant efforts to hold the keep, the inhabitants were ultimately forced to abandon their position, leaving the castle to be claimed by the undead. When the Count of Petals first arrived in the Herald’s Hold, his only company was his vampiric servant Matilda, who had been exiled with him. As the count explored his new home, however, he discovered the various creatures that had settled in the seemingly abandoned keep: gargoyles (area @UUID[.o7t1ryCOoqPlQPys]{A3}), bats (area @UUID[.xvMLPe9fh5hz17q2]{A6}), a strange congregation of undead blasphemers (areas @UUID[.8YKcVNyjbIBae1os]{A14} and @UUID[.kVUE1oVaC9no7Sy7]{A15}), and a sadistic vampire known as the Spider Prince (area @UUID[.A2FWCcZR0QYvVACs]{A19}). Though the castle’s inhabitants eventually accepted the Count as their master, not all the creatures were easily persuaded. The scholarly Alembert (area @UUID[.yhDLKZtpFgtDAQa4]{A16}) submitted to the Count’s rule only after being turned into a vampire servitor. When the harpy Kierke (area @UUID[.SpNILon8LRdBJjxV]{A5}) discovered the castle, she initially clashed with the gargoyles and would have fled had the Count of Petals not intervened. The count felt a strange kinship with the reviled creature and persuaded her to stay with an offer of mutual protection.

Features of the Hold: Since the fall of Lastwall, the once-grand castle has deteriorated due to years of neglect. The hold’s crumbling walls offer numerous handholds, requiring a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move] check to climb. Most interior rooms have 15-foot-high ceilings and thick walls that block all but the loudest sounds. Doors in the castle are reinforced wood with Hardness 15 and 60 HP (BT 30), but most are unlocked. All stairs are steep and count as difficult terrain for creatures moving up or down them.

Though torch sconces can be found on nearly every interior wall, the castle’s current inhabitants don’t need light to see, so most areas are completely dark at night. Within the keep, there are windows only in areas where it is specifically mentioned, with most rooms having only narrow arrow slits. As such, in most areas, creatures are exposed to direct sunlight only if they are positioned within a straight line extending directly from an arrow slit.

Castle Environs.name: Castle Environs
Castle Environs.text:
An old dirt path splits from the road the PCs traveled from Grayce, winding a hundred feet or so around a wooded hill before ending at the castle’s gatehouse (area @UUID[.XERdQM3QdlL5v9Do]{A2}). The castle’s walls and lonely bell tower loom above the treetops as the PCs approach.

If the PCs hesitate to enter through the gatehouse, they can circle the outer wall to find another way inside. The crenelated wall is 20 feet tall and features three sections of 5-foot-wide walkways. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.pprgrYQ1QnIDGZiy]{Climbing} the walls requires a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move] check, or @Check[athletics|dc:20|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move] check if the PCs successfully secure a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.6DCy7tEF1cxaIJMy]{Grappling Hook} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.fyYnQf1NAx9fWFaS]{Rope}. The crenelations on one section of the western wall have partially collapsed, making the climb in that area even easier (@Check[athletics|dc:15|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move] check, or @Check[athletics|dc:5|options:action:climb|name:PF2E.Actions.Climb.Title|traits:move] check with a grappling hook).

Development

If the PCs scout the castle’s exterior for at least 30 minutes at night, they notice one of the count’s servants, @UUID[Actor.nUM6kXOi4EByJKAF]{Matilda Heisen} (area @UUID[.M8DKs0KzTQONPdll]{A12}), emerge from the gatehouse with her animated broom @UUID[Actor.3tbuWyoOWD4ykJuI]{Bristles}, circle the castle, and pick a single bloom from the rose bush that grows near the castle’s southern wall. If the PCs approach them, Matilda and Bristles react as described in area @UUID[.M8DKs0KzTQONPdll]{A12}, defending themselves if attacked but otherwise listening to what the party has to say. If the PCs share their plan to destroy the Count, Matilda helps them by sharing the castle’s general layout and the routine of its inhabitants, though she stops short of joining the PCs to confront the Count herself.

Gatehouse.name: Gatehouse
Gatehouse.text:
A dirt path dotted with weeds leads up to the castle’s gatehouse, where a wooden portcullis guards the entrance. The weathered stone structure is covered in creeping ivy, and its pitched slate roof is riddled with leaky holes. Save for the occasional rustle of leaves or the distant call of a crow, the area is eerily silent.

The 30-foot-tall gatehouse serves as the main entrance to the castle. In decades past, only a handful of knights was required to secure the entrance against invaders, but now the gatehouse is completely abandoned and only one of its two portcullises remains. The castle’s inhabitants lower this portcullis during the day, when the count and his servitors are more vulnerable to attacks. After dark, however, the the barrier is raised, allowing the count’s servants to freely roam the surrounding countryside. The wooden portcullis has a Hardness of 10 and 40 HP (BT 20). A PC must make a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20] check to lift it.

Unusual activity at the gatehouse alerts the two gargoyles in area @UUID[.o7t1ryCOoqPlQPys]{A3}, though they wait until intruders reach the courtyard before launching their attack.

Courtyard.name: Courtyard
Courtyard.text:
An imposing keep stands opposite the gatehouse, while the castle’s barracks, stables, and bell tower are built against the outer walls. In the center of the courtyard, an ancient oak tree stretches its gnarled branches toward the sky, casting twisted shadows across the ground. Beneath the tree stands a statue of a mounted knight, his features eroded by weather and time. A dilapidated well sits nearby, its stone rim covered in moss.

All of the castle’s buildings can be accessed through the courtyard. A PC who succeeds at a @Check[society|dc:15|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} recognizes the statue as Sir Levar Bogurdsun, a famous slayer of undead who lived some 200 years ago. The trunk of the oak tree is covered with carvings, mostly the initials of the castle’s former inhabitants. The well contains murky, foul-smelling water teeming with mosquito larvae.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.cvfIkEF6xmWn2soN]{Gargoyles x2}

Creatures: Two gargoyles watch over the courtyard, posing as statues crouched on the keep’s battlements (area @UUID[.EtRlzzGipipd8t1O]{A18}). Unless the PCs make a stealthy approach, the gargoyles notice the intruders and attack.

The harpy Kierke (area @UUID[.SpNILon8LRdBJjxV]{A5}) is likely to notice a fight with the gargoyles. She doesn’t much care for them, so rather than risking her life for them, she watches the battle from her perch atop the bell tower. If the PCs take a beating from the gargoyles, she simply sits back and enjoys the show. If the PCs hold their own, Kierke joins the fight by firing a few stray arrows at them with her bow while staying behind cover. If the PCs return fire or if both the gargoyles fall, Kierke retreats back into the shadows.

Once one of the gargoyle dies, the remaining gargoyle retreats from the castle, never to return.

Bell Tower Stairway.name: Bell Tower Stairway
Bell Tower Stairway.text:
The worn and uneven stairs of this spiral stairway wind upward to the top of the bell tower. Narrow arrow slits pierce the walls, allowing faint beams of light to filter in.

The stairs lead to the top of the bell tower, which rises three stories above ground level. The tower’s stone walls carry echoes to the top, ensuring that any noise made on the steps is heard throughout the structure.

Encounter

Trivial 4

@UUID[Actor.aNOk64aSInxtfBs4]{Spear Launchers x10}

Hazards: Before the fall of Lastwall, the castle’s engineers constructed traps to bolster the tower’s defenses. Kierke taught herself how to re-arm the traps, using them to protect the approach to her roost in area @UUID[.SpNILon8LRdBJjxV]{A5}. The PCs can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.cYdz2grcOcRt4jk6]{Disable a Device} to deal with these traps as normal, or they can simply Interact to poke the stairs ahead of them with a staff or similar object, triggering the hazards from a safe distance.

Development

If the PCs trigger any of the spear launchers or otherwise make noise in the stairway, the harpy Kierke (area @UUID[.SpNILon8LRdBJjxV]{A5}) hears the disturbance and arrives to attack 2 rounds later. She flies down the stairwell to avoid triggering the spear launchers, approaching close enough to take a clear shot with her bow. She then withdraws to a safe location. If the PCs advance such that using her bow becomes disadvantageous, Kierke retreats to her roost at the top of the tower, using defensive tactics as described in that area.

Spear Launchers

Due to the high number of spear launchers in such a small area, we have not placed their tokens on the scene. Instead, you can see their locations marked with a "T" on the map, and you can use the link in the encounter block above to access the trap's statistics.

Bell Tower.name: Bell Tower
Bell Tower.text:
The bell tower rises thirty feet above the castle grounds, offering a view of a bleak and desolate landscape in all directions. Faded banners and crude trinkets cobbled from feathers, hair, and bones adorn the walls. Suspended from a weathered stone arch, a great bell hangs motionless, its bronze surface veiled in a dull green patina.

The bell tower served as both a lookout and a signaling post for the castle’s defenders. The bell was rung to signal enemy troop movements and other important events.

Encounter

Low 4

@UUID[Actor.heCBkcFdQFb0M22J]

Creature: A harpy named Kierke (malicious female harpy 5) has made her home in the bell tower, decorating the area with strange trophies. If intruders make it to the top of her tower, she remains airborne to stay out of reach of melee attacks. Besides shooting her bow, she uses Hungry Winds to pull foes over the tower’s battlements and send them plummeting to the ground. If Kierke decides she’s fighting a losing battle, she attempts to flee, screeching that she’s not going to die for some crumbling old castle as she flies away. Disillusioned with the Count’s ability to keep her safe, Kierke abandons the Herald’s Hold for good.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.AeIugkVFsESOcWoT]

Among Kierke’s trinkets and trophies are a horse marvelous miniature, a potion of flying, and an assortment of coins and jewelry worth 23 gp.

Stables.name: Stables
Stables.text:
The stables stand eerily silent, though the musky smell of animals still fills the air. Cobwebs hang from the weathered rafters, and the ground is littered with piles of mouldering hay and bits of broken tools.

In the past, the stables were used to house the mounts of the castle’s residents and their guests.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.xnpuGO8jEMba9wy5]{Giant Bats x4}

Creatures: The stables are now home to a group of giant bats. They roost among the rafters and are easily disturbed by any intruders. The bats pursue the PCs into the courtyard, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeezing} through one of the stable’s windows if necessary.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.V2I3MF98SiBb1J6q]

One of the stalls contains the skeletal remains of a horse. A rotting saddlebag buried beneath the bones contains coins and silver trinkets worth 37 gp.

Barracks.name: Barracks
Barracks.text:
This rectangular building is lined with rows of wooden double bunk beds, their straw-filled mattresses mouldering and moth eaten. A dining table with benches occupies the northern end of the space. Cobwebs drape the sagging wooden beams overhead, and specks of dust dance in the musty-smelling air.

Once a place of bustling activity, the barracks for the castle’s soldiers now sit in eerie silence. A storage locker rests at the foot of each bunk bed, but the contents of the lockers have long since been looted.

The headless corpse of vampire hunter Garren Shirvolt lies sprawled on the barracks floor. After sneaking into the castle and observing its sinister inhabitants, Garren made the fatal mistake of assuming this room was a safe place to rest. Garren’s presence was noticed by the gargoyles as he passed through the courtyard (areas @UUID[.o7t1ryCOoqPlQPys]{A3} and @UUID[.EtRlzzGipipd8t1O]{A18}), leading to his capture and subsequent beheading by the Count of Petals.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.VqIb7iEZ9mZrYq7a]

The Count of Petals took Garren’s weapons and most of his valuables, destroying his wooden stakes and religious symbols, and claiming the hunter’s rapier for himself. A few less valuable items have been left behind. Next to Garren’s body lies a locket containing a portrait of his partner, Lorain. Garren’s backpack functions as an adventurer’s pack that also contains a crowbar, a hammer, and a grappling hook. A hand mirror lies next to Garren’s body, but it’s been smashed to pieces.

Among the items in Garren’s backpack is his journal, which takes 4 hours to read in full. The journal contains crucial vampire-fighting knowledge: their aversion to garlic and religious symbols of holy deities, their lack of a reflection, and their inability to cross running water unaided or enter a home without invitation. The journal also details the two most effective ways to kill a vampire—exposure to sunlight or a stake through the heart. The journal discusses Garren’s search for the Count of Petals, which took him all around Ustalav and finally to Grayce. Throughout the journal, Garren frequently mentions the count being responsible for Lorain’s death.

The journal’s most recent entry recounts how Garren entered the castle around noon, climbing over a damaged section of the wall and sneaking into the keep. Garren describes the great hall (area @UUID[.zm9GYwWrV1XD30DP]{A10}) as a horrific display of depravity and notes his fruitless search for the Count’s resting place. Garren was convinced that finding the Count’s coffin would allow him to destroy the vampire without a direct confrontation, but that the Count went to great lengths to hide the coffin’s location. Garren concludes that the imagery in the chapel (area @UUID[.kVUE1oVaC9no7Sy7]{A15}) was a puzzle that held the answers he sought, but the location was too dangerous to explore further.

Reward

Award each PC 30 XP for discovering Garren’s body and the clues about the Count of Petals.

Entrance Hall.name: Entrance Hall
Entrance Hall.text:
Battered and tarnished shields and faded banners decorate the walls of the castle’s entrance hall. Several heavy wooden doors lead to other areas of the castle. Most of the doors are closed, but the one to the south stands ajar, revealing a spiral staircase winding upward.

This hall is the main entrance to the keep. The main doors lead to the castle’s central stairway (area @UUID[.JteTIjVJURYtjqE0]{A9}), the great hall (area @UUID[.zm9GYwWrV1XD30DP]{A10}), and a corridor that connects the servants’ quarters, pantry, and kitchen (areas @UUID[.M8DKs0KzTQONPdll]{A12}, @UUID[.C2rtQm7pdaO6G6lR]{A13} and @UUID[.8YKcVNyjbIBae1os]{A14}). Another smaller door leads directly into the kitchen, but it is stuck, requiring a successful @Check[athletics|dc:20|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open}.

Ambience

@UUID[Playlist.4kc6sYSc56Q2KYTT.PlaylistSound.hg7GQ6hkWQxRsGg3]{The Count's Castle}

As the party enters the castle proper, you can play this ambience sound.

Stairway.name: Stairway
Stairway.text:
These spiral stairs connect all of the keep’s levels—the crypt beneath the keep, the lower level, the upper level, and the battlements at the top. However, the bottom of the stairs have collapsed, and heavy pieces of stone and mortar now block the entrance to the crypt (area @UUID[JournalEntry.xiLOxiL2uVSICHbL.JournalEntryPage.m2FhD9E96S2qvSJO]{A21}). Any PC trained in Crafting estimates that it would take about 6 hours of work to clear the rubble. A character who succeeds at a @Check[crafting|dc:15] check deduces that the collapse was intentionally engineered to block the entrance without causing extensive damage to the surrounding structure. (Before abandoning the castle, the defenders collapsed the stairs to the crypt to prevent the undead invaders from defiling it.)

Clearing the stone blocks is an arduous task, requiring three successful @Check[athletics|dc:20] checks. Each attempt, whether successful or not, takes 2 hours, though a critical success reduces the time for that check to 30 minutes. Other characters can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.HCl3pzVefiv9ZKQW]{Aid} with a @Check[athletics|dc:10] or @Check[crafting|dc:10] check.

Unlike the lesser vampires that serve him, the Count of Petals can turn into a cloud of vapor, allowing him to slip through cracks in the rubble and enter or leave the crypt via the stairway, even while the entrance remains blocked.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.PuQfRynUSrG90bys]{Clear Stairway Rubble}

If the characters put in the work to clear the rubble, you can run the above macro to enable the Stairway's scene region to reach the basement level!

Great Hall.name: Great Hall
Great Hall.text:
This opulent chamber is lit by dozens of candles burning in chandeliers or set in niches along the walls. In the middle of the room, a banquet table is set with jeweled chalices, fancy silverware, and arrays of dark red rose petals. A tower of plates balances precariously at one end of the table, with flies and other insects swarming over the remnants of the feast the dishes once held.

An enormous, floor-to-ceiling tapestry hangs across the chamber’s southern wall. From west to east, the tapestry depicts an eagle clutching the rising sun, an angel holding the midday sun aloft, and a gold-scaled dragon waving farewell to the sunset.

Once a grand dining hall for the castle’s ruling family, the Count of Petals now uses this chamber for his decadent midnight feasts. At night, dozens of candles burn throughout the room, filling the area with bright light. During the day, only a few sputtering candles remain, and heavy curtains block what little light might enter the chamber through the arrow slits on the northern and western walls.

If the PCs arrive in this area during the day, they can inspect the mess atop the dining table. The chalices all show traces of dried blood, but bits of gnawed flesh on the plates suggest that creatures other than vampires participated in the previous night’s revelries.

Encounter

— or Extreme 4

Creatures: There are no creatures here during the day, but around midnight, the hall comes alive as the castle’s other monstrous inhabitants gather for their nightly feast. On any given night, the @UUID[Actor.3XAnernU8xBNNj0Q]{Count of Petals} can be encountered here, accompanied by one of the groups of creatures from the kitchen, the library, or the cellar (areas @UUID[.8YKcVNyjbIBae1os]{A14}, @UUID[.yhDLKZtpFgtDAQa4]{A16}, or @UUID[.A2FWCcZR0QYvVACs]{A19}). If the Count’s minions report a disturbance, the Count and his entourage investigate the area where the intruders were spotted, then begin a room-by-room search of the entire castle. If they fail to find the intruders, they return to the great hall, staying alert but resuming their feast.

If the PCs approach the Count on peaceful terms, the vampire acts curious, even courteous, at first. If Matilda (area @UUID[.M8DKs0KzTQONPdll]{A12}) is present, the Count asks her to fetch some wine from the wine cellar (area @UUID[.V7EVWmIAFvspxt8H]{A20}) before inquiring about the reason for the PCs’ visit. Sooner or later, however, the Count politely informs the PCs that he can’t let them leave the castle alive.

The PCs can persuade the Count to change his mind and let them leave peacefully with a successful @Check[deception|dc:27|options:action:lie|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check to Lie, a @Check[diplomacy|dc:25|options:action:request|name:PF2E.Actions.Request.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental] check to Request, or a @Check[intimidation|dc:27|options:action:coerce|name:PF2E.Actions.Coerce.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,emotion,exploration,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.tHCqgwjtQtzNqVvd]{Coerce}. If Alembert (area @UUID[.yhDLKZtpFgtDAQa4]{A16}) introduced the PCs to the Count, they gain a +5 circumstance bonus on these checks. On a failure, the count and his entourage surround the PCs and attack.
