The Count’s minions fight until destroyed, but if the Count is reduced to fewer than half his Hit Points, or if more than half of his followers are defeated, he Turns to Mist and retreats to the crypt (area @UUID[.m2FhD9E96S2qvSJO]{A21}), leaving his allies to deal with the PCs. Similarly, once there aren’t enough creatures left in the castle to form a proper hunting party (that is, once he has 3 or fewer surviving allies), the Count retreats to the crypt, hoping the PCs won’t find him.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.MHc71JzPsinVtt4r]

One of the chalices on the table is more ornate than the others, bearing an image of a soaring eagle similar to the tapestry hanging on the southern wall. The chalice is worth 25 gp, but more importantly, it is one of the items required for solving the puzzle in the chapel (area @UUID[.kVUE1oVaC9no7Sy7]{A15}).

Development

The tapestry on the southern wall is a bit faded but otherwise in excellent shape. Like the eagle goblet, the tapestry’s design is a clue to the puzzle in the castle’s chapel. The tapestry is much too large to transport without great effort, but it can be easily pushed aside to reveal the archways leading into area @UUID[.NALj5J3sq5UETLfp]{A11}.

Gallery.name: Gallery
Gallery.text:
The empty, broken frames that litter the floor suggest this room was once a portrait gallery. The chamber is now bare, however, with only faded spots on the walls where pictures once hung. Three low stone plinths are arranged near two archways to the north, while another pair of plinths stand against the southern wall. A suit of rusty plate armor clutching a glaive stands on display atop each of the southern plinths, while a third stands on the central plinth to the north. The eastern and westernmost plinths are empty.

This chamber was once a gallery where portraits of the castle’s ruling noble family were displayed. When the Count moved in, he shredded these portraits and smashed their frames onto the floor.

Encounter

Low 4

@UUID[Actor.CFlx1tkRxKC9qAC7]{Animated Armors x3}

Creatures: The suits of plate armor atop the plinths are enchanted to obey the orders of the castle’s owner. Unfortunately for the PCs, this means the constructs now serve the Count of Petals. Though the Count prefers living (or, more accurately, unliving) servants, he has ordered the armors to attack anyone who enters the room unaccompanied.

The armors remain motionless until a PC moves adjacent to one of them, at which point all three animate and attack. The armors fight until destroyed but don’t pursue characters who retreat from the gallery.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.Vy5HPXFvAEwgz72o]

A PC who succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:15|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search} the area notices a wall mirror in an iron frame lying face down in the chamber’s northwest corner. The mirror’s glass is intact and bears a minor enchantment: it only reflects the image of the current owner of the Herald’s Hold. As with the animated armors, technically the castle’s owner is now the Count of Petals, and thus the mirror reflects only the Count’s image. Because this is a magical effect, the mirror can reflect the Count, despite the fact that vampires don’t typically cast reflections. The Count hasn’t seen his reflection since his transformation, and if the PCs brandish the mirror, they can use the Count’s reflection to trigger his Revulsion. The mirror is an item with 1 Bulk about the size and shape of a typical shield. It can even be strapped to a forearm, though it shatters like a normal mirror if it takes any damage.

The mirror loses its magical properties if taken from the Herald’s Hold, permanently becoming a mundane (though finely made) mirror worth 65 gp.

Development

The Count ordered the suits of armor that once stood atop the empty daises to assist another of his servants, the vampire scholar Alembert. The PCs might encounter the missing armor if they venture into the castle’s library (area @UUID[.yhDLKZtpFgtDAQa4]{A16}).

Servants' Quarters.name: Servants' Quarters
Servants' Quarters.text:
The door to this room is usually locked. The room’s current occupant, the vampire servitor Matilda, typically carries the key, placing it on the dressing table beside the door when she returns here each morning to rest. Without the key, the door’s simple lock requires three successful @Check[thievery|dc:20|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks to open. Alternatively, the door can be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forced Open} with a successful @Check[athletics|dc:23|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check. A PC who listens at the door and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20] check might hear Matilda sobbing and muttering to herself on the opposite side.

The south wall of this sparsely furnished room is covered with heavy, dark curtains, casting the chamber in perpetual shadow. Two simple beds are pushed against the eastern wall, while a dust-covered dressing table with a cracked mirror stands against the opposite wall beside a rickety wardrobe.

This room was once used to house the castle’s small staff of servants. All the items in the room are rather ordinary, and many are either worn out or completely broken. The beds on the east wall show no sign of having been slept in for many years. A character who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the wardrobe and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:20|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check notices that the wardrobe’s back wall is false, concealing a narrow space in which stands a wooden coffin.

Encounter

Low 4

@UUID[Actor.nUM6kXOi4EByJKAF] @UUID[Actor.3tbuWyoOWD4ykJuI]

Creatures: Matilda Heisen (despondent female vampire servitor 4), once a diligent and loyal servant and the Count of Petals’ first victim, resides in this room. After succumbing to his hunger and drinking Matilda’s blood, the Count regretted what he had done and tried to revive her by feeding her some of his own blood. When Matilda didn’t recover, the Count buried her in his rose garden. She rose as a vampire the following night and has continued to serve the Count as an undead ever since.

During the day, Matilda sleeps inside her coffin, but loud sounds such as Forcing Open the chamber’s door or critically failing an attempt to Pick the Lock awaken her.

Initially, Matilda is suspicious of intruders, but she harbors a deep resentment toward the Count of Petals and might provide information about the nightly routines of the Count and his other servants if the PCs don’t act aggressively toward her.

She knows that the Count sleeps in the crypt beneath the castle (area @UUID[.m2FhD9E96S2qvSJO]{A21}) during the day. Though the stairs to the crypt are blocked with rubble, Matilda suspects that a secret door leads into the crypt from the wine cellar (area @UUID[.V7EVWmIAFvspxt8H]{A20}). If the PCs can make their way past the Spider Prince (see area @UUID[.A2FWCcZR0QYvVACs]{A19}), Matilda can even lead them directly to where she believes the secret door to be, though she doesn’t know the means by which to open it. With a successful @Check[diplomacy|dc:21|options:action:request|name:PF2E.Actions.Request.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.DCb62iCBrJXy0Ik6]{Request}, a PC might be able to convince Matilda to assist the party in other ways, but she fears her master too much to ever confront the Count directly.

At night, Matilda serves the Count, typically carrying bottles of blood from the wine cellar to the great hall or sweeping the castle’s chambers and corridors with Bristles, her animated broom friend. Though Bristles is mindless, the broom acts as if it has a personality, by, for example, shaking its handle in disapproval when someone drops something on the floor. Occasionally, Matilda wanders outside the castle to pick a bloom from the rose bush the grows near the castle’s southern wall (as described in area @UUID[.fdORBkuM7MqdBLUF]{A1}). She spends the rest of her time sobbing quietly in this room.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.PLsvym33YhNriTpM]

One of the drawers in the changing table contains a guardian rose.

Reward

If the PCs befriend Matilda—either here or outside the castle as described in area @UUID[.fdORBkuM7MqdBLUF]{A1}—award them 60 XP, as if they had defeated her and Bristles in battle.

Pantry.name: Pantry
Pantry.text:
This storage room is filled with broken crates and leaky wooden barrels stacked haphazardly against the rough stone walls. The floor is littered with splintered wood, scraps of cloth, and mounds of foul-smelling muck that might have once been grain. Heavy iron hooks dangle from the ceiling beams, some still clutching rusted chains or frayed ropes.

The pantry was once used to store food for the castle’s living inhabitants, but it has long since fallen into disrepair. A concealed hatch in the floor in the room’s southeast corner opens into the castle’s basement (area @UUID[.A2FWCcZR0QYvVACs]{A19}). Discovering the hatch requires a successful @Check[perception|dc:15|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search}, though if Matilda accompanies the PCs (or even if she mentioned the hatch’s existence), the PCs can locate it automatically.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.aZFMDe9SD88ey9RO]{Reveal Hatch}

If the characters discover the hatch, you can click on the macro above to move the crate out of the way, revealing the hatch and a scene region that can move the characters to the castle's basement cellar in A19.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.iICvyvPzfyJe4vzk]{Cockroach Swarms x2}

Creatures: Cockroaches and other vermin have been feasting on the sacks of grain and other foodstuffs stored in the castle’s pantry for years. The roaches largely ignore the castle’s unliving inhabitants, but as soon as a PC enters the room, two cockroach swarms emerge from beneath the heaps of rotting grain to attack them. A swarm reduced to fewer than half its Hit Points disperses, scuttling through cracks in the pantry’s floor and walls.

Kitchen.name: Kitchen
Kitchen.text:
Two stone hearths, their cold, soot-stained mouths agape, are built into the northern wall of this kitchen. Wooden tables scarred with knife marks and worn with age run down the center of the room. A heap of cauldrons, pots, and pans lies in the northeast corner beside a mound of firewood. A lingering scent of ash and stale grease fills the air.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.qvHORqASyD9Poqym]

Creatures: The kitchen is now inhabited by a group of sangrists, undead born from bodies that were completely drained of blood. If the PCs didn’t make a ruckus while entering the room (by @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Forcing Open} the door from area @UUID[.M1EzYYOXmYYmvclI]{A8}, for example), they find the sangrists standing beside the worktables rocking back and forth with their mouths wide open. Once they sense the presence of living creatures, the sangrists begin to twitch, and a low, grinding sound fills the air as their teeth gnash together. After a few moments, they rouse from their stupor and attack. In battle, the sangrists attempt to surround the PCs, circling around them through the pantry (area @UUID[.C2rtQm7pdaO6G6lR]{A13}) if necessary.

In years past, servants would labor over the hearths here, preparing elaborate dishes for the castle’s inhabitants.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.AoBkMGA7ronvdYMa]

A beautiful silver chalice bearing the gilded image of a dragon sits atop one of the worktables. The chalice is worth 25 gp and is one of the items the PCs need to solve the puzzle in the chapel (area @UUID[.kVUE1oVaC9no7Sy7]{A15}).

Chapel.name: Chapel
Chapel.text:
Ancient wooden coffins rest atop low stone biers to the north and south of the entrance to this grand chapel. To the west, an altar overlooks the space from atop a raised platform. Five-foot-tall stained-glass windows high up on the southern wall cast colorful patterns across the floor, which is set with an intricate mosaic of painted tiles, each about a hand’s width across.

Once a chapel devoted to Iomedae, this sacred space now looks desolate, with most of its relics missing or destroyed. The coffins contain nothing but old bones: the mortal remains of respected clerics who once served at the Herald’s Hold, but whose identities are now lost to time.

The entire chapel comprises a complex puzzle with two parts. The first part involves placing three chalices in the correct spots throughout the chapel. When sunlight hits the stained-glass windows at dawn, noon, and sunset, the windows function as lenses, focusing beams of light that reveal the correct chalice locations: a specific spot on the altar, inside the central arrow slit on the north wall, and within an empty niche in the room’s northeast corner. If the PCs happen to be in the chapel at one of the allotted times (at dawn, noon, or sunset), they automatically notice the corresponding location illuminated by the beam of light. Calculating the angle of a beam at any other time requires a successful @Check[nature|dc:20] or @Check[astronomy-lore|dc:18] check, though doing so during the day is a bit easier than at night, reducing the DC of the check by 2.

If the PCs have gathered the chalices from the great hall (area @UUID[.zm9GYwWrV1XD30DP]{A10}), the kitchen (area @UUID[.C2rtQm7pdaO6G6lR]{A13}), and the lord’s bedroom (area @UUID[.Y49cHKMjNj5kXJ0T]{A17}), they can arrange them throughout the chapel. Each chalice bears a unique image, and their correct locations are shown on the tapestry in the great hall: the eagle chalice (dawn), the angel chalice (noon), and the dragon chalice (sunset). The chalices can be placed at any time of the day (or night), provided they are placed in the correct locations. Once this is done, a @UUID[Actor.3bSnGA1Qlh75Y67k]{secret compartment} within the altar slides open, revealing a small key.

The second part of the puzzle involves rearranging tiles in the floor mosaic into the correct positions. Any PC who @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Searches} the mosaic notices three empty slots in the center of the mosaic. Three tiles elsewhere in the mosaic—one bearing the image of a sword, one a tower, and the third an olive branch—can be easily removed from their settings and placed into the empty slots. The book the PCs might have discovered in the library (area @UUID[.yhDLKZtpFgtDAQa4]{A16}) gives a clue as to the right order in which the tiles must be placed: sword, tower, olive branch. Placing the tiles correctly causes a hidden compartment in the chapel floor to click open, revealing a fortified storage box secured with an average lock. The small key from the first puzzle opens the box. Without the key, opening the box requires four successful @Check[thievery|dc:25|options:action:pick-a-lock|name:PF2E.Actions.PickALock.Title|traits:manipulate] checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} or a @Check[athletics|dc:30|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force it Open}, though critically failing the Athletics check breaks the moderate healing potion inside. The box contains the items detailed in the Treasure section.

Even if the PCs become stuck on the chapel puzzle, they can brute force their way to the storage box. Retrieving the key without first placing the chalices is difficult but possible, requiring a successful @Check[perception|dc:24] check first to discover the secret compartment, followed by a @Check[athletics|dc:24|options:action:force-open|name:PF2E.Actions.ForceOpen.Title|traits:attack] check to Force Open the compartment or a @Check[crafting|dc:22] or @Check[thievery|dc:22] check to dismantle the altar itself. The loose tiles and empty slots are obvious to anyone who makes even a cursory examination of the mosaic, and once the PCs discover them, they should be able to place the tiles in their proper order simply through trial and error. Finally, if Matilda (area @UUID[.M8DKs0KzTQONPdll]{A12}) is with the PCs, she might be able to assist, either by deducing some part of the puzzle herself or suggesting that the party explore other parts of the castle to track down further clues.

Encounter

Severe 4

@UUID[Actor.OqbsNdSR6G08odm0] @UUID[Actor.qvHORqASyD9Poqym]{Sangrists x4}

Creatures: When undead forced the castle’s former inhabitants to abandon the hold, the serving chaplain, a cleric of Iomedae named Genevye, stayed behind, believing that Iomedae would save her. When no salvation came, Genevye forswore her faith, transforming into a herexen, a blasphemer against her former deity. Today, Genevye’s “congregation” is made up entirely of sangrists, the twisted remnants of the castle’s fallen soldiers, who loyally defend her against intruders. As soon as they spot the PCs, Genevye and her followers attack, spewing blasphemies about Iomedae, such as “She never was the Inheritor!”

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.rtoQ3Vitd8w2On37]

The fortified storage box contains healer’s gloves, a moderate healing potion, and an ornate, wrought-iron torch fitted with an everlight crystal and an iron hood that can be closed to hide the crystal and its light. The torch is etched with a symbol of a serpent coiled around a chalice. The torch is worth 25 gp and also functions as a special key for opening the secret door in the wine cellar (area @UUID[.V7EVWmIAFvspxt8H]{A20}).

Reward

For solving both parts of the chapel puzzle, award each PC 30 XP.

Library.name: Library
Library.text:
The air in this library smells of old paper. Towering shelves crammed with books, their leather spines cracked with age, cast long shadows across the aisles.

The castle’s library contains an impressive collection of books—mostly religious tomes and historical documents, but also a small section of romantic and heroic fiction. Unfortunately, due to their age, most of the books fall apart if handled or are otherwise illegible.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.AtsqvkPa1H5o5ZWQ] @UUID[Actor.CFlx1tkRxKC9qAC7]{Animated Armors x2}

Creatures: The library is home to Alembert (scholarly male vampire servitor 4), who was once a scholar and advisor to the castle’s ruling family. When undead overran Lastwall, Alembert managed to hide from the invading monsters and spent several years alone in the castle before eventually being captured and transformed into a vampire by the Count of Petals. Alembert has since continued to pursue knowledge about various subjects, including the nature of vampirism. He’s curious about the PCs and tries to gather information from them.

If the PCs engage in friendly conversation, he tries to talk them into joining him at the count’s feast.

During the day, Alembert sleeps in his coffin, which is hidden under a secret panel in the floor beneath a large, ornate desk in the library’s southwest corner. Discovering the panel requires a successful @Check[type:perception|dc:25|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TiNDYUGlMmxzxBYU]{Search}.

Two animated armors stand guard at either end of the library, appearing to be rusted suits of armor identical to those the PCs might have encountered in the castle’s gallery (area @UUID[.NALj5J3sq5UETLfp]{A11}). The animated armors spring to life to defend themselves and Alembert if the PCs do anything remotely threatening, including trying to steal the suits of armor or moving the desk under which Alembert rests.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.3Hti8XYP9pMV4jsJ]

Some of the books in the library are still in good condition, and a few of them are valuable. Any PC who spends 15 minutes searching the library’s contents and succeeds at a @Check[perception|dc:19] or @Check[society|dc:19] check finds three books worth 10 gp each, including one titled The Founding of Lastwall. Upon picking up this book, one of its pages—intentionally torn off and placed back inside—falls out. The page is from the book’s epilogue and reads, “The founding of Lastwall: the battles fought, the strongholds built, and the peace we sought.” This is a clue for solving one of the puzzles in the chapel (area @UUID[.kVUE1oVaC9no7Sy7]{A15}). Further, consulting the book grants a +2 circumstance bonus on any check made to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about Lastwall’s history.

The Lord's Bedroom.name: The Lord's Bedroom
The Lord's Bedroom.text:
This opulent bedroom features a once-luxurious bed draped with moth-eaten sheets and plush silk pillows. A wardrobe stands against the wall opposite the bed, its doors slightly ajar to reveal old and tattered clothing. A writing desk cluttered with papers and quills sits beneath an arrow slit in the wall overlooking the courtyard. The chamber’s walls are adorned with faded tapestries depicting armies of mounted knights charging undead hordes and other past glories.

This room served as the private quarters for the castle’s ladies and lords. In addition to the clothes and personal effects—all of which are worn or damaged beyond repair—the room contains a number of letters and documents of historical significance.

A PC who spends 10 minutes sorting through the papers on the writing desk can attempt a @Check[society|dc:10] check or a @Check[perception|dc:15] check. Each successful check uncovers one of the following documents until there are none left to discover.

  • A letter written in a hurried hand by a former steward explains how the castle’s defenders collapsed the stairs to the crypt before abandoning the keep, to prevent the undead invaders from defiling the bodies interred there.

  • A journal entry written by a Lady Elara nearly 15 years ago details the planting of a rose bush outside the wall as a symbol of hope and remembrance.

  • A third document, written by a former chaplain 50 years ago, speaks of the religious significance of the chalices and tile mosaic in the chapel, hinting at their role in the puzzle in that area.

  • An expense report from over 100 years ago details the payment of 2,000 gold pieces for engineering work completed in the castle’s crypt, approved by one Sir Cedric.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.17K7K9SmWMarb02C]

In addition to the papers on the writing desk, there is an ornate silver hand mirror and a beautifully made platinum chalice bearing the image of an angel. The hand mirror is worth 5 gp. The chalice is worth 25 gp and is one of the items the PCs need to solve the puzzle in the chapel (area @UUID[.kVUE1oVaC9no7Sy7]{A15}).

Battlements.name: Battlements
Battlements.text:
A narrow spiral stairway opens onto the battlements at the top of the keep. To the north lies the courtyard, bordered by the gatehouse, the bell tower, and the castle’s high stone walls. To the south, a wooded slope stretches away from the castle, its dense canopy shifting gently in the wind.

Once a vital defensive position, the battlements allowed sentries to patrol the castle’s highest level, providing a clear view of both the inner courtyard and the surrounding land. In times of siege, rainwater from the keep’s sloped roof was collected in concealed drains to supplement the castle’s reserves.

Encounter

— or Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.cvfIkEF6xmWn2soN]{Gargoyles x2}

Creatures: A pair of gargoyles roosts on the battlement facing the courtyard (area @UUID[.o7t1ryCOoqPlQPys]{A3}). The PCs have likely already encountered the gargoyles, but if they managed to sneak into the keep without triggering the attack in area @UUID[.o7t1ryCOoqPlQPys]{A3}, it happens here instead. The gargoyles usually pose as decorations; if the PCs are unaware of them, the gargoyles ambush the party by attempting to push the weakest-looking character over the battlements.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.qMZadFtLsB8lruny]

On the northern side of the walkway, the gargoyles have gathered a pile of valuables taken from their victims. The pile contains 43 gp worth of jewelry and assorted coins, a jade cat talisman, and two lesser healing potions.

Cellar.name: Cellar
Cellar.text:
The air in this underground chamber is noticeably cooler than in the castle above and carries with it a faint, musty odor. Rows of wooden shelves, crates, and barrels line the walls, and dusty cobwebs hang from the vaulted ceiling, creating a thick canopy overhead.

The castle’s basement once served as a storage area for food, water, tools, and other supplies. The cool temperature made it ideal for preserving perishable foodstuffs, though anything that was once edible here spoiled long ago.

Encounter

Moderate 4

@UUID[Actor.DknfT9ksMiZlBxRZ]{Spider Prince} @UUID[Actor.Z1VrAwBPnLCx3vQJ]{Hunting Spiders x2} @UUID[Actor.EfADWv5gic1nL12f]{Hampering Webs x3}

Creatures: The basement is home to a vampire servitor who calls himself the Spider Prince (sinister male vampire servitor 4). The Spider Prince and his pet hunting spiders took up residence in the Herald’s Hold shortly after the fall of Lastwall. When the Count of Petals was exiled to the “abandoned” castle, the Spider Prince eagerly pledged his allegiance to the more powerful vampire.

During the day, the Spider Prince sleeps inside his coffin, which is cleverly affixed with webbing to the ceiling in the chamber’s northwest corner. The spiders guard the Prince’s coffin and attack intruders who wander too close to it or stumble into their webs (see Hazards below).

Loud sounds, such as those of intruders fighting the spiders, awaken the vampire. Two rounds later, the coffin’s lid flies open, and the Spider Prince emerges. With a sinister smile, the Prince greets the PCs by saying “What prey has fallen into our web?” before joining the battle. If the Spider Prince gains the upper hand, he likes to toy with his prey rather than finishing them off too quickly.

The Spider Prince is familiar with Matilda, as she often passes through his lair to retrieve bottles of blood from the wine cellar in area @UUID[JournalEntry.xiLOxiL2uVSICHbL.JournalEntryPage.V7EVWmIAFvspxt8H]{A20}. If Matilda accompanies them, the PCs might be able to convince the Spider Prince that they are guests of the Count of Petals by succeeding at a @Check[deception|dc:22|options:action:lie|name:PF2E.Actions.Lie.Title|traits:auditory,concentrate,linguistic,mental,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie}. A failure on the check, however, causes the Prince to attack the party immediately.

Hazards: The spiders’ webbing has three sticky, spiraling webs that extend from the floor to the ceiling, designed specifically to ensnare intruders.

Wine Cellar.name: Wine Cellar
Wine Cellar.text:
The walls of this wine cellar are lined with oak barrels and racks holding dozens of bottles, and the air carries the scent of aged wine.

This cellar still contains many barrels and bottles, some filled with fine vintages, while others hold blood from the count’s victims, stored here for his consumption. The wine barrels each bear a symbol indicating the winemaker’s brand. From left to right, the symbols are the sun rising over an oak tree, a griffin standing guard over a shield, a lion wearing a crown, a sword entwined with a laurel wreath, and a serpent coiled around a chalice.

The wall near the barrel with the serpent and chalice mark has a secret door that leads to the crypt (area @UUID[.m2FhD9E96S2qvSJO]{A21}). The mechanism was designed by an engineer at the request of a noble named Sir Cedric Bahlemann.

Cedric had the secret door built so he could sneak into the wine cellar and back without being noticed. To open the secret door, a specific iron torch must be placed in a torch holder on the wall next to the barrel. Rotating the torch triggers the mechanism that unlocks the door. After Cedric’s death over a century ago, this torch key has remained stored in the chapel (area @UUID[.kVUE1oVaC9no7Sy7]{A15}).

Noticing seams in the wall where the secret door is located requires a successful @Check[perception|dc:25|options:action:seek|name:PF2E.Actions.Seek.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check. The check result also reveals that the opening mechanism was primarily built on the other side of the wall, making it difficult to open without figuring out the specific means of opening the door. As a result, disarming the mechanism from the wine cellar side requires a successful @Check[thievery|dc:30] check, while doing so from the crypt side lowers the DC to a @Check[thievery|dc:20] check.

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.bHd3OMZQ9smld6eg]

In one of the racks, there is a bottle of vintage red wine of exceptional quality worth 25 gp.

Crypt.name: Crypt
Crypt.text:
At the center of this labyrinthine crypt is a central tomb with two imposing statues flanking its entrance. Multiple corridors stretch out in other directions, leading to smaller tombs. The air is cold and still, carrying the musty scent of damp earth.

For centuries, this crypt served as the final resting place for the noble families of the region. During the fall of Lastwall, the crypt’s main entrance was sealed with a well-executed collapse, making the secret entrance through the wine cellar the only viable way to access it. The Count of Petals discovered the crypt and claimed it as his lair. Using his ability to turn to mist, he can enter and leave easily, and he was able to transport his coffin into the crypt.

The crypt consists of ten family tombs, each containing [[/gmr 2d4#closed coffins]] closed coffins placed in recessed stone niches stacked along the walls. The Count of Petals placed his coffin in the Bahlemann tomb, which is directly northwest of the central tomb. The count noticed that the Bahlemanns’ funeral traditions and aesthetics are similar to his family’s, so his coffin doesn’t stand out too much. Unless the PCs were able to follow the count to his coffin, they have to first find it if they intend to get rid of the count for good.

A PC can move the lid of a coffin as a single action, provided that they succeed at a @Check[athletics|dc:20] check. To expedite the search, while inside a tomb, a PC can observe the coffins and attempt a @Check[crafting|dc:20|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], @Check[occultism|dc:20|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], @Check[religion|dc:20|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret], or @Check[society|dc:20|options:action:recall-knowledge|name:PF2E.Actions.RecallKnowledge.Title|traits:concentrate,secret] check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.1OagaWtBpVXExToo]{Recall Knowledge} about craftsmanship and traditions related to coffins, or a @Check[perception|dc:20] check to notice telltale signs of frequent passage. If the check is successful the character can rule out the possibility that the coffin belongs to him. When the PCs eventually find the count’s coffin, it is easy to tell it’s the correct even if the vampire is away at the time because it’s half filled with soil from his native Ustalav.

Encounter

Severe 4

@UUID[Actor.3XAnernU8xBNNj0Q]{The Count of Petals} @UUID[Actor.TcoRgbWxolzLelFb]{Collapsing Ceiling x5}

Creature: During the day, the Count of Petals sleeps in his coffin in this underground chamber, sheltered from sunlight and other outside threats. If the PCs make a loud entrance, for example, by laboring for hours to clear the collapse or triggering a new collapse within the crypt, the count awakens. He stealthily observes the characters for a while and attacks at an opportune moment. In his lair, the count feels cornered and threatened, so he uses every trick at his disposal to win. He starts by attempting to control one of the PCs with @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.OsOhx3TGIZ7AhD0P]{Dominate}, turning them against their allies. He is aware of all the collapsing sections in the crypt and leads the PCs to them but avoids triggering them himself. He uses his climb Speed or alternate forms to avoid being hindered by obstacles. If possible, he fights one character at a time, retreating to a safer position if too many characters can attack him.

Hazards: Tall vases and urns clutter some squares in the crypt, counting as difficult terrain. Further, the ceiling is weakened in certain areas of the crypt and can collapse when triggered.

Macro

@UUID[Macro.YRycZXHsF9tojQfw]{Collapse Crypt Ceiling}

You can click on the macro above to bring up a handy menu that will let you easily locate one of the collapsing ceiling areas and trigger a collapse! This will reveal a rubble tile, play a sound effect, and enable an area of greater difficult terrain in the affected square.

Difficult Terrain

@UUID[Scene.Tceul7Epr4A29l1j.Region.lDBe6cAc0qqHEEXN]{Crypt Vases}

There are also squares of the crypt have been set as difficult terrain due to the scattered urns. You can configure the visibility of these squares as desired by clicking on the "Crypt Vases" link above, for example "Always for Gamemasters" or "Always for Observers."

Treasure

@UUID[Actor.uxIzlbsG2imK5VZ9]

The beautifully crafted silver rapier that the count is carrying belonged to Garren. Most relics have been removed from the crypt, but in the second-largest tomb that is adjacent to the crypt’s west wall, there is a lion’s shield resting on top of an ancient sarcophagus.

Reward

If the PCs manage to permanently destroy the Count of Petals, award each character 50 XP as a story award for their efforts.

Concluding the Adventure.name: Concluding the Adventure
Concluding the Adventure.text:
With the Count of Petals destroyed, the PCs have ended a serious threat that could have cost many townspeople in Grayce their lives. The count’s surviving minions scatter in disarray, no longer bound by the powerful vampire’s influence. The PCs’ journey back is uneventful, and even the weather stays good all the way to Grayce—perhaps a good omen.

As they cross the Chapel Bridge, a relieved Sancovel Durantine greets them and listens intently to their tale. The citizens of Grayce, who were initially skeptical of the vampire threat, now celebrate the PCs’ victory. Fram Trangle, the proprietor of the Sing-A-Long Bar, quickly composes a new song, immortalizing the PCs’ bravery and the fall of the Count of Petals. However, despite the PCs’ success, the people of Grayce learned a lesson they won’t soon forget: they should never be lulled into thinking that their town is completely safe from vampires.
